abstract: Volcanic in origin, seamounts are widely scattered throughout the world’s ocean basins. The exact number of seamounts in the world’s ocean basins is, however, unknown. abstract: Sea Surface Temperature (SST) plays a crucial role in climate studies, tropical cyclone prediction, and marine resource management. title: From air quality forecasting to integrated and intelligent urban prediction systems
abstract: Air quality forecasting has evolved into a multi-component enterprise integrating chemical transport models, emissions, observations, data assimilation, and artificial intelligence. We argue that future progress will depend less on refinement of individual components than on integrating their interfaces across urban physics, atmospheric chemistry, machine learning, dense observation networks, human activity, and decision-making systems. We outline ten emerging directions that together constitute a transition towards integrated and intelligent urban prediction systems.

Through self-attention-based representation learning, the framework jointly models categorical and continuous transaction characteristics while overcoming limitations associated with conventional machine learning and sequential architectures

abstract: Seismic instability around underground passageways is governed by rock cracking, ground deformation, groundwater condition, support response, and earthquake demand. abstract: Assessing contaminant-induced dysfunction in complex living systems is critical, but remains technically challenging. Current methods rely predominantly on destructive endpoint readouts or low-dimensional measurements, which often fail to detect early sublethal changes in freely behaving organisms. abstract: Underwater acoustic target class-incremental open set recognition remains difficult in real marine environments, where target categories are open, labeled samples are limited, and new targets must be rejected before being incorporated into the recognition system. abstract: Spinal infections are a serious category of deep-seated infectious diseases that pose significant threats to human health. They are caused by a broad and complex spectrum of pathogens, including bacteria, fungi, and rare opportunistic organisms. Traditional diagnostic methods often face limitations in timeliness, accuracy, and source-tracing capability. abstract: Hydrological modelling is essential for water-resources assessment and climate adaptation planning; however, its application in many African basins is constrained by sparse hydro-meteorological observations, limited monitoring networks, and high uncertainty in groundwater recharge and subsurface-flow processes. abstract: El presente trabajo analiza el impacto de la inteligencia artificial en las agencias de colocación, las empresas de trabajo temporal y los servicios públicos de empleo desde la perspectiva del Derecho del Trabajo. El estudio examina cómo la implantación de algoritmos y sistemas automatizados de decisión transforma los procesos de intermediación laboral, modificando las formas tradicionales de selección, clasificación y asignación de trabajadores. abstract: Artificial water bodies are becoming more numerous, and their importance at both local and global scales is growing. abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), smartphones and computer vision are expanding the use of non-contact approaches for measuring river surface velocity and estimating discharge. This review combines bibliometric analysis with a qualitative synthesis of video-based river hydrometry, with emphasis on sensing platforms, image-processing methods, validation procedures and sources of uncertainty. abstract: Underwater fish detection is challenging. Fish can be very small in images. The contrast in scenes is often weak. Turbid water can hide details. abstract: Abstract Clay content is an important determinant of soil physical and chemical behaviour, influencing water retention, nutrient availability, and agricultural productivity. Accurate spatial prediction of clay distribution is therefore important for digital soil mapping and sustainable land management. This study compared Random Forest (RF), Cubist, Gradient Boosting Machine (GBM), and Ordinary Kriging (OK) for predictive mapping of clay content in the tropical Guinea Savanna of Kaduna State, Nigeria. title: Understanding Biogeographic Patterns in Sepiolidae (Cephalopoda)
abstract: ABSTRACT The biogeography of the bobtail squid family Sepiolidae is reviewed. Species of the Sepiolinae subfamily are only found in coastal waters of the ‘Old World’, with a high degree of diversification in the Mediterranean Sea and the Coral Triangle in the Indo‐Pacific region. The Rossiinae subfamily inhabits coasts of both the Old and New Worlds. Finally, the Heteroteuthinae subfamily exhibits widespread distribution patterns in the oceans of the whole world. This article analyzes how Defense Economics and the Political Economy of the Sea interact in the interpretation of three Brazilian strategic maritime programs: the Submarine Development Program (PROSUB), the Tamandaré-Class Frigates Program (PFCT), and the Blue Amazon Management System (SISGAAZ). abstract: Abstract We develop a random analog predictor (RAP) algorithm for the forecasting of Arctic sea ice extent (SIE) on seasonal timescales. abstract: Recent studies use machine learning (ML) models to analyze complex patterns in COVID-19 vaccination coverage, adverse effects, and antibody-mediated immune response. abstract: Abstract Modern marine surveys generate tens of thousands of underwater images per expedition, yet many are unusable due to image quality deterioration. Manual quality screening is labour‐intensive, subjective and inconsistent across observers and teams, hindering reproducible science, creating large backlogs of unprocessed imagery, and limiting real‐time algorithmic and robotic applications. abstract: The growing urgency of climate change and sustainable development has positioned green finance as a central mechanism for channeling capital toward low-carbon transitions and environmental protection. abstract: The Internet of Underwater Things (IoUT) supports marine sensing, environmental monitoring, subsea inspection, and autonomous underwater operations. However, IoUT communication is constrained by limited bandwidth, long propagation delay, time-varying underwater channels, intermittent connectivity, and strict energy budgets. abstract: Accurate prediction of cumulative plastic strain (CPS) is essential for assessing the deformation stability of marine strata subjected to artificial ground freezing (AGF). This study aims to clarify how variations in clay content and pore-water salinity regulate cyclic responses after freeze–thaw (FT) disturbance. abstract: Object detection and classification in videos has emerged as a core challenge in computer vision, with applications spanning autonomous driving, surveillance, healthcare, robotics, and human– computer interaction. Unlike still-image object detection, video-based detection requires handling additional complexities such as temporal coherence, motion blur, occlusion, and real-time constraints. abstract: This study investigates the influence of bottom topography on the development of instabilities in Gulf-Stream-like jets using a two-layer quasi-geostrophic model. abstract: Rip currents pose significant threats to coastal safety and to autonomous marine vehicles operating nearshore. abstract: Flood-prone Bangladesh requires accurate short-term rainfall prediction, yet conventional numerical weather prediction (NWP) models remain computationally intensive and regionally limited in skill. This study evaluates and compares four deep learning (DL) architectures — Simple Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Stacked LSTM, Bidirectional LSTM (BiLSTM), and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) — against the physics-based Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model for one-hour-ahead rainfall forecasting across six climatologically diverse stations in Bangladesh. Traditional approaches typically rely on behavioral observations or indirect neural measures, which limits direct insight into learners' internal cognitive representations. abstract: Background Superficial fungal infections present a growing threat to global public health. Traditional diagnostic techniques, including microscopy and culture, are time-consuming and subjective, often limiting diagnostic accuracy. Artificial intelligence (AI)-driven diagnostic tools offer a promising adjunct to improve efficiency and standardization of microscopic fungal detection. Methods We systematically compared six deep learning models, including the You Only Look Once (YOLO) series, the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) series and the Detection Transformer (DETR). title: A Lightweight Channel–Frequency Joint Attention Network for Underwater Ship-Radiated Noise Separation
abstract: Underwater acoustic signals (UAS) in marine environments are often contaminated by noise from biological activity, ocean waves, and equipment. Under low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) conditions, target ship-radiated components and background noise are strongly mixed, making reliable underwater detection, recognition, and communication challenging. abstract: Accurate stratigraphic characterization is essential for offshore geotechnical engineering, where nearshore marine sediments commonly exhibit strong spatial variability and complex stratigraphic transitions. Although machine learning (ML) methods have shown promise for CPTU-based stratigraphic identification, random sample-based validation may overlook spatial dependence among CPTU measurements and consequently overestimate model generalization. title: Rethinking Potential Flood Damage Assessment: A Data‐Driven Alternative to Varnes‐Based Models
abstract: ABSTRACT Reducing flood damage is a key challenge for both administrators and communities, particularly in the face of increasing climate‐related impacts. A fundamental prerequisite for effective damage reduction is a detailed understanding of the spatial distribution of territorial susceptibility to flood damage. abstract: Abstract This present study introduces a cloud-based geospatial and machine learning framework for assessing coastal urban heat island (UHI) dynamics in Thoothukudi coastal region, Southern India, using 12 seasonal Landsat composites (2010–2025) processed through Google Earth Engine (GEE). Seasonal classification followed Indian Meteorological Department definitions: Summer (March-June), Northeast Monsoon (October-November) and Winter (December-February). title: F-MNet: flux-modulated network for radial power prediction of space reactors
abstract: Rapid and accurate prediction of radial power distribution is crucial for the design and operation of space nuclear reactors. However, traditional Monte Carlo methods incur prohibitively high computational costs, while conventional data-driven surrogate models face severe overfitting and insufficient generalization capabilities under small-sample and data distribution shift conditions. title: Comparative Machine Learning Approaches to Landslide Susceptibility in Southeastern Türkiye
abstract: Landslides are among the most destructive natural hazards in mountainous regions, causing severe economic losses and infrastructure damage. Reliable susceptibility mapping is essential for hazard mitigation and sustainable land-use planning, particularly in tectonically active areas such as southeastern Türkiye. abstract: This study develops a deep learning-based object detection model using YOLOv8 to detect Bawal Bintang/Star Pomfret fish (Trachinotus Blochii) in real time and with high accuracy from a video dataset captured in a 3x3x3 m3 Floating Net Cage (KJA) off the Karimunjawa coast. The video was taken using an Underwater Camera placed at a position 1.5 meters deep at KJA. This study aims to develop an automated fish monitoring system to detect Star Pomfret fish and improve efficiency and accuracy in fisheries resource management. title: Dual-porosity-Permeability Modeling in Carbonate Reservoirs: A Review on Characterization Techniques,Modeling Approaches, and CCS Applications
abstract: Carbonate reservoirs are extremely heterogeneous owing to fractures, vugs, micropores, and karst features. This heterogeneity complicates fluid-flow prediction, characterisation, and simulation in both naturally fractured reservoirs and carbon capture and storage (CCS). Dual-porosity modeling remains the dominant approach for capturing matrix–fracture interactions in these systems. title: Advancing Sustainable Development in OECD Countries: Carbon Emission Efficiency, Growth–Emission Decoupling, and Digital–Structural Transformation
abstract: ABSTRACT Advancing sustainable development requires reconciling economic growth with carbon reduction. This study investigates carbon emission efficiency (CEE), growth–emission decoupling, and digital–structural transformation in 35 early OECD member countries from 1995 to 2023. It combines the IGT decoupling model, a three‐stage DEA framework using the Super‐EBM model, the GML index, and truncated regression to evaluate decoupling patterns, static and dynamic CEE, and the drivers of low‐carbon transition. title: Artificial intelligence driven framework for enhancing sustainability and resilience in communal cattle insurance in Lupane District Zimbabwe
abstract: Communal cattle farming in Sub-Saharan Africa continues to face destabilization from non-linear climate variability, yet insurance penetration remains negligible. In Lupane District, Zimbabwe, uptake is exceptionally low at approximately 0.01%, despite recurrent droughts that threaten household livelihoods. This study aimed to develop an AI-driven framework to enhance sustainability and resilience in communal cattle insurance within the district. abstract: Software-Defined Networking (SDN) enhances network programmability and manageability through decoupling the control and data plane, though the same has resulted in the controller being an attractive assault target. abstract: ABSTRACT Acoustic Emission (AE) technology is a key technical means for real-time damage monitoring of composite materials.However, its accuracy in identifying composite damage mechanisms and capacity for deep information mining remain constrained by the traditional paradigm of analyzing individual features of high-dimensional AE signals one by one. title: Noninvasive diagnosis of Alzheimer’s disease: a review of emerging biomarkers and multimodal approaches
abstract: Noninvasive biomarkers are expanding access to biological assessment of Alzheimer’s disease (AD). This review evaluates blood-based, neuroimaging, retinal, electrophysiological, digital, and behavioral measures alongside structured cognitive and functional assessment, and examines multimodal and machine-learning approaches for detection, differential diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment monitoring. title: Autonomous Underwater Vehicle Hull Design: Design Principles, Hydrodynamic Evaluation and Optimization
abstract: Autonomous Underwater Vehicles have become essential platforms for ocean exploration, environmental monitoring, offshore engineering, and military applications. As the primary hydrodynamic component of an AUV, the hull significantly influences drag, endurance, maneuverability, and payload capacity. With advances in computational fluid dynamics (CFD), parametric modeling, optimization algorithms, and artificial intelligence, AUV hull design has evolved from empirical approaches to simulation-driven and intelligent optimization frameworks. title: Regulatory language limits satellite-based enforcement in marine protected areas
abstract: Abstract The international community has committed to protect 30% of the ocean by 2030, and satellite monitoring can now detect industrial fishing inside marine protected areas (MPAs) at near-global scale. Yet remote detection establishes only a vessel’s identity, position, time, and movement; whether those facts can support enforcement action depends on how the law is written. abstract: This study proposes an integrated deep-learning framework for rapid urban flood hazard mapping and damage prediction from compact rainfall descriptors. A simulation-based reference database linked synthetic rainfall scenarios with grid-based flood-depth maps generated by a validated rainfall-runoff and inundation model and category-specific damage indicators derived from damage assessment. title: Explainable Deep Learning Reveals Future Changes in East Asian Extreme Winter Predictability
abstract: Deep learning-based approaches have emerged as powerful tools for seasonal prediction, yet their skill remains limited for extreme anomalies, and warming climates may alter predictability sources. Here we present a convolutional neural network (CNN)-based framework to assess how seasonal predictability changes in a future climate, focusing on East Asian extreme winters. Our CNN, trained on CESM2-LENS simulations for historical and SSP3-7.0 scenarios and optimized with Amplitude Focal Loss, reliably captures seasonal mean and extreme temperatures. title: Bibliometric analysis of VR interventions in cancer research based on multiple databases: mapping research hotspots and developmental trends
abstract: Background Virtual reality (VR) has become an increasingly popular tool in cancer care over the years. It shows promise in areas like pain management, psychological support, surgical training, and rehabilitation. Even though more studies are being done, there has not been a thorough analysis of the research trends in this field. This study looks at how VR interventions in cancer research have evolved over the past two decades, identifies research hotspots, and explores future directions. abstract: Most Caribbean reef-building corals reproduce by broadcast spawning numerous egg-and-sperm bundles simultaneously into the water column prior to external fertilization. This is a pivotal bottleneck in the lifecycle of broadcast-spawning organisms because it relies on the synchronization of gamete release to precise species-specific nights and times. However, changes in spawning patterns have been documented in a wide variety of species from different oceans. title: An uncertainty-aware compute continuum architecture for underwater species detection
abstract: Continuous underwater ecological observations generate massive volumes of visual data from heterogeneous systems. Automated object detection is increasingly used to extract organism abundance information from them, but long-term deployments are constrained by limited bandwidth and power, as well as by uncontrolled environmental variability that degrades data quality and model reliability. title: A comprehensive review of marine and coastal waste collection robots covering mobility and waste collection mechanisms
abstract: Coastal and marine ecosystems are progressively influenced by geological and anthropogenic factors along with increasing levels of human-induced pollution such as plastics, chemical substances, and heavy metals. Such pollutants affect both marine biodiversity and human health through bioaccumulation and ecosystem degradation. Acute, efficient, and innovative engineering solutions are needed, in which robotics should emerge as a key enabling technology for exploration. abstract: Abstract Background Although the Southeastern United States (SE US) has been identified as a major terrestrial carbon sink, the balance of CO 2 and CH 4 fluxes from its wetlands remains poorly constrained due to strong environmental heterogeneity and limited regional-scale assessments. In this study, we used observations from 24 wetland sites located in the SE US, including freshwater and salt marshes, to train machine learning models (Random Forest, XGBoost, Support Vector Machine, Artificial Neural Network, and Partial Least Squares Regression) to predict monthly mean gross primary productiv

abstract: High-entropy alloy composites (HEACs) extend compositionally complex alloy design by coupling a multi-principal-element matrix with discrete ceramic, carbonaceous, metallic, or high-entropy reinforcement architectures. Their performance is therefore governed not only by the chemistry of the constituent phases, but by reinforcement size and topology, interfacial reaction thermodynamics, defect populations, and the thermal–mechanical history imposed during consolidation or solidification. abstract: Changes at the land–sea interface reveal whether mangrove systems advance seaward, retreat landward, or undergo coastal squeeze as their seaward and landward boundaries converge. Yet global assessments have largely relied on area change, with less focus on these directional processes. This study applies a global coastline-normal transect framework to Global Mangrove Watch data for 1996, 2008, and 2020. abstract: Drought is a natural disaster with serious impacts on agriculture, water resources management and ecosystem balance. Ongoing global warming and climate change exacerbate drought cases. Therefore, proper tools are essential for long-term drought monitoring and efficient drought forecasts. The Palmer Drought Severity Index (PDSI) is a reliable indicator developed to monitor long-term drought trends and is widely used to define agricultural and hydrological droughts. abstract: ABSTRACT Coral reefs are under increasing threat from local and global stressors, resulting in changes to the composition and spatial structure of benthic habitats. This study uses high‐spatial resolution satellite imagery and landscape metrics to analyse changes to the shallow, turbid reef at Sebastião Gomes on the Abrolhos Bank in the Southwestern Atlantic Ocean between 2010 and 2024. abstract: Monitoring sea-level variations in tidal flats is essential for managing coastal flooding, environments, and aquaculture facilities. title: Machine learning prediction of chloride convection-zone depth in marine tidal concrete with model explainability and experimental validation
abstract: Reliable prediction of chloride convection-zone depth is important for service-life assessment of tidal-zone concrete, but most data-driven chloride studies focus on surface concentration or diffusion-related indicators. This study proposes a data-driven prediction and explainability framework for chloride convection-zone depth. abstract: Abstract This study presents a simulation-driven deep learning framework for vibration-based damage detection and localization in composite structures using mode shape images. CNNs are trained exclusively on numerically simulated data and directly validated against experimental measurements, addressing the domain gap between numerical models and real-world structural behavior without requiring experimentally labeled data for training. title: Physics-Informed Digital Twin for Climate-Induced Degradation Prediction in Aging Coastal Bridges
abstract: Climate change has accelerated the deterioration of aging coastal bridges by increasing chloride exposure and environmental variability, creating significant challenges for long-term Structural Health Monitoring. While Digital Twin technology enables real-time infrastructure monitoring, existing approaches often lack explicit representation of the physical mechanisms governing structural degradation. title: A comprehensive review on recent pretrained multimodal deep learning models from architectures to future directions
abstract: In recent years, multimodal deep learning has made great progress, enabling artificial intelligence to learn across text, audio, images, video, and other data. title: Integrating molecular approaches for standardised monitoring of North Sea biodiversity and ecosystem dynamics
abstract: The North Sea is among the largest and most productive shallow marine ecosystems, heavily influenced by historical and ongoing exploitation. Monitoring of North Sea biodiversity is vital for a better understanding of ecosystem responses to ongoing anthropogenic pressures and for informing effective management and conservation strategies. abstract: Global assessments project widespread coral reef degradation under continued ocean warming and acidification, underscoring the urgent need to identify and account for the full diversity of coral reef systems within conservation planning. Atolls are dynamic reef-ocean-land systems whose persistence depends on coral reef sediment production, land-sea connectivity, and cross-ecosystem nutrient subsidies. abstract: Abstract A detailed geochemical assessment from Ennure Creek was conducted to evaluate metal distribution, ecological risk, and potential human health impacts. abstract: Accurate classification and localization of Cloud-to-Ground (CG) lightning are essential for the development of reliable early warning systems in tropical regions and the improvement of thunderstorm monitoring. This study proposes a multimodal machine learning framework for CG lightning classification and polarity-based localization with synchronized atmospheric and electromagnetic measurements collected in Melaka, Malaysia, in 2024. abstract: Abstract. The importance of carbon storage in continental seafloor sediments is increasingly recognized, yet the role of benthic macrofaunal biodiversity in the regulation of these processes remains poorly understood. Benthic macrofauna contributes to organic carbon cycling through respiration and secondary production, while the sediment reworking (bioturbation) and ventilation (bioirrigation) of infauna promote the redistribution and remineralization of organic matter in sediments. abstract: Detection of anomalies in the ionosphere is essential for ensuring reliable timing, navigation, and positioning services of the Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS). This study proposes a machine learning approach to anomaly detection during severe geomagnetic storms based on the Wavelet Transform with the Isolation Forest algorithm. abstract: Marine heatwaves are increasing in both frequency and intensity, exposing coral reefs to prolonged periods of thermal stress and driving recurrent mass coral bleaching. abstract: Microplastic (MP) contamination in commercially important freshwater fish represents an emerging concern for aquatic ecosystem integrity and human food safety. This study presents an interpretable machine learning framework for predicting and assessing MP accumulation in European sea bass (Dicentrarchus labrax), Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus), bighead carp (Hypophthalmichthys nobilis) and crucian carp (Carassius auratus) collected from four retail markets in Yichang City, Hubei Province, China. abstract: Wastewater lagoon systems remain a dominant form of secondary treatment for small communities in the United States due to their low energy requirements, operational simplicity, and affordability. Despite their widespread use, national inventories of lagoon systems are fragmented, inconsistently reported, and often outdated, with non-discharging systems particularly underrepresented. These data gaps limit effective infrastructure planning, environmental assessment, and equitable allocation of resources. title: Conditional updates of neural network weights for increased out of training performance
abstract: This study proposes a method to enhance neural network performance when training data and application data are not very similar, e.g., out of distribution problems, as well as pattern and regime shifts. In contrast to previous approaches to out of distribution problems, which alter the inputs and outputs of an operator, our approach alters the operator itself. Here, we especially aim to alter the weights and biases of a neural network to mitigate the out of distribution problem. title: Taxon‐specific community structure partitions marine particle size spectra into stable and dynamic components
abstract: Abstract Oceanic particle size distributions (PSDs) link plankton community structure to biogeochemical cycling. Although the influence of community composition on size spectra is well recognized in theoretical approaches, long‐term empirical evidence connecting taxon‐specific variability to bulk PSD structure remains limited. Here, we use 9 yr of taxon‐resolved PSDs spanning ~ 7–100 μ m in the surface waters of the oligotrophic North Pacific to show that deviations from canonical scaling are structured, repeatable, and attributable to variability in specific taxa. title: Multiscale pH fluctuations on a stable algal reef community (SE Sardinia, Tyrrhenian Sea)
abstract: The Mediterranean Sea is threatened by ocean acidification and warming, in combination with habitat loss, pollution, invasive species, and overexploitation. Assessing local high-frequency pH variability in the context of relevant basin-scale time series data is essential to understand ecosystem vulnerability. We report the results of the Italian national pH monitoring based on the Marine Strategy Framework Directive, and the pH dynamics observed at Capo Carbonara. An experimental station equipped with a pH sensor and CTD probe was deployed at 32 m depth on a sandy bottom bordered by Coralligen
institutions: Istituto Superiore per la Protezione e la Ricerca Ambientale

title: The policy implementation paradox: governance failure and elite capture in Southeast Asia’s green transition
abstract: Achieving equitable green growth requires substantial institutional reorganization, often committed to through formal Circular Economy (CE) and Bio-Circular-Green (BCG) transition frameworks. Despite public policy narratives highlighting grassroots sustainability and the inclusion of small enterprises, the underlying political-economic processes and structural barriers that dictate their execution remain insufficiently understood. title: Projected intensification of summer upwelling along the Southeastern Coast of China
abstract: Coastal upwelling is a key dynamical process along the southeastern coast of China, regulating regional circulation, biogeochemical cycling, and marine ecosystem dynamics. While previous studies have provided valuable insights into the mechanisms and variability of this coastal upwelling, its future evolution and underlying physical drivers under climate change remain unclear. Here, we investigate projected changes in coastal upwelling along the southeastern coast of China during 2006–2100 using a high-resolution (0.1°) coupled-model realization under the Representative Concentration Pathway 8

title: Three honours across three professional communities: Emeritus Professor Dr. Kwan Hoong Ng and the regional evolution of radiology and medical physics

title: A rapid-updating method for anthropogenic NO x emissions based on convolutional neural networks and TROPOMI NO₂ observations
abstract: Nitrogen oxides (NO x = NO + NO2) are air pollutants primarily emitted from anthropogenic sources, however, bottom-up anthropogenic NO x emission inventories often suffer from update delays. The TROPOspheric Monitoring Instrument (TROPOMI) provides near-real-time, high-resolution NO2 column densities, offering new opportunities for timely NO x emission prediction. Given the short lifetime of NO x in the lower troposphere, local emissions can influence observations over distances of ~100 km. title: Comparative analysis of the applicability of artificial intelligence models for code generation
abstract: This article analyses the potential for using selected artificial intelligence models in the code generation process during the development of a web application. The analysis was conducted in the Windsurf environment using the Open Data Explorer project as a case study. These models were compared in terms of functional effectiveness, implementation efficiency, the quality of the generated code, project stability, and the types of errors that occurred during subsequent iterations. title: A Hybrid Quantum Optimization Framework for Oil Spill Detection Using Marine Radar
abstract: Oil spills at sea pose a serious threat to marine ecosystems and coastal economic development. Therefore, rapid and accurate detection of oil spills is crucial for emergency response and environmental protection. Marine radar offers unique advantages in short-range, continuous, and all-weather monitoring, making it an important supplementary tool for oil spill detection. title: An attention-enhanced residual network framework for structural damage detection based on structural health monitoring data
abstract: Local damage in steel structures often produces only subtle differences in vibration responses, and measurement noise can further reduce identification robustness. To address these challenges, this study proposes a structural damage identification method that combines Markov transition field (MTF) encoding with a coordinate-attention-enhanced residual network. First, vibration responses are discretized into a finite number of states using approximate equal-frequency binning and then converted into MTF images. title: Social Representations of Artificial Intelligence from Basic Education Teachers in Aguascalientes
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) in education has evolved to integrating advanced models such as ChatGPT, and it’s therefore conceived as a complementary tool that promotes personalized learning and processes optimization, despite some ethical challenges related to access inequalities, algorithmic biases, dehumanization, and the fear of teacher replacement. title: Content Validation of a Scale for Assessing Artificial Intelligence Use in Learning
abstract: The purpose of this study was to determine the content validity of a scale designed to evaluate the use of artificial intelligence in university learning (EPIA-U). The instrument consists of 28 items distributed across four dimensions—Academic support, Study personalization, Satisfaction with use, and Perceived dependence—and was subjected to the judgment of nine experts with backgrounds in education, technology, and research. title: El poder infraestructural en Inteligencia Artificial
abstract: Os estudos de comunicação e mídia frequentemente analisam as dinâmicas de poder na inteligência artificial (classificatória, preditiva, generativa, agentiva, etc.). No entanto, escassos estudos abordam o poder emergente do desenvolvimento infraestrutural da IA. Portanto, este ensaio explora —com uma perspectiva genealógica — três dimensões da servitização do aprendizagem profundo. Primeiro, a composição da pilha de tecnologia da IA e a plataformização de microsserviços distribuídos (I). Segundo, a integração e reconfiguração das práticas cotidianas (II). title: The burden of inflammatory bowel disease in Asia (1990–2023) and projections to 2050: A comprehensive analysis of the 2023 global burden of disease study
abstract: BACKGROUND: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), including ulcerative colitis (UC) and Crohn's disease (CD), is becoming an increasingly important public health concern in Asia, with rising incidence and prevalence reported across the region. Despite progress in global burden studies, data gaps remain in Asia due to variations in healthcare and socio-demographic factors. This study aims to address these gaps by assessing the burden of IBD across Asia from 1990 to 2023, focusing on regional trends in UC and CD. title: Where wet biomass waste-to-energy can work: An open-data readiness screen for Southeast Asia
abstract: Wet biomass is often presented as a large renewable-energy resource in Southeast Asia, but resource size alone does not identify where implementation evidence is strong enough to justify detailed assessment. This study develops an open-data pre-feasibility screen for three contrasting pathways: anaerobic digestion of the organic fraction of municipal solid waste (OFMSW), palm oil mill effluent (POME) biogas/compressed biomethane (bio-CNG), and livestock biogas. title: Between the Sacred and the Synthetic: The Future of Religious Imagination through Artificial Intelligence
abstract: This study examines how Gemini, GPT, and Adobe Firefly visualize Islamic worship, sacred space, and Muslim futures. The corpus comprises 72 images generated from ten verbatim English-language prompts submitted to each platform. Every prompt-platform combination was run at least twice, yielding 24 outputs per platform. Content analysis of the full corpus compared the retention of prompt-defining Islamic motifs, futuristic framing, ritual and spatial organization, textual and calligraphic treatment, human or post-human agency, and genre hybridization. title: Scalable and Physics-Aware Graph Neural Network for Emulating Peak Storm Surge Over Large Geo-Spatial Domains
abstract: Surrogate models, or metamodels, provide a versatile data-driven emulation of peak storm surge predictions to support coastal risk assessment applications. They are established using databases of storm simulations developed using a high-fidelity hydrodynamic model, with the objective of replacing that model in subsequent predictions. The surge predictions in this context are spatially distributed over a large coastal domain with up to millions of nodes. title: Integrating Remote Sensing, Geographic Information Systems, and Machine Learning for Environmental Monitoring and Sustainable Resource Management
abstract: Environmentally sensitive coastal areas are rapidly becoming urbanised, increasing pressure on vegetation, wetlands, surface-water resources and the natural resource base. The current study combines remote sensing, Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and machine learning to evaluate changes in Land Use/Land Cover (LULC) and environmental conditions in the Lekki–Ajah axis of Lagos State, Nigeria. Built-up areas, vegetation, wetlands, surface water and bare/exposed land were mapped using multitemporal satellite imagery and spatial datasets. title: Challenges and innovations in machine learning-driven hate speech detection on X (formerly Twitter): A methodological and taxonomic review
abstract: Detecting hate talk on public news manifestos, particularly X (formerly Twitter), has enhanced a bigger focus on document excavating and the study of natural language processing (NLP). This systematic literature review (SLR) offers an itemized test of current approaches, machine intelligence forms, challenges, and time engaged in hate talk discovery. The review covers 91 research documents written from 2016 to 2022, preferred through an all-encompassing election process. title: Deep learning–assisted coral morphology cover across 742 sites on the Great Barrier Reef (2022–2025): A Great Reef Census citizen science dataset
abstract: Abstract Citizen science can expand the spatial extent of coral reef surveys, but its value is often limited by inconsistent data quality and slow manual analysis. Here we combine volunteer‐collected imagery with deep learning to overcome these constraints, delivering validated coral cover data at scale. We present 46,879 benthic seascape images from 742 sites across 267 reefs on the Great Barrier Reef, collected by Great Reef Census volunteers between September 2022 and February 2025. institutions: Queensland Department of Environment and Science

title: Exploring pre-service teachers’ STEM readiness in Indonesia, Malaysia, and Thailand: Comparative insights from teacher education programs
abstract: STEM education has become a central agenda for enhancing human resource quality and global competitiveness. This study explored pre-service teachers’ readiness to implement STEM teaching in Indonesia, Malaysia, and Thailand, with particular attention to their conceptual understanding, implementation ability and experience, perceived barriers and institutional support, and attitudes toward STEM education. title: Propagation-physics-guided channel augmentation and temporal–spectral fusion for domain-robust underwater acoustic target recognition
abstract: Underwater acoustic target recognition (UATR) is essential for ocean-intelligence sensing, but deep learning-based models often suffer from performance degradation under ocean acoustic domain shift. This problem arises because ship-radiated noise recorded under different propagation channels, vessel operating states, background noise levels, and recording configurations may exhibit substantial distribution discrepancies. title: Hip Fracture Registry and Audit Readiness in Southeast Asia: A Scoping Review and Public-Evidence Implementation Gap Map
abstract: Hip-fracture registries and audit systems support feedback, benchmarking, and quality improvement, but the public visibility of this infrastructure across Southeast Asia is unclear.This review mapped publicly identifiable registry readiness, audit, care quality, and secondary prevention evidence for hip-fracture care across Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) countries.We conducted a scoping review and public-evidence implementation gap map across the 10 ASEAN member states.Searches covered PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature (CINAHL)

title: Towards optimized forward–forward training for neural networks
abstract: Abstract This study investigates and enhances the Forward–Forward (FF) algorithm, a novel neural network training approach recently introduced by Geoffrey Hinton. Unlike Back-Propagation (BP), which relies on separate forward and backward passes, FF performs two forward passes, one with positive (real) data and one with negative data, potentially generated by the network itself. title: Ecological recovery, maintenance-dependent protection: a synthesis of three nature-based solutions for coastal resilience in New Jersey
abstract: Hurricane Sandy in 2012 led to an extensive deployment of coastal nature-based solutions (NbS) in New Jersey, providing a unique opportunity to evaluate their physical and ecological performance under multi-year monitoring programs. This study presents a comparative synthesis of documented outcomes across three NbS categories implemented in New Jersey, including beach nourishment and dune restoration on the Atlantic coast, thin-layer placement (TLP) of dredged material for estuarine salt marsh restoration, and living shorelines based on constructed oyster reef systems in Delaware Bay. title: Microplastic contamination in edible invertebrate from seafood markets along the Egyptian Red Sea and Mediterranean Sea
abstract: Marine environments contain plastic debris that potentially elicits adverse effects in aquatic organisms. In Egypt, microplastic pollution has been recognized as a significant issue; however, risks associated with human consumption have not been fully elucidated. Here, we evaluated the frequency of occurrence, abundance, and distribution of microplastics (MPs) in edible marine invertebrates (mussel, shrimp, and crab) sold at markets along the Mediterranean and Red Sea coasts of Egypt. title: Application of Machine Learning-Based Models in Early Detection of Production Anomalies in Oil and Gas Wells
abstract: The early detection of production anomalies in petroleum wells is critical for optimizing operational efficiency, reducing downtime, and mitigating environmental risks, particularly in complex and prolific regions like the Niger Delta. This study investigates the application of both unsupervised and supervised artificial intelligence models for anomaly detection using historical well production data. journal: Gazi University Journal of Science Part A Engineering and Innovation

title: How heterogeneous environmental regulations shape marine sustainable development: evidence from coastal China
abstract: Marine sustainable development requires reconciling economic growth with environmental protection, making the design and selection of effective environmental regulatory instruments increasingly important under tightening marine ecological constraints. In this study, marine sustainable development is measured by marine green total factor productivity (MGTFP). title: Asymmetric bloom lengthening drives high-latitude ocean chlorophyll accumulation imbalance
abstract: Terrestrial ecosystems maintain a stable time-allocation budget between growth and senescence, but whether this applies to the ocean remains unclear. Using fused satellite LiDAR and ocean-color data (2007–2022), we show that marine phenology is variable and asymmetric. In high latitudes ( > 50°N), the bloom growth-to-decline ratio (RGD) is declining by ~5.3% per decade. title: Internal Solitary Waves in the Xisha Areas: Evidence From SWOT Observations
abstract: Abstract The Xisha Islands, situated in the northwestern South China Sea, are characterized by diverse topography conducive to a wide range of oceanic dynamic processes. Internal solitary waves (ISWs), large‐amplitude nonlinear waves in continuously‐stratified oceans, are pivotal for oceanic energy transport, vertical seawater mixing, and material exchange. This research leverages Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) mission data to investigate ISWs near the Xisha Islands. title: SEMANTIC SEGMENTATION OF OIL-CONTAMINATED LAND FROM PLANETSCOPE IMAGERY USING NEURAL NETWORK MODELS
abstract: Monitoring of oil-contaminated land is a pressing challenge for Kazakhstan. During the Soviet era, oil production at a number of fields relied on the so-called pit method, whereby drilling waste, process fluids, and associated wastewater were collected in purpose-dug earthen pits adjacent to extraction sites, leaving a substantial legacy of oil-contaminated areas requiring remediation and systematic monitoring. abstract: Aquaculture pond health depends on continuous water quality assessment.Dissolved oxygen probes and titration apparatus remain costly for smallholder farmers.Affordable monitoring therefore demands sensors a microcontroller can read directly.Published IoT deployments converge on temperature, pH and turbidity sensing.Most machine learning studies instead train on full laboratory panels.Such accuracy claims assume instrumentation that target farmers rarely own.Our work restricts model inputs to three microcontrollermeasurable parameters.Five classifiers and one quantized neural network were bench
journal: INTERANTIONAL JOURNAL OF SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH IN ENGINEERING AND MANAGEMENT

title: Environment-conditioned deep learning for severe convection nowcasting
abstract: Severe convection produces localized hazards that often require warnings before radar echoes fully reveal storm development. Convective initiation and the maintenance of intense convection remain challenging for radar-only nowcasting because pre-convective signals may be absent from recent radar observations, and strong echoes often decay rapidly in forecasts. title: Predicting long-term degradation of prestressed bridge girders using a hybrid finite element and deep learning approach
abstract: Prestressed concrete girders are widely used in bridge and railway infrastructure. However, their long-term performance is highly vulnerable to environmental effects, particularly corrosion, which significantly compromises structural serviceability and durability. Accurately quantifying corrosion-induced deterioration over extended periods remains challenging due to the substantial time and computational demands of conventional finite element analyses. title: Gigantes tecnológicos y poder en plataformas de inteligencia artificial: una revisión crítica
abstract: Estudios críticos, administrativos y técnicos de comunicación y de ciencias sociales suelen diagnosticar vínculos estrechos entre los gigantes tecnológicos (Big Tech) y el nuevo verano de la inteligencia artificial (IA). Ese consenso se sintetiza en la idea de Big AI y supone que los modelos subsimbólicos funcionan bajo la premisa “más grande es mejor” (bigger is better). title: Flood susceptibility in a coastal backwater floodplain: a spatially validated multi-event SAR framework for Alappuzha, India
abstract: Flood susceptibility mapping (FSM) is dominated by studies of upland catchments. At the same time, near-sea-level coastal and backwater floodplains, where inundation is shaped by reclamation, land use, tidal influence and constrained drainage rather than relief, remain comparatively under-explored. Existing studies also commonly rely on single-event inventories and machine-learning models validated through random data partitioning, which can overestimate predictive skill in spatial data. title: APPLICATION OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE ON MARKETING PERFORMANCE, GUEST SATISFACTION AND LOYALTY: IMPLICATIONS FOR SUSTAINABLE INTERNATIONAL HOTEL BUSINESS IN ABUJA, NIGERIA
abstract: The growing adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping hotel marketing and guest-service delivery, yet empirical evidence on its implications for guest satisfaction and loyalty in developing hospitality markets remains limited. This study examined AI applications in selected international hotels in Abuja, Nigeria, focusing on their perceived contribution to marketing performance, guest satisfaction and loyalty, as well as barriers to adoption. title: Low-impulse slamming response and residual flexural capacity of seawater-degraded CARALL fibre-metal laminate marine panels
abstract: The carbon–aluminium couple behind CARALL fibre-metal laminates is galvanically active in seawater, and the metal–composite bond suffers first. title: A Hybrid Deep Learning Framework for Tropical Cyclone Intensity Estimation With Spatiotemporal Features and Physical‐Persistence Adjustment
abstract: Abstract This study proposes SOPHIENet (TC Satellite‐Observed Physical‐Persistence and Spatiotemporal Hybrid Intensity Estimation Network), a hybrid framework for Tropical Cyclone (TC) intensity estimation. SOPHIENet integrates a convolutional neural network, the Convolutional Block Attention Module, and a physical‐persistence adjustment mechanism. journal: Journal of Geophysical Research Machine Learning and Computation

title: From track to impact: a review of multi-hazard typhoon forecasting and resilience
abstract: While recent advancements in tropical cyclone prediction have been extensively documented, existing review literature remains heavily fragmented into isolated academic domains, such as artificial intelligence, data assimilation, or coastal hydrodynamics. This fragmentation obscures the operational reality of disaster risk reduction. To address this critical gap, this paper presents a transdisciplinary systematic review of the entire end-to-end climate service value chain. title: Transboundary marine radioactive pollution under China’s ecological and environmental code: implementation gaps and directions for reform
abstract: Marine radioactive contamination can cross national boundaries, limiting the effectiveness of legal responses confined to a single jurisdiction. China has responded by progressively developing its legal framework through successive revisions to the Marine Environment Protection Law of the People’s Republic of China and the consolidation of relevant rules in the Ecological and Environmental Code of the People’s Republic of China (EEC). title: A review of the effectiveness of solutions to achieve the good environmental status of the marine environment
abstract: Europe’s seas are at the nexus of a “triple crisis” of biodiversity and habitat loss, climate change, and pollution, increasingly eroding the ecosystems’ resilience and capacity to provide ecosystem services. Although essential, existing European Union policies, especially the Marine Strategy Framework Directive (MSFD), proved insufficient. title: Cleaner peri-urban agricultural transitions under nitrogen-related water constraints: A teacher-validated evaluation of land-use alternatives in Almere Oosterwold, the Netherlands
abstract: Peri-urban agriculture is increasingly expected to contribute to sustainable urban development while reducing the environmental pressures associated with land-use change and water-quality degradation. A key challenge is how to compare alternative agricultural configurations that maintain productive land use while lowering nitrogen-related environmental burdens before implementation. This study develops a teacher-validated framework for evaluating cleaner peri-urban agricultural land-use alternatives, using Almere Oosterwold, the Netherlands, as a living-lab case. title: Multi-Index Assessment of Potentially Toxic Metal Contamination in Mangrove Sediment of the Port Klang Coastal Area, Malaysia
abstract: Mangrove sediments in the Port Klang coastal area are long-term sinks and secondary sources of potentially toxic metals in an urban port-estuarine setting. This study assesses surface mangrove sediments from five stations across the Port Klang coastal mangrove-estuarine area, a tropical port system where Klang River catchment inputs, tidal exchange, port operations, shipping, industrial estates and estuarine resuspension interact. title: Redes neuronales artificiales en psiquiatría. Generalidades y aplicaciones
abstract: Desde sus primeros tiempos, la inteligencia artificial ha encontrado un campo fértil de aplicación en el dominio médico; quizá por la forma en que se modelan y abordan eventos, y por la apertura del personal sanitario. Lo importante es que ha ayudado a resolver de manera práctica problemas de interés; según la época, se han aplicado algoritmos de tendencia. title: Climate-driven habitat loss of Chinese sturgeon in the Northwestern Pacific and implications for marine protected area design
abstract: The conservation of endangered anadromous fishes depends on understanding their full-lifecycle habitat requirements, yet the marine phase of Chinese sturgeon ( Acipenser sinensis ) remains a critical knowledge gap despite over 90% of its lifespan occurring at sea. We integrated multi-source occurrence data (satellite tagging, bycatch records, environmental DNA, and online databases) and applied an ensemble modeling framework (Biomod2 with eleven algorithms) to predict habitat suitability across the Northwestern Pacific Ocean (100°E–150°E, 10°N–55°N). title: Terrain-Adaptive Hydrostatic-Pressure-Assisted Seawater Reverse Osmosis with Managed Brine Return and Conjunctive Groundwater Blending in the Qattara Depression, Egypt: A Screening-Level Conceptual Study
abstract: Inland desalination in arid regions involves trade-offs among seawater conveyance, desalination energy, brine management, and freshwater delivery. This study presents a screening-level conceptual assessment of a terrain-adaptive hydrostatic-pressure-assisted seawater reverse osmosis (HP-SWRO) corridor in the Qattara Depression, Egypt. title: Bearing capacity and safety factors of ring foundations in spatially variable soils: a hybrid FELA-machine learning approach
abstract: Abstract Ring foundations efficiently support axisymmetric structures like silos, storage tanks, chimneys, and cooling towers with reduced concrete volume compared to solid circular foundations. Their ultimate bearing capacity is strongly affected by asymmetric loading and spatial variability in soil properties. This study presents a hybrid machine learning framework to predict normalized bearing capacity factors and safety factors for ring foundations in spatially variable cohesive-frictional (c-φ) soils. title: Deep-learning climate emulator ACE2 reveals a global decrease in 15th-century tropical cyclone frequency under El Niño-like sea surface temperatures
abstract: Abstract The relatively short modern observational record limits our understanding of the relationship between global tropical cyclone (TC) frequency and sea surface temperature (SST), resulting in uncertain future TC projections. Using novel deep-learning-based past-millennium simulations with the Ai2 Climate Emulator version 2 (ACE2), we provide insight into the connections between SSTs and TCs. title: Few Annotations, High Accuracy: Transfer Learning and Data Augmentation Improve Passive Acoustic Monitoring of the Vulnerable African Manatee
abstract: ABSTRACT Monitoring elusive and threatened species remains a major challenge in ecology and conservation, particularly in turbid aquatic environments. The African manatee ( Trichechus senegalensis ), listed as Vulnerable by the IUCN, remains difficult to survey using visual methods, limiting reliable assessments of its distribution and population status. title: Machine learning-aided groundwater level and CO2 emission estimations in Indonesian tropical peatland
abstract: ABSTRACT Tropical peatlands store a large fraction of global soil carbon and emit large amounts of CO 2 from peat decomposition and root respiration. abstract: The conservation of Komodo dragons ( Varanus komodoensis ), an apex predator whose top-down regulation of ungulate prey helps sustain savanna ecosystem balance, and an iconic yet endangered species, requires a nuanced understanding of habitat suitability, wildfire susceptibility, and conservation zoning within Komodo National Park (KNP), Indonesia. abstract: Exploration and reflection on problem-based learning building critical thinking. This study develops a classification system for nine marine fish species by combining VGG19-based feature extraction with XGBoost. Using 9,000 balanced RGB images from the Kaggle Large-Scale Fish Dataset, the workflow includes EDA, preprocessing, an 80:20 data split, feature extraction, and model training. title: Energy-efficient clustering and mobile sink routing in wireless sensor networks using quantum-inspired optimization and deep learning
abstract: Wireless sensor networks (WSNs) require energy-efficient clustering and adaptive routing to maintain reliable communication and prolong network lifetime under varying node density, initial energy, communication range, packet size, residual energy, routing distance, latency, and mobile-sink conditions. However, conventional clustering and routing methods generally optimize these aspects separately, resulting in inefficient energy distribution, increased routing overhead, unstable sink mobility, and reduced network sustainability. title: Fundamentos técnicos y dilemas éticos en los modelos de lenguaje natural en las Inteligencias Artificiales
abstract: El siguiente artículo tiene como objetivo mostrar los fundamentos de los generadores de lenguajes naturales dentro de las inteligencias artificiales, desde la elucidación de las Redes Neuronales hasta las arquitecturas Transformers de los modelos GPT. Explicar los fundamentos técnicos permitirá entender cómo funciona la “comprensión del lenguaje” bajo estas nuevas tecnologías, contrastándolos con los desafíos éticos que presentan estos nuevos avances y el impacto de su uso sin una adecuada supervisión humana.

abstract: Bluff-body flows combine early separation, coherent wake organization, vortex shedding, and strong sensitivity to geometry, Reynolds number, inflow condition, and three-dimensional transition. These features make them both canonical fluid-mechanics benchmarks and demanding targets for neural-network-based modeling. This review provides a representative, physics-oriented synthesis of neural-network approaches for bluff-body flows. title: Water intelligence for adaptive wastewater infrastructure: integrating artificial intelligence, advanced materials, living technologies, and resource recovery
abstract: ABSTRACT Wastewater infrastructure must accommodate variable influent loads, complex contaminant mixtures, stringent discharge requirements, water reuse, and resource-recovery objectives within a single operational system. This review defined water intelligence as the evidence-gated capacity to acquire reliable observations, infer system states, generate constrained decisions, implement physically realizable interventions, verify outcomes, and update operation within predefined safety boundaries. abstract: The rapid propagation of disinformation through social media presents a significant challenge because information diffusion is characterized by complex interactions among users and continuously evolving temporal patterns. Conventional deep-learning and transformer-based approaches primarily focus on textual or sequential representations and may not fully capture the structural and temporal characteristics of information propagation. abstract: La introducción de los vehículos autónomos constituye una de las transformaciones más significativas de la movilidad contemporánea, con el potencial de redefinir la manera en que las personas y los bienes se desplazan. abstract: Rutting deformation in flexible pavements of Southwest Nigeria constitutes a persistent infrastructure failure. abstract: Accurate water-level prediction is essential for effective water resource management in Kazakhstan. Reservoirs play an important role in irrigation, hydropower generation, and water supply. abstract: Abstract Dithered simultaneous‐source acquisition improves seismic survey efficiency but introduces complex overlapping blending noise that hinders subsequent processing and inversion. Therefore, deblending becomes an essential step for providing high‐quality data. While deep learning has shown promise for deblending in nonshot domains, existing methods often treat gathers in isolation, overlooking the potential of interrelationships between adjacent records. title: MACHINE LEARNING FOR URBAN HEATING VECTOR ESTIMATION TO SUPPORT CITY DECARBONIZATION
abstract: To support urban decarbonization, XGBoost classifiers were developed to predict residential heating energy vectors in Spain using open cadastral, census, and Energy Performance Certificate data. Training across climate zones C1, D1, and D3 evaluated the impact of non-spatial, coordinate-derived, and neighbour-corpus features. abstract: Introduction Detection of underwater waste in freshwater environments remains a challenging task due to the scarcity of domain-specific annotated datasets and adverse visual conditions caused by poor visibility, inconsistent illumination, color degradation, and suspended particles. Unlike existing underwater debris datasets that primarily focus on marine environments, freshwater pond ecosystems remain relatively underrepresented. abstract: La expansión de la inteligencia artificial en ámbitos estratégicos plantea un problema específico para el derecho internacional público: dificulta identificar dónde ocurre un hecho jurídicamente relevante y, como consecuencia, qué conducta debe ser atribuida, a qué sujeto y en qué condiciones puede activarse la responsabilidad internacional. title: Retos para la ética de la investigación clínica en el contexto de las inteligencias artificiales: hacia una inteligencia aumentada
abstract: El auge y la penetración de los modelos de inteligencia artificial en todos los ámbitos de la vida humana constituyen un fenómeno continuo y dinámico.La investigación científica igualmente se ha visto permeada por el advenimiento y la democratización cada vez mayor de dichas tecnologías.Su implementación, desde el tratamiento de datos hasta su utilización en la redacción científica, hace que el uso de estos recursos deba observarse desde una perspectiva ética que nos permita reflexionar sobre hasta qué punto su uso resulta adecuado y si constituye o no un riesgo para las personas participantes

title: El insustituible juicio humano: Desafíos de la revisión por pares frente a la Inteligencia Artificial en el Proceso Editorial de manuscritos científicos
abstract: En publicación científica se han probado distintos incentivos para optimizar el proceso de revisión por pares (RPP), sin lograr un impacto significativo en los tiempos y calidad de las revisiones. La irrupción de la Inteligencia Artificial (IA) y de los grandes modelos de lenguaje (LLM) prometen revolucionar el futuro de la RPP. Objetivo: Analizar los desafíos que plantea la IA en el proceso de RPP, revisar la evidencia y proponer lineamientos para el proceso editorial de Andes Pediatrica. title: Cetacean acoustic occurrence in the Southern Ocean from biologged southern elephant seals
abstract: The Southern Ocean is a crucial habitat for multiple species of cetaceans, from mysticete species to odontocetes such as sperm whales and delphinids. However, their presence at high latitudes is still poorly known due to the remoteness of the area, with little literature on delphinid presence and sparse sampling along mysticete migration routes. title: An Automated Deep Learning-Driven Data Analytics Approach for Silica Content Prediction in Potential Iron Flotation Using Real-World Mineral Processing Plant Operational Data
abstract: In the mineral sector, flotation is an extensively applied process to separate useful minerals from waste materials. On the other hand, it remains challenging due to numerous interacting physical and chemical components that complicate process control in real-time plant environments. Due to this, data-driven methods are applied to analyze and model flotation behavior. In iron flotation, predicting the silica content in iron ore concentrate is crucial for assessing final product quality and plant performance. title: Markers of resilience to stony coral tissue loss disease and putative probiotic functions in the microbiomes of the coral, Orbicella faveolata
abstract: Abstract Stony coral tissue loss disease (SCTLD) is widespread within the Caribbean and affects at least 22 species of reef-building coral. Bacteria have been implicated in the etiology of SCTLD, but the community of bacteria and archaea may also contribute to SCTLD resistance. To identify potential mechanisms through which microbes contribute to SCTLD resistance, we sequenced metagenomes from 41 colonies of the threatened coral, Orbicella faveolata, in the lower Florida Keys. title: Graph hybrid neural network integration for enhanced diabetic retinopathy detection in retinal image
abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a progressive microvascular complication of diabetes that affects the retina. This study presents a hybrid graph neural network (GNN) architecture that combines a graph isomorphism network (GIN) with GraphSAGE to improve performance and interpretability in diabetic retinopathy (DR) classification. The framework captures both local and broader lesion relationships, which enhances classification–especially when labeled data are scarce. title: Predicting Early Childhood Stunting and Associated Factors in Kenya Using Machine Learning
abstract: Background: Stunting in the first two years of life remains a major public health concern in Kenya, affecting about one in five children and leading to long-term consequences on cognitive development and economic productivity. Traditional, largely reactive approaches that rely on linear statistical models have a limited ability to capture the complex, non‑linear determinants of stunting. abstract: Abstract This work presents a machine learning approach for analyzing the corrosion behavior of AZ31 magnesium alloy using digital images acquired with a smartphone camera assembled to a homemade studio. abstract: The movement of European eels (Anguilla anguilla) has long been a mystery keeping scholars on their toes. abstract: Abstract The archaeal symbiotic Nanobdellales have been isolated with their hosts from a shallow hot marine vent off Iceland and from terrestrial hot springs in Yellowstone National Park and Japan. title: A New Approach in Diabetes Diagnosis: Performance Comparison using Machine Learning Algorithms
abstract: According to the International Diabetes Federation (IDF), approximately 589 million adults are expected to be living with diabetes in 2025. This number continues to rise due to unhealthy eating habits and poor quality of life. Early and accurate diagnosis is crucial to prevent organ damage and improve patient outcomes. This study aims to develop a method for predicting diabetes without requiring individuals to visit healthcare facilities or undergo laboratory tests, using machine learning (ML) techniques to enable early intervention. title: Jornalismo de dados e Inteligência Artificial: Estudo de casos para compreender alcances e limitaçõesda automatização na América Latina
abstract: This paper analyzes ten cases of AI integration in data journalism (two global, eight Latin American). AI expands operational capacity (volume and speed) but does not replace epistemic decisions, which remain under editorial control. The automation gradient —signaling, predictive scoring, large‑scale classification, total output validation— is proposed as an alternative to the automatic/semiautomatic binary. In Latin America, the main constraint is data governance: the lack of public information in processable formats limits the reach of AI, regardless of the models’ capabilities.

title: Climate-mediated population declines in the common Floridian coral, Porites astreoides
abstract: Despite global coral reef degradation, Porites astreoides has become increasingly dominant on Florida and Caribbean reefs and is often considered climate-resilient. However, whether its apparent success reflects an increase in absolute abundance or simply a rise in relative abundance remains unclear, as does its ability to persist under continued climate stress. title: Object-based image analysis supporting site selection in Posidonia oceanica restoration efforts
abstract: Posidonia oceanica meadows are a valuable yet vulnerable coastal ecosystem endemic to the Mediterranean Sea, providing key ecosystem services. However, these habitats have declined markedly over the last decades due to multiple anthropogenic stressors. Given their low natural recovery rates, active restoration through transplantation has become a widely adopted strategy to mitigate this loss. title: An adaptive federated deep learning approach for efficient DDoS detection in IoT edge networks
abstract: Abstract The rapid growth of the Internet of Things (IoT) has expanded the attack surface of modern networks, motivating the need for accurate detection of DDoS and botnet activity in resource-constrained settings. Centralised intrusion detection systems (IDS) face privacy, scalability, and heterogeneity challenges that limit their suitability for IoT. This study suggests a Federated Learning-based Intrusion Detection System (FL-IDS) for IoT edge networks in order to get around these restrictions. abstract: El presente artículo analiza la relación entre el desarrollo de la inteligencia emocional y los desafíos que plantea el uso creciente de la tecnología en el ámbito educativo. abstract: Ensuring the safety and sustainability of gas distribution networks depends heavily on the timely detection of pipeline leaks, since leaks that go unnoticed can cause substantial losses and create serious safety risks. When applied to multi-class leak types, however, conventional detection approaches often prove insufficiently accurate. abstract: Abstract Offshore seismic swarms north of Puerto Rico and the Virgin Islands remain poorly characterized due to limited azimuthal coverage from the inland Puerto Rico Seismic Network (network code PR). title: Deep learning framework for weather aware spatiotemporal traffic speed forecasting on mountainous tourist roads
abstract: Accurate traffic speed prediction plays a crucial role in optimizing traffic management and mitigating incident impacts. However, the presence of complex and dynamic spatiotemporal dependencies, coupled with changes in weather conditions, makes predicting the main components of traffic flow a major challenge. abstract: Coastal wetlands provide essential habitats for migratory waterbirds. Although wetland restoration is increasingly implemented, its effectiveness in improving habitat quality and the ecological mechanisms underlying such improvements remain insufficiently understood. Focusing on Jiangsu Yancheng Wetlands & Rare Birds National Natural Reserve, a key site along the East Asian-Australasian Flyway, this study evaluated whether and how restoration enhanced wintering habitat quality for the endangered Red-crowned Crane ( Grus japonensis ). abstract: Abstract Water table depth (WTD) is a key control on wetland ecology, hydrology, and forest productivity in coastal plain landscapes, yet continuous groundwater records are rarely available. This limitation makes it difficult to quantify climate controls on groundwater response and derive wetland hydrology indicators. This study addressed these gaps in the Santee Experimental Forest, South Carolina, using 13 wells across three watersheds. title: Imbalance-robust predictive maintenance using deep learning with virtual measurement modeling and explainable AI
abstract: Abstract Predictive maintenance (PdM) has become a key enabler of intelligent industrial systems; however, its effectiveness is often constrained by measurement uncertainty, the absence of raw sensor signals, and severe class imbalance between normal and failure events. This paper proposes a measurement-aware predictive maintenance framework that utilizes operational variables as virtual measurement proxies, enabling measurement-oriented analysis without requiring raw sensor signals. abstract: The increasing scale, structural complexity, and service requirements of bridge infrastructure have created a growing need for reliable and intelligent structural health monitoring (SHM) systems capable of continuously assessing structural condition and supporting timely maintenance decisions. abstract: The obligate coral-symbiotic crab Trapezia septata is a key mutualist in Pocillopora coral holobionts, providing essential services such as predator defense and sediment removal. However, fundamental life-history parameters, particularly growth rates and lifespan, remain unquantified, hindering the development of predictive population models for coral reef restoration. abstract: The integration of sustainable energy into atmospheric water harvesting offers a promising solution for supplementary water supply in off-grid and dry regions. abstract: Abstract Air pollution in Africa is a critical public health issue that results in deaths of people, especially in places where urbanisation and vehicle emissions are increasing. To minimize risks, the present study used spatial analysis and a hybrid Genetic Algorithm–Machine Learning (GA–ML) approach to predict mortality rates. abstract: Dynamic operation of reverse osmosis (RO) systems can produce flux–pressure hysteresis even when intrinsic membrane transport properties remain constant. abstract: Ecotourism promotes sustainable development, but evaluating tourists’ experiences becomes difficult because of different multi-source feedback. abstract: Many governments allocate access to high-rent natural resources through long-term concessions rather than competitive auctions. abstract: In the Ganges-Padma Basin, flood peaks integrate complex signals from monsoon rainfall, antecedent basin wetness, and upstream discharge. abstract: Accurate prediction of heat flow is critical for geothermal resource assessment yet remains challenging in structurally complex basins because of sparse measurements and the coupled effects of multiple geological processes. abstract: The corrosion behavior of weathering steels in marine atmospheric environments emerges from the synergistic interactions among alloy chemistry, exposure duration, and environmental loading, exhibiting strong nonlinearity and multiscale coupled responses. abstract: Sargassum blooms in the tropical North Atlantic have surged to unprecedented levels, causing massive algal tides that severely impact coastal ecosystems. abstract: Abstract Advancing the design of polymeric membranes through material screening and discovery offers a powerful strategy to guide future membrane fabrication tailored to a wide range of separation challenges. However, there is a need to develop explainable artificial intelligence frameworks capable of recognising workflow steps and producing interpretable reports from long, untrimmed video sequences. abstract: Abstract Greenhouse gases (GHGs) such as Carbon Dioxide (CO 2 ), Methane (CH 4 ), and Nitrous Oxide (N 2 O) play critical roles in global climate change. abstract: Marine organic waste, including fish processing byproducts, shellfish residues, aquaculture waste, aquatic plant biomass, and coastal beach wrack, represents an abundant yet underutilized biomass resource with significant potential for supporting a circular bioeconomy. This review comprehensively evaluates recent advances in the valorization of these marine waste streams through sustainable biotechnological and thermochemical approaches. abstract: Accurate integrated water vapor (IWV) estimates are essential for atmospheric monitoring, yet reanalyses can retain systematic discrepancies relative to in situ observations. This study develops a radiosonde-informed machine learning framework to correct ERA5-derived IWV over Europe and assess spatial and temporal generalization. abstract: Control over reservoir water levels and gate settings at the spillways is key for preventing floods, protecting people living downstream, and efficient utilization of stored water especially when the reservoir is nearing its maximum capacity. This research project centers on the Shetrunji Reservoir in Gujarat, India, investigating the potential of machine learning to improve operations. abstract: Mass coral bleaching events linked to climate change are a major contributor to the global degradation of coral reefs. Recovery largely depends on the growth of survivors and successful coral recruitment; however, recruitment is highly variable and influenced by many factors. This study quantified the size structure of coral communities within Laamu Atoll, in southern Maldives, using colonies < 5 cm in diameter as a proxy for recent coral recruitment. Recently, biomass-derived carbon materials are compelling candidates for bifunctional electrocatalysts, benefiting from their renewable nature, low cost, inherently porous architecture, and naturally doped heteroatoms. abstract: ABSTRACT Artificial intelligence (AI) has rapidly transformed smart surveillance systems, significantly leveraging technologies such as deep learning, computer vision, and adaptive monitoring. abstract: Abstract Urban heat stress is increasing in semi-arid Mediterranean towns, making the identification of Urban Cool Island (UCI) patterns essential for climate-resilient urban planning. This study developed an integrated remote sensing, GIS, and explainable machine-learning framework to map potential UCI locations in Oued Zenati, northeastern Algeria, using Landsat 9 imagery and geospatial environmental variables processed in Google Earth Engine. title: A partnership business model for a sustainable sea salt industry in Indonesia
abstract: In Indonesia, the domestic sea salt industry faces major challenges for supply and demand. Therefore, this study seeks to develop a partnership business model aimed at fostering sustainability in the Indonesian sea salt industry. Utilizing an exploratory descriptive methodology with a qualitative focus, this study incorporates the business model canvas, sustainability aspect, partnership canvas, and value innovation framework. abstract: Three marine protected areas, i.e., Borkum Reef Ground, Sylt Outer Reef, and Dogger Bank, have been established within the European NATURA 2000 program in the German Exclusive Economic Zone of the North Sea. Within them, we analysed the effect of the varying impact of mobile bottom-contact fishing on infauna communities in selected focus areas as a baseline study prior to the exclusion of mobile bottom-contact fishing since 2023.
