title: TILE: Bridging LLMs and Table Foundation Models for Tabular Learning with Strings
abstract: Real-world tables are often heterogeneous, combining numerical features with free-form string columns. Table foundation models (TFMs) excel on numerical tables but require strings to be encoded numerically, while large language models (LLMs) hold semantic knowledge but are not designed for tabular predictions. Most existing bridges use LLMs as plug-in encoders for cell strings, yet how to extract representations effectively for tabular learning remains underexplored. title: Identifying Arctic states vulnerable to rapid ice loss with a convolutional neural network
abstract: This work investigates the incidence of rapid ice-loss events in the Arctic, in which a substantial fraction of September sea-ice is lost in only a few years. Such events are seen to occur in climate model simulations forced with increasing greenhouse gas concentrations, but not as yet in the relatively short observational record. We train a convolutional neural network (CNN) using six large climate model ensembles to diagnose vulnerability to rapid ice-loss events. title: OceanFlow: Coherent Flow Matching for Probabilistic Ocean Modeling
abstract: Probabilistic ocean modeling is essential for risk-aware marine operations, climate analysis, and scientific decision-making, where downstream decisions depend on the conditional distribution of future ocean states rather than a single deterministic trajectory. Recent data-driven ocean models have made deterministic global ocean modeling increasingly accurate and efficient, but probabilistic ocean modeling remains underdeveloped. title: Prediction-Informed Landing Window Planning for UAV Landing on USV in High Sea States
abstract: Autonomous landing of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) on unmanned surface vehicle (USV) is difficult in high sea states. Existing hierarchical landing methods often infer future USV motion only implicitly from short observation histories, which limits their ability to adapt to severe and rapidly changing sea conditions. This paper presents a prediction-informed hierarchical control framework. A pretrained model is developed to explicitly predict the USV attitude during high-level landing decisions. title: Feature Space Adaptation for Effortless Gaussian Process Flows
abstract: Outside the linear-Gaussian regime, conditional sampling from Gaussian processes (GPs) is challenging. Recent methods such as FlowGP (Moss et al., (2026)) can condition on arbitrary non-linear and non-Gaussian statements, but at considerable cost: an expensive iterative and high-dimensional diffusion that requires hand-specified kernel hyperparameters. title: NAViLoss: An Underwater Navigation-Aware Dual-Residual Objective for Physics-Consistent Learning
abstract: Autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) commonly rely on inertial navigation systems (INS) aided by Doppler velocity logs (DVLs) for reliable underwater navigation. Accurate DVL velocity estimation is therefore essential for successful operation. Recent learning-based methods have demonstrated improved DVL velocity estimation, particularly under degraded measurement conditions. title: REACT: Physically and Chemically Consistent Reconstruction of Marine Active Tracers
abstract: Reconstructing global sea surface pH from sparse observations is critical for monitoring ocean acidification and understanding marine carbon cycling. Traditional assimilation and inverse models are physically grounded but costly for large-scale reconstruction. Recent black-box and physics-guided AI models improve efficiency, but are mainly designed for passive tracers, where the reconstructed variable is also the transported inventory. title: On-Board Anomaly Detection for Efficient Marine Environmental Monitoring
abstract: Marine ecosystems are impacted by various threats such as oil spills, algal blooms, and sediment floods, which disrupt habitats, wildlife, and human activities. Advances in satellite imagery and Artificial Intelligence (AI) have enhanced our capabilities for early detection and mitigation of such hazards. In this paper, we propose a marine event detection pipeline for Earth observation satellites equipped with multi- or hyperspectral sensors. title: Reliability-aware short-term roll prediction for unmanned surface vehicles via multi-task learning and adaptive centralization
abstract: Reliable roll prediction of unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) is essential for ensuring navi?gational safety and enhancing autonomous decision-making. While existing studies primarily focus on improving prediction accuracy, the quantification of prediction reliability remains insufficiently addressed. title: Can Cybernetic Twins Function as Regulators for Sustainable (Sea)Food Systems?
abstract: Feeding the growing global population without permanently overshooting local-to-planetary boundaries demands a transition from conventional resource extraction to holistic models. Current digital twin applications in (sea)food systems primarily emphasize predictive monitoring and decision support, whereas their integration with heterogeneous socio-economic-ecological systems (SEES) remains incomplete. title: Leveraging Digital Twins for Bridge Maintenance Prioritization following Coastal Flood Events
abstract: Abstract Bridges are critical to the US transportation network and are essential components of our infrastructure systems. Coastal floods can disrupt these structures, isolating communities and highlighting the urgent need for effective maintenance and prioritization strategies. This study introduces a digital twin framework that evaluates the impacts of coastal floods on bridge substructures by integrating multisource data and employing spatial algorithms like inverse distance weighting and k - d tree methods to model flood severity. title: A Digital Twin Framework for Monitoring and Fault Identification of Marine Internal Combustion Engines
abstract: Monitoring the current technical condition of a marine internal combustion engine and diagnosing the causes of deviations of its operating parameters from reference values are important tasks for ensuring the efficient and safe operation of marine power plants and vessels in general. This study develops a digital twin framework for marine engine diagnostics and demonstrates its integration with the DEPAS 5.0W diagnostic system. abstract: Abstract We present a localized data assimilation (DA) scheme based on sequential Markov Chain Monte Carlo (SMCMC) (Ruzayqat et al., 2024, https://doi.org/10.1002/qj.4710 ), a provably convergent method for filtering high‐dimensional, nonlinear, and potentially non‐Gaussian state‐space models (SSMs). title: Hydrodynamic Modeling of Maximum Tidal Levels at the Tondano River Estuary
abstract: The Tondano River Estuary is an area affected by the interaction of tides, currents, winds, and bathymetric conditions that affect sea level and hydrodynamic conditions of the coastal area. This study aims to analyze the maximum tidal height at the Tondano River Estuary using the MIKE 21 Flow Model (FM). title: Hyperspectral Satellite Imagery for Digital Twinning of Boreal Forests
abstract: Digital twins of the Earth require Earth observation data streams that are both spatially continuous and informative about the state of the modelled system. For forests, the standard optical data source is Sentinel-2, whose 10 m multispectral imagery trades spectral detail for spatial resolution; the forthcoming operational imaging spectroscopy missions CHIME and SBG will offer the opposite trade-off with 30-m pixels and hundreds of spectral bands. title: A localized weighted ensemble adjustment Kalman filter for high-dimensional nonlinear data assimilation
abstract: Abstract Particle filters provide a nonlinear Bayesian framework for data assimilation, but global weights often degenerate in high-dimensional geophysical systems. Ensemble Kalman filters are stable with practical ensemble sizes, yet their Gaussian and locally linear updates can be restrictive for nonlinear observations and non-Gaussian forecasts. title: Temperature, Sea Ice, Depth, and Traits Drive Fish Distributions in the Barents Sea
abstract: ABSTRACT Aim Marine species are increasingly impacted by climate change, forcing them to adapt or redistribute to remain within their environmental niches. How the combined effects of environmental gradients and species traits influence the distribution of species with distinct biogeographic affinities remains poorly understood. The goal of this study is to identify the role of the environment, as mediated by species' traits, in shaping the fish communities of a high latitude marine environment with a clear biogeographic transition zone. abstract: The deep ocean plays a critical role in the global climate system. However, satellite Earth observation is limited to the sea surface, while in-situ measurements struggle to achieve synchronous coverage over vast oceanic areas. Ocean Acoustic Tomography (OAT) is an essential method for retrieving large-scale interior ocean parameters; however, its path-integral nature leads to high-dimensional and ill-posed inverse problems when applied to the deep ocean. abstract: Abstract. Accurately representing abyssal water masses and their inter-basin pathways remains a challenge for global ocean models and reanalyses. In this study, we investigate how horizontal and vertical resolution influence the simulation of abyssal waters by first evaluating three ocean reanalyses and one forward ocean model, focusing on Antarctic Bottom Water pathways from the Weddell Sea to the Argentine and Brazil basins and through the Vema Channel. title: A digital twin of a vessel as an independent multidisciplinary didactic unit of maritime educational programs
abstract: This article provides a brief description of the digital twin concept, both in general and as it applies to maritime shipping. The need for a separate "digital twin" didactic unit in maritime educational programs is analyzed, and the corresponding arguments are presented. Selected information on existing courses at Russian universities focused on mastering the digital twin concept is summarized and analyzed. The place of digital twins in postgraduate programs is specifically considered. The staffing and methodological support issues for studying this didactic unit are assessed.

abstract: This study aims to provide a comprehensive overview of the current technological landscape regarding Digital Twins (DT) in the shipbuilding industry, including their integration with Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) and their effects on maintenance. title: Uncertainty-aware digital twin-driven fault-tolerant control for autonomous underwater vehicles using temporal fusion transformer-based fault diagnosis
abstract: Autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) operate in challenging marine environments. The actuator faults, propulsion degradation and environmental disturbances can significantly compromise mission safety and tracking performance. Existing studies have primarily focused on either fault diagnosis or fault-tolerant control as separate tasks. A limited attention has been given to integrating fault diagnosis, predictive digital twins and uncertainty-aware control within a unified framework. title: Extreme events of 2024 in the Tropical Indian Ocean: leveraging heterogeneous multi-platform observations from NODC-INCOIS
abstract: Frequent tropical cyclones in the North Indian Ocean significantly disrupt coastal and marine environments. This study integrates multi-platform datasets – including satellites, Argo floats, moored buoys, and tide gauges – to analyze the ocean‒atmosphere response to four 2024 cyclones: Remal, Asna, Dana, and Fengal. Satellite and Argo data revealed marked sea surface cooling, elevated chlorophyll-a, and thermocline uplift. title: Decoded Antarctic snow accumulation history reconciles observed and modeled trends in accumulation and large-scale warming patterns
abstract: Abstract. Ice-core reconstructions indicate that increased snow accumulation on the Antarctic Ice Sheet mitigated global sea level rise by ~11 mm during 1901–2000. However, in the most recent 40 years of more intense observation and warming, the trend in the Antarctic-wide accumulation rate has been negligible. We attribute these trends by evaluating Earth system model experiments in comparison with dynamically consistent reconstructions of surface climate. title: Interpreting Air Temperature Trends Across the Antarctic Peninsula Between 1979 and 2025
abstract: Abstract The near‐surface temperature of the Antarctic Peninsula is marked by strong spatio‐temporal variability. In situ observations are scarce and therefore have limited spatial coverage. Furthermore, ERA‐5 reanalysis does not have a sufficient spatial resolution to capture the steep topography and other climate gradients of the peninsula. Here, we evaluate and use the regional climate model RACMO2.4p1 to demonstrate that the average warming in the Antarctic Peninsula, as well as over all individual ice shelves, has been statistically insignificant between 1979 and 2025. When radar and hourly gauges are scarce: Sharpening gridded precipitation estimates using daily observations
abstract: Long-term hourly precipitation data are critical for many applications. However, in many regions, particularly during earlier historical periods, limited hourly observations have prevented the development of reliable hourly gridded products. In contrast, daily observations are often more readily available. In this study, we introduce and evaluate a framework for incorporating daily gauge observations for hourly precipitation estimates under data-limited conditions. abstract: Abstract. Marine heatwaves (MHWs) are prolonged anomalies of warm sea surface temperature (SST) that can disrupt marine ecosystems, physical climate processes, and human coastal activities. MHW definitions vary due to different stakeholders requirements, such as ecological scientists and climate scientists having differing yet specific thresholds and metrics. title: Adaptive Model Parameter Estimation Triggered by the Beneficial Observation Rate from Forecast Sensitivity to Observations
abstract: Abstract In NWP, the assimilation of various observations contributes to improving forecast accuracy. The contribution of each observation can be estimated by existing methods. Empirically, it is well known that only a fraction of assimilated observations are diagnosed as beneficial, meaning that they improve forecast accuracy. Previous studies have indicated that the beneficial observation rate depends on model imperfections. Sequentially Conditioned Screening for Marine Aquaculture Siting in Contested Tropical Coastal Waters: Framework Formulation and a Worked Example
abstract: Marine aquaculture siting in tropical coastal waters is usually treated as a scoring problem: criteria are weighted, cells are ranked, and constraints enter as low scores that a high score elsewhere can offset. Where the sea is already allocated to tourism, conservation, shipping and customary fishing, this treatment misrepresents the decision, because prior claims are not weak preferences. This paper formulates a screening framework built on the opposite premise. title: How extreme river discharge events shape coastal biogeochemical dynamics: the 2024 northern Adriatic case
abstract: Abstract. In 2024, the northern Adriatic Sea experienced marked levels of eutrophication, as indicated by unusually high surface chlorophyll concentrations observed by remote sensing and in-situ measurements. In addition, exceptionally high Po river discharges, in the form of repeated and intense events, were recorded from March to June and in October. abstract: Abstract. The impact of mesoscale vertical motion on the thermodynamic, microphysical, and convective transformations of marine cold air outbreaks (MCAOs) is still largely unknown, partly due to scarce high-resolution observations in upstream Arctic regions. Therefore, this study investigates the effects of mesoscale subsidence on the evolution of the atmospheric boundary-layer (ABL), cloud phase, and precipitation for a case study of a shallow MCAO observed in the Fram Strait in March 2022 during the HALO–(AC)3 campaign. title: Cascading fishery collapse associated with thermal habitat degradation, marine heatwaves, and predator influx
abstract: Global climate change and intensifying marine heatwaves contribute to abrupt fishery collapses. We investigate the fishery collapse of the Japanese flying squid (Todarodes pacificus) in the East Sea (Sea of Japan), which provides an early warning for climate-driven species replacements in warming oceans. Using multi-decadal observations (1993–2025), we identify a teleconnection where an intensified early-summer La Niña amplifies autumn–winter marine heatwaves within major fishing grounds. title: River and Coastal Flooding Hazard in the Vistula Outlet, Poland
abstract: Flood risk at river-coast interfaces is an increasing concern under climate change and sea level rise, yet limited attention has been given to areas where riverine and coastal processes interact dynamically. This study assesses the river and coastal flood hazards in the Vistula River outlet, Poland, using multisource datasets handled via Geographical Information System (GIS) analysis. title: Realising the potential of ecological digital twins as decision support tools
abstract: Ecological digital twins are continually updating models used for decision-making. Current progress in ecological digital twinning has focused on overcoming the technological and modelling challenges to create a continually updating system. We argue that attention should now also focus on effectively integrating digital twins into decision-making systems to inform timely action. This requires the direct inclusion of end users and greater focus on the socio-political context. title: Surface Chlorophyll‐ a Trends in the Mediterranean Sea: Seasonal Bloom Dynamics and Drivers
abstract: Abstract Chlorophyll ‐a (Chl ‐a ) is the most widely used proxy for phytoplankton biomass, bloom intensity, and trophic status in marine ecosystems. We analyzed 27 years (1998–2024) of 1 km‐resolution satellite‐derived Chl ‐a data across the Mediterranean Sea and evaluated long‐term trends, bloom phenology, and seasonal variability in relation to sea surface temperature, mixed‐layer depth, and nutrient dynamics. abstract: Membrane distillation (MD) has significant potential for freshwater production in dynamic marine environments. However, existing studies mainly focus on static operating conditions, leaving the transient heat and mass transfer response to sloshing-induced disturbances insufficiently understood. abstract: Since August 2023, treated water containing tritium, a hydrogen radionuclide, has been discharged into the coastal Pacific seawater facing Japan, and this discharge is planned to continue for a few decades for gentle release under controlled tritium concentrations in the treated water. This study evaluated the potential accumulation of tritium in edible seaweed on the Fukushima coast under the release conditions of the treated water. abstract: Abstract. The Gulf of Maine and the surrounding Northeast U.S. Continental Shelf are experiencing rapid marine environmental change arising from complex regional dynamics that challenge near-term (1–10 years) predictive capabilities for valuable living marine resources. Here, using a high-resolution regional ocean model, we demonstrate skilful decadal forecasts of ocean bottom habitat characteristics including bottom temperature, dissolved oxygen (O2), pH and aragonite saturation state (Ωar). abstract: Recent observations in the eastern Arabian Sea reveal the persistent presence of surface-floating tarballs along India's west coast from May to December. These tarballs originate from oil seepage caused by accidental spills, shipping activities, shipwrecks, or natural seepage, and undergo weathering that results in a hardened outer layer with a semi-solid interior. This study develops a simulation-based digital-twin control prototype that synchronizes vessel flow, berth occupancy, equipment activity, shore-power demand, renewable supply, battery state, grid import, and modelled emissions. title: Integrated retrieval of ocean surface wind and current fields from single-geometry SAR observations through a physically constrained Bayesian framework
abstract: Ocean surface winds and currents are coupled through air–sea interaction but are commonly retrieved independently from spaceborne synthetic aperture radar (SAR). For operational single-geometry SAR, simultaneous wind–current retrieval is underdetermined and remains reliant on background information. We propose a physically constrained Bayesian framework that combines radar backscatter and Doppler centroid anomaly measurements to retrieve 10-m wind and radial surface current. title: Differential Impacts of Proxy Archives on Paleoclimate Reconstruction Performance
abstract: Abstract Reconstructing past climates is challenging because pre‐instrumental observations are geographically sparse and proxy records are noisy; data assimilation offers one approach to address these limitations. Although such reconstructions are now widespread, the extent to which different proxy archives determine their accuracy remains unclear. Due to its nature as a concentration basin, where evaporation exceeds freshwater inputs, the combined effects of rising salinity and increasing heat content are expected to play a key role in shaping the basin's dynamic. title: Aqua mangrove Tetrapod-2
abstract: Coastal erosion and land degradation are increasingly critical challenges caused by rising sea levels and intense ocean wave dynamics. While conventional concrete tetrapods offer immediate structural defense by dissipating wave energy, their reliance on heavy Ordinary Portland Cement (OPC) and steel reinforcement causes severe ecological damage, marine toxicity, and carbon emissions. Conversely, natural mangrove bio-shields provide excellent long-term shoreline protection, but young saplings frequently experience high mortality on open coasts due to wave shear forces and soil washout. abstract: Extreme hydrological events are critical drivers of coastal hypoxia, yet their impacts remain poorly constrained under future warming. Coastal oxygen depletion occurs when physical oxygen supply fails to offset biological oxygen demand, with stratification, nutrient enrichment, and warming further intensifying oxygen loss. abstract: Abstract. Availability of high-quality sub-hourly sea level data is essential for understanding of a wide range of oceanic processes, including tidal oscillations, seiches, storm surges, tsunamis (including meteotsunamis), and their impact on sea level extremes and coastal flooding. Freely accessible sea level databases often contain time series measured with hourly or even longer sampling step, or they contain high-frequency data that have not undergone quality control procedures. title: ENSO modulated wave power variability and multi decadal analysis of wind speed, and wave characteristics along a vulnerable coastal zone of the southeast Arabian Sea
abstract: Abstract This study presents a comprehensive assessment of wind and wave climate variability along a vulnerable coastal zone in the southeast Arabian Sea, with particular focus on ENSO-modulated wave power variations. The analysis integrates a decade of in situ wave observations and long-term ERA5 reanalysis data (1940–2022) to characterize multi-decadal trends and spatial variability. abstract: Abstract A combination of model simulations and field observations collected in 2023 and 2024 near Seagreen, Scotland’s largest Offshore Wind Farm (OWF), is used to assess when, where and by how much (physical) changes induced by OWFs structures become detectable and environmentally relevant. Seagreen has the deepest (> 55 m) fixed bottom foundations of any OWF in the world (in 2026), and in offshore deep (> 50 m) waters there is the potential for OWFs structures to perturb natural ocean mixing and modify seasonal stratification. abstract: The integration of urban digital twins and artificial intelligence is changing city management by introducing innovative methods for simulations, observations, and control. However, their application is primarily technical and spatially restricted to certain regions. abstract: Abstract. title: North Atlantic chlorophyll blooms modulate European hydroclimate and terrestrial productivity
abstract: Marine and terrestrial ecosystems are usually treated as separate components of the global carbon cycle, and whether variability in ocean biology reaches plant growth on land has remained unclear. Here we show that phytoplankton blooms in the high-latitude North Atlantic are linked to summer productivity across central Europe. abstract: Abstract. In November 2024, there was an extreme event within the Bothnian Bay, a sub-basin of the Baltic Sea, when a record low sea level of -153 cm was measured at Kemi, at the northern end of the basin. This minimum was 34 cm lower than the previous minimum measured in 2022. abstract: Abstract. The ongoing evaluation and refinement of the Copernicus Ocean Monitoring Indicators (OMIs) is essential to ensure their scientific robustness and operational relevance. This process takes place within a context of continuous advances in upstream products and the need to adapt methodologies to evolving scientific priorities and decision-making requirements. title: Evaluation of SCHISM experimental forecasts of total water levels along the Thanh Hoa–Nghe An coast
abstract: At the Institute of Meteorology, Hydrology, Environment and Marine Sciences, the SCHISM model has been studied and experimentally applied to forecast total water levels along the Thanh Hoa–Nghe An coast. In 2025, SCHISM was tested for forecasting several monsoon events and typhoons affecting the Thanh Hoa–Nghe An region. This paper evaluates experimental total-water-level forecasts for Typhoon Kajiki (August 2025) and Typhoon Bualoi (September 2025). title: Adverse Impact of Explicit Ocean‐Wave Coupling on the Climatology of Tropical Cyclones and Their Environment in E3SM
abstract: Abstract Upper‐ocean processes play a pivotal role in the development of tropical cyclones (TCs) through their modulation of sea surface temperatures, and consequently, air‐sea fluxes and the large‐scale storm environment. While most fully‐coupled Earth system models represent key processes such as vertical mixing, few incorporate the effect of surface ocean waves. title: Why do numerical models simulate contrasting primary productivity responses in the North Pacific during the Last Glacial Maximum?
abstract: Primary productivity (PP) of the ocean is a crucial factor controlling of the carbon cycle of the Earth. The Last Glacial Maximum (LGM) provides a valuable end-member climate state for evaluating its control. Numerical models, however, disagree on how PP in the North Pacific responded to LGM climate, limiting mechanistic interpretation of proxy records. abstract: Abstract. Seasonal depletion of dissolved oxygen (DO) in stratified shelf seas has important consequences for benthic and pelagic ecosystems and biogeochemical cycling. There is a need to understand the importance of different processes contributing to the bottom water oxygen budget, and how those processes might change in a warmer ocean. Using CTD observations from the UK Shelf Sea Biogeochemistry programme, we construct a summer DO budget for the bottom waters of the Celtic Sea and use the budget to assess how bottom water DO might change in a warmer climate. abstract: Following nearly two decades of mass loss, the Antarctic Peninsula has experienced mass accumulation since 2021. Using data from GRACE (Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment), GRACE-FO (Follow On), satellite altimetry, and meteorological reanalysis, we investigate the post-2021 mass accumulation and its climatic drivers. abstract: The biological pump (BP) constitutes a key component of the global carbon cycle by mediating the export of organic carbon from the surface ocean to the deep sea. However, long-term variability of BP strength in the northeastern Indian Ocean (NEIO), particularly within the strongly stratified Bay of Bengal (BoB), remains inadequately constrained due to the complex interplay between monsoon forcing and freshwater-induced stratification. title: Coupled watershed and estuary modeling of microplastic transport and retention in the Delaware river basin
abstract: Abstract Microplastics (MPs) are an emerging environmental concern owing to their widespread presence and ecological impacts. We develop a coupled watershed–estuary modeling framework to simulate MP transport from terrestrial sources to estuarine systems. The Distributed Hydrology Soil Vegetation Model (DHSVM) is enhanced to represent point and nonpoint MP sources and is coupled with the Finite Volume Community Ocean Model (FVCOM) to capture estuarine transport. title: Land-atmosphere feedback amplifies circulation-dominant fire weather risk over eastern Siberia
abstract: Wildfires in eastern Siberia have intensified significantly in recent decades. This intensification is closely linked to rising vapor pressure deficit (VPD), a key indicator of fire weather risk. Previous studies have shown that atmospheric circulation increases VPD through subsidence-induced warming and drying, but the extent to which the circulation-driven VPD increase is realized through land–atmosphere feedback remains unclear. title: Analysis of the performance of a top-hinged flap-type wave energy converter using a RANS-VoF numerical model
abstract: The performance of a full-scale top-hinged flap-type wave energy converter in the open sea is analyzed numerically in this study. A free surface flow Reynolds-Averaged Navier-Stokes numerical model is used with the ANSYS Fluent® software. The flap, 7 m long, is immersed in a flume 10 m deep, and subject to waves with periods from 6 to 12 s and height of 1.5 m. The Power Take-Off (PTO) is modeled as proportional to the angular velocity of the flap. title: Surface Ozone Variability and Meteorological Drivers at Coastal and Mountain Sites in Bulgaria
abstract: The study is based on simultaneous measurements of surface ozone concentrations and meteorological parameters over a period of about two years in mountainous and coastal regions in Bulgaria. The average O3 at the mountain station (Rozhen) is 48 ppb, and at the coastal station (Ahtopol), 41 ppb. It is found that extremely low and high ozone concentrations are less common in the mountainous area than in the coastal area. title: Constrained optimal control and hydrodynamic scaling of the RM3 two-body point absorber
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive hydrodynamic and multiscale optimization framework for the Reference Model 3 wave energy converter deployed at the La Serena site, Chile. Using ERA5 reanalysis data, the study evaluates device performance within a rigorous numerical framework that compares uncontrolled and WecOptTool-optimized strategies. The optimization yields a mean site power of 183.43 kW —representing a 33.02% increase over the uncontrolled baseline of 137.89 kW —and an annual energy production of 1,606.81 MWh/yr , a net gain of 398.86 MWh/yr compared to the 1,207.95 MWh/yr base. title: Climate trends in the Azerbaijani Caspian Sea sector and associated atmospheric circulation indices
abstract: ABSTRACT This study analyzes recent climatic changes in the Azerbaijani Sector of the Caspian Sea (ASCS) and their relationships with large-scale atmospheric circulation. Long-term changes in meteorological variables, river runoff, and sea level were assessed using data from 33 hydrometeorological stations and gauging posts for 1981–2024. title: EnviFlux (v1.0): a simplified surface flux inversion tool based on four-dimensional variational data assimilation (4D-Var)
abstract: Abstract. This paper introduces EnviFlux, which is a software tool (written in C++) to study the inverse problem of estimating the distribution of fluxes of a trace gas at the Earth's surface. This is done using a four-dimensional variational technique, which combines information from (i) synthetic observations of the trace gas spanning a defined time window, (ii) a transport model linking the initial concentration and surface fluxes to predictions of the observations, and (iii) a-priori information. Near-inertial waves (NIWs) play a fundamental role in transferring wind energy into the ocean interior and sustaining diapycnal mixing, yet their wintertime characteristics and interactions with mesoscale eddies remain insufficiently understood. abstract: Groundwater flow modeling in urban areas is of great importance in the context of water level depletion due to the high population, unplanned urbanization and industrial growth. In N’Djamena, groundwater is the main source of drinking water. Under these conditions, groundwater flow modeling is essential to better understand the dynamics and behavior of the urban groundwater system of the city. abstract: Abstract. While ocean surface submesoscales have been extensively studied, their counterparts in the bottom boundary layer (BBL) remain little explored. abstract: Abstract. Human-centred design (HCD) is increasingly prioritised as studies show human experience is critical in infrastructure use, and recent policies call for more socially responsive design. Tsunami impacts intensify as sea level rise (SLR) raises baseline water levels and reduces existing defence effectiveness, yet HCD informed approaches are rarely tested under projected SLR. abstract: Central Asia, as a typical arid and semi-arid region, experiences precipitation variability that critically influences water security and ecological balance. abstract: Abstract. abstract: Abstract. In the Namib Desert, fog is an essential water source and occurs when and where advected marine stratus clouds intersect with the land surface. However, the meteorological controls of the cloud base height are still insufficiently understood. This study aims to develop a basic understanding of the relevant processes. abstract: Rivers are vital for water security, yet scalable freshwater monitoring and global knowledge of river mean depth and discharge remains limited by sparse in situ data, satellite observations of river surface only and global river flow estimations relying on models with insufficient hydraulic information. abstract: Abstract. Coastal urban environments exhibit strong vertical and horizontal heterogeneity in aerosol properties, complicating process-level understanding of aerosol–cloud interactions. abstract: Abstract This study presents an 11‐year climatology of thunderstorm (TS) hours and associated environments in Australia, based on ground‐based lightning observations and a regional reanalysis. Spatial and temporal variations in TS frequency are explored using heat maps and a cluster analysis applied to the average seasonal and diurnal cycles of TS at every grid point. abstract: Rapid urban expansion in secondary cities of Sub-Saharan Africa has intensified pressure on land resources and infrastructure, exposing the limitations of conventional planning systems reliant on periodic assessments. While Geographic Information Systems (GIS), Remote Sensing (RS), and Artificial Intelligence (AI) have improved monitoring, their integration into continuous Spatial Digital Twin (SDT) environments remain limited in Nigeria. abstract: Abstract River deltas are shaped by the interplay of water discharge and sediment transport, yet numerical studies often assume steady conditions that fail to capture flood stochasticity. We investigate the morphodynamic response of idealized lacustrine delta lobes to discharge amplitude under stochastic monsoonal flood fluctuations. abstract: This study provides a quantitative characterization of the seasonal stratification cycle in the southeastern Caspian Sea using a multiyear hydrographic dataset (2011–2019) collected across seven cross-shore transects, spanning all four seasons including winter. MLD progresses from shallow spring mixing (mean ≈ 10 m) to deep winter convection (mean ≈ 57 m), with season explaining 76% of MLD variance (ANOVA, p < 0.001, η 2 = 0.76). abstract: The underwater acoustic radiation of deepwater submersibles has become a growing concern in both academic and industrial communities. This study investigates the structure-acoustic coupling characteristics of a novel deepwater pressure hull, idealized as a triple spherical shell. A numerical model is established using a combined finite element and boundary element method to analyze the vibro-acoustic response of the target structure. title: Recent change in northward migration of the East Asian summer front and increased compound wet–hot conditions
abstract: The East Asian summer front (EASF) plays a key role in regional precipitation and heat stress, yet its long-term positional changes remain poorly understood. Using a front-tracking algorithm applied to ERA5 reanalysis (1979–2025), we identify northward migration of the EASF during both the active frontal season and late summer, with a more robust 1.92° shift in late summer. These shifts are associated with enhanced moisture transport, regional weakening of the upper-level jet, and localized sea surface temperature warming that has intensified and spatially broadened in recent decades. title: Hyperspectral Remote Sensing Unveils Phytoplankton Succession in Hurricane Wakes
abstract: Abstract Hyperspectral satellite data from the NASA mission, PACE (Plankton, Aerosol, Cloud, ocean Ecosystem), can be used to investigate the effects of hurricanes on phytoplankton composition. Results from four Atlantic Ocean hurricanes show the expected increases in chlorophyll‐a concentration associated with deepening of the mixed layer depth (MLD). abstract: Freeze–thaw deformation in frost-susceptible soils couples heat transfer, phase change, water redistribution and irreversible thaw deformation. This study develops an axisymmetric Voronoi–Delaunay lattice framework with a finite-element-analysis-program (FEAP)-compatible residual–tangent organization, embedded displacement-jump histories and a bounded temperature-dependent creep law. abstract: Abstract Ocean heat content (OHC) is sensitive to errors in the vertical representation of temperature, particularly in regions characterized by strong thermohaline gradients. This study evaluates an empirical fractional-order integral procedure in six scenarios encompassing the tropical Atlantic, Indian, equatorial Pacific, and South Atlantic oceans. abstract: Abstract. Sea Surface Salinity (SSS) trends and variability have been studied for long periods of time, using historical archives and Argo float data. Studies in the past have shown that the long-term (50+ years) salinity trend patterns reveal freshening in the climatological fresh region and an increase in salinity in the already salty region, indicating an intensification of the hydrological cycle. abstract: Geogrid reinforcement can effectively improve the engineering properties of coral sand and has considerable potential for application in island and reef engineering. abstract: Floating breakwaters are increasingly considered for offshore applications, including marine aquaculture. However, existing studies have primarily focused on wave attenuation, while the potential of different configurations to provide favorable aquaculture environments remains insufficiently explored. This article aims to: (i) compare the hydrodynamic performance of various fixed floating breakwaters, including box-type, plate-attached, π-type, and hybrid systems, with a consistent width ( B f ) and configuration-dependent draft ( D f ); and (ii) propose an initial framework for their aquacult

title: Climatology and mechanisms of low-level jets over southeastern coast of mainland China during the early-summer rainy season
abstract: Abstract Low-level jets (LLJs) significantly impact early-summer rainy season over the southeastern coast of mainland China (SECC), yet northerly LLJs over this region remain understudied compared to their southerly counterparts. Utilizing decade-long hourly ERA5 reanalysis, this study establishes a comprehensive climatology and dynamical framework for distinct LLJ types over the SECC. title: Modulation of interannual variability of strong wind events over eastern China by tropical sea surface temperature variability
abstract: Strong wind events (SWEs) threaten human safety, infrastructure, and wind energy over eastern China. Using empirical orthogonal unction (EOF) analysis, this study investigates the interannual variability of SWEs during 1979–2020 and its response to tropical sea surface temperature (SST) forcing. abstract: Atmospheric refraction is a fundamental source of systematic error in geodetic surveying, EDM, and line-of-sight visibility analysis. Practitioners assume κ = 0.13, a mid-twentieth-century average inappropriate for most conditions. title: Seasonal Variations in Aerosol Trace Element Source Contributions and Deposition Fluxes to the North Pacific Subtropical Gyre
abstract: Abstract Trace elements deposited in the marine environment affect ocean biogeochemistry in numerous, complex ways. This study quantifies seasonal aerosol trace element (TE) fluxes and evaluates their variability and potential sources over a 2‐year period in the North Pacific subtropical gyre (NPSG). We established the Hawaii Aerosol Time Series (HATS), which includes weekly integrated total suspended aerosol particle collections alongside sampling the cosmogenic radionuclide 7 Be. title: Stochastic cloud fluctuations drive Arctic winter radiative bistability
abstract: In Arctic winter, the boundary layer occupies two preferred radiative states, a cold, clear state and a heat-trapping, cloudy state, that strongly regulate surface energy loss over sea ice. Yet, reanalyses and climate models are often biased toward a single intermediate state. Using a stochastic differential equation framework applied to 27 years of high-resolution observations, we show that the observed bistability is not sustained by multiple deterministic equilibria: The mean restoring tendency is effectively single-well, while background meteorology alone cannot explain rapid transitions.

title: Intensification of near-inertial currents in the Atlantic Ocean over the past two decades
abstract: Near-inertial currents (NICs) play a key role in surface material redistribution and ocean mixing, yet their long-term variability remains poorly known. Using in situ current measurements from surface drifters, we provide observational evidence for a pronounced intensification of surface NICs in the Atlantic Ocean over the past two decades (2003–2022). Basin–mean NIC strength increases at a rate of 3.8 ± 1.7% per decade, with a spatial pattern characterized by strengthening in the South Atlantic and the high-latitude North Atlantic, and weakening in the low-latitude North Atlantic. abstract: Ocean Thermal Energy Conversion (OTEC) is a promising renewable energy technology capable of providing continuous baseload power while simultaneously supporting freshwater production and other deep-seawater applications. As a carbon-neutral energy source, OTEC aligns with global Sustainable Development Goals related to clean energy and climate action. abstract: ABSTRACT Warm‐season extreme precipitation over North and Northeast China is a major regional hazard and is strongly influenced by large‐scale atmospheric circulation. However, how large‐amplitude wave activity varies among different spatial patterns of extreme precipitation remains insufficiently understood. title: C-band polarimetric Doppler weather radar observations of waterspouts over the southern Indian peninsular coast of the Arabian Sea
abstract: Waterspouts are intense, small-scale vortices that develop over water surfaces, typically forming under weak synoptic disturbances combined with localised differential heating. In this study, the three-dimensional structure and dynamical characteristics of two waterspout events observed by the C-band Polarimetric Doppler Weather Radar (C-DWR) at Thumba (8.537°N, 76.865°E) are analysed. The first event occurred near Shangumugham Beach, close to Thumba, during the afternoon of 26 November 2017, two days prior to the passage of Cyclone Ockhi over the region. title: Digital Stress-Testing of Urban Transport Resilience: Analyzing Systemic Isolation against Megathrust Tsunamis in Southern Java
abstract: Sustainable urban mobility is defined not only by efficiency but by its resilience to catastrophic disruptions. The coastal district of Palabuhanratu, Indonesia, faces a critical vulnerability where its transportation network is bisected by major rivers, posing a severe risk during a potential Megathrust Tsunami (Mw 8.8). This study uses digital technologies for urban infrastructure analysis to evaluate transport system failure modes. title: On large-scale wind-drift ocean currents: An asymptotic approach in spherical coordinates
abstract: Starting from the Navier–Stokes equations in rotating spherical coordinates with depth-varying density and eddy viscosity, we derive an asymptotic model describing non-equatorial wind-generated ocean drift currents. Our approach allows for large-scale flows that cannot be captured by classical tangent-plane approximations. title: Flooding with brackish water disrupts Liriodendron tulipifera sap flux in an ecosystem-scale experiment
abstract: Coastal forests are retreating due to sea‑level rise and extreme precipitation events, yet the physiological mechanisms that precede woody plant decline remain poorly constrained. We used the ecosystem‑scale TEMPEST (Terrestrial Ecosystem Manipulation to Probe the Effects of Storm Treatments) experiment; annual, plot‑level freshwater and saltwater flooding of a mid‑Atlantic deciduous forest, to quantify short‑ and long‑term responses of sap flux in three tree species: Acer rubrum, Fagus grandifolia, and Liriodendron tulipifera. title: Measuring large-scale mCDR using a novel Atmospheric CO₂ Perimeter Flux (ACPF) method
abstract: Achieving net-zero CO₂ emissions globally requires an annual removal of on the order of 7–9 Gt CO₂; but current CO₂ removal (CDR) measurement methodologies are not designed to quantify marine CDR (mCDR) at the megaton-to-gigaton scales required for climate relevance. This perspective presents a new methodology, the Atmospheric CO₂ Perimeter Flux (ACPF) method, an atmospheric-domain framework for the monitoring, reporting, and verification (MRV) of marine carbon dioxide removal. title: Tsugaru Gyre development in summer 2025
abstract: Abstract The Tsugaru Warm Current (TWC) flows eastward through the Tsugaru Strait from the Japan Sea to the North Pacific, influencing the water-mass distribution, marine ecosystems, and fisheries in the confluence region east of Japan. In this study, we conducted shipboard observations during the transition phase of the TWC from its coastal mode to its gyre mode in early July 2025. Subsurface information obtained from these in-situ observations at key locations is highly valuable for validating model simulation products, together with satellite observations. title: Indian Ocean Convection Modulates the Early‐Winter Pacific‐North American Response to El Niño
abstract: Abstract The El Niño‐Southern Oscillation is a dominant driver of Pacific‐North American (PNA) variability on seasonal‐to‐interannual timescales through its influence on tropical Pacific convection. However, the early‐winter PNA response exhibits pronounced event‐to‐event diversity during El Niño. title: Meteorological Impact Assessment Software for Maritime Transport in the Western Part of the Black Sea
abstract: Maritime transportation in the western part of the Black Sea is strongly affected by meteorological conditions such as wind, waves, and visibility. This paper presents a software system designed to evaluate and predict these impacts using real-time and historical data. The system integrates data processing, statistical analysis, and predictive models to assess navigational risks and support route optimization. abstract: Abstract Cyclone Harry affected Sicily, Calabria, and Sardinia between January 19 and 22, 2026, producing heavy rainfall, strong winds, and coastal impacts across the central Mediterranean. We assess how the associated meteorological conditions differ between the present climate (1988–2025) and a cooler past (1950–1987) using the multivariate ClimaMeter analog attribution protocol applied to the European Centre for Medium‐Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) Reanalysis Version 5 (ERA5). title: The South Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation at 34.5°S in 2017 and 2022
abstract: Abstract The Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) at 34.5°S is investigated using hydrographic data from two research cruises conducted in 2017 and 2022. title: Integrated Structural Assessment of an Industrial Port Jetty under Vessel Upgrading in Gresik
abstract: Increasing the vessel class at an existing jetty can be governed by structural resistance, lateral pile response, marine equipment, or water depth. This study evaluates a 10,000 DWT pile-supported precast dry-bulk jetty at Industrial Port, Gresik, for 20,000, 30,000, and 40,000 DWT vessels. The assessment used project drawings, vessel particulars, bathymetry, borehole and SPT records, metocean data, finite element modelling, reinforced-concrete capacity checks, pile axial and lateral evaluation, fender and bollard screening, and a finite element method model. title: Forecasting coastal dune mobility: a logistic regression model driven by meteorological data and climate indices
abstract: Abstract. Predicting dune mobility under changing climatic conditions remains a challenge in aeolian geomorphology, particularly in data-scarce regions. This study presents a novel application of binomial logistic regression to forecast dune activation and migration using readily available meteorological data. We combine established dune mobility indices (Tsoar and Lancaster) into a new integrated index (TsoLa) and evaluate its performance against observed dune migration rates derived from satellite imagery. title: Pyrite sulfur isotope heterogeneity across the Nanhua Basin records intensified biogeochemical cycling on continental slopes during Marinoan deglaciation
abstract: The termination of the Marinoan Snowball Earth (∼635 Ma) reorganized ocean circulation and biogeochemical cycling, but the spatial recovery of marine primary productivity remains poorly constrained. Here we present a basinal scale sulfur isotope (δ 34 S) dataset from the upper Nantuo Formation of South China, based on disseminated pyrite and coeval pyrite nodules from 19 sections spanning shallow shelf, continental slope, and basin environments. title: Numerical investigation on the hydrodynamic behaviour of a wind-solar-aquaculture integrated floating structure
abstract: To address the challenges of spatial competition, high construction costs, and cumulative environmental impacts associated with traditional single-function offshore resource development, this study proposes an innovative wind-solar-aquaculture integrated structure named “AquaEnergy”. The system integrates floating offshore wind turbines, aquaculture cages, and floating photovoltaic panels within the same marine area, enabling the synergistic development of renewable energy and aquaculture while promoting green and low-carbon utilisation of ocean resources. title: Requirements and challenges of process-based modeling for intermediate wheatgrass, a perennial cereal
abstract: Intermediate wheatgrass (IWG) is a perennial cereal suitable for climate-resilient cropping systems. Given the brief selection history, however, process-based models for IWG, and for perennial cereals generally, remain scarce. This scarcity currently prevents the projection of the crop’s performance across diverse environments and management regimes. To support the development of robust IWG models, this semi-systematic review evaluates 43 peer-reviewed articles. title: Interdecadal Phase Shifts of Winter Asian‐Pacific Oscillation Modulate the Warm Arctic‐Cold Eurasia Pattern
abstract: Abstract Against the backdrop of global warming, warm Arctic‐cold Eurasia (WACE) has garnered extensive scientific attention. However, the drivers of its interdecadal variability remain insufficiently understood. Using reanalysis data and pre‐industrial control simulations, we demonstrate that winter Asian‐Pacific Oscillation (APO), a dominant upper‐tropospheric atmospheric mode over the Asian‐North Pacific sector, modulates the WACE variability at the interdecadal timescale. abstract: Engineering biopolymer-based hydrogels with robust load-bearing capacity, reversible mechanical programmability, and adaptive actuation remains difficult due to weak physical crosslinking and porous structure. Inspired by the mutable dermis of sea cucumbers, a collagen-alginate double-network elastomeric (CoDE) hydrogel integrates a covalently crosslinked collagen cryogel scaffold with an ionically crosslinked alginate sacrificial network. title: Hybrid Multi‐Gateway Authentication Protocol for 6LoWPAN‐Based Marine Wireless Sensor Networks
abstract: ABSTRACT This paper proposes a secure and efficient three‐factor authentication scheme to address the security issues in the integration scenario of multi‐gateway wireless sensor networks (WSNs) and 6LoWPAN in marine Internet of Things (IoT). Existing approaches exhibit vulnerabilities to cryptographic breaches, single‐point failures, high computational costs, and inefficient long‐distance transmission in maritime settings. title: Characteristics and Ambient Conditions of Mesoscale Convective Systems Moving Offshore in the Yangtze‐Huai River Basin, East China
abstract: Abstract This work for the first time studies the characteristics and environment conditions of mesoscale convective systems (MCSs) that move offshore (i.e., land to sea, LS) in the Yangtze‐Huai River Basin (YHRB), East China. In the warm season (April–September), LS MCSs account for 25.5% of the total MCSs, exhibiting a decreasing trend from spring (April–May) to later summer (August–September). title: Modeling the dynamic responses of a 2 × 2 gravity-type fish cage group under combined wave-current conditions
abstract: The hydrodynamic response of gravity-type cage groups under harsh open-ocean sea states is closely linked to long-term production safety. However, severe wave-current forcing may produce response transitions and internal load-path changes that remain insufficiently resolved for interconnected cage groups. This study develops a numerical model of a 2 × 2 cage group using the lumped-mass method and examines how wave height (H), wave period (T), and angle of attack (α) govern its motion responses, volume loss rate, and mooring tensions. title: Post-Landfall Persistence and Poleward Recurvature of Intense Western North Pacific Typhoons through a Track-Conditioned Moisture-Bridge Mechanism
abstract: Abstract Why some intense western North Pacific typhoons remain hazardous for one to two days after mainland-China landfall whereas others weaken rapidly remains unresolved. This study examines that contrast using 1979–2020 Joint Typhoon Warning Center best tracks and ERA5 reanalysis fields. title: Evaluation of Heatwave Severity in Southeastern Europe Through the Excess Heat Factor
abstract: The analysis of extreme weather events is a key aspect of present-day climate change research due to their significant socio-economic and ecological impacts. This study investigates the spatiotemporal variability of extreme heat events in Southeastern Europe using the Excess Heat Factor (EHF), which has proven to be an effective metric of heatwave severity. Building on the concept of Heatwave Event Moments (HEMs), we developed a framework to identify and analyze heatwaves using both reanalysis and observational data. title: Rockfall hazard assessment at Baia Castle cliff (Phlegrean Fields, Italy): implications for cultural heritage sites in a seismically active volcanic area
abstract: Coastal cliffs developed in volcanic tuffs are highly susceptible to instability due to the combined effects of structural discontinuities, marine erosion, and seismic activity. This study presents a multi-method assessment of rockfall hazard at the Baia Castle cliff (Phlegrean Fields, southern Italy), an area affected by ongoing bradyseism and with a significant cultural heritage exposure. title: Technological Singularity and Sustainable Development: A Conceptual Framework for Cognitive Infrastructure, Sustainable Mobility, and Cultural Capital
abstract: The article explores the fundamental transformations occurring at the intersection of the approaching technological singularity and the implementation of the sustainable development paradigm. The shift from classical (reactive) management models of urban and regional infrastructure to proactive systems driven by Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) is substantiated. title: Development and Evaluation of an Ensemble Regional Storm Surge Forecasting Model for the Coasts of Korea
abstract: This study developed an Ensemble Regional Tide⋅Storm surge Model (ETSM) with 26 atmospheric ensemble members to generate diverse storm surge prediction scenarios along the Korean coast. The predictive accuracy and probabilistic performance were evaluated through seasonal experiments in 2024 and case studies of typhoons from 2022 to 2024, comparing results with observed sea levels and the Regional Tide⋅Storm surge Model (RTSM). title: Environmental heterogeneity and hydrocarbon-associated patterns in deep-sea meiofaunal communities following the Deepwater Horizon spill
abstract: Hydrocarbon contamination is associated with benthic ecosystem variation, yet biological responses are often heterogeneous and can be modified by organic enrichment and spatial environmental gradients. Hydrocarbon-associated patterns were evaluated for deep-sea meiofaunal communities at 109 stations sampled during September-October 2010. title: Catching fire – On cremations in Late Iron Age Åland Islands, Baltic sea
abstract: The cremation was an important part of the mortuary rituals in Late Iron Age Åland Islands, c.550–1050 CE. More than 10 000 burial mounds with cremations found in c.440 farmstead cemeteries are known from the Åland Islands. The burial practice is characteristic of those common in Eastern Sweden. We here analyse how the cremation was carried out, considering detailed macroscopic analyses of the level of calcination of the cremated remains of humans and included animals. abstract: ABSTRACT Aim Endothermic marine mammals face significant thermoregulatory challenges due to heat loss in the highly conductive marine environment. Allen's rule states that endothermic animals in cold environments have smaller appendages than those in warmer environments. While body size adaptations in marine mammals are well‐studied, the role of appendage size as an adaptation to different thermal habitats remains unclear. title: Contrasting nutritional proxies and methylmercury exposure in zooplankton delivered by little auks across Greenland and Svalbard
abstract: Zooplankton forms a key trophic interface in Arctic marine ecosystems, transferring both nutritional resources and contaminants to higher consumers. Yet these dimensions are rarely evaluated together in the prey actually selected and delivered by predators under natural foraging conditions. title: Predicting environmental health-related search patterns using freely available digital and reanalysis data: A critical evaluation of Google Trends and global datasets for Morocco
abstract: Climate change and environmental degradation increasingly threaten urban public health, yet monitoring infrastructure is often unavailable in resource-constrained settings. This study develops and critically evaluates a machine learning framework that predicts environmental health-related search behavior , used as a low-cost digital proxy rather than a measure of clinical burden, in Morocco using exclusively open-access global datasets. title: Regional Trends in Northern Hemisphere Summer Extratropical Cyclone Activity and Their Link to Precipitation and Temperature Trends
abstract: Abstract In recent years a robust weakening of the storm tracks has been identified in reanalysis data. This trend has been linked to coinciding changes in surface temperature extremes and precipitation over land. Here we use a surface‐based metric to quantify regional trends in the boreal summertime low‐level extratropical cyclone activity (ECA) and link this to surface impacts. title: TREND AND ANOMALY OF TEMPERATURE SERIES IN WEST AFRICAN COASTAL URBAN AREAS: THE CASE OF ABIDJAN, CÔTE D'IVOIRE (1985-2024)
abstract: Climate change is accompanied by a growing intensification of temperatures at the local scale, as observed in several cities of the sub-region, yet their evolution and trends remain insufficiently quantified. This study aims to examine the trends and anomalies of temperatures in the city of Abidjan over the period 1985-2024. title: Revisiting how the euphotic depth is computed
abstract: The method of computing the euphotic depth, the depth horizon in the ocean above which light is sufficient for net primary production, has lacked consensus in the literature. Although many still use a % light level as a definition, a practice which dominates textbooks in oceanography, the modeling community uses a constant basal respiration to set the threshold. title: Investigation of Flow Structures in an Aquaculture Tank Under Rolling Excitation Using Statistical Analysis and Proper Orthogonal Decomposition
abstract: Large-scale offshore aquaculture vessels provide an effective approach for expanding marine aquaculture; however, the complex flow characteristics induced by water circulation systems and vessel motion remain insufficiently understood. In this study, a numerical model based on the volume of fluid (VOF) method and the k-ω SST-DES turbulence model was developed to investigate the vortex flow characteristics. title: Changing wind hazards for Mediterranean airports: the case of Cyclone Harry (2026)
abstract: Abstract Mediterranean storms and cyclones can generate hazardous wind conditions with major implications for aviation, yet the link between large-scale dynamics and airport-scale impacts remains poorly quantified. Here, we analyse Cyclone Harry, a January 2026 Mediterranean cyclone that affected several major airports, and place it in a climatological context using ERA5 reanalysis and analoguebased composites for past (1950 to 1987) and present (1988 to 2025) conditions.We examine the synoptic structure, low-level dynamics, thermodynamic environment, and airport-scale impacts through wind spe

title: Contrasting Algorithm Dependence of Extratropical Cyclone and Bomb Cyclone Statistics over the North Pacific
abstract: Abstract Bomb cyclones are high-impact extratropical cyclones characterized by rapid deepening. Although their climatology and long-term changes over the North Pacific (NP) have attracted considerable attention recently, it remains unclear whether bomb cyclone statistics are robust across different cyclone tracking algorithms. title: Relative Sea Surface Temperature Regulates Tropical Cyclone Size‐Intensity Evolution Through Convective Features
abstract: Abstract Relative sea surface temperature (SST), defined as local SST minus the tropical mean, is linked to tropical cyclone (TC) size growth, but its role in coupled size‐intensity evolution remains unclear. Using 23 years of global observations, we show that relative SST regulates very deep convection (infrared brightness temperature <208K), thereby modulating both TC intensification and size expansion. title: Nonlinear dynamics of time-variable slope circulation
abstract: Abstract. Bottom topography strongly constrains ocean circulation in the Arctic, and both theory and numerical modeling suggest that nonlinear flow–topography interactions influence slope-following currents. Yet, how such interactions modify the circulation response to time-variable surface forcing remains poorly understood. abstract: Climate change and the increasing frequency of extreme heat events have intensified thermal stress, particularly in Mediterranean regions, posing significant challenges to human health, quality of life, and sustainable urban development. Therefore, accurate assessment of outdoor thermal comfort has become increasingly important for supporting climate adaptation and planning strategies. abstract: Manufacturing is undergoing a profound transformation driven by digitalization, reshaping traditional processes into interconnected and intelligent systems. Industry 4.0, a contemporary strategy rooted in smart manufacturing principles, integrates advanced technologies such as cyber-physical systems (CPS), internet of things (IoT), artificial intelligence (AI), digital twins (DT), cloud computing, and big data analytics. abstract: Abstract. This study investigates the hydrodynamic and mixing processes at the estuary–shelf transition of a microtidal system, and the buoyant plume generated at the Patos Lagoon mouth (Brazil). title: Thermal–Fluid–Solid Coupling Analysis of Enhanced Heat Transfer and Thermal Stress in Shark Skin Micro-Rib Tubes
abstract: A multi-field coupled numerical model integrating fluid flow, convective heat transfer, and thermal stress is established for a shark-skin-inspired V-shaped micro-rib heat exchange tube. Using the shear stress transport (SST) k-ω model, its thermal–hydraulic performance is compared with a smooth tube, revealing the mechanism of vortex-induced thermal boundary layer disturbance. abstract: Local erosion around foundation elements, generally referred to as ’scour’, is of major concern when designing hydraulic structures. abstract: In this study, we improved a previously published numerical model linking the core composition to the core temperature during accretion by introducing the possibility of chemical disequilibrium during the segregation of the core in the magma ocean phase. title: Field performance of hatchery produced Asian green mussel, Perna viridis (Linnaeus, 1758) and strategies to optimise its farming
abstract: This study evaluates the field performance of hatchery produced Asian green mussel, Perna viridis (Linnaeus, 1758) seed across three estuarine sites viz., Ashtamudi, Neendakara, and Vellimon in Kollam District, Kerala, south India, under varying stocking densities. title: Contrasting seasonal organization of Arctic dynamical and thermodynamic variability
abstract: Arctic atmospheric circulation and near-surface temperature are physically coupled, yet it remains unclear whether their spatial coherence changes in the same way across seasons. Using ERA5 reanalysis for 1940-2024, we directly compare winter (DJF) and summer (JJA) anomalies of 500 hPa geopotential height (Z500) and 2 m air temperature (T2M) over the Arctic. title: Effect of hydrostatic pressure on transport-reaction processes of cement paste under sulfate attack
abstract: Cementitious materials in deep-sea environments may be simultaneously subjected to hydrostatic pressure and sulfate exposure, leading to coupled transport–reaction processes that differ from those under conventional sulfate attack. title: Non-tidal ocean loading from Río de la Plata storm surges: empirical modeling at the Argentine–German Geodetic Observatory (AGGO) over its first decade of operation
abstract: Frequent storm surges in the Río de la Plata estuary produce non-tidal ocean loading signals detectable at the Argentine–German Geodetic Observatory (AGGO), affecting the space geodetic and gravimetric techniques co-located at the site. An empirical model of water level variations across the estuary is developed for the period 2016–2025, covering the first decade of operation of AGGO, using observations from seven tide gauge stations distributed along the Río de la Plata, complemented by two modeled stations derived from astronomical tidal predictions and a global storm surge model. title: Beyond Linear Regression: A Non-Linear Hygroscopic Growth Correction for Satellite-Derived PM2.5 Estimation in Tropical Environments
abstract: Fine particulate matter (PM2.5) estimation from satellite-derived Aerosol Optical Depth (AOD) is often biased in humid tropical environments because aerosol water uptake enhances optical extinction without a corresponding increase in dry particulate mass. This study develops a physics-informed, non-linear AOD-to-PM2.5 conversion framework that explicitly accounts for hygroscopic growth. title: Evaluation of the E3SM Version 3 Stratosphere Performance
abstract: Abstract The interactions between the stratosphere and the troposphere have significant impacts on human activities and Earth system variability. In the third release version of the low‐resolution Energy Exascale Earth System Model (E3SMv3), the representation of the stratosphere is improved through vertical grid refinement in the lower stratosphere and the implementation of the linearized ozone scheme version 3 (Linozv3). title: Cyber-Physical Testing of Wind-Assisted Ships: Recent Developments and Open Data Set for the SOBC-1 Bulk Carrier
abstract: Abstract This paper presents recent improvements in the cyber-physical test method for wind-assisted ships at SINTEF Ocean. In particular, a dynamic lifting line method, that interacts in real-time with the physical ship model, enables now modelling transient aerodynamic effects, sail-hull interaction, and sail-sail interactions. The behaviour of a free-running wind-assisted ship can therefore accurately be documented also during sudden changes in wind velocity or other transient conditions. title: Nonlinear Release of Subinertial Diurnal Internal Tides Forms Spiral Internal Solitary Waves
abstract: Abstract Earth's rotation imposes a dynamical barrier on the free propagation of internal tides at high latitudes, raising questions about the fate of tidal energy poleward of the critical latitude. Satellite observations reveal spiral internal solitary waves (ISWs) along the continental slope of the South Orkney Plateau. Although these waves might be attributed to direct steepening of low‐frequency internal tides, theoretical estimates of their propagation speed are nearly twice those inferred from observations. title: Drivers governing the seasonality of new particle formation in the Arctic
abstract: Abstract. New particle formation (NPF) is the phenomenon wherein gaseous precursors form critical clusters of barely a few nanometres in diameter, after which, under favourable conditions these particles can grow to climate-relevant sizes. Here we present measurements from 2022 to 2024 of particle and ion number size distributions from the Zeppelin Observatory (ZEP), an Arctic research station situated on the western edge of Svalbard. Storm-Track Variability in Synoptic Forcing During Heavy Lake-Effect Snow Events over Lake Michigan
abstract: Lake-effect snow (LES) has traditionally been studied from a mesoscale perspective, with comparatively less attention devoted to the role of synoptic-scale forcing. This study quantifies the prevalence and magnitude of synoptic forcing during 116 heavy LES events affecting the eastern shore of Lake Michigan between 1997 and 2024. Events were identified from the NOAA Storm Events Database and classified into five storm-track categories: Alberta Clippers (ACs), Colorado Lows (COs), East Coast Lows (ECs), Great Lakes Lows (GLLs), and anticyclones (HIs). title: Latitudinal changes in moist heatwaves across the Northern Hemisphere during 1950–2023
abstract: The intensification of moist heat extremes under global warming represents a critical hazard to human health and ecosystem stability. However, the distinct spatiotemporal evolutionary patterns of moist heatwaves (MHWs; relative humidity ≥40%) versus extreme moist heatwaves (EMHWs; relative humidity ≥70%) across different latitudinal zones remain insufficiently understood. Utilizing ERA5 reanalysis data, this study presents a comprehensive analysis of the latitudinal characteristics of MHWs and EMHWs over the Northern Hemisphere land during 1950–2023. abstract: Mesh-free Lagrangian methods including smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH) are ideal for complex ocean engineering involving large free-surface deformations, yet their high computational cost in 3D large-scale domains remains a barrier. Hybrid coupling strategies combine mesh-based far-field solvers with near-field SPH to offer a solution; however, a core challenge has been maintaining consistent free-surface tracking along 3D interfaces under multi-directional waves. title: Generation and Propagation of Eastern Subpolar North Atlantic Salinity Anomalies
abstract: Abstract The Eastern Subpolar North Atlantic (E‐SPNA) upper ocean experiences pronounced interannual salinity variations that influence the global overturning circulation, yet a quantitative understanding of their life cycle remains lacking. Based on an ocean circulation state estimate, we combine budget analysis with particle tracking to quantify the generation and propagation of E‐SPNA salinity anomalies. title: A VFIFE-based non-contact monitoring approach for mooring line tension in floating offshore wind turbines
abstract: The safety of mooring systems is critical for Floating Offshore Wind Turbines (FOWTs), yet contact-based tension monitoring suffers from difficult installation, susceptibility to damage and limited long-term reliability. This study proposes a non-contact monitoring method based on the Vector Form Intrinsic Finite Element (VFIFE), which determines mooring tension from the measured motion of the floating platform. title: Predicting winter cold surge scenarios using ensemble forecasting and clustering techniques
abstract: East Asian cold surges develop through several distinct spatiotemporal evolution patterns, each characterized by a different intensity and duration. Beyond forecasting whether a cold surge will occur, anticipating which type will develop would allow the likely evolution scenario to be foreseen in advance, providing valuable lead time for disaster preparedness. title: Horizontal-plane pendulum-based inertial wave energy harvester with sprag-clutch rectification for unmanned surface vehicles
abstract: Unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) increasingly support long-duration ocean observation, yet their mission endurance remains constrained by limited onboard energy storage. Wave energy offers a continuous, weather-independent supply, although most pendulum-based harvesters respond to only a single motion axis. This study presents a horizontal-plane pendulum-based inertial wave energy harvester integrated within the USV hull, with the pendulum configured parallel to the XY-plane to simultaneously exploit pitch and roll excitation. title: How 3D Processes Drive Trench Infill and Sand Wave Regeneration After Dredging
abstract: Abstract Dynamic bedforms, such as sand waves, may pose a threat to offshore energy infrastructure. Due to their impact on seabed mobility, dredging is often required to reduce risks, for example, to avoid cable exposure. However, commonly used data‐driven methods cannot predict the evolution of partially dredged sand waves. abstract: Snow density is a key parameter for calculating snow water equivalent, snow albedo, snow emissivity, and snow mechanical properties. It is therefore essential in water resource management, snow-air energy exchange computation, cold regions engineering design, and avalanche prevention. In a warming climate, snow density is undergoing rapid changes, which pose challenges for static snow density evolution equations in predicting spatiotemporal variability. title: Green Port Transformation in Renewable Energy and Sustainable Water Port Management: Strategies for Climate-Resilient Maritime Infrastructure
abstract: Ports play a critical role in global trade infrastructure, however they are also a significant source of GHG emissions, energy use as well as marine environmental damage. The shift towards “green ports” has become a strategy to lessen the ecological footprint and enhance the efficiency of port operations by incorporating renewable energy sources, sustainable water management, and climate-resilient infrastructure. title: Sensitivity analysis of annual energy production and associated economic losses due to external wake effects on offshore wind clusters: A case study of the Shinan offshore wind cluster in southwest sea of Korea
abstract: This study investigates the quantitative effects of external wake interactions and inter-farm spacing within a large-scale offshore wind cluster, focusing on the Shinan Cluster in Korea. As the country moves forward with government-led site development under the forthcoming Offshore Wind Special Act, the spatial clustering of multiple wind farms raises concerns about potential energy yield reductions and associated revenue losses caused by external wake effects. abstract: A víz alatti kisugárzott zaj (underwater radiated noise, URN) predikciója a haditechnikai alkalmazásokban és a tengeri környezet védelmében egyaránt stratégiai jelentőségű. title: A waste-integrated hydroxyethyl cellulose–brine electrocoagulation platform for CO₂ uptake and enhanced crude oil recovery
abstract: Managing high-salinity reject brine, CO₂ emissions, and declining oil recovery presents interconnected challenges across the water–energy nexus. This study investigates an integrated waste-derived hydroxyethyl cellulose–electrocoagulation–CO₂ (HEC─EC─CO₂) platform for brine treatment, gas-phase CO₂ uptake, solid recovery, and enhanced oil recovery (EOR). title: Changes in bioclimatic indices in the Arctic in 1991–2025
abstract: In the context of a changing climate, a comprehensive assessment is required of the impact of climatic conditions on the comfort of the living environment. This study evaluates changes in bioclimatic indices assessed on the basis of model reanalysis across the marine and land Arctic within the boundaries of the WMO Arctic Regional Climate Center — Network under ongoing climate change. Data from two periods were used: the WMO reference period (1991–2020) and the recent five-year period (2021–2025). title: Downside-risk pre-positioning for resilient scheduling of an off-grid deep-offshore electricity-hydrogen integrated energy system under extreme weather
abstract: An off-grid deep-offshore electricity-hydrogen integrated energy system (DOEH-IES) provides a practical carrier for onsite offshore wind utilization and multi-energy coordination. However, under typhoon conditions, coupled wind-wave effects and platform motion reduce the available power of floating offshore wind turbines (FOWTs), introducing a time-varying downside risk that conventional scheduling methods often fail to mitigate proactively.
