title: Methodology for a human-centric CIM: Translating non-geocoded citizen perceptions into spatial indicators
abstract: To address the growing complexity between the built environment and urban life, modern urban planning has increasingly relied on digital technologies for decision-making, including City Information Modeling (CIM). While CIM has matured from standards and data integration to real-time analytics and digital twins, most initiatives optimize physical systems while struggling to incorporate “intangible” citizen-generated data. title: Secular polar motion from non-surface-loading processes estimated using satellite gravimetry
abstract: SUMMARY Polar motion (PM) provides an independent, observation-based constraint on global mass redistribution, but interpretation of its long-term variability is primarily limited by uncertainty in the glacial isostatic adjustment (GIA) contribution, for which conventional model-based estimates exhibit substantial differences. Here we develop a refined approach that uses primarily GRACE and GRACE Follow-On (GRACE-FO) observations to estimate the secular PM associated with non-surface-loading processes, predominantly GIA. title: Contrast in the Boundary Layer Convergence Lines at Desert−Oasis Border With Different Vegetation Gradient
abstract: Abstract Motivated by an observed asymmetry in boundary layer convergence lines (BLCLs) between the Kubuqi and Ulan Buh desert borders of the Hetao Oasis in northern China, this work aims to document the differences in BLCL frequency and convective initiation and their potential drivers. Using radar, surface Automatic Weather Station, and reanalysis data in June–August from 2012 to 2022, we found that the Kubuqi border had more frequent, earlier‐forming, and more convective BLCLs, whereas the Ulan Buh border had fewer, shorter‐lived, and more tortuous ones. title: Temperature-dependent durability assessment of fly-ash concrete under coupled chloride-sulfate attack
abstract: Coupled chloride–sulfate attack is a key cause of durability degradation in concrete structures in coastal and saline environments. Existing research mostly focuses on single-ion attack or limited coupled mechanisms, lacking a unified model for fly-ash concrete that simultaneously considers temperature effects, chemical activity, multi-ion competitive interactions, calcium leaching, physical binding of chloride, and mechanical damage. abstract: Since the early 1960s, many studies have documented ionospheric virtual height oscillation with periods ranging from 30 min to 3 h. However, in this investigation, we find a consistent, much larger period in the oscillations of virtual height, as estimated using Coastal Ocean Dynamics Applications Radars (CODARs), whereas few previous studies have consistently observed periods of oscillation in this range. title: A Generation Mechanism of Thorpe‐Detected Turbulence: A Case Study Using WRF Model Simulation
abstract: Abstract Turbulence in the free atmosphere has been widely estimated using the Thorpe method, which identifies vertical inversions in potential temperature profiles as evidence of overturning. However, the mechanisms driving Thorpe‐detected turbulence remain poorly understood, due largely to limitations in spatial and temporal resolution of observational and reanalysis datasets. This study presents the first real‐case numerical simulation of Thorpe‐detected turbulence using the Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model. title: Materials and architected structures for underbody blast mitigation in armoured fighting vehicles: From conventional protection systems to additively manufactured metallic lattices
abstract: Armoured Fighting Vehicles (AFVs) must survive distinct but interacting threat classes, including kinetic-energy and armour-piercing projectiles, shaped-charge jets, high-velocity fragments, top-attack munitions, and buried mine/IED blast. This review therefore positions underbody energy absorbers within the wider layered protection architecture, while deliberately focusing its detailed assessment on mine/IED blast mitigation. title: Contrasting Effects of Turbulence on Tropical Cyclones During Landfall
abstract: Abstract Planetary boundary layer (PBL) turbulence modulates tropical cyclone (TC) intensity through competing mechanisms: (a) frictional dissipation that weakens TCs and (b) frictional convergence that drives stronger low‐level inflow and intensifies TCs. Three landfalling TCs (Beryl, Francine, and Milton) were simulated to examine how enhanced PBL turbulence affects TC intensity during landfall. title: Heat stress and heatwave trends across Türkiye (1975–2024) using the Extended Heat Index
abstract: Heat stress is an increasingly important climate-related hazard in regions experiencing rapid warming and changing temperature–humidity interactions. This study examines heat stress and heatwave trends across Türkiye during 1975–2024 using ERA5 reanalysis data aggregated to the provincial scale. Heat stress was quantified using the Extended Heat Index (EHI), which integrates air temperature and relative humidity to represent physiologically meaningful thermal exposure. title: Small but mighty: Evaluating the community-scale tidal stream energy potential of Midcoast Maine
abstract: In the State of Maine, USA, tidal stream energy resources over a large swath of coastline have remained largely under-evaluated. Former resource assessments have traditionally focused on spatially broad, high-energy areas in the region, such as the Western Passage, that show good potential for grid-scale energy contributions on the order of 10-100 MW. abstract: Agricultural irrigation systems can bear the heavy losses of water through runoff, evaporation, and deep percolation. Crop water requirements vary with crop species, growth stage, soil properties, evapotranspiration, weather, and plant water status; therefore, irrigation scheduling based on a single parameter is insufficient. abstract: This study develops multi-layer perceptron (MLP)-based geoid prediction models for Taiwan using 1′×1′ gravity-anomaly grids, EGM2008 to degree and order 2159, and GNSS/levelling control information. A unified MLP model and an empirical zonal MLP model were constructed to account for spatial differences in terrain and gravity-field characteristics between the Central Mountain Range and coastal regions. title: Instrumental Artefacts Can Reverse Apparent Lightning–Climate Trends
abstract: Abstract Lightning is an Essential Climate Variable, yet long‐term detection records may be compromised by changes in detection technology. Using more than three decades of Austrian lightning observations (1992–2024), we show that instrumental artefacts can reverse the apparent sign of lightning–climate trends. While raw records suggest a significant decline in cloud‐to‐ground lightning, a meteorological reanalysis‐driven reconstruction reveals a robust upward trend in cloud‐to‐ground flash occurrence, with the strongest increase over Alpine terrain. abstract: Abstract Arctic cold air outbreaks (CAOs) produce low‐level cloud patterns influencing the surface radiative balance. The stability parameter (boundary‐layer height over Monin‐Obukhov length) is theorized to distinguish shear‐driven roll convection from buoyancy‐driven cellular convection, but observational evidence remains limited. title: Deciphering inhibitor dynamics and valorization pathways in Eichhornia crassipes biorefineries: Beyond the fermentative hurdle
abstract: Eichhornia crassipes (water hyacinth) has attracted growing attention as a sustainable feedstock for biofuel production and resource recovery due to its rapid growth, high carbohydrate content, and invasive nature. However, large-scale commercialization remains constrained by biomass recalcitrance, pretreatment-induced inhibitor formation, and inadequate integration of conversion pathways. abstract: Abstract Typical climate model resolutions preclude the explicit simulation of most of the spectrum of atmospheric gravity waves (GWs). Climate models must therefore rely on GW parameterizations, which observations help constrain. Between 2011 and 2021, Loon LLC launched thousands of balloons, some of which flew close enough together to be affected by the same GW packet. abstract: The fast industrial digitalization process results in the implementation of Internet of Things (IoT) technologies into the big automated plants to improve its operational precision, reliability, and sustainability. The paper presents a novel IoT-based instrumentation architecture to predictive maintenance and remote monitoring in the scale of industrial setup. title: Plastic pellets pollution on the French Atlantic coast: Investigating the Loire estuary
abstract: Plastic pellets are among the most frequently microplastics reported in coastal environments. However, their distribution and sources remain poorly documented in metropolitan France, particularly along the Atlantic coast. This study combined a literature review, fieldwork, and model simulations to produce an up-to-date data status on pellet occurrence in metropolitan France, and major potential source areas. abstract: The growth of tourism in Saudi Arabia is taking place via a number of destinations spread across the region, and the success of these destinations relies on infrastructure systems that are reliable, ecologically compatible, safe when in operation, and capable of adapting afterwards. abstract: Despite progress in continental United States (CONUS) tornado forecasting, operational seasonal outlooks remain challenging due to intrinsic predictability limits. While previous studies link the El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO) to spring tornado frequency, relying on single tropical indices misses crucial regional variability. abstract: Offshore island and nearshore energy systems in southern Vietnam remain constrained by diesel dependence, fuel-logistics risks, and carbon emissions. abstract: The present study examines the evolution of the phase velocity of surface gravity waves propagating against an opposing current in the vicinity of wave-blocking conditions, defined as flow regimes in which the wave-energy flux can no longer propagate upstream relative to an adverse background current. title: Wetland restoration enhances ecological quality in urbanizing regions
abstract: Abstract Introduction Rapid urbanization and climate change drive widespread wetland degradation, yet it remains unclear whether wetland restoration improves ecological quality (EQ), a composite indicator reflecting vegetation, thermal, hydrological, environmental, and soil conditions at regional scales in highly urbanized landscapes. title: How Data Uncertainty Influences Estimates of Root Zone Water Storage Capacity
abstract: Abstract Root zone water storage capacity () sets the lower limit on the water available to plants and is critical for modeling terrestrial water and carbon fluxes. Due to subsurface heterogeneity in soils, roots, and geology, in‐situ measurements of are infeasible at regional to global scales. Instead, is often estimated using a water balance approach—calculating the difference between precipitation and evapotranspiration to approximate water deficits. title: Dust Loading Increases During Topsoil Flash Droughts Under Rapid Surface Drying and Vegetation Stress
abstract: Abstract Using satellite‐derived dust optical depth (DOD), reanalysis meteorology, and a global topsoil flash drought (TSFD) inventory for 2003–2022, we find that TSFD events are associated with increased dust loading at the global scale. During TSFD events, 44.7% of land pixels exhibited positive DOD anomalies. The net global DOD anomaly increased significantly over the study period; however, this trend cannot be attributed solely to TSFD‐related effects, as changes in background environmental conditions may also have contributed. title: Tornado environments derived from ERA5 over Indonesia
abstract: Abstract Tropical maritime regions, such as Indonesia, experience tornadoes. However, the tornado environment in Indonesia remains poorly understood. In this study, we analyzed convective and kinematic parameters associated with 119 tornado cases from 2010 to 2024. Prior to examining tornado environments, the performance of ERA5 reanalysis was evaluated against sounding observations. ERA5 tends to underestimate some parameters in tropical maritime regions, particularly low-level parameters (0–1 km) compared to mid- and deep-level parameters (0–3 km and 0–6 km). title: Historical climate extremes in Europe and the connection between spring precipitation and summer heat
abstract: Abstract. Hot European summers are often preceded by dry springs such as in 2022, but also in 1473 or 1540, two well-known summers of catastrophic heat. Spring precipitation deficits deplete soil moisture levels, which can amplify extreme summer temperature anomalies in Europe through land-atmosphere feedback mechanisms and altered atmospheric circulation. However, the link is not particularly strong, and hence long time series might help to better elucidate the mechanisms. title: A Hybrid Bi‐ LSTM ‐ AM Framework for Improving Extreme Rainfall Prediction and Bias Correction
abstract: ABSTRACT Reliable forecasting of extreme rainfall remains a critical challenge for flood management in climate‐sensitive regions. This study develops and evaluates an attention‐augmented, bidirectional long short‐term memory framework (Bi‐LSTM‐AM) used for gauge‐based prediction and raster‐based bias correction for extreme rain events. The resulting prediction and bias‐correction models are trained by station observations and reanalysis data during 1980–2019. title: Sensitivity analysis of the simulation of tropical cyclone Amphan using the WRF model
abstract: The sensitivity of twenty-four physics option combinations in the Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model is investigated through simulations of the track, intensity, and landfall of tropical Cyclone Amphan. Simulation accuracy is evaluated using data from an international best track archive. Track performance is assessed using root mean square error (RMSE), while intensity is evaluated by comparing the minimum sea level pressure (MSLP) and the maximum wind speed measured at a height of 10 m above sea level. title: Regional variability in growth and biometrics of yellowfin tuna in Indian waters
abstract: Introduction: Yellowfin tuna, Thunnus albacares , a commercially important pelagic species widespread across the Indian Ocean, plays a critical role in Indian fisheries. Understanding regional variation in biometric and demographic parameters is essential for achieving effective stock assessment and fisheries management. This study evaluated regional differences in growth patterns and condition of yellowfin tuna across the Indian Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ). title: Spatiotemporal Covariability of Extreme Precipitation and Integrated Vapour Transport Over the Tibetan Plateau During 1979–2015
abstract: ABSTRACT Extreme precipitation and atmospheric moisture transport are closely linked components of the Tibetan Plateau (TP) hydroclimate, but statistical covariability should be distinguished from causal control. We analyse extreme‐precipitation and integrated vapour transport (IVT) indices over 1979–2015 using APHRODITE precipitation and ERA5 reanalysis. title: Characteristics of Energy Dissipation Rate at the Standard Weather Observatory Under Various Atmospheric Conditions and Its Application to Aviation Turbulence Intensity
abstract: Abstract Accurate prediction of low‐level turbulence (LLT) is critical for aviation safety, particularly for the emerging urban air mobility industry and aircraft takeoffs and landings. To better understand and predict these hazards, the characteristics of the energy dissipation rate (EDR) in the atmospheric boundary layer (ABL) were investigated using 8‐year high‐frequency sonic anemometer observations collected at multiple altitudes of the 307‐m meteorological tower in the Boseong Standard Weather Observatory (BSWO), South Korea. title: The influence of vapor pressure deficit changes on global terrestrial evapotranspiration
abstract: Abstract. Vapor pressure deficit (VPD) is increasingly recognized as the primary driver of uncertainty in future global evapotranspiration (E) trends. Accurately characterizing the spatiotemporal dynamics of VPD and clarifying its mechanisms of influence on terrestrial E are crucial for improving water-use efficiency, optimizing ecosystem structure and function, and addressing the challenges of global climate change. title: Wind conditions shape co-migration fidelity in trans-Saharan birds at a Mediterranean stopover site
abstract: Weather is a key driver of bird migration, particularly near ecological barriers, where migratory species often converge before crossing. While its effects on individual timing are well documented, how weather reshapes the temporal assemblage of migratory bird communities remains unexplored. title: Development and evaluation of the ECHAM6-iMAPLE v1.0 coupled atmosphere–ecosystem model
abstract: Abstract. Land-atmosphere interactions play a fundamental role in regulating climate variability, ecosystem productivity, and air quality through coupled exchanges of energy, water, carbon, and reactive trace gases. However, many Earth system models adopt simplified representations of vegetation physiological processes, leading to biases in terrestrial carbon and water fluxes and increased uncertainties in climate simulations. title: Extreme wave height estimation using a hybrid distribution approach
abstract: Accurate estimation of design wave heights is paramount for the safety and resilience of coastal infrastructure. However, extreme value analysis with limited samples faces two critical challenges: spurious identification of bounded EV-III distributions due to statistical fluctuations, and severe underestimation risks stemming from uncertain finite upper limits. title: Lake Urmia desiccation drives building heating and cooling energy demand in northwestern Iran
abstract: Abstract The progressive desiccation of terminal lakes under global climate change represents an emerging environmental challenge with significant implications for regional climate and building energy demand. This study investigates the impact of Lake Urmia desiccation on building energy consumption across 13 cities in the Lake Urmia Basin in northwestern Iran during 2001–2023. Using MODIS land surface temperature, Landsat water-extent monitoring, MERRA-2 reanalysis, and GPM precipitation data, we generated 299 year-specific weather files for 13 cities across the Lake Urmia Basin. title: The impact of along-strike variations in overriding plate thickness on subduction dynamics and mantle flow
abstract: Subduction zones are inherently three-dimensional systems and exhibit pronounced trench-parallel variability in key observables, including the deformation style of the overriding plate, trench migration rates, slab geometry, and mantle flow patterns. Geodynamic models typically invoke external mantle flow and/or along-strike variations in the properties of the subducting slab to explain this variability, often neglecting the influence of the overriding plate, despite growing evidence of its strong control on subduction dynamics. title: High‐Resolution Downscaling of a Lightweight Climate Emulator Using Diffusion‐Based Super‐Resolution
abstract: Abstract High‐resolution climate fields are essential for the assessment of their regional and local effects. Current global climate models, along with being computationally expensive, are often too coarse for applications that depend on local extremes and orographic gradients. Machine learning offers a computationally efficient route for both climate emulation and super‐resolution from coarse simulations to finer spatial scales. title: Bio-inspired design and laser additive manufacturing of novel twisted lattice metamaterial for enhanced strength and energy absorption performance
abstract: Drawing inspiration from natural helical architectures, a biomimetic twisted lattice metamaterial (TLM) derived from an octet lattice was manufactured using laser powder bed fusion (LPBF), which addresses the inherent drawbacks of traditional lattices and promotes their mechanical performance. The forming quality of the TLMs was analyzed using SEM and micro-CT methods. title: Assessing mangrove sensitivity to thermal variations through a satellite-based analysis on the southern São Paulo coast, Brazil
abstract: Abstract Mangroves near subtropical range limits may benefit from fewer cold constraints, yet warmer conditions can also increase atmospheric water demand. These competing possibilities were examined in the Cananéia-Iguape Coastal System, southeastern Brazil, by combining ERA5 2 m air temperature with MODIS normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI), enhanced vegetation index (EVI), and leaf area index (LAI). title: Tropical Indo-western Pacific forcing expedites warming in the northern Canadian-Greenland Arctic
abstract: Since the beginning of modern satellite monitoring around 1980, near-surface and tropospheric temperatures in the northern Canadian-Greenland Arctic have substantially warmed, with magnitudes comparable to those in the pan-Arctic. However, the main causes of this marked regional warming and its magnitude in future projections remain debated because of large inter-model spread across historical and future periods. title: The OpenSat4Weather dataset: Ku-band satellite link data for precipitation monitoring
abstract: Abstract. The TV-SAT signals received by the ground antennas of Satellite Microwave Links (SMLs) can be opportunistically used for identifying and quantifying precipitation. Hence, SMLs can serve as low-cost rainfall sensors complementary to conventional instruments. However, a significant challenge for opportunistic sensors, such as SMLs and their terrestrial counterpart, i.e., commercial microwave links (CMLs), stems from potential ownership issues, possibly hindering progress in the development of processing tools and validation studies. title: Construction of a Global Atmospheric Refractivity Model for Optical Wavelengths Based on Temporal Evolution Characteristics
abstract: Abstract Atmospheric refractivity model accuracy is important for refraction correction, starlight refraction navigation, and related optoelectronic applications. To address the insufficient understanding of refractivity temporal evolution and the lack of clear criteria for selecting model temporal resolution, this study constructs a global four‐dimensional gridded atmospheric refractivity data set from ERA5 reanalysis data for 2015–2024, with a spatial resolution of 0.25° × 0.25° and an hourly temporal resolution. title: Cloud vertical structure across China from a national Ka-band cloud radar network: thermodynamic, dynamical, and land-surface controls
abstract: Abstract. Cloud vertical structure plays a central role in regulating Earth’s radiation balance and hydrological cycle, yet it remains poorly represented in weather and climate models due to limited high-resolution observations. Using a newly established national network of 80 Ka-band cloud radars, we provide the first high-spatiotemporal-resolution characterization of cloud vertical structure across China for 2024 and quantify its thermodynamic, dynamical, and land-surface controls. title: Towards a reliability-aware virtual sensor framework for smart water infrastructure: An offline residual-based change-point analysis
abstract: Water utilities increasingly depend on Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) sensors to support infrastructure planning, predictive asset maintenance, operational asset monitoring, and digital-twin applications. However, physical IIoT sensors remain vulnerable to sensor drift, calibration degradation, device failure, and communication outages, creating data observability gaps that can reduce confidence in analytics-driven operational decisions. title: Tracing the Journey of Microplastics from Aquatic Ecosystems to Seafood
abstract: Microplastic pollution has become an important environmental issue due to the widespread occurrence, persistence, and biological accessibility of small plastic particles in aquatic ecosystems. Fish and other seafood organisms are of particular concern because they may come into contact with microplastics at different stages of their life cycle. These particles can be taken up directly from contaminated water and sediments or indirectly through the consumption of contaminated food. title: RHITA: a web tool for real-time detection of extreme weather events
abstract: Abstract. Extreme weather hazards are increasing and stakeholders need rapid, transparent information during unfolding events. We present RHITA (Real-time Hazard Identification and Tracking Algorithm), an open-source framework and web tool for near real-time detection and tracking of weather-related hazards over Europe. RHITA identifies grid cells exceeding local quantile thresholds, groups them into spatial clusters, and links clusters through time to reconstruct three-dimensional events in longitude, latitude, and time. title: Climatology of large-scale atmospheric conditions favorable to clear-air turbulence over Europe (1950–2025): the role of quasi-biennial solar modulation
abstract: Abstract Turbulence represents a primary hazard for aviation, with Clear-Air Turbulence (CAT) posing a unique threat due to its visually undetectable nature. This study evaluates the 75-year temporal evolution of the macro-environmental atmospheric conditions favorable to CAT over Europe and North Africa from 1950 to 2025. Using monthly ERA5 reanalysis data at 200 and 225 hPa, seven synoptic-scale diagnostic indices were analyzed: Horizontal Divergence (HDG), Richardson Number (Ri), NCSU1, Brown Index (BRI), Ellrod Index (EI1, EI2), and Potential Vorticity (PV). title: Intrinsic transition mechanism of shallow convection in the wintertime extratropics
abstract: Abstract We examined the evolution of shallow convective structures in the atmospheric boundary layer in response to changes in the basic state. Idealized numerical experiments were designed to reflect a typical winter monsoonal environment with prescribed sea surface temperatures (SSTs) varying from 273 to 287 K. title: Quantification of wave–current interactions in a tide-dominated harbour: A fully coupled modelling study of Darwin Harbour, Australia
abstract: The present work investigates the effects of wave-current interactions in a tidally dominant harbour, using Darwin Harbour in Australia as a case study. Numerical experiments were performed using a two-way coupled FVCOM modelling system across five distinct configurations: a hydrodynamic model, a fully coupled wave-current interaction model, a wave model, a fully coupled model excluding wind forcing, and a fully coupled model without swell input. title: Warm-sector heavy rainfall over the eastern China plains: identification, characteristics, and precursor dynamic signals
abstract: Abstract. Warm-sector heavy rainfall (WSHR) features small spatial scales, posing critical forecast challenges, while its fractional contribution to regional heavy rainfall and its short-term precursors remain poorly quantified. title: Spatial distribution, transport patterns, and dynamic processes of microplastics in global rivers: A review
abstract: : Rivers serve as the principal pathway for transporting microplastics from land to the ocean, thereby playing an indispensable role in their global transport. This study conducted a bibliometric review based on 176 field-observation datasets and 323 mechanism-related publications spanning 2004-2026 to synthesise the spatial distribution, transport patterns and dynamic processes of microplastics in global river systems. title: Hysteresis of western North Pacific tropical cyclone activity under multiple CO 2 removal scenarios
abstract: Abstract Tropical cyclone (TC) activity is expected to change under future climate mitigation pathways, yet its response to carbon dioxide removal (CDR) remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate the hysteretic response of the genesis potential index (GPI) over the western North Pacific (WNP) using an Earth system model under four idealized CDR scenarios with different peak CO 2 concentrations. title: Probable Maximum Precipitation Estimation Under Climate Change: Addressing Sampling and Bias Correction Uncertainties Using Large Ensemble Climate Simulations
abstract: Abstract This study presents an integrated framework for estimating Probable Maximum Precipitation (PMP)‐equivalent return levels under climate change, addressing two critical challenges: sampling uncertainty for rare events and the validation of bias correction under different global warming scenarios. Leveraging large regional climate model ensembles, the framework combines spatial transposition, based on L‐moment homogeneity, with ensemble pooling to expand the effective sample size to nearly 10,000 independent annual maxima per location. title: Assessing power system vulnerability to climate-related stressors and shocks: The case of Indonesia
abstract: Climate change and extreme weather are increasing the vulnerability of power systems globally, particularly in emerging economies such as Indonesia. Yet, existing studies often assess these impacts in isolation, focusing on individual components or specific hazards, leaving system-level effects—at provincial and national scales—under-examined. To address this gap, we develop an integrated, spatially explicit approach to assess an energy system's climate-related vulnerabilities and their impacts, and apply the approach to Indonesia. title: A Synthesis of Research on the Rollover Stability of Prestressed Concrete Girders Supported on Elastomeric Bearings
abstract: Rollover stability is a critical concern for prestressed concrete bridge girders, particularly during handling, transportation, and erection when lateral restraint is limited. The growing use of long-span, slender sections has increased their susceptibility to rollover instability, especially under the combined influence of geometric imperfections, thermal gradients, eccentric loading, and inclination and deformation of bearing surfaces. title: Interannual and seasonal evolution of supraglacial drainage systems on Nivlisen Ice Shelf, East Antarctica
abstract: Abstract. Supraglacial channel networks (SCNs) represent critical components of the surface drainage system on Antarctic ice shelves, facilitating the redistribution of meltwater, including into and out of supraglacial lakes, potentially influencing ice-shelf stability. However, the seasonal and interannual variability in their spatial extent, structural evolution, and climatic sensitivity remain poorly quantified, particularly compared to observations of supraglacial lakes. abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding the variability and evolution of precipitation extremes associated with climate change is essential to support adaptation strategies, risk management, and civil protection. In this context, this study investigates the climatology, observed trends, and future projections of precipitation extremes in the Southeast Atlantic Hydrographic Basin (SAHB), a region of great socioeconomic relevance in Brazil. abstract: Ocean wave energy resources are immense and, if harnessed, can serve as a reliable source to support a significant portion of electricity needs. However, the technology to convert wave power into useful electrical power is still cost-intensive. One significant challenge is inefficient Power Take-Off (PTO) control technologies. title: Estimating Twomey forcing sensitivity to aerosol plume spreading rates
abstract: Abstract. The amount of sunlight that reaches Earth's surface can be reduced by increasing cloud droplet number and decreasing droplet size (i.e., Twomey forcing), a central idea underpinning the Marine Cloud Brightening strategy. Cloud albedo depends nonlinearly on cloud droplet concentration, meaning the spatial extent of aerosol plumes could be an important constraint on the brightening potential. title: Dynamical and thermodynamic mechanisms driving the April 2025 severe thunderstorm over eastern India
abstract: On 10 April 2025, a severe thunderstorm impacted eastern India, causing disastrous impacts across 19 of Bihar's 38 districts. Survey-estimated peak surface winds of 120 km/h (based on structural damage assessment) contributed to 63 deaths—40 from wind-related hazards and 23 from lightning strikes—with the district of Nalanda experiencing the most extensive devastation. title: Decadal predictions of wind, solar and compound power indicators to support the European renewable energy sector
abstract: Abstract. Renewable energy production is strongly influenced by climate variability and change, making the energy sector sensitive to fluctuations on decadal timescales. Decadal climate predictions, which aim to forecast climate variability over the next few years, therefore offer potential value for anticipating near-term changes in wind and solar resources and supporting climate-informed energy planning. title: A design wave method for the prediction of extreme combined wind-wave loads on floating wind turbines
abstract: The design wave approach has been used in the past to evaluate short-term extreme wave loads on offshore structures, effectively reducing the required test duration compared to the irregular wave Monte Carlo approach. The method uses short-duration wave episodes specifically designed to excite extreme loads. Also known as response-conditioned waves (RCW), they are used in a multi-fidelity framework, where the load statistics are first estimated using an efficient low-fidelity surrogate response model. abstract: Denitrification is the primary pathway for fixed nitrogen (N) removal from aquatic systems. Its occurrence in sediments is promoted by suboxic conditions, high organic matter reactivity, sharp redox transitions, and the co-occurrence of multiple N-transformation processes. title: Identification of optimal ERA5 model level for wind resource assessments in mountainous terrain
abstract: Abstract. Accurate estimation of hub-height wind speed is crucial for wind resources assessment at prospective sites. Traditionally, long-term wind speed series are derived from short-term site observations combined with reanalysis products, most commonly the ERA5 single-level data at 10 m and 100 m heights. However, the coarse spatial resolution of ERA5 limits their reliability in complex mountainous regions, leading to weak correlations with local wind measurements due to not adequately resolved near-surface flow. abstract: The stability of airport infrastructure is critical to preventing structural cracks, preserving high-precision equipment, and maintaining air traffic under heavy, repetitive loads. In this context, an in-situ geotechnical characterization and shallow foundation design study was conducted for a building at Cotonou Airport. The geotechnical investigations were based on three piezocone tests (CPTu) carried out to refusal depths of 8.0 to 9.0 meters. title: CFD-Based Numerical Optimization of the Thermal Performance of PCM-Integrated Hollow Bricks: Combined Effects of Cavity Geometry and Phase-Change Temperature under Hot-Climate Conditions
abstract: Abstract This study presents a two-dimensional transient CFD investigation of the thermal performance of hollow bricks incorporating air, glass wool, and phase change materials under the hot-climate conditions of Kairouan, Tunisia. Five brick geometries and three PCMs-RT26, RT30, and RT34 were evaluated over a 24-h thermal cycle using ANSYS Fluent R19. title: Model development for microbial growth in underground hydrogen storage reservoirs
abstract: Abstract The topic of underground hydrogen storage brings microbial processes into the focus. Underground porous structures provide excellent living conditions for microorganisms because their habitat is protected but still allows a supply of substrates and nutrients. As a consequence, microorganisms exist and make a substantial contribution to many subsurface porous media systems, as e.g. oil and gas reservoirs and underground gas storages. title: Spontaneous zonal symmetry breaking of tropical rain belt
abstract: Abstract The intertropical convergence zone (ITCZ) is a central component of tropical climate, yet the conditions under which a tropical rain belt remains zonally extended or becomes unstable to zonal organization remain poorly understood. Here we investigate this problem using idealized non‐rotating kilometer‐scale simulations forced by a prescribed sea surface temperature (SST) distribution that varies only in the meridional direction. abstract: Abstract Tropical cyclone (TC) forecasting is essential for disaster preparedness, yet accurate intensity prediction remains challenging, particularly during rapid intensification. This study proposes TianXing‐TC, a lightweight probabilistic post‐processing framework that leverages ensemble forecasts from the AI weather prediction model TianXing and integrates multi‐source TC‐related information. abstract: Abstract In paleomagnetism, records of paleosecular variation (PSV) on centennial timescales are often based on magnetic measurements from lava flows. However, samples from recent flows that cooled in known magnetic fields often fail to produce the expected paleomagnetic directions, and samples from the same flow often show large within‐ and between‐site dispersion. abstract: Rooftop photovoltaic (PV) deployment supports urban decarbonization, but its local microclimatic effects and interactions with urban morphology remain underexplored, particularly in coastal cities such as Sendai, Japan. The current study uses the weather research and forecasting (WRF) model with PV parameterization scheme and local climate zone (LCZ) data at 400 m resolution to conduct five experiments (exp_ctrl, exp_25, exp_50, exp_75, and exp_100) representing 0–100% citywide PV roof coverage during the hottest week of 2025. abstract: The Tampa Bay estuary is a vital ecological and economic hub, whose productive, shallow-water habitats are highly vulnerable to both chronic anthropogenic stress and acute environmental disturbance events (e.g., extreme weather, human incidents). abstract: ABSTRACT The presence of large wood (LW) and logjams as flow obstructions in rivers results in, among other processes and forms, backwater and scour pools. title: Mechanical and numerical evaluation of expansive soils for flexible road pavement stabilization using sugarcane bagasse ash and lime
abstract: Abstract The expansive, highly swelling clay soils, which have low bearing capacity, result in damage to flexible pavements. Utilizing locally available waste materials to develop low-cost, sustainable stabilizers improves the engineering properties of the subgrade. Laboratory-strength enhancement, establishing links between material-level stabilization and structural response via numerical modeling, has become a landmark. This study aims to assess the combination of sugarcane bagasse ash (SCBA) with lime as a remedial measure for expansive soil and its effect on flexible pavement performance.

abstract: Volcanic ashfall has only recently been recognized as a destabilizing hazard for small craft, as evidenced by vessel capsizing during the 2011–2012 Cordón Caulle eruption in Argentine Patagonia. abstract: This study examines a section of a centralized district heating network for which the optimal pipe diameter and flow velocity must be determined. abstract: Abstract Rainfall-induced shallow landslides are typically attributed to short-term meteorological triggers such as rainfall intensity and duration. abstract: Understanding regional wetting and drying under global warming remains challenging. Here we show, using global climate simulations and 191 records of past climate, that terrestrial moisture changes over the past 21,000 years follow a pronounced latitudinal pattern. abstract: Abstract. Blowing snow sublimation is a key boundary-layer process on the Greenland Ice Sheet that removes and redistributes snow and thereby influences the surface energy balance. abstract: The Sunda strait, part of The Sunda Megathrust, is one of Indonesia’s most tsunamigenic regions and is recognised as highly susceptible earthquakes and tsunami related hazard. abstract: Fatigue damage limits the service life of metallic structures, including mobile working machines. title: From Static Biomimetics to Programmable and Adaptive Systems: Advances in Milli-structures in Directed Fluid Transport
abstract: Abstract Directed fluid transport is critical to diverse applications spanning water purification, atmospheric water harvesting, point-of-care diagnostics, thermal management, and energy conversion, yet conventional microfluidic systems often require external pumps and complex infrastructure, severely limiting their scalability and adaptability. Directed fluid transport enabled by milli-structured surfaces has rapidly evolved from static, one‑way capillary designs to dynamic, reconfigurable and programmable systems. title: Changes in the annual cycle in shallow subarctic groundwater regimes over 50 years
abstract: Seasonal groundwater level regimes are exposed to climate change, with implications for drought and flood risks, water supply, agriculture, and ecosystems. Changes in the intra-annual groundwater fluctuations are accentuated in quickly responding shallow aquifers found worldwide, but particularly in subarctic regions, where the cold winter season attenuates infiltration and evaporation. To identify the types of subarctic groundwater regimes and their responses to the changing climate, 50-year groundwater level data from 52 monitoring stations throughout Finland were analyzed. abstract: High-resolution regional forecasts support disaster mitigation and sectoral decisions, yet numerical regional models remain costly. Here we introduce AERO-ODE, a physics-guided framework that combines global dynamical information, parameterization increments, and regional terrain constraints. title: Improving the CLASSIC (v1.8) snow model to better simulate Arctic snowpacks
abstract: Abstract. This study enhances the snow model of the Canadian Land Surface Scheme including Biogeochemical Cycles (CLASSIC), with a particular focus on Arctic environments. Key snow model physics improvements include adjustments to the thermal conductivity at the top of the first soil layer, a revised computation of the temperature at the snow–soil interface (hereafter, bottom snow temperature), and the addition of a windless exchange coefficient in sensible heat flux calculations. title: INTEGRATION OF RISK-BASED RESILIENCE STRATEGIES INTO INTELLIGENT SAFETY MANAGEMENT OF SHIP-PORT CYBER-PHYSICAL SYSTEMS
abstract: The article presents an integrated scientific and methodological concept of navigation safety management based on risk-oriented and resilience strategies in the context of cyber-physical interaction between ship and port systems. The aim of the study is to develop a conceptual model of risk-oriented planning for maritime transport networks that ensures increased reliability of mooring operations under operational uncertainty. title: Flow dynamics of cryolava or impact melt on Titan’s surface
abstract: Titan, a unique body in the solar system, resembles a life-size Miller–Urey experiment where pockets of liquid water might interact with abundant organic matter. Its young surface (less than a billion years) shows signs of material exchange with the interior, and an isotopic signature is detected in the atmosphere. Cryovolcanism and meteor impacts represent potential high energy mechanism for these exchanges. title: History of anthropogenic Phosphorus inputs (HaPi) to the terrestrial biosphere from 1860 to 2020
abstract: Abstract. Nitrogen and Phosphorus (P) are essential nutrients for sustaining life on Earth and have been increasingly applied in global agriculture to meet the growing demand for food production. Quantifying the spatial and temporal dynamics of nutrient inputs to the terrestrial biosphere is crucial for analyzing nutrient flows in crop-livestock systems, managing nutrient resources sustainably, and mitigating nutrient-related environmental impacts. title: Role of atmospheric circulation and anthropogenic forcing in the extreme 2025 European summer heatwave
abstract: Abstract In summer 2025, an extreme heatwave propagated northeastward across Europe, sequentially affecting Southwestern (SWEU) and Northern (NEU) Europe with record-breaking durations in the 1979-2025 record. However, the roles of atmospheric circulation and anthropogenic forcing in the 2025 European high-temperature conditions remain unclear. Here we show that atmospheric circulation explains 82.5% (95% uncertainty interval: 65.0-99.0%) and 51.9% (37.0-65.2%) of the regional mean maximum temperature (Tmax) anomalies averaged over the respective heatwave periods in SWEU and NEU, respectively,

title: A Fermatean fuzzy fault tree and Bayesian network hybrid for collision and grounding risk in a congested strait
abstract: Collision and grounding remain the dominant accident categories in congested straits, where dense crossing traffic, sharp bends and strong currents act together with human and technical failures. Quantitative risk assessment in such waters is hampered by scarce failure data and by the vagueness of expert judgement. This study proposes a hybrid model that couples Fermatean fuzzy fault tree analysis with a Bayesian network for the assessment of collision and grounding risk during the transit of a congested strait. journal: Journal of Marine and Engineering Technology

title: Uncertainty in Precipitation Estimates Warrants Greater Consideration in Debris‐Flow Research
abstract: Abstract Quantitative precipitation estimates (QPEs) may provide a valuable data resource for investigations of postfire debris flows. In mountainous regions where debris flows typically occur, gauge coverage can be sparse; gridded QPEs offer remotely sensed and/or physics‐based precipitation estimates where no direct measurement is available. However, different gridded QPEs often tell contrasting stories about the magnitude, timing, and location of precipitation during a storm, which can lead to biases or misrepresentations of triggering rainfall in debris‐flow studies. title: Precipitation nowcasting model based on multi-source data fusion and efficient additive attention
abstract: Short-term precipitation nowcasting serves as an indispensable technical support for the early warning and risk management of meteorological hazards. To improve the nowcasting accuracy by leveraging complementary information from multi-source data, this study proposes a precipitation nowcasting model based on multi-source data fusion and efficient additive attention (EAA-MNFP). title: Research Proposal for Investigation and Assessment of the Fishing Ban Effect on Songjiang Perch in the Fuyang Section of the Qiantang River Based on Broadband Acoustic Technology
abstract: Songjiang perch (Trachidermus fasciatus) is a catadromous fish with important ecological and conservation value in the Qiantang River, and it is also a national Class II protected wild animal. To evaluate the protection effect of the fishing ban period on Songjiang perch in the Fuyang section of the Qiantang River, this study intends to use a broadband scientific echosounder to measure the acoustic characteristics of Songjiang perch by the controlled method and the modeling method, and to conduct two acoustic surveys at night in May and July in the Fuyang section of the Qiantang River. title: How Predictable Was the Extreme Precipitation Preceding the May 2019 Arkansas River Floods?
abstract: Abstract In May 2019, unprecedented extreme rainfall over the central United States (US) facilitated severe flooding along the Arkansas River. The well‐documented relationship between atmospheric rivers (ARs) and central US heavy precipitation motivated investigation into AR relevance to this event and its predictability on extended timescales. title: Finite-element analysis to assess the influence of cutback geometry on strain concentration in concrete-weight coated pipelines
abstract: Strain concentration at the field joints of concrete-weight coated (CWC) pipelines, driven by stiffness discontinuities between coated and uncoated sections, remains a key design challenge because the effects of cutback geometry are not fully understood, especially when different pipe stiffnesses are envisageable. This study introduces a stiffness-dependent framework to quantify how cutback geometry influences strain concentration across the investigated pipe configurations. title: Anthropogenic aerosol reduction contributes to faster flash drought onset in a changing climate
abstract: Flash droughts have emerged as severe hazards, posing growing challenges to natural and socioeconomic systems, yet the influence of recent aerosol reductions on their onset remains unclear. Here, we investigate the impacts of aerosols and their underlying mechanisms using multi-source observations and large-ensemble climate simulations. Lower aerosol levels are increasingly linked to severe soil moisture deficits, with aerosol effects on onset-speed variability intensifying across 69.2% of regions. abstract: The aim of this work was to develop a statistically substantiated typology of thermal conditions of calendar years for Almaty and a quantitative analysis of its transformation against the background of ongoing climate change. A two-stage approach was used for the study. The first stage: dimensionality reduction using principal component analysis (PCA) followed by k-means clustering to identify integral year types. title: Simulating jökulhlaups from an ice-marginal lake within a 2D model of subglacial drainage and basal sliding
abstract: Abstract. Ice-marginal lakes are an increasingly common feature of glacierised landscapes, and their sudden drainage beneath glaciers (a jökulhlaup) can threaten downstream communities and infrastructure. Numerous efforts to model jökulhlaups have been made, however, because these models are 1D representations of a single channel connected to a lake, they cannot simulate lateral jökulhlaup propagation through the subglacial system. title: European Climate Signals in Water Budget Dynamics
abstract: Monitoring the water budget helps us understand and manage the available water in a specific area, as well as track its use. Knowing the water budget (i.e., the difference between water inflow and outflow) allows us to predict water shortages or surpluses. In these times of climate change, the risk of extreme events such as droughts and floods is rising. The study considered the area of the European continent, classified according to the Koppen-Geiger climate zones, as it features a highly diverse climate. title: Rossby wave diversion as a source of subseasonal predictability for extreme Meiyu-Baiu events
abstract: Meiyu-Baiu, the distinct rainy season in subtropical East Asia, is characterized by a quasi-stationary Meiyu-Baiu Front (MBF) along which excessive rainfall and mega floods often occur. This study shows that the spatial stationarity of MBF, and thus its potential to generate catastrophic flooding is inherently modulated by synoptic-scale disturbances over northeastern East Asia. The activity of these disturbances is coupled with the Northern Annular Mode (NAM) and the subtropical westerly jet across the subseasosnal timescales. title: Spaceborne multi-sensor tracking reveals hydrologic decoupling during the record-breaking Sahara flood
abstract: Satellite remote sensing enables large-scale quantification of extreme hydrologic events in data-scarce regions, yet the integration of multi-sensor observations to resolve hydrologic responses remains limited. The record-breaking 2024 Sahara flood presents a unique opportunity to evaluate satellite-based characterisation of hydrologic extremes in hyper-arid environments. title: Anthropogenic aerosol forcing of European windstorms in CMIP6 climate models
abstract: A recently developed set of historical storm reconstructions were extensively validated by insurance loss data and revealed how European windstorm damages were three times higher in the 1980s and '90s compared to a few decades before and since. A better understanding of these slower fluctuations could improve how this costly risk is managed. Here, we explore the impacts of anthropogenic aerosols (AA) on European property damage using results from DAMIP (Detection and Attribution Model Intercomparison Project) climate model experiments. title: Distilling complexity: stylized facts as explicit, auditable foundation for ecological theory and modeling
abstract: Ecological models routinely rely on broad empirical regularities to constrain theory and validate predictions, yet these regularities are typically applied implicitly under alternative labels such as "patterns", "laws", or "benchmarks." Such implicit applications obscure a model's empirical commitments, hide unverified assumptions, mask scale dependencies, and hinder transfer across systems. title: From concept to action: Driving impact through responsible research practices in the International Polar Year 2032–2033 An early career perspective
abstract: Regions at the poles are warming at rates two to four times higher than the global average, driving profound environmental, societal, and geopolitical changes. As Polar Early Career Researchers with careers extending into and beyond the 5th International Polar Year in 2032–2033, we have a responsibility to shape research practices that are impactful, ethical, and sustainable. We argue that current definitions of research impact often prioritize narrow, quantifiable metrics, overlooking cultural, environmental, and long-term consequences. title: Intersections of climate and society: cold stress vulnerability in Northern Norway
abstract: Extreme cold profoundly shapes health, livelihoods, and social well-being in northern communities, yet research on social vulnerability to such conditions remains limited. This study provides a framework for integrating social, demographic, infrastructural, and institutional dimensions into an assessment of vulnerability to extreme cold in northern Norway. abstract: The aim of the article is to increase the efficiency of hydrometeorological support users for the population and enterprises leaders by implementing a new paradigm. The failure of enterprises to account for all climate and change-related risks, combined with the absence of systematized and formalized impact forecasts and recommendations for preventive actions, leads to increased losses. title: Conceptual analysis on synergetic retrievals of self-consistent aerosol property climate data records
abstract: The influence of aerosols on climate is determined not only by their global distribution but also by their composition. However, so far, a large fraction of the development efforts for satellite-based aerosol retrievals has focused on inverting from different single instruments the total column aerosol optical depth (AOD), as measure of the total abundance of atmospheric aerosols. title: Long-term changes and attribution of lake water levels on the Tibetan Plateau revealed by multisource satellite altimetry data
abstract: ABSTRACT Monitoring Tibetan Plateau (TP) lakes is constrained by harsh environments and methodological limitations. To overcome the limited spatiotemporal coverage of single-mission satellite altimetry and the shortcomings of conventional linear analyses, we integrated CryoSat-2 and Sentinel-3A/B altimetry observations with a multilevel robust anomaly-detection framework to generate water-level time series for 11 representative TP lakes (2010–2026). title: Quantifying Groundwater–Surface Water Exchange on a River Island: A Comparative Analysis of Direct and Indirect Methods
abstract: Abstract Groundwater–surface water exchange is a key hydrological process that governs river water quality and aquatic ecosystems. However, the quantification of such exchange remains uncertain, especially within river island aquifers where exchange processes are highly heterogeneous. In this study, direct seepage meter measurements and indirect Darcy‐based estimates of exchange fluxes were compared under consistent spatiotemporal conditions within the aquifer of Jungsa Island, a river island in the lower West Nakdong River, South Korea. title: Convectively Coupled Equatorial Waves in a Global Storm‐Resolving Model
abstract: Abstract We show how reducing the fall speeds of rain and ice leads to reduced biases of Convectively Coupled Equatorial Waves (CCEWs) in convection‐resolving configurations of the Icosahedral Non‐hydrostatic Model (ICON). In particular, reducing the fall speeds of rain and ice leads to stronger activity over the wavenumbers and frequencies associated with convectively coupled Kelvin waves, inertio‐gravity waves, mixed Rossby‐gravity waves, equatorial Rossby waves, and the Madden‐Julian oscillation, and to weaker activity of tropical depressions. title: Process based modelling of breaker bar evolution with submerged vegetation under regular waves
abstract: This study investigates how submerged vegetation influences breaker bar development using the process based IH2VOF-SED model, which couples a two-dimensional vertical Reynolds averaged Navier–Stokes solver with sediment transport and bed evolution. The model is evaluated against laboratory measurements for bare and vegetated beach profiles under regular erosive waves. title: The Growing Role of Evaporative Demand in Driving Record‐Breaking Droughts in the Amazon Basin
abstract: Abstract Amazon droughts have historically been driven by precipitation deficits, but recent escalating drought events highlight a regime shift toward “hot droughts.” By decomposing historical drought drivers (1979–2024), we show that rising evaporative demand (represented by potential evapotranspiration, PET) now acts as a primary driver of drought intensification. title: Hydro-morphological investigations on local scour around inclined piles under wave conditions
abstract: Scouring is a problem that should be considered while designing bridges; scour around inclined piles in the presence of waves has rarely been researched. However, in reality, many inclined braces are used for aesthetic reasons, which alters the flow properties depending on their exposure to the flow field. The purpose of this work is to numerically examine the flow behavior and local scour evolution around inclined piles downstream under wave conditions. title: Long-term climatology of vertical profiles of polarimetric variables and ice-microphysical retrievals at X-band – Part 1: Radar calibration
abstract: Abstract. In a two-part series of papers, a climatology of quasi-vertical profiles (QVPs) of polarimetric variables and ice-microphysical retrievals such as ice water content, total number concentration and mean volume diameter is presented. QVPs are generated from plan position indicator scans at 18° elevation angle measured with the X-band radar located in the city of Bonn in western Germany between 2013 and 2023. title: Global climate impact of land-surface change driven by radiative effects
abstract: Abstract A robust proportionality between radiative forcing and global-mean temperature has been established for most climate drivers. However, land-surface changes are considered an exception due to their potential to alter surface hydrology, introducing non-radiative effects that may rival those from surface albedo changes. title: Long‐Term Fish Assemblage Responses to Instream Restoration in Boreal Streams: Insights From a 24‐Year BACI Study
abstract: ABSTRACT Freshwater ecosystems are increasingly threatened by human activities and climate change, emphasizing the need for effective habitat restoration supported by long‐term monitoring. We examined fish species responses to instream restoration in six boreal streams in northern Finland over a 24‐year period (1999–2022) using a Before–After–Control–Impact (BACI) design, including 3 years before and 21 years after restoration. title: A State‐of‐the‐Art Study of Vortex‐Excited Vibration Problems in Large‐Span Flat Steel Box Girder Bridges
abstract: ABSTRACT Windborne vibration of large‐span bridges occurs from time to time, especially the abnormal windborne vibration of urban bridges, which often causes public panic. The paper consists of four parts. Specifically, the first part analyzes the wind challenges of large‐span bridges, including the formation mechanism of wind‐induced vibration disaster of large‐span bridges and typical cases, as well as the limitations of the current wind design codes. title: Chemical characterization and source apportionment of PM 10 in Belgrade, Serbia: influence of local and regional anthropogenic and natural sources
abstract: Abstract. Substantial efforts and improvements in air quality across Europe lowered levels of air pollutants including particulate matter (PM) in the last decades. However, significant proportion of the European population still lives in areas exceeding WHO recommendations, especially in Northern Italy, Balkans and Eastern Europe, including Serbia. abstract: Abstract. Uncertainties in natural systems are pervasive, varied, and unavoidable due to inherent open system complexity and limited knowledge. Therefore, the evolution of a natural system cannot be predicted deterministically and probabilistic forecasts are commonly used to account for these uncertainties. title: Integrating urban air mobility, unmanned aerial systems, and eVTOL in the low-altitude economy: Bibliometric analysis of research hotspots and development trends
abstract: The low-altitude economy (LAE) has rapidly developed in recent years, driven by technological innovation, policy support, and market demand, offering a transformative solution to urban traffic congestion and promoting environmental and energy-saving benefits. However, in the context of LAE, a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of key topics such as urban air mobility (UAM), unmanned aerial systems (UAS), and electric vertical takeoff and landing (eVTOL) technologies remains incomplete and lacks systematic exploration. title: Diverse coupling between climate change, socio-economic factors and climate potential productivity in Africa
abstract: Africa’s accelerating climate warming has rendered its climate potential productivity (CPP) increasingly vulnerable, raising global concerns over biodiversity, water resources, and food security. Understanding the long‑term evolution of CPP and its driving mechanisms has therefore become an urgent research priority. This study analyses the spatiotemporal patterns and correlates of CPP across Africa, using the Thornthwaite Memorial model in combination with trend detection, correlation, and econometric analyses. title: Macroscopic and mesoscopic mechanical behavior of the interface between piles and unsaturated sand under vertical cyclic loading
abstract: Understanding the degradation of pile bearing capacity under vertical cyclic loading requires an in-depth investigation of the pile–unsaturated sand interface. abstract: Planning a green hydrogen project couples siting, generation, electrolysis, storage, conversion and cost decisions that are usually assessed in separate tools. This paper presents an integrated web-based decision-support platform for the planning and analysis of green hydrogen value chains. abstract: The "Karakoram Anomaly" - the atypical stability of glaciers in a warming climate-has introduced considerable uncertainty into projections of regional water resources. abstract: Climate change has increased the need for effective educational approaches that can promote climate-related awareness and environmentally responsible behaviors. This study investigates the effects of a passive 360-degree virtual reality educational intervention on climate change awareness and operational water consumption in a real industrial setting. abstract: Shale diagenesis is a complex geochemical process governed by the coupled evolution of minerals, organic matter, and fluids during burial. abstract: Abstract Flood behavior is characterized by complex spatial and temporal interdependencies that have been often overlooked in hazard and risk assessment, where traditional approaches have been either assuming independence across large regions or imposing uniform return periods within catchments. abstract: Global seafood production generates millions of tonnes of nutrient-rich processing side-streams that remain underutilised despite their potential as sustainable sources of high-value compounds and renewable resources. This review critically examines emerging engineering strategies for transforming seafood residues into value-added products within the framework of the blue circular economy. abstract: ABSTRACT Power systems with high shares of variable renewable energy increasingly face balancing challenges that extend beyond intraday variability to multiday shortages, seasonal mismatch, resource adequacy and system resilience. Salt cavern hydrogen storage (SCHS) has emerged as a promising underground hydrogen storage option for renewable‐dominated smart energy systems. abstract: Aerosol optical depth (AOD) is a core indicator for quantifying atmospheric pollution, and its spatiotemporal variation is strongly influenced by meteorological factors, including water vapor, a critical driver of atmospheric moisture transport and energy balance. To investigate the role of water vapor in AOD modeling, this study integrates global navigation satellite system (GNSS), precipitable water vapor (PWV), and ERA5 meteorological data to develop a high-resolution spatiotemporal AOD model over Europe, at 0.25° spatial and 1-hour temporal resolution. abstract: This study aims to systematically analyze and evaluate the fault sealing properties in the Zhuhai Formation of the Pearl River Estuary Basin using an in-situ stress calculation model. By constructing an in-situ stress calculation model, the distribution characteristics of in-situ stress are analyzed, and a fault sealing evaluation index system is established. abstract: Fault diagnosis in safety–critical industrial infrastructure is often hindered by the data scarcity of catastrophic failures and subjective uncertainty inherent in domain knowledge. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a novel Hybrid Knowledge-Data Fusion method via a HW-TOPSIS-FTA-FBN model. abstract: A variety of chemical and dynamical processes in the troposphere and stratosphere affect tropical total column ozone (TCO), the net effect of which may cause changes in surface UV radiation and impact human and ecosystem health. We use dynamical linear modeling to estimate changes in tropical TCO and partial column ozone (PCO) in the troposphere and three stratospheric layers to assess agreement between satellite composites and chemistry-climate model simulations from two multi-model experiments (CCMI-1 and CCMI-2022). title: Atmospheric Circulation Drives Dry‐to‐Wet Abrupt Alternation in the Lancang–Mekong River Basin
abstract: Abstract The Lancang–Mekong River Basin (LMRB), a crucial transboundary region that sustains millions of people across Southeast Asia, faces growing threats from compound hydrological extremes under climate change. Among them, dry‐to‐wet abrupt alternation (DWAA) is particularly critical, intensifying risks to agriculture and water security. abstract: This study investigates how alternative blade-root and blade-tip loss corrections influence steady aerodynamic predictions for a 200-kW horizontal-axis wind turbine (HAWT) within a Blade Element Momentum (BEM) framework. A controlled comparison is performed using theoretical, semi-empirical, and performance-based loss formulations and three related RISØ-A1 blade configurations. title: A long-term dataset of tropical cyclone radius of maximum wind in the Western North Pacific Based on a Bayesian consensus of multiple estimates
abstract: Abstract The radius of maximum wind (RMW) is one of the key parameters for characterizing the structure of tropical cyclones (TCs). Although multiple methods have been developed to estimate the RMW, their estimates can sometimes differ substantially and are not always available, making it difficult to construct a comprehensive long-term RMW dataset. abstract: Recent urbanization and overexploitation have significantly degraded groundwater quality in the shallow unconfined aquifer in Barjisiyah. The study area is located within the discharge area and is exposed to natural salinization from the underlying layer and anthropogenic sources with limited rainfall recharge. abstract: Climate conditions can significantly affect plant dormancy and growing season, impacting crop development and its productivity. Temperature is considered the primary driver of grapevine phenology, with endodormancy and ecodormancy largely regulated by chilling and forcing accumulations, respectively. title: UTILIZATION OF BRACKISH WATER IN AGRICULTURE: POTENTIALS, CHALLENGES, AND MANAGEMENT
abstract: Brackish water offers compelling opportunities for agricultural use, especially in regions experiencing water scarcity and limited freshwater resources. However, its utilization requires careful supervision, considering factors such as crop salinity tolerance and soil composition to prevent adverse effects. abstract: ABSTRACT Lifetime estimation regarding leading‐edge erosion of wind turbine blades involves a series of mathematical and statistical procedures, including regression fitting, tolerance interval formulation, and weathering modeling approaches. This work investigates the intermediate steps in the fatigue assessment process and the associated sources of variability, using data from a whirling arm rain erosion test (RET) machine, time‐series liquid precipitation and wind data from two sites, and the IEA reference 15 MW wind turbine. abstract: Abstract Recent climate change is most clearly manifested in rising global temperatures, with regionally amplified warming observed in Central Europe, including its mountainous areas. This study analyses trends in mean annual and seasonal air temperatures and evaluates the influence of atmospheric circulation on temperature extremes in Central European mountains during 1961–2025, comparing the periods 1961–1990 and 1991–2025. abstract: Bridgmanite, the main mineralogical phase in the Earth's lower mantle, is intrinsically anisotropic and may therefore generate seismic anisotropy in actively-deforming regions, particularly subduction zones. abstract: Abstract. Heat has emerged as a major public health concern. abstract: Urban safety governance is critical for China’s sustainable urbanization. abstract: Climate change and air pollution affect nearly every major organ system, altering both the presentation of disease and patient responses to pharmaceutical treatments. abstract: Wind disturbances at low altitudes increase energy consumption and safety risks for multirotor unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) in densely built urban environments. High-fidelity computational fluid dynamics (CFD) is too expensive for online path planning, while threshold methods represent hazardous regions as binary no-fly zones. abstract: Abstract Subseasonal-to-seasonal precipitation forecasts are highly relevant for a wide range of practical applications and risk management, but their skill decreases substantially at longer lead times. title: Spatiotemporal characteristics of vegetation responses to compound drought and heatwave events in Central Asia
abstract: With climate warming intensifying, compound drought and heatwave (CDHW) events have become more frequent and intense in arid Central Asia, severely affecting vegetation growth. abstract: This research examines how city images of Istanbul’s Historic Peninsula are evolving with artificial intelligence and expanding user-generated content. abstract: This study integrates AMS 14C dating of 12 plant specimens, Bayesian modeling, and Tibetan texts to establish the first high-resolution construction chronology for key structures of the Guge ancient city in western Tibet. abstract: La actual pérdida de la biodiversidad demanda ciudadanos capaces de comprender y actuar frente a problemas ambientales complejos, por lo que es necesario formarlos en dicho sentido desde edades tempranas. title: Twenty years of Kilimanjaro observations across 5000 m reveal tropical elevation-dependent warming under clear-sky conditions
abstract: Abstract Mountain regions are experiencing rapid climate change. However, temperature trends along elevation gradients remain poorly understood in the tropics, where long-term high-elevation air temperature ( T air ) observations are sparse. Here, we examine elevation-dependent warming (EDW) on Mount Kilimanjaro by combining a unique long-term in situ T air transect with Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS) land-surface temperature (LST), surface and topographic datasets. abstract: Implicit information on land use conflicts in territorial spatial planning texts directly affects the coordination and implementability of planning schemes. abstract: Abstract. The flash flooding across Central Texas on July 4th, 2025, caused more than 130 fatalities and property losses exceeding 20 billion dollars. abstract: Lack of comprehensive evaluations of spatial thermal comfort parameters across Iraq remains a concern as the risks of excessive heat and climate change increase. abstract: The hydrological systems of watersheds are increasingly affected by climate change, resulting in altered rainfall patterns, more intense droughts, and disrupted runoff. Although recent studies in Iraq have applied statistical downscaling and CMIP6 projections to selected watersheds and water-resource systems, province-scale assessments of how seasonal temperature and precipitation classes may spatially redistribute across Anbar Province under multi-model CMIP6 scenarios remain limited. abstract: The rheological behavior of paste, particularly regarding pumpability and in-situ dispersion, is critical for the safe and efficient disposal of mine tailings using paste technology. title: Self-Adaptive Edge-Intelligent IoT Framework for Real-Time Water Quality Monitoring and Predictive Control
abstract: Monitoring water quality is important for environmental safety and public health in places with fast-changing or unstable water conditions. Conventional monitoring approaches are slow to respond, not scalable, and lack real-time decision-making ability. To address these limitations, a research framework is proposed based on an intelligent edge-IoT architecture for real-time monitoring and assessment of water quality parameters. abstract: Rapid urbanization and the expansion of Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) in tropical megacities often overlook the microclimatic experience of pedestrians, leading to severe Urban Heat Island (UHI) effects and thermal discomfort. This study introduces and computationally evaluates the Bioclimatic Transit-Infill Housing (BTIH) concept, a medium-density housing model with minimum parking, located at the Blok A Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) station in Jakarta, Indonesia. abstract: Abstract The Elaine Dorothy Cu-Au deposit, located in the Mary Kathleen Domain of the Mount Isa Inlier, Australia, records the interaction of Paleoproterozoic skarn metasomatism, fluid evolution, and deformation. abstract: Abstract Driven by the global energy transition and China's dual-carbon goals, oil and gas field development faces challenges in achieving sustainable development. Oilfield-geothermal co-development (OGC) offers a pathway for revitalizing mature oilfields and supplying low-carbon energy. abstract: The digital documentation of riverside cliff grottoes has long been hindered by acquisition blind spots caused by steep terrain and irregular cliff faces. abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding sex‐specific parental roles is critical for interpreting reproductive strategies in long‐lived, monogamous birds with low fecundity. title: Research on thermodynamic performance of a gas-steam combined cycle with rotating detonation combustion
abstract: Conventional gas-steam combined cycles are constrained by the substantial irreversibility of constant-pressure combustion, whereas integrating a rotating detonation combustor (RDC) may lower the turbine exhaust temperature and thereby impair the steam bottoming cycle. In this study, a thermodynamic model of a methane-fueled RDC-based gas-steam combined cycle is developed and compared with a conventional constant-pressure-combustion combined cycle. title: Using climate models in climate assessments: a Bayesian perspective
abstract: Outputs from complex Earth system models (ESMs) participating in the Coupled Model Intercomparison Project (CMIP) are a major source of information for policy-relevant assessments of climate change. The way we view and interpret the CMIP archive shapes our understanding of the real world, yet many assessments present analysis choices only implicitly. abstract: Abstract. Historical text sources represent a central, yet methodologically challenging basis for the reconstruction of convective weather events. This study examines the extent to which historical reports on thunderstorms and hailstorms contain reliable climatological information, despite heterogeneous sources, varying degrees of detail and linguistic diversity. abstract: Abstract. Accurate estimation of regional-scale terrestrial carbon budgets is of great importance but remains challenging. With particular advantages, the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks method shows potential in improving regional carbon budget upscaling estimations. Here, based on LSTM, we upscale regional net ecosystem carbon exchange (NEE) with available flux tower measurements and satellite land surface observations in North America. abstract: The structural integrity of aging high-rise concrete infrastructure requires frequent, high-precision inspections, yet traditional manual methods remain heavily reliant on labor-intensive, costly, and inherently dangerous techniques such as gondolas or rope access. This research aims to address these critical industry challenges by developing an innovative, autonomous cyber-physical framework that integrates Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) tactile scanning with advanced Vision-Language AI Models (VLM). title: Characterizing lightning NO x production in the Ebro Valley with meteosat 12 LI and LMA observations
abstract: Abstract. Lightning is one of the main sources of NOₓ in the Earth’s atmosphere, yet there is considerable variability in NOₓ production during thunderstorms. title: Non-monotonic response of net dust deposition kinetics to low wind speeds
abstract: Abstract. Dry deposition is a major sink for mineral dust, yet its behavior under weak winds remains poorly constrained and is often parameterized monotonically with wind speed.
