title: RISK-BASED INSPECTION AND QUALITY CONTROL OF ELECTRICAL INFRASTRUCTURE
abstract: Electrical infrastructure in oil, gas and industrial facilities is exposed to ageing, variable loading, harsh environments, construction defects, maintenance backlogs and operational change. Conventional inspection programmes often apply fixed intervals to broad equipment classes, even though failure probability and consequence differ substantially between assets. abstract: Accurate estimation of the rainfall erosivity factor (R-factor) is fundamental for soil erosion prediction and informed land conservation. This study provides a comprehensive review of the historical evolution and current status of R-factor estimation, ranging from simplified empirical equations to complex process-based models. abstract: This study investigates a novel solar-driven hybrid desalination system integrating Mechanical Vapor Compression (MVC) and Thermal Vapor Compression (TVC) cycles. The way in which the extreme event is defined has a major influence on the attribution result. A frequently overlooked aspect concerns the temporal dependence of extremes. abstract: This study presents a synthetic proof-of-concept surrogate-assisted simulation–optimisation framework for identifying potentially mineralised locations using groundwater copper-isotope observations. title: Wind gusts prediction using multivariate time series classification
abstract: Wind speed intermittency is a key challenge for integrating wind energy into the energy mix. Accurate wind power forecasting in wind farms is crucial for mitigating this issue. A major source of uncertainty in nowcasting and short-term wind power prediction arises from wind gusts. abstract: This study presents a sensitivity based optimal control framework for enhancing solid particle transport in petroleum pipelines. A nonlinear dynamic model is developed to describe particle velocity evolution under the effects of drag force, mixture density, particle size, and bounded ﬂow disturbances. abstract: Abstract Intraplate volcanism in Northeast Asia, located in a distant back‐arc setting, challenges conventional models of mantle convection and volatile cycling. abstract: Abstract Land surface models are fundamental for simulating coupled carbon, water and energy exchanges in Earth system models, yet their performance remains poorly constrained across Africa's diverse hydroclimatic gradients. abstract: Abstract High seismic velocity keels extending to depths greater than 200 km underlie the oldest parts of continents, the Precambrian cratons. These keels have probably been formed early in Earth’s history, and the preservation of these deep, cold, and highly viscous roots in a convective mantle remains enigmatic. abstract: Abstract. There are numerous subglacial lakes in Antarctica, typically covered by thick ice sheets. title: A prototype multi-hazard early warning system integrating flood and landslide forecasting: application in the upper Garonne River Basin
abstract: Multi-Hazard Early Warning Systems (MHEWS) are essential for disaster risk management, yet operational implementation remains limited by challenges in hazard integration, forecast uncertainty, and computational requirements. This study develops and evaluates a fast and lightweight prototype MHEWS integrating fluvial flooding and shallow landslide forecasting. abstract: Polymer additive manufacturing (AM) has rapidly grown from a prototyping technology to a manufacturing platform that can fabricate complex geometries, lightweight structures, customized products, and multifunctional components in a broad spectrum of industries. abstract: ABSTRACT The study examines how hard and soft power influence the organizational effectiveness of State corporations (SCs) in Kenya, a public‐sector context characterized by complex political dynamics and competing interests. abstract: High-resolution soil moisture (SM) information is essential for hydrological, agricultural and climate studies. abstract: The increasing adoption of portable and wearable audio devices is accelerating the use of piezoelectric actuators as alternatives to conventional dynamic speakers, enabled by their ultra-thin, lightweight factor, low power consumption, and ability to transform non-traditional surfaces into efficient sound-radiating elements. abstract: Abstract Urbanisation fundamentally alters the sensory landscape, creating novel acoustic environments where anthropogenic noise acts as a rigorous filter on wildlife communities. abstract: Climate oscillations are intrinsically out-of-equilibrium phenomena, yet the connection between their predictability and nonequilibrium thermodynamic properties remains unexplored. We develop a coarse-grained stochastic thermodynamic framework for Ornstein-Uhlenbeck (OU) processes and apply this framework to climate data via linear inverse models (LIMs), linking predictability, entropy production, dynamical activity, and path action. title: Similar evapotranspiration responses mask contrasting modes of water access during drought in California
abstract: Atmospheric warming raises evaporative demand, but actual evapotranspiration (ETa) may track demand or decouple under water limitation. Here, we quantified demand-tracking ability from regression slopes relating deseasonalized ETa and reference evapotranspiration (ETo) anomalies across California during 2008-2024. Forests and croplands retained similar positive tracking under severe drought, whereas grasslands and shrublands showed weak or negative responses. title: A Two-Element Capsule Antenna for Near-Field Polarization MIMO in Wireless Capsule Endoscopy
abstract: Multiple-Input-Multiple-Output (MIMO) technology is considered to be a viable method for spectral efficiency and data rate enhancement in wireless communications. This article presents a two-element capsule antenna with orthogonal current distributions for polarization multiplexing in a wireless capsule endoscopy (WCE) application at 915 MHz. The proposed antenna was evaluated in a MIMO link where it served as the transmitter and an existing on-body antenna was the receiver. title: Two-way actuator-line coupling of a geometrically exact finite-volume beam with incompressible and free-surface flow
abstract: Slender flexible structures such as mooring lines, aquaculture netting, and aquatic vegetation are too thin to be resolved economically by a body-fitted mesh, yet they exchange momentum with the flow in both directions. This paper presents a finite volume actuator-line formulation for the fluid--structure interaction of such structures, in which a geometrically exact Simo--Reissner beam, discretised by cell-centred finite volumes, is coupled two-way to an incompressible finite volume flow solver through conservative, parallel-consistent transfer operators. title: Exploiting UAV Attitude for Covert Communications: Dynamics-Consistent Trajectory-Attitude Co-Design
abstract: Existing trajectory designs for covert communications with uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs) typically rely on point-mass kinematics, which overlook the inherent coupling between flight maneuvers and antenna orientation. Motivated by recent studies linking UAV acceleration to attitude, we investigate dynamics-consistent trajectory and attitude co-design for rotary-wing UAV covert communications. title: Polarforming for MIMO Covert Communications
abstract: Covert communication conceals wireless transmission activity, but conventional multi-antenna designs rely mainly on spatial beamforming and can be constrained by limited spatial degrees of freedom. This paper investigates polarization-reconfigurable antenna (PRA)-aided multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) covert communication, where Alice and Bob perform transmit and receive polarforming, respectively, and Willie uses a vertically polarized antenna for radiometric detection. title: Interplay between Excitability and Noise in Analog Spiking Neurons
abstract: A spiking neuron is a dynamical system exhibiting a limit cycle (a spike) when subject to sufficiently excitatory input. Famous neuroscience experiments by Bryant and Segundo as well as Mainen and Sejnowski revealed that the spike times of some biological neurons are more reliable when subject to time-varying stimuli compared to constant ones. Provided with an industrial physics-based transient noise SPICE simulation framework compatible with foundry transistor compact models, we have demonstrated similar behaviours for a CMOS analog spiking neuron designed for neuromorphic computing hardware

title: Spatial patterning and selection: How the environment shapes molecular complexity
abstract: Assembly theory predicts that a distinguishing signature of life is its ability to produce complex molecules in abundance, opening new possibilities for life detection. Experimental validation of this approach has so far relied on abiotic controls like meteoritic material, or simple, well-mixed chemical systems. However, decades of research in self-organization have shown that spatial patterning can foster dynamical complexity. title: Molecular Structure Effects in Low-Lying $P$-wave Bottom-Strange Meson Spectrum
abstract: Recently, the LHCb Collaboration reported a new narrow bottom-strange meson, $B_{s0}^*(5700)$ with mass $M= (5698.9 \pm 1.5 \pm 0.6)$~MeV, width $Γ<9.8$~MeV, and spin-parity $J^P=0^+$ in the $B_s^0π^0$ invariant-mass spectrum. title: Inclined surfaces bias bacterial swarming expansion and edge organization
abstract: Bacterial swarming is the collective expansion of dense populations of motile cells across hydrated soft surfaces, yet gravity is usually treated as a fixed background condition in standard horizontal assays. We used surface inclination to examine how agar-surface orientation relative to gravity affects the expansion of Enterobacter sp. SM3 swarms. title: Science of Nuclear Fusion: Insights and Ideas
abstract: Advances in several physics domains open up novel paths to smaller scale, higher energy density opportunities to advance small systems for nuclear fusion. Here we survey both legacy and several novel “table-top” approaches which attract current interest. We furthermore address a few related practical and challenging nuclear science topics arising in the context of magnetic confinement and inertial confinement fusion. title: WEEVIL: design and commissioning of an ice-sublimation chamber and a cryogenic submillimeter radiometer for studying rarefied gas plumes
abstract: We present WEEVIL (WatEr Emission of Vapor from Ice in the Laboratory), an experimental facility developed to study ice sublimation under laboratory conditions to support observations of comets and icy moons. The setup combines a submillimeter heterodyne radiometer and a high-vacuum cryogenic chamber, enabling spatially and temporally resolved monitoring of gas plumes formed during ice sublimation under controlled laboratory conditions. title: Entropy-Stable and Well-Balanced Discontinuous Galerkin Methods for the Compressible Euler Equations in Vector-Invariant Form
abstract: We develop structure-preserving methods for the compressible Euler equations with gravity in vector-invariant form and potential temperature as a prognostic variable within the flux-differencing discontinuous Galerkin spectral element method (DGSEM) framework. By discretizing the nonconservative terms as symmetric and antisymmetric products, we derive two-point numerical fluxes that conserve both the thermodynamic entropy and the total energy. title: Discrete Boltzmann model at Burnett level for compressible multicomponent flows under external forces
abstract: A discrete Boltzmann model at the Burnett level is established to investigate compressible multicomponent flows with external forces. A set of 25 discrete velocities is designed to provide high isotropy and numerical stability. Both the equilibrium discrete function and the force term are constructed using a moment-matching approach, ensuring that 25 independent kinetic moments are accurately recovered. title: Generalised Mixing-Plane Method for Compressible Reacting-Mixture Flows in Steady Multiphysics Turbomachinery Simulations
abstract: The mixing-plane method plays a pivotal role in steady simulations of multiple turbomachinery components. With advances in computational power, a whole-engine gas turbine simulation is no longer an elusive approach. However, whole-engine simulations require simultaneous coupling of the compressor, turbine and combustor. A key challenge is that the working fluid after the combustor can no longer be treated as a perfect gas, since the combustion introduces composition variations and combustion products. title: Contact lens with stretchable distributed-feedback laser for intraocular pressure monitoring
abstract: Continuous monitoring of intraocular pressure (IOP) is essential for the diagnosis and management of glaucoma, yet existing clinical methods rely on intermittent in-clinic measurements that miss critical diurnal fluctuations. Smart contact lenses are an attractive platform for continuous IOP tracking, and optical strain sensors are particularly promising thanks to their high sensitivity and natural readout. title: Strategic Environmental Assessment for the Ukrainian Community Development Strategies: European Union Practice
abstract: Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA) is an important tool for integrating environmental considerations into territorial planning and sustainable development. This study compares SEA practices in the United Kingdom, Poland, Romania, and Ukraine to identify best European practices and formulate recommendations for Ukraine. The study used a comparative approach based on analysis of legal frameworks, consultation systems, and official SEA reports. title: A proposed methodology for defining the criteria of ‘Good Environmental Status’ for artificial light at night in marine waters
abstract: There is now a growing recognition internationally that the impacts of Artificial Light at Night (ALAN) on marine biodiversity require regulation. How ALAN should be regulated and what constitutes ‘Good Environmental Status’ (GES) for underwater ALAN remain open questions that if resolved would accelerate the integration of ALAN management into existing policy instruments. title: DNA-based monitoring uncovers contrasting salinity-driven diversity patterns of bacterial and protist plankton in the Baltic Sea area
abstract: Salinity has been identified as a primary factor structuring community composition in global diversity assessments of free-living bacteria in non-extreme environments. It remains unknown whether the same is true for protists. Moreover, changes in alpha diversity of both bacteria and protists across the brackish salinity gradient remain elusive. Here, we analyzed protist and bacterial diversity using DNA metabarcoding across 398 surface water samples synchronized with national monitoring of the Baltic Sea and the Kattegat-Skagerrak. title: Ocean changes and the impacts in the Polar Regions
abstract: Covering about 20 % of the global ocean, the polar ocean areas are among the most sensitive regions of the Earth climate system, where today climate change is reshaping processes that influence global circulation, sea level, and climate far beyond the poles. Here, we develop an ocean narrative that integrates physical, ecological, and societal indicators, to illustrate polar ocean change. title: Patterns and environmental drivers of marine annelid distribution in the Arctic Ocean
abstract: The Arctic Ocean (AO) is experiencing declining sea ice extent and thickness and increasing sea surface temperatures, with cascading consequences for the entire ecosystem. Here, we compiled all available occurrence records of marine Annelida from the Ocean Biodiversity Information System (OBIS) and the Global Biodiversity Information Facility (GIF) and analyzed the number of records, the number of species, and expected species richness (ES15 and ES50) in relation to depth, ecoregion, ca. 12,500 km 2 hexagonal cell and associated them with environmental drivers. title: On the Fidelity of Oxygen Isotope‐Based Sea Level Reconstructions: A Case Study of Marine Isotope Stage 3
abstract: Abstract Although foraminiferal oxygen isotope records (δ 18 O F ) have long been used to develop time‐continuous estimates of past global ice volume, growing evidence indicates that the ice volume and temperature contributions to δ 18 O F diverge considerably over the last glacial cycle. title: Hidden subsurface suspended sediment export from Greenland's marine‐terminating glaciers
abstract: Abstract Runoff and calved ice volumes from the Greenland Ice Sheet are well constrained, but quantifying the associated suspended sediment flux remains challenging. Here we present near‐terminus observations from three glacierized fjords in southeast Greenland, combining full‐depth turbidity profiles and current velocity from summer 2024 to evaluate sediment export. title: Mathematical Modelling of the Black Sea Coastline Considering its Fractal Structure and Grid Generation
abstract: Introduction . The coastline of a reservoir is a complex natural object, which geometry has irregularity and signs of selfsimilarity, and the length depends on the scale of measurement. Despite the widespread study of its fractal properties, the transition to a digital representation of the coastline is a complex procedure and is a current topic of research. title: Ocean acidification pushes Mediterranean marine calcifiers toward a tipping point
abstract: Abstract The increasing emission of carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) is altering seawater chemistry, lowering ocean pH and threatening marine biodiversity. Predicting how marine biota will be adversely affected by ocean acidification (OA) remains a key challenge. Here, we document that functional morphological traits offer a more robust metric of calcifier sensitivity to OA than taxonomic diversity alone. title: Documented technology adoption in environmental impact assessment: a mixed-methods study of adoption–perception gaps in Korea
abstract: Despite rapid advances in AI, big data analytics, GIS, real-time monitoring, and predictive modeling, their integration into environmental impact assessment (EIA) practice remains poorly documented. This study employs a sequential explanatory mixed-methods design to examine documented technology adoption in Korean EIA and Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA). abstract: E-commerce in emerging and fragile markets often develops faster than the physical logistics systems required to support reliable and efficient order fulfillment. This study develops an integrated geographic information system (GIS) and multi-criteria decision-making framework for evaluating candidate cities for e-commerce fulfillment hubs in Libya. title: Spatial variability in seawater chemistry across an intertidal mangrove–coral reef boundary
abstract: Context Edge effects at habitat boundaries can generate strong physicochemical gradients that structure coastal ecosystems. Although environmental gradients within coexisting mangrove–coral habitats are well documented, spatial variability in seawater chemistry across intertidal mangrove–reef boundaries remains under-characterised. abstract: This paper provides an overview of global GIS education and evaluates geospatial education in Uzbekistan on a regional level. An integrated approach based on combining bibliometric analysis and thematic interpretation was used to explore 325 articles listed in Scopus and Web of Science databases between 2016 and 2025. title: Overlooked contribution of organic alkalinity in Arctic Ocean margins biases ocean acidification estimates
abstract: Organic alkalinity has been recognized as a potentially substantial fraction of total alkalinity in coastal waters. title: SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT FOR ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION IN BANGLADESH: CHALLENGES AND OPPORTUNITIES
abstract: Bangladesh exemplifies a central paradox of sustainable development: how to maintain rapid economic and social progress without undermining the ecological systems upon which development depends. This paper critically examines Bangladesh's environmental governance architecture, the major barriers to its effective implementation, and opportunities for achieving a just green transition. abstract: Introduction. The article presents the findings of a study aimed at analyzing the experience of hydrocarbon extraction in hard-to-reach marine and coastal areas of the Arctic. The Arctic zone, which has significant hydrocarbon reserves, is a promising, but meanwhile extremely difficult region for oil production, given that the rate of glacier melting is increasing. title: Impacts of Coastal Infrastructure Upgrades on the Endangered Marine Alga Nereia lophocladia
abstract: ABSTRACT Coastal protection infrastructure is routinely upgraded to address structural degradation and rising sea levels. Such work can have unintended ecological impacts depending on the habitats and species involved, as well as the environmental mitigations undertaken. Here, we completed an 8‐year assessment of the impact of a breakwater upgrade at Coffs Harbour (Australia) on the abundance and size of the endangered marine brown alga Nereia lophocladia . title: A GIS-based approach for assessing island landscape visual character: Reciprocal land–sea visual characterization in the Zhoushan Archipelago, China
abstract: Coastal tourism, port expansion, and land reclamation are intensifying pressures on island landscapes, highlighting the need for systematic visual assessment to support sustainable planning and management. To address this need, this study develops a GIS-based approach for the Zhoushan Archipelago that uses character mapping as the spatial organizing basis and examines reciprocal land–sea viewing conditions, from the sea toward land and from land toward the sea, across foreground and background zones. title: Comparing Strava and survey-based data for coastal recreation accounting
abstract: Coastal zones provide recreational ecosystem services across land and sea, yet spatial data for ecosystem accounting is limited. We compared Strava activity data with survey-based public participation GIS (PPGIS) data across the Oslofjord, Norway, to assess spatial and sociodemographic biases in crowdsourced recreation accounting. abstract: Abstract The Greenland and Antarctic ice sheets exhibit high variability in flow speed, over multiple orders of magnitude. This flow integrates forcings from complex, multi-scale and spatially heterogeneous pressure gradient and friction fields into smooth and continuous flow fields, over a finite scale known as the longitudinal coupling length (LCL). title: Cardiac responses to underwater sound playback in juvenile green and loggerhead sea turtles: an exploratory biologging study
abstract: Anthropogenic underwater noise is an increasing concern in marine environments, yet physiological responses of sea turtles remain poorly understood. We examined cardiac responses to underwater sound playback in three juvenile green turtles (Chelonia mydas) and four juvenile loggerhead turtles (Caretta caretta) maintained after incidental capture. abstract: Microbial consortia are essential for the degradation of complex hydrocarbon mixtures in coastal environments, yet the functional basis of consortium performance rarely resolved at strain level. title: Multilocus phylogeny and historical biogeography of the pill millipede genus Rhopalomeris (Diplopoda, Glomerida) in Thailand
abstract: Abstract Southeast Asia is widely recognized as a global biodiversity hotspot with a complex geological history and high species richness across multiple taxa. The pill millipede genus Rhopalomeris Verhoeff, 1906 has received increasing taxonomic attention in recent years, with several new species described, particularly from western Southeast Asia, including Thailand and Myanmar. title: Status of Sea Bamboo (Isis hippuris Linnaeus, 1758) in Bunaken National Park, North Sulawesi, Indonesia
abstract: Isis hippuris Linnaeus, 1758, commonly known as sea bamboo, is a gorgonian octocoral of the family Isididae that plays a vital structural and ecological role in coral reef ecosystems. It is also recognised for producing unique bioactive secondary metabolites, particularly hippuristanol, which exhibits potent antiviral and cytotoxic properties. Despite its conservation and pharmacological importance, baseline demographic data for I. hippuris across North Sulawesi marine protected areas remain scarce. abstract: Abstract Particle size and physical properties such as stiffness and adhesiveness affect sinking velocity and flux in the ocean, yet conventional two‐dimensional measurements lack accuracy and mechanical information. In this study, we applied atomic force microscopy (AFM) to quantify three‐dimensional size and physical properties of marine particles. title: Silicate accumulation in taxonomically diverse seaweeds: morphology, uptake, visualization and environmental responses
abstract: Abstract Silicon is required by some microalgae but use and accumulation by seaweeds has been quantified in few taxa. This study aimed to examine biogenic Si (bSi) in taxonomically and morphologically diverse seaweeds, measure Si uptake rates, assess the effects of environmental conditions on bSi, and visualize Si within seaweed tissues. bSi was determined in 57 seaweed taxa across 17 taxonomic orders collected around Tasmania, Australia. title: Spatial disparities in surf-resource sustainability: Implications for coastal policy and marine education in Taiwan
abstract: This study situates global surf sustainability within the Taiwanese context, where recreational surfing has developed since the 1980s and expanded internationally after 2010, yet region-wide assessments of surf-resource sustainability remain limited. Little is known about how sustainability conditions vary across Taiwan’s coastal regions, which sustainability dimensions contribute most strongly to these disparities, and what implications such patterns have for coastal governance and marine education policy. title: An Ecosystem-Based Marine Spatial Planning Approach for Sustainable Natural Resources Management in the Bangladesh Delta
abstract: Despite the establishment of maritime boundaries with Myanmar (2012) and India (2014), which secured sovereign rights over approximately 118,813 km² of the Bay of Bengal, marine space is still managed on a sector-by-sector basis, and no marine spatial plan has been prepared. This study identifies significant ecological, economic, and cultural areas within Bangladesh's maritime zone, and proposes a framework for the blue economy and develops an ecosystem-based model of marine spatial planning (MSP). title: Combined effects of elevated temperature and fluoxetine exposure on early development of the sea urchin Paracentrotus lividus
abstract: Temperature rise associated with climate change increases the vulnerability of coastal species, which are also exposed to pharmaceuticals. We investigated the effects of thermal stress and fluoxetine (FLX), alone and in combination, on early developmental stages of the sea urchin Paracentrotus lividus, a key coastal species. Gametes, zygotes and embryos were exposed to ambient (18°C) and near-future projections (21°C, 24°C) to identify the most sensitive developmental stage to warming. abstract: Extreme weather occurrences, particularly in densely populated coastal places like India, cause loss and devastation, hindering disaster preparedness and long-term viability of vulnerable populations. Research shows that hybrid models, such as Bayesian Networks and Coastal Vulnerability frameworks, outperform traditional methods for measuring coastal vulnerability to Sea Level Rise (SLR). title: ANOVATS: a subsampling-based test to detect differences among short time series in marine studies
abstract: Assessing marine ecosystems is important for understanding the impacts of climate change and human activity, as well as for maintaining healthy oceans and ecosystems. In marine science, it is common for biologists and geologists to identify regional differences based on expert knowledge, frequently through data visualization. title: A source-to-sea decision-support framework for wet-weather wastewater load management: evidence from Jiaozhou Bay
abstract: Coastal concentration compliance can overlook increased wastewater throughput during wet weather. We developed a source-to-sea decision-support framework using 2019–2022 wastewater, river, and marine observations from Jiaozhou Bay, China. title: Tecnologías de información geográfica y gerencia pública en salud: hacia una vigilancia epidemiológica territorial de la enfermedad diarreica aguda en Perú y América Latina
abstract: La enfermedad diarreica aguda (EDA) persiste como problema prioritario de salud pública en Perú y América Latina. Mediante una revisión sistemática PRISMA de 30 estudios (Scopus y SciELO, 2000-2026), se analizó cómo las Tecnologías de Información Geográfica (TIG) —autocorrelación espacial e indicadores LISA— identifican clústeres de riesgo de EDA. Se concluye que estas herramientas constituyen activos estratégicos de gerencia pública en salud, con potencial para optimizar la planificación territorial, la asignación presupuestaria y la capacidad de respuesta institucional ante brotes.

title: Analisis Kesesuaian Lahan Budidaya Minapadi Berbasis SIG dan AHP di Kecamatan Tanjungkerta, Kabupaten Sumedang
abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis kesesuaian lahan budidaya Minapadi di Kecamatan Tanjungkerta, Kabupaten Sumedang, melalui integrasi Sistem Informasi Geografis (SIG) dan metode Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP), serta mengevaluasi kualitas air pada lima lokasi sampel sebagai pendukung pengembangan minapadi. Data primer meliputi pH, suhu, oksigen terlarut (DO), Total Dissolved Solids (TDS), dan amoniak, sedangkan data sekunder meliputi sumber air, jenis tanah, topografi, tutupan lahan, kerentanan gerakan tanah, dan kerawanan gempa. Pembobotan AHP dilakukan melalui perbandingan berpasangan
journal: Geodika Jurnal Kajian Ilmu dan Pendidikan Geografi

title: Tracing Groundwater–Seawater exchanges using geochemical tracers (radon, radium, stable isotopes of water) in a seasonally frozen beach
abstract: Groundwater–seawater exchanges remain poorly documented in subarctic and arctic regions, particularly during winter, when coastal ice alters hydrogeology conditions and limits sampling opportunities. This study investigates winter groundwater dynamics at a seasonally frozen beach by combining the use of various geochemical tracers. Stable water isotopes (δ 2 H and δ 18 O) were used to identify the origin of the water, whereas short-lived radioisotope tracers ( 222 Rn, 223 Ra, 224 Ra) were used to trace subsurface geochemical processes along the groundwater flow path, from the upper beach to th

title: 4-MBC in Australian sunscreens as an unmonitored discharge pathway into Great Barrier Reef coastal waters
abstract: Abstract 4-Methylbenzylidene camphor (4-MBC, also known as enzacamene), a chemical UV filter prohibited or never permitted across the EU, UK, China, ASEAN, US, and Japan, remains legal in Australian therapeutic sunscreens at concentrations up to 4% w/w. The European Scientific Committee on Consumer Safety concluded in 2022 that no safe concentration could be established, and the UK Scientific Advisory Group on Chemical Safety confirmed this in 2025. title: Constraint-Based Adaptive Grids for Compact Representation of Marine Scalar Fields
abstract: Fixed-block representations can obscure heterogeneous local variability in marine scalar fields. We present a deterministic adaptive representation in which anchored dyadic tiles merge under a field-normalized local-range rule and a realized-tile diameter cap. Area-weighted tile values provide lossy reconstruction, whereas exact tile-to-cell membership preserves the link to the authoritative source grid. title: Rheumatic Heart Disease Burden and Sex Differences in China and ASEAN Countries, 1990–2030: A Comparative Analysis from the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023
abstract: Background: Rheumatic heart disease (RHD) remains a major public health concern in low‑ and middle‑income countries. Systematic comparisons between China and the ten ASEAN member states examining sex disparities are scarce. Methods: Using Global Burden of Disease Study 2023 data, we analyzed RHD burden in China and ten ASEAN countries from 1990 to 2023. Key measures included age‑standardized prevalence (ASPR), mortality (ASMR), and disability‑adjusted life‑years rates (ASDR). title: Mathematics anxiety and problem-solving ability in numerical methods courses: A repeated cross-sectional study across two Southeast Asian universities
abstract: Mathematics anxiety (MA) impedes mathematical learning by taxing cognitive resources, negatively affecting problem-solving ability (PSA). Some evidence suggests that the strength and nature of this negative association may vary across educational and cultural contexts. However, cross-cultural studies on MA and PSA, especially in Southeast Asia, remain limited. This study investigated cohort-level patterns of MA and PSA in a transnational Numerical Methods course at Universiti Tun Hussein Onn Malaysia (UTHM) and Universitas Pahlawan (UP), Indonesia. title: Marine habitat use and movement of sympatric anadromous Dolly Varden and Arctic Char in the Canadian Arctic
abstract: Abstract Objective Inuit subsistence fishers in Kugluktuk, Nunavut, Canada, have noticed changes in the timing and locations of their catches of Arctic Char Salvelinus alpinus and northern form Dolly Varden S. malma malma (collectively referred to by the community as “char”) in the past ∼20 years. In response, an ongoing research program was formed to study char in partnership with the Kugluktuk Hunters and Trappers Organization. The occurrence of sympatric populations of anadromous Arctic Char and Dolly Varden is rare but was recently identified in Coronation Gulf, Nunavut, where char populat
journal: Transactions of the American Fisheries Society

title: Experimental snowball earth viscosity drives the evolution of motile multicellularity
abstract: Abstract During the 70-million-year span of the Cryogenian Snowball Earth glaciations, low ocean temperatures beneath global sea ice increased water viscosity up to fourfold. In the absence of adaptation, unicellular organisms living in this viscous environment were limited in their ability to move and acquire nutrients. We experimentally test the hypothesis that multicellularity evolved in order to overcome this viscosity-induced metabolic deficit. title: Landscape of Targetable Genetic Alterations in Advanced Cholangiocarcinoma among Patients in Southeast Asia
abstract: Cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) is a heterogeneous form of biliary tract cancer, for which treatment options remain limited; however, molecular profiling technology has helped in uncovering genomic mutations that can be used in precision oncology. This molecular profiling study has been carried out retrospectively in order to investigate the genomic alterations that are targetable in advanced cholangiocarcinomas of Southeast Asia. Samples from 126 patients were analyzed through targeted next generation sequencing in order to identify somatic mutations, copy number alterations, and gene fusions. Ident
institutions: Sathyabama Institute of Science and Technology

title: Three decades of marine bioregions evolution through analysis of phytoplankton phenology
abstract: Abstract. Ocean biogeochemistry is undergoing significant modification in response to climate change. To better understand these evolution, we present a novel ocean monitoring indicator approach that tracks the temporal evolution of marine bioregions of similar phytoplankton phenologies. Chlorophyll-a concentration observations from remotely sensed ocean color describe seven distinct marine bioregions characterized by their unique patterns of phytoplankton biomass seasonality. title: Winter disturbances drive community change in subarctic eelgrass meadows
abstract: The dynamics of winter sea ice and icefoot play a fundamental role in structuring intertidal ecosystems in subarctic environments. However, ongoing climate warming is altering ice regimes across northern shorelines. In the St. Lawrence marine estuary (Canada), reduced formation of icefoot increasingly exposes benthic habitats to winter-related disturbances. We investigated how such disturbance influences eelgrass ( Zostera marina L.) meadows and associated benthic communities using a before-and-after comparison spanning the 2024-2025 winter season. We used a sampling design that compared areas

title: Assessment of Ocean Thermal Energy Conversion Potential in Cenderawasih Bay, Papua, Indonesia: Energy Performance, Techno-Economic Feasibility, and Environmental Considerations
abstract: This study evaluated the potential of Ocean Thermal Energy Conversion as a renewable electricity source in Cenderawasih Bay, Papua, Indonesia. Ocean temperature data from the World Ocean Atlas for 1955-2018 at station 21576 were analyzed to characterize the surface and deep-water thermal conditions and to assess the performance of an open-cycle Ocean Thermal Energy Conversion system. The assessment covered thermodynamic efficiency, electrical power generation, production cost, freshwater production, and potential environmental impacts. title: Remobilized volcanogenic sediments boost photophysiological activity in three symbiotic reef-building coral species
abstract: Abstract Coral reefs that surround volcanic islands are continually influenced by run-off carrying remobilized volcanogenic sediments. Although unaltered volcanic ash is known to supply trace metals that enhance coral holobiont productivity, the impacts of long-term exposure to weathered tephra, a far more likely scenario in island settings, are less understood. title: Meandering shorelines: The potential for multi-level habitat complexity to ecologically enhance artificial coastal defences
abstract: Artificial coastal defences simplify, linearize, and homogenize the coast, leading to reduced species diversity, ecological functioning, and ecosystem services. Previous active management research has shown that greater habitat complexity at millimeter to decimeter scales increases the diversity of fauna and flora living on constructed shores, however, little is known regarding the potential effects of increasing the scale of complexity on larger marine species. Testing this experimentally is challenging, hence, as a first step, we conducted a meta-analysis on movement patterns, home ranges, a

title: Global triazine herbicide pollution impairs marine phytoplankton nutrition through disruption of acetyl-CoA-related metabolism
abstract: Herbicide contamination impairs marine primary productivity, yet its subcellular impact on phytoplankton carbon allocation remains poorly understood. Global monitoring (1990–2023) revealed triazine herbicides as the dominant coastal pollutants, with atrazine and simazine exceeding 80% detection frequency; their combined toxicity corresponded to a median atrazine-equivalent concentration of 0.68 nmol L −1 . title: From shark hunters to sea guardians: Environmental literacy transformation and socio-ecological transformation of the Bajo people in Sapeken Islands, East Java-Indonesia
abstract: The Bajo people are known for their closeness to and dependence on the sea. Over the past few decades, the Bajo people have undergone significant changes that are worth examining. This study aims to analyze the socio-ecological transformation of the Bajo people who inhabit Sadulang Besar Island, Sapeken Archipelago, East Java, with particular attention to how environmental literacy, intergenerational learning, and shifting livelihood strategies have contributed to changes in marine practices and ecological identity. They have transformed from shark hunters into key actors in environmental lite

title: Hydrodynamics of bio-mimetic sponge arrays with non-uniform triangular arrangement under wave actions
abstract: Bio-inspired marine structures have attracted increasing attention as nature-based solutions for modifying coastal hydrodynamics and enhancing momentum exchange. Previous studies on isolated and dual sponge-inspired elements have shown limited hydrodynamic effectiveness under relatively low-height waves, where velocity redistribution and turbulence generation remain weak. To address this limitation, the present study proposes and experimentally fabricates a bio-mimetic pillar coral composed of non-uniform triangular sponge elements arranged in a progressive three-line configuration. title: Ocean predators as indicators of nano- and microplastic prevalence in pelagic food webs
abstract: Abstract Quantifying nano- and microplastics (NMPs) in ocean predators is fundamental to understanding the prevalence of these contaminants and potential impacts on ecosystem health. Pyrolysis gas chromatography tandem mass spectrometry with lipid correction was used to determine NMP concentrations and polymer composition in the muscle tissue of two pelagic predators (dolphinfish [ Coryphaena hippurus ], yellowfin tuna [ Thunnus albacares ]) across the Atlantic, Pacific, and Indian Oceans. Species-specific differences in NMP concentrations were observed, with body burdens often markedly lower

title: Macrobenthic community turnover along a compressed depth gradient in the East Sea
abstract: The East Sea of Korea is a semi-enclosed marginal sea characterized by a steep bathymetric gradient, creating a compressed environmental gradient that provides an ideal study area for investigating benthic macrofaunal communities. Still, quantitative assessments of community patterns across the continuous coastal-to-deep-sea gradient remain limited in the East Sea of Korea. This study analyzed the distribution and community transition patterns of macrobenthic communities along the continuous coastal-to-deep-sea depth gradient in the East Sea. In total, 26 samples were collected using box cores
institutions: Korea Institute of Ocean Science and Technology
Korea University of Science and Technology

title: Marine holobionts: a model arena for host–microbe biology, from ecosystem function to biotechnology
abstract: Abstract Microbial symbioses are the operating system of marine biology. Nearly every macroscopic organism in the ocean exists as a holobiont, the consortium composed of a eukaryotic host and its bacterial, archaeal, microeukaryotic and viral partners. Marine holobionts span a broader range of the metazoan tree of life than likely any other ecological setting on the planet. This breadth makes the marine realm a uniquely informative system to investigate how host-microbe partnerships shape organisms and ecosystems. In this review, we discuss marine holobionts around three integrative themes. Fi

title: Advanced Assessment of the Agro-Silvo-Pastoral Coherence in Transboundary Transitional Water Regions
abstract: Transitional waters play a vital role in the ecological health and sustainability of coastal areas. According to European Union legislation, transitional waters are coastal water bodies influenced by freshwater flows but are partly saline due to their proximity to the sea. This study focuses on agricultural and forestry regions adjacent to transboundary transitional waters—i.e., areas where two or more countries share an estuary, tidal inlet, delta, or lagoon and have a contiguous border in their territorial waters. The objective of the study is to determine the patterns of riparian agroforest

title: Phosphate-Modified Co/BaTiO₃@Vulcan Nanocomposite for Stable Seawater Oxygen Evolution
abstract: This study presents a design strategy for developing corrosion-resistant anode materials, establishing a successful baseline for further optimization in the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) during direct seawater splitting. Cobalt nanocomposites supported on BaTiO₃ and Vulcan XC72R carbon black were synthesized via a combined sol-gel and microwave-assisted methodology using cellulose phosphate (CP) as a structural template and phosphorus source. institutions: Institute of Electrochemistry and Energy Systems
Institute of Metal Science, Equipment and Technologies

title: Environmental Security of the Gulf During Armed Conflict: Marine Pollution Risks, GCC Preparedness, and a Regional Emergency-Response Framework
abstract: The Gulf is a strategically crucial and environmentally vulnerable semi-enclosed marine system supporting petroleum industries, international shipping, desalination facilities, coastal ecosystems, and urban centers. Alongside chronic industrial and maritime pressures, armed conflict introduces severe risks via direct military operations, targeting of energy infrastructure, drone and missile strikes, hazardous material releases, and disruption of monitoring networks. This review evaluates the potential marine pollution consequences of armed conflict in the region, examining historical precedent
journal: International Journal of Law Management & Humanities

title: Seascape genomics reveals high genetic diversity and apparent panmixia in endemic Southern Ocean phytoplankton
abstract: Abstract The adaptive potential and resilience of cold‐adapted phytoplankton to climate change have the potential to impact polar marine food webs and global biogeochemical cycles. Two central but poorly constrained facets of adaptive potential in polar phytoplankton are standing genetic diversity and its spatial structure. Here, we partially sequenced 30 field isolate genomes of a commonly‐occurring endemic Southern Ocean (SO) phytoplankton, the diatom Actinocyclus actinochilus , and analyzed patterns in standing genetic diversity and geographic structure. title: Small-scale fishers’ perceptions and behavioural responses to marine protected areas implementation
abstract: Marine protected area (MPA) implementation can lead to fishers’ displacement and opposition to conservation efforts. Yet, evidence on how MPAs affect fishing operations is limited, especially for the small-scale sector. Surveys and participatory mapping exercises (n=93) were carried out with small-scale fishers in four Mediterranean and one Black Sea MPA to investigate fishers’ behavioural responses and perceptions to MPA implementation. Industry-led mitigation of seal bycatch in North Sea pelagic trawl fisheries: Evaluating excluder device effectiveness and policy implications
abstract: Bycatch of marine mammals in commercial fisheries presents conservation, operational, and regulatory challenges, particularly in the Greater North Sea where trawl fisheries targeting forage fish overlap with seal foraging habitats. This study evaluates the effectiveness of two seal excluder devices—the DPPO’s excluder tube and the PFA’s excluder grid—designed to reduce incidental seal captures in sandeel and herring fisheries, respectively. title: Distribution-based assessment reveals structural shifts in a protected estuarine gastropod, Clithon retropictus (Mollusca: Gastropoda)
abstract: Understanding temporal variation in estuarine populations is essential for conserving species inhabiting environmentally heterogeneous coastal habitats. Clithon retropictus is a protected brackish-water gastropod in South Korea that inhabits algae-covered stones in small tidal rivers and is vulnerable to changes in salinity gradients, substrate structure, and fragmentation of estuarine habitats. We evaluated long-term changes in the abundance structure of this species using national-scale ecological monitoring data collected from 2016 to 2024. Rather than relying solely on mean abundance, we a

title: Reproductive thermoregulation in marine mammals: mechanisms, adaptations and evolutionary implications
abstract: Marine mammals inhabit thermally challenging environments in which maintaining internal body temperature is essential for survival, metabolic function, and reproductive success. Unlike terrestrial mammals, many marine male species lack external reproductive structures (e.g. scrotum), raising questions about how reproductive temperatures are regulated in the absence of conventional cooling mechanisms. This review synthesizes current knowledge of reproductive thermoregulation in marine mammals, with a focus on cetaceans and pinnipeds, and highlights key anatomical and physiological adaptations.

title: Intra-annual dynamics of larval fish assemblages and their environmental associations in the central Southern Black Sea
abstract: Larval fish assemblages are crucial indicators for monitoring marine ecosystem dynamics and the recruitment potential of fishery stocks. This study investigates the spatiotemporal dynamics of larval fish assemblages in the central Southern Black Sea (Sinop) and the environmental parameters shaping these patterns. An intra-annual monthly sampling survey identified 35 species across 20 families; the assemblage structure was dominated by Engraulis encrasicolus, Gobius niger, Sprattus sprattus, Mullus barbatus and Trachurus mediterraneus. title: Paleotempestological record from an arid coastal desert: multi-proxy evidence for marine storms, aeolian pulses, and flash floods in the lower Drâa Valley, Moroccan Sahara, over the last century.
abstract: : Understanding the past variability of extreme events is essential for assessing their evolution in the context of the ongoing climate change. This study aims to distinguish types of extreme-event deposits preserved within a single arid sedimentary basin to better understand the differences in sedimentological signatures produced by contrasting hazards in arid coastal environments. Two short sediment cores were retrieved from the Drâa River estuary on the southern Moroccan Atlantic coast, a complex environment influenced by marine storm activity, aeolian processes and episodic fluvial floods.
institutions: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

title: No effect of short‐term exposure to ocean acidification on individual‐level variation in behaviour and susceptibility to predation in a Great Barrier Reef damselfish
abstract: Abstract Ocean acidification, caused by rising carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) in the atmosphere, has been reported to negatively impact a wide variety of behaviours in fishes, including activity, exploration, and predator avoidance. These effects have been documented at the population level, but many animal species naturally show large and repeatable individual‐level differences in behaviour. title: Cumulative impact of climate change and adaptation measures on Venice and its lagoon
abstract: Abstract Adaptation measures to climate change can generate unintended environmental consequences, particularly in vulnerable coastal systems. In the Venice Lagoon, the Mose mobile barrier system was designed to protect the city from sea-level rise and storm surges, still ensuring the lagoon-sea exchange. However, under climate change the frequency and duration of Mose closures will increase and this might modify lagoon water renewal and affect ecosystem properties. institutions: National Institute of Oceanography and Applied Geophysics
Consortium for Coordination of Research activities Concerning the Venice Lagoon System

title: Determination of seasonal groundwater recharge potential in the coastal mining town of Jose Panganiban, Philippines
abstract: Coastal groundwater resources are highly vulnerable to the combined risks of heavy metal contamination and saltwater intrusion where artisanal small-scale gold mining is active. This study used a GIS-based analysis to identify susceptible coastal aquifers in the municipality of Jose Panganiban, Philippines, by examining the reduction in groundwater potential coincident with the seasonal oscillation of precipitation, the main driver of recharge. journal: Journal of Degraded and Mining Lands Management

title: Effects of the summer season and religious holiday periods on tropospheric NO₂ levels in Türkiye’s coastal tourism destinations: A Sentinel-5P/TROPOMI and GIS-based analysis (2023–2025)
abstract: This study investigates tropospheric NO2 variations observed in the Mediterranean and Aegean regions—Türkiye’s prominent coastal tourism hubs—during the 2023–2025 period, within the context of seasonal summer intensity and short-term mobility during Eid al-Fitr (Ramadan Feast) and Eid al-Adha (Feast of Sacrifice). The study utilizes Sentinel-5P/TROPOMI tropospheric NO2 data to generate daily regional median values for selected coastal tourism districts. title: Microphytobenthos Primary Production and Organic Matter Mineralization Along the Sea Level Gradient in a Tropical Mudflat
abstract: Tropical tidal flats represent more than half of the global tidal flat area, however information on the ecological and biogeochemical role of microphytobenthos (MPB) in tropical environments remains scarce. The objective of this study was to analyze the changes in sediment biogeochemistry, MPB, community composition and net metabolism along the sea level (SL) gradient in a tropical tidal flat (Punta Morales, Gulf of Nicoya, Costa Rica). title: Fin whale movement patterns from the Mediterranean sea reveal summer habitat use in the North Atlantic and potential feeding behavior
abstract: Abstract Understanding the movements of highly mobile marine species is essential for identifying critical habitats and developing effective conservation measures. Although occasional movements of fin whales ( Balaenoptera physalus ) between the Mediterranean Sea and the North Atlantic Ocean have been reported, the extent to which these movements represent a recurrent component of Mediterranean fin whale ecology remains unclear. institutions: Instituto de Instrumentación para Imagen Molecular

title: Offshore wind farm impacts on marine fauna across taxa and ecological levels: A global review
abstract: The expansion of offshore wind farms (OWFs) is central to global decarbonization strategies, yet their effects on marine biodiversity are only partially understood. This systematic review synthesizes 221 publications up to June 2025 to assess the ecological impacts of OWFs on marine fauna living below the sea surface. The evidence base is uneven, heavily focused on North European waters, fish, and invertebrates, while expanding OWF regions and marine mammals remain underrepresented. title: Functional Identity Drives Directional Shifts in Freshwater Plankton Biomass–Size Relationships
abstract: Body size is a master variable in ecology that can predict ecosystem-level processes and reflect environmental conditions across diverse ecosystems. In freshwater ecosystems, the relationship between body size and biomass provides a powerful tool for characterizing community structure and trophic transfer efficiency. While these relationships are well established at the whole-community level, responses within plankton functional groups with distinct ecological characteristics have yet to be explored. title: Development of A Composite Sustainability Index Within An Integrated Coastal Zone Management Framework: A Case Study of Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
abstract: Coastal regions are increasingly under compounded pressures from climate change and rapid socioeconomic development, and integrated approaches to sustainability assessment are needed. This study assesses coastal sustainability in Ho Chi Minh City by developing a composite sustainability index (CSI) structured around three key dimensions: socioeconomic, ecoenvironmental, and institutional management. title: Spatial prioritization of urban green infrastructure for heat mitigation: a gis-mcda approach in Chennai, India
abstract: Urbanization and loss of vegetated land have amplified the Urban Heat Island (UHI) phenomenon which severely worsens urban climate in the main cities of the developing nations. This research develops a GIS-based multi-criteria decision analysis (GIs-MCDA) framework to quantify green space shortfalls, surface thermal exposure, and urban microclimates across the Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC), India. High-resolution Landsat 8/9 TIRS and OLI data were processed to generate Land Surface Temperature (LST) and NDVI layers for illustrating microclimatic surface temperature and vegetation patterns,

title: First record of the green mussel Perna viridis (Mytilidae: Bivalvia: Mollusca) in the Mediterranean Sea and occurrence of Perna perna on Alexandria coast, Egypt: Morphological and molecular analyses
abstract: The Mediterranean Sea is one of the world's regions most exposed to marine bio-invasion. It faces growing colonization pressure from Indo-Pacific taxa, including the marine mussels Perna viridis and Perna perna . The Asian green mussel ( P. viridis ) is consistently flagged as a high-priority potential invader in the European Union risk assessments. Its establishment in Mediterranean waters has not been confirmed. title: Stronger Together: Isograft Fusion Accelerates Recovery and May Facilitate Heat‐Evolved Symbiont Transmission in Bleached Adult Corals
abstract: Experimentally evolved, heat-tolerant algal symbionts (heat-evolved; HE) offer a promising means of enhancing coral holobiont thermotolerance under warming oceans. However, translating their benefits into restoration practices requires scalable delivery methods. Coral tissue fusion may provide one such pathway by facilitating HE symbiont transfer to wild corals; however, its feasibility remains largely untested. title: Self-reporting alkalinity-responsive hydrogel for visual monitoring and microenvironment remodeling of seawater-immersed infected wounds
abstract: Seawater-associated infected wounds involve alkaline and hyperosmotic stress, polymicrobial contamination, biofilms, and persistent inflammation, collectively delaying healing. Herein, we developed QCB-Au@SPG, a pH-responsive hydrogel integrating fluorescent antibacterial QCB-Au, an alkali-sensitive SA-PBA network, and photocrosslinkable GelMA. QCB-Au@SPG exhibited a linear fluorescence response across pH 4–8 (R² = 0.998), enabling semi-quantitative visualization of pH variation, while alkaline conditions moderately enhanced QCB-Au release. title: Visualizing Reversible Uranyl (UO 2 2+ ) Capture and Release With Self‐Indicating Porous Organic Polymers
abstract: Seawater uranium extraction is a promising sustainable energy pathway; however, practical application requires advanced adsorbents that combine reversible, high uranium‐uptake capacity with the ability to track sorption cycles. Herein, we report self‐indicating porous organic polymers (POPs), Sal‐POP and Im‐POP , containing uranyl (UO 2 2+ ) ion‐coordinating salphen and o ‐hydroxy imine cores with UO 2 2+ binding energies up to −71.94 kcal mol −1 as uranium adsorbents, and demonstrate their reversible, high uranium extraction capacities up to 0.114 g g −1 h −1 . title: Cultivation of Cladophora glomerata Under Low‐Salinity Conditions: Ecological Controls, Production Constraints and Baltic Sea Deployment
abstract: ABSTRACT Brackish and freshwater coastal systems often combine nutrient enrichment with proximity to wastewater, aquaculture and coastal infrastructure, yet macroalgal cultivation under low‐salinity conditions remains poorly validated. This review evaluates whether Cladophora glomerata , commonly managed as nuisance biomass, can be developed as a seasonal crop and nutrient‐recovery tool in low‐salinity systems, with emphasis on the Baltic Sea. title: Spatial Variability and Long‐Term Trends in Winter Phytoplankton of the Warming Eastern Mediterranean Sea
abstract: Abstract The Eastern Mediterranean Sea (EMS) is among the fastest‐warming ocean regions, but the impacts of this warming on phytoplankton are unclear. Here, wintertime field observations were conducted across the EMS. These observations showed that small photosynthetic eukaryotes (<20 μm) dominated phytoplankton communities, collectively accounting for >60% of total chlorophyll a (Chl‐a) despite severe nitrate‐ and phosphate‐depleted conditions. title: Guild‐Based Metacommunity Internal Structure: Insights From Waterbird Assemblages in a Dynamic Estuarine System
abstract: ABSTRACT Aim Understanding how ecological processes shape species assemblages in dynamic environments is central to community ecology. Estuarine waterbirds are a compelling system for metacommunity analysis because their high mobility, functional diversity and sensitivity to environmental variation make them well suited to examine how assembly is partitioned in a highly mobile group. title: Distinct drivers control trace metal distributions through the Atlantic Ocean
abstract: Trace metals (TMs) including iron, manganese, cobalt, nickel, copper, zinc, cadmium, and lead have important biogeochemical roles in the ocean. However, the controlling factors of TM distributions have not yet been quantified and investigated on an ocean scale. Here we take a holistic approach to demonstrate that transport through water masses formed in high latitudes can explain 60–90% of dissolved TM distributions and >75% of TM inventories in the interior Atlantic. title: Measuring Dry Deposition of Sea Spray Aerosol and Height of Aerosol Plume Using a Controlled Wave Pool
abstract: Abstract Deposition of sea spray aerosols facilitates atmospheric corrosion of materials, requiring maintenance and replacement over time. However, the dimensions of sea spray aerosol plumes produced from breaking waves have not been well‐characterized, limiting useful prediction of particle transport downwind and atmospheric corrosion. Therefore, this project aimed to measure sea spray aerosol production from breaking waves in a controlled environment at several elevations to obtain the height profile of an aerosol plume. title: Prorocentrum pseudonux sp. nov. ( Prorocentrales, Dinophyceae ): A new nanoplanktonic dinoflagellate from the open tropical Pacific Ocean
abstract: SUMMARY While phytoplankton from the coasts of temperate seas has received considerable attention, phytoplankton from the open tropical ocean, especially the smallest fraction, remains understudied. Here, we describe a new nanoplanktonic dinoflagellate from the tropical Pacific Ocean. Prorocentrum pseudonux sp. nov. is slightly oval in thecal view, measuring 6–9 μm long and 5–8 μm deep. The theca is smooth with a few pores of different size classes. title: Episodic High‐Latitude Occurrence of Walleye Pollock ( Gadus chalcogrammus ) in the Central Arctic Ocean Associated With Warm Subsurface Conditions: Multi‐Year Environmental DNA and Larval Evidence
abstract: ABSTRACT Episodic high‐latitude occurrences of subarctic fish due to Arctic warming present significant challenges for managing high‐latitude ecosystems. In this study, we present four consecutive years (2021–2024) of integrated environmental DNA (eDNA) monitoring and larval surveys for walleye pollock ( Gadus chalcogrammus ) conducted aboard the Korean icebreaker IBR/V Araon in the Chukchi Sea (CS) and Central Arctic Ocean (CAO). title: Carbon fluxes within an Arctica islandica habitat in the German Baltic Sea
abstract: Ongoing climate change and rising CO 2 emissions highlight the need to understand ecosystem carbon cycling to guide the conservation of carbon-rich, biodiverse habitats. We investigated organic carbon cycling and storage associated with the long-lived bivalve Arctica islandica in the German Baltic Sea. Through filtration and bioturbation, A. islandica may enhance the burial of organic carbon in deeper sediment layers. title: Visualizing the penetration behavior of tapered thread piles via transparent soil: Effects of thread design
abstract: With superior construction efficiency and load-bearing performance, precast tapered thread piles hold significant potential for offshore and coastal infrastructure. However, their installation mechanics remain poorly understood, and visual experimental investigations are scarce. title: PREFERENCES OF DIGITAL NOMADS: ANALYZING POPULAR DESTINATIONS AND DECISION-MAKING FACTORS THROUGH INTERACTIVE DATA VISUALIZATIONS USING PUBLIC ACCESS DATABASES
abstract: Digital nomadism is a rapidly spreading form of location-independent work that is fundamentally transforming the global labour market, economy, and tourism. The aim of this study is to quantitatively explore and model the destination preferences of digital nomads and to present an innovative, interactive data visualization framework. Our research analyses the structural changes of the period 2021-2024 following the logic of the PEST model (Political, Economical, Social, Technological). title: Comparative Evaluation of Seawater-Based and Conventional Fixatives on Histological Quality in Broiler Chicken Tissues
abstract: Lung, liver, brain, heart, kidney, and spleen tissues obtained from 60 broiler chickens at a commercial abattoir in Afyon Province were fixed using six fixation solutions consisting of 10% neutral buffered formalin (NBF) or 70% ethanol, each prepared with distilled water, seawater (salinity approximately 38‰), or a distilled water–seawater mixture. This study evaluated the effect of seawater as a solvent component on histomorphological preservation and hematoxylin–eosin (H&E) staining quality. title: Transformación Digital de la Gestión Financiera Universitaria: Implementación del Sistema SCVRP con Inteligencia de Negocio y Dashboards Interactivos
abstract: La dependencia de procesos manuales para validar pagos universitarios suele provocar errores administrativos y retrasos que afectan a los estudiantes. Para resolver esta situación, se implementó el Sistema de Control de Verificación de Recibos de Pago (SCVRP) en el Tecnológico Nacional de México, Campus Lerdo. Este trabajo no se limitó a digitalizar documentos físicos, sino que buscó transformar los datos financieros en herramientas de gestión útiles. title: Eco-phenotypic characterization of Candida palmioleophila from poultry litter and marine environments: implications for One Health
abstract: Candida palmioleophila is an emerging opportunistic yeast frequently misidentified within the Meyerozyma guilliermondii complex, potentially obscuring its clinical and ecological relevance. Although its clinical significance is increasingly recognized, the phenotypic characteristics of environmental isolates remain poorly explored. This study evaluated the eco-phenotypic profiles of 14 C. palmioleophila isolates recovered from two anthropogenically influenced environmental sources: poultry litter (n = 6) and urbanized coastal environments (n = 8). title: Antifungal potential and ecological perspectives of selected seagrass species from tropical coastal meadows
abstract: Seagrasses have gathered increasing attention due to their multifaceted ecological roles. Apart from their ecological significance, seagrasses have exhibited potent antifungal properties, indicating potential for diverse applications. The antifungal efficacy of methanolic extracts derived from five seagrass species ( Cymodocea serrulata , Cymodocea rotundata , Halodule pinifolia , Halophila ovalis , and Syringodium isoetifolium ) was assessed against pathogenic fungal strains using the agar well diffusion method. title: Epistemic justice and deep-sea mining: UNCLOS’s facilitation of epistemic diversity the International Seabed Authority’s decision-making process
abstract: The paper discusses epistemic justice as a central justice framework to be considered in the regulatory process of exploitative deep sea mining, with the aim of bringing attention to the relevance of epistemic justice and diversity to deep sea mining scholarship. Epistemic justice is here understood as deeply connected to a broader social equity, and entails the fair treatment of different ’knowers’ and a creation, sharing, and validation of knowledge that is fundamentally diverse rather than based on one dominant knowledge-tradition. title: New evidence of the early stages of establishment of the parrotfish Sparisoma cretense (Teleostei: Labridae) following northward and westward range expansion in the Mediterranean Sea
abstract: Abstract Sparisoma cretense is undergoing a range expansion across the Mediterranean Sea, yet its establishment at northern latitudes of the westernmost Mediterranean remains uncertain. During July 2025, patterns consistent with the establishment of S. cretense in Cabrera National Park (39º 09’ N; 2º 57’ E) were assessed, and habitat features associated with its occurrence were identified. Underwater visual censuses were conducted, recording abundance, total length, sex, habitat composition, and the hydrodynamic exposure level of each locality. title: Best Practices in Open and Reproducible Antarctic Marine Sediment Core Research
abstract: Abstract Marine sediment cores from Antarctica are archived by national programs for reuse and resampling by future researchers, creating a resourceful way to conduct Antarctic science. With reduced budgets to conduct Antarctic field work and to collect new sediment cores offshore of the icy continent, the accessibility of these archived cores and availability of core data are in high demand. title: Molecular approaches to phylogeny and species boundaries in Lethrinus (Teleostei, Lethrinidae): insights from a taxonomic complex along Mozambique coast
abstract: Abstract Accurate species delimitation is essential for understanding the evolutionary processes that generate and maintain biodiversity, particularly in marine systems characterized by high connectivity and widespread distributions. Reef-associated fishes of the Indo–West Pacific provide an ideal framework to investigate these dynamics, yet many taxa remain poorly resolved due to morphological conservatism and cryptic diversity. title: Environmental and economic assessment of alternative marine energy pathways using integrated life cycle analysis
abstract: The maritime sector faces increasing pressure to reduce greenhouse gas emissions while maintaining economic feasibility. In response to the International Maritime Organization’s decarbonization targets, alternative marine fuels have gained significant attention as potential pathways toward low-carbon shipping. This study presents an integrated well-to-wake life cycle assessment (LCA) and life cycle cost assessment (LCCA) of marine diesel oil (MDO), liquefied natural gas (LNG), biodiesel, methanol, E-methanol, E-diesel, E-ammonia, and hydrogen using real operational data from a 6177 GT general

title: Interactive Effects of Episodic Warming and Phosphorus Pulses on Plankton Food-Web Rewiring In Freshwater Mesocosms
abstract: Freshwater ecosystems are increasingly exposed to short-duration heatwaves and episodic phosphorus inputs, both of which can substantially alter aquatic community structure and ecosystem functioning. However, the combined effects of these environmental stressors on plankton food-web organization and trophic interaction dynamics remain insufficiently understood. journal: Journal of Aquatic Ecology and Environmental Sustainability

title: Metabolomic profiling and anticancer effects of Red Sea sponges Liosina granularis and Callyspongia crassa on prostate and ovarian cancer cells
abstract: Abstract Marine sponges are rich sources of bioactive secondary metabolites with potential relevance to anticancer drug discovery. This study investigated the metabolomic profiles and preliminary anticancer activity of methanolic extracts from two Red Sea sponge species, Liosina granularis (LGE) and Callyspongia crassa (CCE), using prostate (PC3) and ovarian (SKOV-3) cancer cell models. LC-MS/MS analysis annotated 44 metabolites, including alkaloids, long-chain amides, fatty acids, polyketides, and terpenoids. title: A coupled water-quality–Ecopath with Ecosim model incorporating sand-lance aestivation dynamics in the Harima-Nada Sea
abstract: Sand lance ( Ammodytes japonicus ) is an important forage fish in the Harima-Nada Sea, Japan, but its stock has declined markedly in recent decades under concurrent changes in nutrient availability and water temperature. To clarify the mechanisms underlying these changes, we developed a region-specific coupled water-quality–Ecopath with Ecosim (EwE) model that explicitly incorporates sand-lance aestivation dynamics. title: Self-organized hummock-hollow patterns redistribute salinity stress in coastal meadows
abstract: Self-organization theory predicts that ecosystem functioning and resilience can emerge from feedbacks that generate spatial patterns. These emergent properties have commonly been explained by local positive feedbacks that concentrate limiting resources within productive patches. Here, we identify a stress-redistribution feedback underlying self-organized hummock-hollow patterning. title: Web-Based Extreme Weather Monitoring and Early Warning System for Traditional Fishermen Using IoT Sensor Data
abstract: Extreme weather can disrupt traditional fishing activities and increase safety risks, particularly when local weather information is difficult to access before departure. This study develops a web-based extreme weather monitoring and early warning system for traditional fishermen using Internet of Things (IoT) sensor data. The system integrates an ESP32 microcontroller with a DHT22 sensor, rain sensor, and anemometer to acquire temperature, humidity, rainfall, and wind-speed data at ten-second intervals. title: Shear strength evolution and multi-factor coupling friction model of coral sand-structure interface
abstract: The shear strength of coral sand-pile interface affects the bearing capacity of pile foundation in island and reef engineering. However, there is still a lack of interface shear strength prediction model that can comprehensively consider the influence of multiple factors. In this paper, the influence of roughness of pile (concrete, steel and aluminum alloy), normal stress and relative density of soil on the shear characteristics of pile-soil contact interface is systematically studied by using a large-scale interface shear apparatus developed independently. title: Relating Monthly to Yearly Morphological Changes in Embryonic Coastal Dune Systems
abstract: Abstract Embryonic coastal dunes are dynamic morphological features shaped by wind, waves, sediment availability, and vegetation. Temporal variability in these drivers controls embryo dune dynamics at short timescales (hours–days), while accreting dune systems often show gradual change over longer timescales (years–decades). How shorter‐term variability translates into longer‐term signals in dune dynamics remains poorly understood, partly due to a lack of frequent high‐resolution measurements and frameworks to analyze their full dimensionality. title: Softening mechanism and fatigue performance analysis of heat affected zone in welding of microalloyed submarine flexible pipes
abstract: Subsea flexible pipelines are key equipment in deep-sea resource development, serving as the "lifeline" connecting underwater production systems with surface treatment facilities. Its core function is to safely and efficiently transport various marine resources. The welding Heat Affected Zone (HAZ) is a weak link in the welding joints of submarine flexible pipelines. title: SPATIAL STRATEGIES AND IMPLEMENTATION PATHWAYS FOR THE ALL-AGE FRIENDLY RENEWAL OF OLD COMMUNITIES IN ZHUHAI UNDER THE ORIENTATION OF MODERN MARINE CITIES
abstract: Coastal cities have shifted from outward expansion to reworking the housing stock they already hold, and renewing aging communities has become harder to manage as a result. Three pressures overlap in these neighborhoods: a resident profile that no longer matches the original design brief, almost no slack in the public space budget, and marine-climate risks that accumulate rather than arrive one at a time. title: Sea Turtle Nesting Beach Fidelity Revealed by Satellite Tracking
abstract: ABSTRACT Site fidelity describes the tendency to return to or reuse familiar sites, yet some animals may use alternative sites while maintaining fidelity to primary locations, with consequences for population estimates as well as resilience to changing environments. Here we assessed and compared nesting beach fidelity of hawksbill turtles ( Eretmochelys imbricata ) on Frégate Island, Seychelles using data from beach foot patrols (2017–2025; n = 575 turtles) and satellite telemetry (2023; n = 10 turtles) and then examined the implications of fidelity strategies for population estimates. title: Modulation of ETCCDI-based extreme rainfall indices by ENSO and the Indian Ocean Dipole over topographically complex North Sumatra, Indonesia
abstract: This study examines the characteristics of extreme rainfall in North Sumatra Province, Indonesia, and its teleconnections with the El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO) and the Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD). The analysis uses a blended daily rainfall dataset from 1990 to 2024, combining station observations from the Indonesian Agency for Meteorology, Climatology, and Geophysics (BMKG) with the Climate Hazards Group InfraRed Precipitation with Station (CHIRPS) satellite data. title: Delta morphology reveals timings of early ocean regression and hydrologic shift on ancient Mars
abstract: Abstract Mars’ ancient hydrologic history remains a subject of debate, with competing interpretations suggesting either a large ocean or scattered lacustrine environments. Here, we show that delta morphology on Mars records a shift between these hydrologic regimes. Through controlled tank experiments, we identify two distinct delta types: “lobe-extruding deltas” formed during water-level falls and “stepped fan-deltas” formed during rising water levels. title: Integrating AHP–GIS with Geophysical Validation for Groundwater Recharge Zonation in Samaru, Zaria, Nigeria
abstract: Groundwater plays a critical role in meeting domestic, agricultural, and industrial water demands, particularly in regions where surface water resources are limited or unreliable. Effective identification of groundwater recharge zones is therefore essential for sustainable planning and management. This study delineates groundwater recharge potential zones in Samaru, Zaria, Nigeria, by integrating the Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP) with Geographic Information System (GIS) techniques, supported by geophysical validation. title: Spatial organization and coordinated development of offshore wind industrial chains under governance decentralization: evidence from China's coastal provinces
abstract: Offshore wind industrial chains, encompassing upstream component manufacturing, midstream project development and operation, and downstream grid integration, underpin large-scale utilization, yet their spatial organization, structural linkages, and coordinated development remain underexamined. title: Reviewing the climate change landscape in South Africa’s marine fisheries: progress, gaps, and future directions
abstract: Climate change is reshaping South Africa’s marine ecosystems and fisheries with consequences for ecological productivity, livelihoods and governance. Although research on climate impacts on fisheries has expanded, the overall climate-risk landscape for South African fisheries has not been reviewed using the risk framing proposed in the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) Fifth Assessment Report (AR5).
