title: Fluid–substrate coupled controls on mineral‑phase selection in the Kunlun hydrothermal system
abstract: Abstract Mineral precipitation at submarine hydrothermal vents transfers redox‑sensitive elements from the lithosphere to the ocean. However, conventional plume and sediment‑trap sampling poorly preserves particle‑scale signatures generated at reactive interfaces, hindering robust interpretation of near‑vent mineralization. Here, we deployed open‑cell Fe, Ni, Cu, and Fe–Ni foams within diffuse low‑temperature alkaline fluids of the serpentinization‑driven Kunlun hydrothermal field. title: Mosaic Accumulation of Somatic Genetic Variation and Estimates of Age in the Long‐Lived Reef‐Building Coral Acropora palmata
abstract: Somatic genetic variation (SoGV) accumulates during an organism's lifetime and is traditionally viewed as detrimental rather than adaptive due to links with cancer and senescence. However, in modular organisms like corals, deleterious mutations can be purged at the cellular or polyp level, while adaptive mutations may rise in frequency as polyps create genetically distinct modules. title: Environmental and growth variation of Peucedanum japonicum in coastal areas of South Korea
abstract: Coastal habitats are characterized by steep and spatially heterogeneous environmental gradients that can influence plant population structure, growth and reproductive performance.Peucedanum japonicum is a coastal perennial plant distributed across diverse habitats, but differences in population characteristics and individual performance among populations under different local environmental conditions remain poorly understood.We compared vegetation, environmental conditions, structural characteristics, and individual growth and reproductive traits of P. japonicum across three habitat types in K

title: Design and Implementation of an AIS Vessel Trajectory Visualization System Based on AMap
abstract: To address the challenges posed by the large volume and dense spatial distribution of AIS position data, as well as the limited support for interactive queries in conventional static displays, this paper designs and implements an AIS vessel trajectory visualization system based on AMap. By integrating AMap with ECharts, the system provides coordinated representations of spatial positions and speed variations. It supports two primary functions. title: Design and Implementation of a Centralized Vessel Monitoring System Using API Harmonization
abstract: Vessel tracking is critical for ensuring the safety and operational efficiency of the maritime industry. However, the reliance on tracking devices from disparate commercial vendors (e.g., Vendor A, Vendor B, and G-Track) introduces severe data fragmentation, forcing operators to navigate multiple proprietary dashboards. Furthermore, custom-built Internet of Things (IoT) tracking devices lack interoperability with these existing commercial platforms. title: Assessment of water quality and anthropogenic impacts on surface and groundwater in the Zhambyl region using GIS-technology
abstract: An integrated hydrochemical and geospatial assessment was performed to access the water quality of wastewater accumulation basins and adjacent aquatic systems in the Zhambyl region (southern Kazakhstan) under conditions of increasing anthropogenic impact. Monitoring was carried out at eight sampling points (P1-P8) during three seasonal campaigns (September 2025, November 2025, and January 2026). The measured parameters included pH, oxidation-reduction potential (ORP), dissolved oxygen (DO), salinity, total dissolved solids (TDS), electrical conductivity (EC), and chemical oxygen demand (COD).

title: Hydrometeorological and hydrogeological trends and drought dynamics in a cold-humid, coastal region
abstract: Quantifying groundwater response to droughts remains challenging, as aquifers typically respond to meteorological conditions with delays, and long-term groundwater records remain limited. This study investigated statistical relationships among meteorological, hydrogeological, and hydrological datasets in the Canadian province of Nova Scotia. title: Optimising renewable hydrogen hub locations: A GIS-based spatio-temporal integration framework
abstract: This paper presents a Geographic Information System (GIS)-integrated spatio-temporal optimisation framework for the design of renewable hydrogen hubs. This framework embeds high-resolution spatial datasets directly into an hourly Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) formulation to co-optimise the siting, sizing, and hourly operation of system components, thereby minimising the Levelised Cost of Hydrogen (LCOH 2 ). title: Iron Isotope Fractionation on Vesta Driven by Magma Ocean Process
abstract: Abstract Magma oceans represent a pivotal stage in the early evolution of terrestrial planets. title: Ontogenetic shifts, trophic differentiation, and predator–prey size relationships in Oxyrhopus false coral snakes from Bahia, Brazil
abstract: Abstract Although snakes of the genus Oxyrhopus are generally regarded as opportunistic predators, the relative roles of interspecific dietary differentiation, ontogenetic variation, and predator morphology in their feeding ecology remain poorly understood. We analyzed the diet of 253 preserved specimens representing four Oxyrhopus species from Bahia, Brazil. title: A GIS-based multi-criteria decision analysis for identifying optimal geothermal power plant sites: a case study of the Gulf of Suez, Egypt
abstract: Abstract The Gulf of Suez is a geologically significant rift basin, characterized by Miocene-age formations that formed through extensional tectonics during the Tertiary period, ultimately facilitating the divergence of the Arabian Peninsula from the African continent. This region has considerable geothermal potential, making it a strategically valuable asset for developing clean, sustainable energy infrastructure. title: Underwater hybrid ESD versus conventional ESD for colorectal laterally spreading tumors: a retrospective study
abstract: Background and aims Conventional endoscopic submucosal dissection (C-ESD) is standard for colorectal laterally spreading tumors (LSTs) but is time-consuming. Underwater hybrid ESD (U-Hybrid ESD) is an emerging technique. We compared the efficacy and safety of U-Hybrid ESD versus C-ESD for colorectal LSTs. title: Artificial light at night causes unequal and species-specific shifts in infection risk by a generalist marine parasite
abstract: Abstract Light pollution, in the form of artificial light at night (ALAN), changes the normal physiology and behaviour of animals, leading to alterations in interspecific interactions. Parasitism is likely to be impacted, ranging from altered parasite proliferation and transmission to altered host exposure or susceptibility to infection. How these individual-level effects translate to higher level impacts remains poorly understood. title: Analisis Kerawanan Longsor Berdasarkan Parameter Geologi dan Geospasial di Biluhu Timur, Kecamatan Batudaa Pantai, Gorontalo
abstract: Biluhu Timur Village and its surroundings, located in Batudaa Pantai District, Gorontalo Regency, have a topography ranging from hills to coastal plains and relatively high rainfall, which makes them prone to landslides. This study aims to analyze the geological and geomorphological conditions and to map landslide susceptibility zones in Biluhu Timur Village and its surroundings at a scale of 1:25,000. title: Large-scale marine eDNA database reveals seasonal latitudinal diversity gradients in Japan driven by vagrant fish
abstract: Abstract The spatial and temporal patterns of marine diversity are essential for the sustainable use and management of marine ecosystems. Here, we investigated latitudinal and seasonal diversity gradients of fish genera in Japanese waters using environmental DNA (eDNA) data from 1,765 surveys conducted between 2017 to 2022. We found a negative relationship between genus richness and latitude, consistent with latitudinal diversity gradient (LDG). title: Spatial Assessment of Heat Health Risk in Brussels Through GIS and Local Climate Zone Analysis
abstract: Climate change and rapid urbanization are increasing the frequency and intensity of extreme heat events, posing significant risks to public health in cities. Although numerous studies have investigated urban heat islands and heat vulnerability, spatially explicit assessments integrating environmental, demographic, and urban morphological characteristics remain limited, particularly in European cities. title: Growth, physiological responses, and water quality in juvenile Malabar grouper reared in a low-salinity RAS: An 84-day operational trial
abstract: Recirculating aquaculture systems (RAS) are expanding globally as a sustainable aquaculture technology. Although RAS enable intensive production of marine fish, their high capital and operating costs necessitate strategies that improve growth efficiency while maintaining stable water quality. Low-salinity seawater promotes growth in many marine fish species; however, concerns remain that reduced salinity may impair biofiltration. abstract: This study aims to determine the effectiveness of freestyle swimming learning using a visualization model on the development of students' basic movements at SDN Mekargalih 4. The background of the study stems from the problem of low understanding of freestyle swimming techniques in students, especially related to the coordination of hand, foot, breathing, and body position movements. abstract: Three new alkaloids, colombiains A-C (1-3), together with 8 known ones (4-11), were isolated from the soft coral-derived fungus Cladosporium colombiae CSGL 10M10. title: Complementary Data Sources for Mapping Target Mediterranean Non-Native and Cryptogenic Species: The Role of Local Knowledge and Citizen Science
abstract: Citizen Science (CS) and especially Local Ecological Knowledge (LEK) play an increasingly crucial role in assessing the impacts of climate change on the biodiversity of Mediterranean shallow waters. We explored the use of multiple data sources - including CS, and particularly, LEK and social media - to assess the distribution of selected, especially non-native and cryptogenic thermophilic, marine species in the Mediterranean. This case study aims to test the complementarity and reliability of adequately validated participatory and informal knowledge systems in documenting species occurrences.

title: How Well Can the Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) Satellite Mission Observe Irrigation Canals?
abstract: Abstract The capability of the Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) satellite for observing irrigation canals has remained relatively unexplored. Here, we assess SWOT observability of irrigation canal networks across 22 Asian countries using a new confidence level (CL) metric. Validation against in situ gauge observations showed that higher CL corresponds to significantly lower water‐level retrieval error. Of approximately 795,110 km of canals analyzed, 37.5% (297,799 km) show high confidence, 46.9% (373,035 km) moderate confidence, and 15.6% (124,276 km) low confidence of observability.

title: Stress-dependent shifts in genotoxic sensitivity of zooplankton
abstract: The ocean is increasingly exposed to multiple stressors, including rising temperatures and metal pollution. Zooplankton are central components of the marine food web and understanding lethal responses and underpinning molecular mechanisms across species from different habitats is essential for predicting ecosystem resilience. This study compares two zooplankton species from an Arctic fjord, the near surface-dwelling Acartia longiremis and the lipid-rich, deeper-dwelling Calanus finmarchicus, for their molecular responses to acute and sub-acute temperature and copper (Cu) stress. title: Spatio-temporal analysis of land use/land cover (LULC) changes using GIS techniques in Upper Bhavani River Basin, Nilgiri Hills, India
abstract: The study investigates the land use and land cover (LULC) changes in Upper Bhavani River basin of the Western Ghats over the past four decades (1989–2019) using remote sensing (RS) and geographic information system (GIS) techniques. It also explores the correlation between LULC changes and population growth during this period. The study highlights the importance of mapping and monitoring LULC changes in developing better management strategies for the sustainable development of natural resources. title: Combining eDNA metabarcoding and stable isotope analysis advances diet studies in a colonial, non‐regurgitating seabird
abstract: Understanding seabird diet is fundamental to assessing trophic interactions and predicting responses to environmental change. However, seabird diet studies are often constrained by low taxonomic resolution, invasive sampling methods or reliance on opportunistically collected samples, leaving the diet of important populations such as Common Guillemots Uria aalge in the Irish Sea understudied. title: Probabilistic sustainability evaluation of hybrid breakwaters considering uncertainty in conceptualization and indicator weighting
abstract: One of the distinguishing features of hybrid infrastructure is the need to find balance between multiple functional performances. Multi-criteria decision analysis is an ideal tool for exploring this balance and identifying an ideal solution, but there are few examples of its application to coastal infrastructure. This study conducted a probabilistic, multi-criteria decision analysis-based sustainability evaluation of hybrid breakwater structures considering two sources of methodological uncertainty: conceptualization and weighting. abstract: Mangrove ecosystems are highly vulnerable to coastal environmental change and anthropogenic disturbance. The mangrove forests distributed along the eastern and western coasts of Shenzhen experience contrasting environmental regimes. The eastern coast is influenced by oligotrophic waters of the northern South China Sea and is dominated by native mangrove stands, whereas the western coast, located within the Pearl River Estuary, is subject to elevated nutrient inputs, intensive urbanization and extensive mangrove restoration. title: Hierarchical Organization Modulates Transient Thermal Relaxation Dynamics in Chitinous Cuticles from Marine and Terrestrial Organisms
abstract: Abstract Chitinous cuticles are hierarchical biological composites in which the molecular organization spans multiple structural length scales. Although the relationships between chitin chemistry and mechanical performance have been extensively investigated, the structural factors governing transient thermal relaxation remain poorly understood. abstract: Marine organisms are increasingly exposed to nanoplastics (NPs) and rising temperatures due to climate change, yet their combined effects remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated the interactive toxicity of polystyrene nanoplastics (PS-NPs, 80 nm) and elevated temperature (32 °C vs 25 °C) in marine medaka larvae (Oryzias melastigma) using integrated bioaccumulation analysis, histopathology, and transcriptomic profiling. title: Nature-based experiences support lasting conservation behavior: longitudinal evidence from shark ecotourism in Hawaiʻi
abstract: Shark ecotourism is increasingly promoted as a nature-based solution for ocean sustainability, yet empirical evidence of its long-term impacts on conservation behavior remains limited. We employed a quasi-experimental, longitudinal design to evaluate whether participation in a shark ecotourism program in Hawaiʻi influenced individual conservation behavior over time. Survey data were collected from tour participants and a general public comparison group at the time of the tour and again two years later. title: Secondary Metabolites from the Marine-Derived Fungus Aspergillus udagawae SFC20170619-M03 Exhibiting Disease Control Activity
abstract: In our screening program for novel biocontrol agents, we found that the culture filtrate of the marine-derived fungus Aspergillus udagawae SFC20170619-M03 exhibited disease control activity against several fungal plant diseases, including tomato gray mold, tomato late blight, and pepper anthracnose. title: Revealing diagnostic characters of the box jellyfish Chiropsalmus alipes through high-resolution in situ documentation in the Mexican Tropical Pacific
abstract: The confirmation of species distributions and taxonomic identification is critical for documenting biodiversity under increasing anthropogenic pressures. This objective is challenging for gelatinous plankton due to logistical constraints related to safety and preservation. This study documents and validates the taxonomic identity of live individuals of Chiropsalmus alipes from Bahía de Banderas (Mexican Tropical Pacific), using high- resolution in situ video and photographic records. abstract: Hill slope failure along the roadways is a major problem in hilly and mountainous areas. Landslide hazard zonation maps produced in GIS environment can be utilized for planning and tackle of disasters associated with landslides. The aim of the study is to create landslide susceptibility maps along National Highway 513 from Pasighat to Mariyang, Arunachal Pradesh, India using quantitative approaches such as frequency ratio and Shannon entropy technique. abstract: Due to infrastructural work, Sydsvensk Arkeologi AB conducted an archaeological excavation in 2022 between the Scanian villages Fjälkinge and Gualöv, southern Sweden. The excavation revealed settlements and a cemetery from the Late Neolithic into the Pre-Roman Iron Age. Located at a plausible prehistoric intersection which connects the Lake Ivösjön to the Baltic Sea, and coastal south to the north, the site has the potential to provide new knowledge of ancient road systems and its possibilities for exchange of both ideas and people. abstract: Abstract Host–associated microbiomes play vital roles in species’ ecology and evolution, yet little is known about their shift during the transition from aquatic to terrestrial habitats. title: Whole genome sequencing and comparative genomic analysis of Photobacterium ganghwense CF1.2, the bacterial host of the lytic marine bacteriophage PhCF1.2: Insights into its mobilome and metabolic potential
abstract: Photobacterium species are abundant in marine ecosystems, where they help break down organic matter and serve as hosts of lytic bacteriophages that influence the dynamics of bacterial populations. Here, we report the draft genome sequence and comparative genome analysis of Photobacterium ganghwense strain CF1.2, isolated from Cochin Fisheries Harbour, Kochi, on the south-west coast of India, and identified as the host bacterium of the marine lytic phage PhCF1.2. abstract: The Gulf ecosystem health was of great concern after the explosion of the Deepwater Horizon oil platform (April 2010). abstract: Abstract The increasing scarcity of freshwater resources, coupled with the ecological challenges associated with the disposal of agricultural wastewater, has emphasized the need to develop sustainable injection fluids for enhanced oil recovery (EOR). abstract: Ascetosporea is a group of parasitic protists within Endomyxa that primarily infect marine invertebrates and can cause serious damage to fishery resources such as oysters and prawns. Although approximately 50 species have been formally described, environmental DNA (eDNA) studies suggest that their diversity remains largely underestimated, with many lineages yet to be discovered. abstract: ABSTRACT Open‐pit coal mining severely degrades soil and ecosystem functions, constraining regional sustainability. Vegetation‐based reclamation has therefore been widely adopted as an effective approach to promote soil recovery and ecosystem restoration. abstract: As part of a watershed protection plan, the Texas Water Resources Institute and AgriLife Extension Service developed and distributed an educational postcard (``mailer'') about septic system maintenance to mailing addresses outside of public sewer service areas. The mailer was distributed four times within 1 year. The impact of this mailer was evaluated with a retrospective pre/post-test within a mailed survey. abstract: Abstract Understanding the microbiomes of marine mammals is essential to explore their health, ecological roles and responses to environmental change. We investigated the nasal and anal microbiota of two sympatric subarctic seals, the harbour seal (Phoca vitulina) and the ringed seal (Pusa hispida), using 16S rRNA gene sequencing. abstract: Skeletal systems couple rigid elements with contractile and connective tissues to transmit forces and control movement. title: Spatiotemporal Differentiation and Influencing Factors of Overseas Chinese Architectural Heritage: A Case Study of Minnan, China
abstract: The Minnan region in southern Fujian, China, comprising Quanzhou, Xiamen, and Zhangzhou, is one of China’s major traditional qiaoxiang (overseas Chinese hometown) regions. This study develops a spatial database of 682 Minnan Overseas Chinese Architectural Heritage (MOCAH) sites, divides their formation into four historical periods—Qing Dynasty (pre-1912), Early Republican Period (1912–1936), Wartime Republican Period (1937–1948), and Early PRC Period (1949–late 1970s)—and applies GIS-based spatial and statistical methods to examine their spatiotemporal differentiation and influencing factors.

abstract: ABSTRACT The European green crab ( Carcinus maenas ) is a keystone predator in its native range and one of the world’s most damaging invasive species. Although its invasion success has frequently been associated with exceptional physiological plasticity, comparatively few studies have simultaneously examined organismal energetics, biochemical regulation, physiological organization and mitochondrial genetic diversity across native and invasive populations. abstract: The article addresses air stability effects on whitecap coverage at sea. abstract: Abstract Lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC) remains a challenging malignancy with limited targeted therapies. abstract: Urban landscapes can be defined as an area with high building and population density and functions where a very significant part of the world’s population lives. title: Microplastic Abundance in Water and Sediments in the Opak River Estuary, Bantul, Special Region of Yogyakarta
abstract: Microplastic pollution in estuarine environments has attracted growing attention due to the persistence, widespread distribution, and potential ecological impacts of plastic particles. This study aimed to assess the abundance and characteristics of microplastics in water and sediment at the Opak River Estuary, Bantul Regency, Special Region of Yogyakarta, Indonesia. abstract: Pseudomonas aeruginosa biofilms are recalcitrant to conventional antibiotic therapy due to their extracellular polymeric substance (EPS) matrix, in which Psl polysaccharide serves as the primary structural scaffold. abstract: Abstract Bacterial resistance to heavy metals (HM) poses a significant risk to ecosystems and human health. This study evaluated resistance to HM of 24 bacterial isolates from two deep aquatic environments in southern Brazil: the Guarani Aquifer System (GAS) water and the Rio Grande Cone (CRG) marine sediment. abstract: The self-excited oscillating water jet is widely used in ocean engineering. Its effectiveness stems from the impact of cavitation collapse driven by periodic pressure pulsations. title: Role of Plant Biodiversity in Mitigating Natural Disasters and Enhancing Ecosystem Resilience
abstract: Plant biodiversity plays a pivotal role in buffering ecosystems and human societies against the impacts of natural disasters. Vegetation cover influences hydrological cycles, soil stability, fire regimes and atmospheric processes, thereby mitigating the frequency, magnitude and consequences of disasters such as floods, droughts, cyclones, landslides and wildfires. This study reviews the scientific evidence supporting the role of plant diversity in disaster risk reduction, emphasizing mechanisms such as soil stabilization, hydrological regulation, carbon sequestration and coastal protection. abstract: Satisfaction with the urban environment is among the crucial elements of the quality of urban life. This study examines the results of the most recent wave of the Eurobarometer survey (year 2023), covering 83 European cities, to explore which city characteristics are associated with higher and lower perceived quality of different urban environment areas - air quality, noise levels, green spaces and city cleanliness. abstract: Invertebrate Systematics learning requires physical specimens, as digital media often fail to capture complete morphological traits. Addressing this limitation, this study aims to explore and characterize Bivalve and Gastropod shells from the Gadon coast to evaluate their feasibility as dry learning specimens. abstract: In this study, embryonic development in the gonad and glochidia development in the gill marsupium of Unio delicatus (Bivalvia: Unionidae) were examined using morphological, visual, and statistical analyses. The study was conducted in Gölbaşı Lake (Hatay Province) from January to December 2024, with twenty individuals sampled monthly. title: Hawksbill turtle (Eretmochelys imbricata) nesting enhances meiofaunal abundance and structure in an urban sandy beach
abstract: The northeastern coast of Brazil hosts some of the highest nesting densities of hawksbill turtles ( Eretmochelys imbricata ) in the South Atlantic, where nesting events represent an important pathway for marine-derived nutrient inputs into oligotrophic sandy beaches. Within this context, we evaluated the influence of hawksbill turtle nests on meiofaunal assemblages at a highly urbanized tropical beach during the 2020/2021 nesting season, a period uniquely marked by the COVID-19 pandemic. title: Active nuclease inhibition over passive freezing secures the genomic archive of fish eye lenses
abstract: Fish eye lenses offer a chronological archive of individual life histories and preserve genomic DNA. However, integrating ecological and genetic data is hindered by post-mortem nuclease degradation, and standardized DNA preservation protocols for this tissue remain undefined. We evaluated chemical and thermal preservation methods to maximize DNA yield and integrity from fish lenses. abstract: BACKGROUND: Imported dengue remains a public health concern in non-endemic countries. Local transmission may occur when imported infections coincide with competent vectors and suitable environmental conditions. We developed a cross-national framework for predicting monthly imported dengue risk in Japan and the Republic of Korea. METHODS: We analyzed monthly data from January 2005 to June 2025. title: Quantifying SMART drumline catches in an Australian bather protection program
abstract: The global incidence of shark bites on humans has increased over time, driving the development of shark mitigation strategies to reduce the frequency of human-shark interactions. Traditional lethal shark control programs have used fishing gear aimed at reducing local shark populations. There has, however, been a shift towards more ecologically sustainable, non-lethal approaches. One such method is the SMART (Shark Management Alert in Real Time) drumline, which is designed to capture, tag and relocate target sharks. title: Multi-Horizon Air Quality Index Prediction incorporating Spatial Hotspot Analysis and Meteorological Drivers
abstract: Urban air pollution poses significant environmental and public health challenges in rapidly urbanizing Indian cities. This study presents a GIS-integrated MLframework for multi-horizon (1-24 hours) forecasting of the Air Quality Index (AQI) in Nashik using multi-pollutant time-series data. Air quality observations from four Maharashtra Pollution Control Board (MPCB) monitoring stations at Gangapur Road, Hirawadi, MIDC Ambad and Pandav Nagari were analysed for representative seasonal months (January, April, July and October) of 2025. title: Spatial and temporal variability of urban air quality across functional land-use zones in Eskişehir, Türkiye
abstract: Urban air quality is spatially heterogeneous because emission intensity, land-use function, daily activity, seasonal energy demand, and atmospheric dispersion vary across the urban fabric. This study quantified the short-term spatial and temporal variability of PM2.5, PM10, and CO2 across ten functionally contrasting locations in Eskişehir, Türkiye. Field observations were conducted during four weeks in February and four weeks in May, with measurements collected on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays during morning (08:30–10:30) and evening (17:00–19:00) periods. title: Recent advances in understanding the impact of microplastics on bacterial antibiotic resistance: mechanisms, evidence gaps, and One Health implications
abstract: Microplastic (MP) pollution and bacterial antimicrobial resistance are converging public health concerns. MPs provide persistent, mobile surfaces that can transport antibiotic-resistant bacteria and antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs). After aging and conditioning, MPs can develop biofilms in which resistance determinants accumulate, persist, and undergo horizontal transfer. title: Early‐Stage Distribution of the Invasive Alga Rugulopteryx okamurae on the Catalan Coast: First Quantitative Baseline
abstract: ABSTRACT The non‐indigenous brown alga Rugulopteryx okamurae has rapidly expanded across the eastern Atlantic and the western Mediterranean Sea. The first record on the Catalan coast (NW Mediterranean) was in July 2024 in Llançà (Girona), followed by additional detections at nearby localities. We conducted targeted surveys in June–July 2025 across 13 sampling stations in four localities, combining visual inspections and transects. abstract: Across the great oxidation event (GOE) period, the oceans experienced a major transition from ferruginous (Fe 2+ -rich) to localized euxinic (HS − -rich) conditions. title: Moored observations of the deep western boundary current east of the Gagua Ridge in the Northwestern Pacific
abstract: Abstract The deep western boundary current (DWBC) of the Pacific serves as a lower limb of the meridional overturning circulation that has been identified as a key component of the global climate system. abstract: Peri-urban coastal areas such as Timbulsloko Village, Demak Regency, face increasing development pressure and chronic inundation as a slow-onset hazard that affects residents, public assets, and local micro-enterprises. However, conventional CSL methods are inadequate for precise defect identification due to low data utilization, limited testing efficiency and poor localization accuracy. abstract: Bogam Bay in West Kotawaringin Regency, Central Kalimantan Province is one of the bays that has dynamic potential influenced by local natural, social, economic, and environmental conditions. abstract: This research develops and applies a comprehensive method for identifying landscape spatial units to support landscape character assessment in Latvia. The approach is based on the integration of geomorphological, land-cover, land-use, ecological, and cultural-historical data, complemented by field-based perceptual evaluation. title: “The Guy(s) from California”: Race, the Tax Code, and the Relational Geographies of Rental Housing in Memphis
abstract: This article examines how high net worth, individual investors from coastal markets have reshaped the rental market in Memphis, Tennessee, and could be playing a growing role in housing markets across the United States. Drawing on interviews with local “turn-key” real estate companies and a computational analysis of property data across Memphis, I show how the historical trajectory of racial capitalism, coupled with the fallout of the 2008 financial crisis, has enabled local property managers to channel out-of-state investment from high-cost markets like California into Memphis neighborhoods.

title: Antimicrobial activity of ginsenoside Rh2 against Enterococcus faecalis and its biofilm
abstract: Background Enterococcus faecalis ( E. faecalis ) is frequently associated with persistent root canal infections and treatment failure, and effective strategies for its elimination remain limited. abstract: Context: Climate change and anthropogenic stressors are degrading coastal biogenic habitats, disrupting the vital pathways fish use to shift from nearshore nurseries to offshore reef environments. abstract: Carbon stock assessment is a critical component of climate change mitigation, particularly in coastal areas experiencing rapid land-use change. This study aims to estimate aboveground carbon stocks, potential CO₂ emissions, and the economic value of carbon across various land use and land cover (LULC) types in Sungai Kakap District, Kubu Raya Regency, West Kalimantan, Indonesia. abstract: This study evaluates the application of remote sensing and GIS techniques for mapping geothermal potential areas in the central-western Taiz, Yemen. The objective is to identify prospective areas for hydrothermal water exploration. abstract: Abstract This study presents the results of interdisciplinary research on a unique osseous projectile point bearing visible traces of a black, pitch-like substance, discovered in 2022 during an underwater visual survey of the Žeimena River bed in eastern Lithuania. abstract: Introduction Harmful algal blooms of Alexandrium monilatum and Margalefidinium polykrikoides are a common occurrence in the tributaries of lower Chesapeake Bay, United States of America. title: Targeting Flood Resilience Investments Through a Readiness Gaps Index: Evidence from Mississippi
abstract: Flooding is among the most costly and recurrent disasters globally, including in the United States. The Southeastern United States is vulnerable to billion-dollar climate disasters. In Mississippi, high flood exposure coincides with uneven institutional capacity and socioeconomic constraints, yet existing assessments largely emphasize hazard or social vulnerability in isolation while overlooking integrated readiness for resilience planning. abstract: This study investigates the crustal architecture and tectonomagmatic evolution of the central Chilean Andes (32-34° S) through new U-Pb zircon geochronology. abstract: Abstract Background Forensic DNA phenotyping (FDP) provides vital investigative leads by predicting externally visible characteristics (EVCs). abstract: Social values are increasingly acknowledged in land management and spatial planning, particularly amid urbanization and sustainable development. Yet many planning systems have not institutionalized these values, leaving land-use decisions largely shaped by economic and technical rationalities. title: From signals to species: Improving acoustic classification reliability for North Pacific false killer whales
abstract: This study presents an automated pre-classification data filtering method that increases confidence in the classification of cetacean acoustic events lacking visual verification, while minimizing bias and reducing the need for manual review. The study tests the approach on false killer whale (Pseudorca crassidens) acoustic data from the North Pacific Ocean. A minimum-data requirement derived from sensitivity analyses, combined with filters based on species-specific acoustic characteristics, defines objective criteria for excluding acoustic events before classification. title: Performative Sovereignty Versus Performative Nationalism: Hydraulic Securitization and Abeyance of the Indus Waters Treaty
abstract: ABSTRACT Indus Waters Treaty (IWT, 1960) survived four major wars, decades of cross‐border militancy, and 56 years of parliamentary skepticism in India. However, it could not survive the performative securitization sequence initiated by three terror attacks, that is, Uri (2016), Pulwama (2019), and Pahalgam (2025), leading to IWT's abeyance in 2025. abstract: Bacteriophages play a key role in regulating Vibrio populations in marine environments, and environmental conditions may influence their replication and interactions with bacterial hosts. This study aimed to isolate and characterize the bacteriophage PvVp2, which infects the pandemic Vibrio parahaemolyticus strain KX, and to compare its environmental performance with that of phage CHOED, a lytic phage infecting Vibrio anguillarum . abstract: Balikpapan City was pivotal in the pre-independence petroleum industry. As a vital geopolitical asset, it became a strategic WWII theater between Japanese and Allied forces. Military defense remnants including bunkers, trenches, artillery, and military bases are extensively concentrated in East Balikpapan District. However, the physical integrity of these archaeological sites faces severe degradation from rapid population growth and demographic shifts, triggering massive morphological changes to the area. abstract: This paper presents the comprehensive results of recent archaeological research conducted in the Ain Naga region of Biskra (Algeria), an area notably characterized by a high density of Protohistoric funerary monuments locally known as "Nechaz" or Mounds (Tumuli). Adopting a rigorous interdisciplinary approach, the study effectively combines field archaeological surveys, systematic excavations, and advanced spatial analysis using Geographic Information Systems (GIS) within a modern digitization framework. abstract: ABSTRACT In biological systems, single‐modal stimuli are often insufficient for complex behaviors, whereas multimodal integration significantly enhances environmental perception and decision‐making. Inspired by ants, which synergistically process optical, chemical, and mechanical signals, the development of multimodal neuromorphic devices is highly desirable. title: Analysis of Landslide Susceptibility Toward the Presence of Accommodation Areas (Glamping and Villas) in Kejajar District, Wonosobo Regency, 2025
abstract: This study aims to analyze and map the level of landslide susceptibility in accommodation areas in Kejajar District, Wonosobo Regency, using a Geographic Information System (GIS) approach. Scoring, weighting, and overlay methods were applied to integrate rainfall, slope gradient, soil type, geology, and land-use parameters. The results indicate that Kejajar District is divided into three landslide susceptibility classes: high susceptibility covering 4,936 ha (76%), moderate susceptibility covering 1,515 ha (23%), and low susceptibility covering 37 ha (<1%). title: External validation of EuroSCORE II, additive EuroSCORE, and the STS predicted risk of mortality at 2,600 meters above sea level: a retrospective cohort study from a Latin American cardiac surgery centre
abstract: Background EuroSCORE II, the Additive EuroSCORE, and the Society of Thoracic Surgeons Predicted Risk of Mortality (STS PROM) are widely used cardiac surgery risk models, but their performance has not been evaluated in a cardiac surgery centre located at high altitude (≥2,500 m asl). Methods We conducted a retrospective external validation study using prospectively collected registry data from consecutive adult cardiac surgery procedures performed at Hospital Universitario Mayor-Méderi (2,600 m asl), Bogotá, Colombia, between January 2019 and February 2026 ( N = 1,486). title: Codon-aware multi-scale feature fusion for metagenomic sequence classification
abstract: Microorganisms exert profound influences on both natural ecosystems and human society. As the cornerstone of microbial research, metagenomics relies on the precise analysis of large-scale, multi-source genomic data. However, discriminating among diverse sequence types remains a formidable challenge. To address this, we present CamFi (Codon-aware Multi-scale Feature Fusion), a unified framework integrating overlapping nucleotide-triplet representations with multi-scale dilated convolutions for classifying prokaryotic chromosomes, eukaryotic chromosomes, plasmids, and viruses. title: Microeukaryotic Diversity and Habitat Structuring in a Desiccating Alkaline Maar Lake (Central Mexico)
abstract: Microeukaryotes are important components of microbial food webs in saline and alkaline lakes, yet their diversity and distribution across distinct microhabitats remain poorly understood. We characterized microeukaryotic communities associated with microbialites, microbial mats, hypersaline waters, and sediments in the desiccating maar lake Rincón de Parangueo (central Mexico) using 18S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing. title: Uncovering regional differences in plastic pollution distribution along the Norwegian coast
abstract: Abstract Understanding the mechanisms behind coastal plastic accumulation is crucial for more targeted clean-up actions and policy-making. We used a systematically collected dataset for plastic pollution along the Norwegian coast, added physical and socio-environmental response variables to it, and used linear regression to identify the most important factors that influence plastic accumulation. We used 446 sampling transects on 170 beaches from Norway’s south-eastern, southern, western and northern coasts. abstract: Perkembangan drone berbasis IoT meningkatkan kebutuhan sistem telemetry real-time yang stabil dan efisien. Permasalahan yang dihadapi adalah perbedaan performa komunikasi telemetry antara teknologi WiFi dan LoRa dalam pengiriman data monitoring drone, terutama pada kondisi lingkungan dengan interferensi elektromagnetik yang berbeda. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis perbandingan performa komunikasi telemetry berbasis WiFi dan LoRa pada sistem monitoring drone berbasis IoT. title: Fecal degradation and nutrient loss of manure from cattle offered four bermudagrass cultivars
abstract: Abstract Bermudagrass ( Cynodon spp.) is one of the most common warm‐season perennial grasses utilized in the southeastern United States for pasture or stored forage. However, there is a paucity of data evaluating the fecal nutrient losses overtime by cattle grazing different bermudagrass cultivars. Therefore, the objective of this study was to assess the rate of fecal degradation and nutrient loss over time from cattle offered four different bermudagrass cultivars: Coastal, Russell, Tifton 44, or Tifton 85. title: Shedding light on amphipod behaviour: Baseline locomotion behaviour for laboratory ecotoxicology experiments
abstract: Behavioural endpoints offer a sensitive, non-invasive alternative to traditional mortality assays. Yet, they remain underutilized in regulatory frameworks due to a lack of standardised methodologies and baseline behavioural data. This study investigates the baseline locomotion of the marine amphipod Marinogammarus marinus to external light triggers to support standardised laboratory behavioural assays. title: Instructional Design and Teaching Practice of Curriculum-Based Ideological and Political Education Using an AIS Vessel Big Data Project
abstract: To address insufficient industry context, weak integration of value objectives with technical tasks, and a lack of process-based evidence of educational outcomes in curriculum-based ideological and political education for big data programs at higher vocational colleges, this study introduces a pedagogically adapted Automatic Identification System (AIS) vessel big data project into the course Big Data Analysis and Development and develops a teaching framework that integrates knowledge, competencies, and values. title: Beobachtung der Giftproduktion in Cyanobakterien mittels Klick-Chemie
abstract: Abstract Harmful cyanobacterial blooms are increasing in frequency globally, yet there is still a lack of understanding regarding the biological roles of such toxins. Chemoselective visualization and quantification of cyanotoxin synthesis via high-resolution microscopy in combination with advanced imaging analysis can track cyanotoxin synthesis in producer cells under experimental conditions. Through immunolabeling indicating cellular organelles new information on molecular interactions can be obtained.

abstract: The current work presents a probabilistic seismic hazard assessment (PSHA) for engineering bedrock conditions (Vs30} = 760 m/s) across the Jizan region of southwestern Saudi Arabia. For this purpose, we compiled a homogenised earthquake catalogue covering 827–2022 CE, including historical and instrumental records from multiple authoritative sources. title: INTEGRATED GROUND SURVEY AND REMOTE SENSING APPROACH FOR DIGITAL TOPOGRAPHIC MAPPING OF FEDERAL POLYTECHNIC BAUCHI, NIGERIA
abstract: Accurate and up-to-date topographic information is essential for physical planning, infrastructure development and spatial management of institutional environments. This study evaluated the integration of ground-survey observations, high-resolution remotely sensed imagery and terrain data for digital topographic mapping of Federal Polytechnic Bauchi, Nigeria. title: An Integrated Geospatial and Socio-economic Assessment of Flood Risk in North-western Nigeria Using Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis
abstract: Flood disasters have become increasingly frequent and severe in Nigeria, driven by a combination of climatic shifts and anthropogenic pressures. This research paper assesses flood risk vulnerability across the seven states of the Northwest geopolitical zone (Sokoto, Kebbi, Zamfara, Katsina, Kano, Jigawa, and Kaduna). title: Elevated temperature exacerbates red sore disease caused by Vibrio vulnificus in American eels (Anguilla rostrata)
abstract: The marine pathogenic bacterium Vibrio vulnificus is linked to epizootics of a dermal ulcerative disease, causing high mortality in European and Japanese eels. American eels ( Anguilla rostrata ) experience a similar condition, commonly referred to as red sore disease (RSD). Field studies indicate that V. vulnificus infections highly correlate with RSD in American eels, but causation remains un-established. title: Climate Change, Anthropogenic Stressors, and Livelihood Sustainability in the Sundarbans, Bangladesh: A Field-Based Analysis
abstract: The Sundarbans Forest is a vital mangrove ecosystem where environmental processes and human livelihoods are closely intertwined. In Bangladesh, the forests and adjacent bodies of water provide protection against coastal hazards, support a variety of flora and fauna, capture carbon and sustain communities that rely on natural resources. However, the region is also becoming increasingly vulnerable to hydro-climatic risks and stresses related to human activities. title: Ammonium stress reprograms lignin biosynthesis and carbon allocation in seagrass
abstract: Lignin is a key structural polymer in seagrass cell walls, supporting tissue rigidity, mechanical resilience, and resistance to hydrodynamic forcing. However, it remains unclear how nitrogen-driven eutrophication affects lignin biosynthesis by reshaping the carbon allocation required for structural investment. title: Breaking limits: rapid sea-to-summit ascent of Mount Everest (8,848 m) in 3 days 23 hours following normobaric-hypoxic pre-acclimatization and staged supplemental oxygen in a non-elite athlete
abstract: Introduction Traditional ascent of Mount Everest (8,848 m) typically requires 40–50 days of on-mountain acclimatization. Normobaric hypoxia (NH) pre-acclimatization is a practical home-based alternative; however, no peer-reviewed case report has described a sea-to-summit Everest ascent completed in under four days by a non-elite individual without prior on-mountain acclimatization rotations. title: Do salmon recipes work for cod? Environmental challenges and regulatory pathways in Norwegian aquaculture
abstract: Aquaculture governance in Norway has largely developed around the rapid expansion of Atlantic salmon farming, while repeated efforts to establish cod aquaculture have resulted in limited and discontinuous production. Recent improvements in breeding, biological performance, and market conditions have, however, renewed commercial interest in cod farming and raised a central policy question: to what extent can regulatory frameworks developed for salmon be transferred to cod aquaculture? title: Paper in the Floodplain: and other instructions for drawing
abstract: This essay will bring together a body of work that attempts to capture human performance and natural phenomena on paper as a way of drawing and scoring encounters with place. In what ways do place (and land) escape our efforts to represent and capture it, while simultaneously embedding its temporal marks, ciphers, and imprints? In this essay, drawing is a mode of listening and attuning to change and a way to care and collaborate with land, that enables artists to reflect on environmental constraints and shifting landscapes. title: Real-time single-molecule imaging in zebrafish embryos uncovers noncanonical translation
abstract: Abstract Precise spatiotemporal control of protein synthesis is essential during embryogenesis, yet directly measuring translation kinetics in vivo remains challenging in vertebrates. In particular, it remains unclear how translation efficiency is determined for key developmental regulators, and which kinetic steps limit their production. title: An AI visual chatbot system for climate heat risk communication and decision-making in at-risk agricultural communities
abstract: Information on heat-related health risks that is based on meteorological data and forecasts is important for outdoor workers, farm managers, and many other stakeholders, but visualization and interpretation of climate data in a user-friendly way remains a challenge. This proof-of-concept research developed Sol, an artificial intelligence (AI) chatbot to conveniently interpret and communicate heat stress risks through smartphones and other devices. title: Flushing‐Assisted Saline Immersion Endoscopic Submucosal Dissection in the Rectum: A Video‐Based Feasibility Series
abstract: ABSTRACT Flushing endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) is a refinement of saline immersion ESD in which energy‐synchronized saline flushing from the knife tip is hypothesized to disperse micro‐bubbles and facilitate more controlled coagulation at the tissue interface. We retrospectively evaluated the technical feasibility of this approach in 10 rectal procedures performed at a tertiary referral center. title: Spatio-temporal Dynamics of Riverbank Erosion and Accretion and Their Socio-economic Impacts: A Case Study from Bhola Island of Bangladesh
abstract: Riverbank erosion and accretion are natural and ongoing geomorphological processes in the huge delta of Bangladesh, driven by the mighty Ganges-Brahmaputra-Meghna river systems. The turbulent rivers of Meghna and Tetulia are posing serious threat to two high-risk erosion unions of Hasanagar and Pakshia in Burhanuddin Upazila of Bhola district. In these coastal tracts, high tidal surges and faster monsoon floods are continuously eating up homesteads and farmlands. title: HYDROCHEMICAL AND STABLE-ISOTOPE SIGNATURES OF GROUNDWATER IN THE VIETNAMESE MEKONG DELTA AND THEIR MANAGEMENT IMPLICATIONS
abstract: Groundwater is a strategic water source in the Vietnamese Mekong Delta (VMD), particularly during the dry season and in coastal areas affected by drought and salinity intrusion. However, the delta aquifer system is not a single homogeneous reservoir; it is a multi-layered sedimentary system separated by clay, silt and sand units, with distinct recharge sources, residence times, hydraulic connectivity and salinization risks. title: Which Barriers Drive the Others? Modelling the Interdependencies of Integrated IoT-Blockchain-Big Data Analytics Adoption in Emerging-Economy Maritime Logistics
abstract: Integrated Internet of Things (IoT), blockchain, and Big Data Analytics (BDA) offer substantial potential to improve visibility, trust, coordination, and decision-making in maritime logistics. However, their combined adoption remains constrained by interdependent technological, organisational, and environmental barriers, particularly in emerging economies. abstract: The efficiency of ship maintenance is essential to ensure operational readiness, minimize docking duration, and control maintenance costs. In practice, the implementation of the Planned Maintenance System (PMS) on TB. Flores 1 at PT Bintang Samudera Mandiri Lines is influenced by operational schedules, maintenance windows, crew workload, equipment conditions, spare-part availability, procurement lead time, and ship-shore coordination. abstract: El proyecto se propuso evaluar integralmente las condiciones productivas, ambientales y socioeconómicas de los viñedos implantados en la costa del río Paraná (Entre Ríos), con el objetivo de generar conocimiento aplicado que oriente estrategias de manejo sustentable de artrópodos. title: Energy-exergy analysis of SWRO desalination adopting energy recovery devices of PX and HTC in an island plant case
abstract: This study examines the energy-exergy performance of seawater reverse osmosis (SWRO) desalination systems equipped with pressure exchanger (PX) and hydraulic turbocharger (HTC) energy recovery devices at an island plant to identify optimal configurations for sustainable water production. The methodology integrates experimental measurements with multi-scale modeling, including WAVE simulations, Gibbs and ion exergy models, and direct work analysis of the high-pressure pump. title: Wastewater Generation and Environmental Pathways in Libya: An Evidence-Based National Accounting Framework
abstract: Reliable national wastewater accounts are difficult to construct where direct flow measurements, treatment-plant records, and discharge inventories are incomplete. This study develops an evidence-aware accounting framework to estimate domestic wastewater generation and distinguish sewer-connected from non-networked sanitation pathways across Libya’s 22 administrative areas. abstract: Abstract Advanced scintillation materials capable of simultaneously delivering ultrahigh efficiency, exceptional stability, and multifunctional X-ray imaging remain elusive because of intrinsic trade-offs in conventional scintillators. Hernin, a defect-engineered Ce3+-activated borosilicate glass was developed. It exhibits high internal/external quantum efficiencies of 92.4%/85%, an ultrafast lifetime of 142.3 ns, and XEL intensity further reaching 190% of BGO after “bright-burning effect”, setting a new performance benchmark for Ce3+-activated glass scintillators. title: Ventusky as a Geography Learning Tool: Enhancing Students' Spatial Thinking through Problem-Based Learning in Atmospheric Dynamics
abstract: Spatial thinking is a crucial competency in geography education, but students' mastery of this capacity is lacking, particularly in comprehending abstract atmospheric phenomena. The purpose of this study is to assess the impact of the Ventusky-assisted Problem-Based Learning (PBL) model on students' spatial thinking abilities in the Atmospheric Dynamics topic. abstract: ABSTRACT This work develops lightweight, sustainable PP/rPP/biocarbon composites targeting automotive applications. abstract: Background: Focusing on Manado, Indonesia, a coastal destination balancing growth and ecological risk, we develop and test an integrative model grounded in stakeholder and legitimacy theories that links environmental management accounting (EMA), CSR commitment, and environmental disclosure quality (EDQ). title: Deciphering coccolith formation: advanced microscopy insights from the biomineralization of Gephyrocapsa huxleyi
abstract: Coccolithophores are unicellular marine phytoplankton that produce complex and intricately shaped mineralized scales called coccoliths. Coccoliths are produced in an intracellular vesicle where crystal nucleation occurs, from which several individual calcite units develop with anisotropic crystallographic facets, prompting studies into the cellular mechanisms that control crystal growth within the cell. title: Monitoring Sustainable Rural Tourism Development in Post-Conflict Areas Using Remote Sensing and Geospatial Analysis
abstract: This study examines how rural tourism supports sustainable development, economic recovery, social stability, and cultural preservation in post-conflict regions, using Transcarpathia, Ukraine, as a case study for 2022–2024. It applies a mixed-methods approach combining satellite remote sensing, GIS-based spatial analysis, and socio-economic indicators to assess land-use change, infrastructure recovery, ecological stability, and socio-economic resilience. abstract: Abstract Cultivated kelps are a scalable marine feedstock for renewable polymers, but regional aquaculture supply chains lack engineering benchmarks for the alginate yield and quality. Here, we apply a lower-hazard citrate-based process to quantify bioplastics-relevant alginate metrics across cultivated northeast Pacific kelps from commercial farms in British Columbia (Canada) and Alaska (USA). abstract: Indoor air pollution in waterfront communities of Port Harcourt poses significant public health concerns due to poor housing conditions, marine activities and inadequate ventilation. title: Can passive samplers replace biota in risk assessment of resuspended contaminated sediments?
abstract: Resuspension of contaminated sediments elevates turbidity and mobilises sediment‑bound polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) into the water column, increasing their bioavailability and toxicity to aquatic organisms. Passive samplers (PS), which accumulate the freely dissolved fraction of contaminants, have the potential to replace biota as a non‑invasive tool for estimating exposure and toxicity. title: Multi‐Scale Assessment of Population Exposure to Landslides in Vietnam
abstract: ABSTRACT Vietnam's complex terrain and monsoon climate create extensive landslide‐prone conditions, yet the population exposure patterns of its urban, rural, and demographic groups remain insufficiently quantified. This study combines the Global Landslide Non‐Susceptibility Map (GLNSM), high‐resolution population layers, urban–rural settlement data, and GADM administrative boundaries in ArcGIS 10.8 to estimate population exposure to landslide‐prone areas from the national scale to the district scale. title: Integrating land-use dynamics, water quality, and multi-criteria ecological suitability for fish sanctuary prioritization in three major river basins of Bangladesh
abstract: Riverine ecosystems in monsoon-dominated regions are increasingly constrained by interacting pressures from land-use change, hydrological alteration, and water-quality degradation, yet these drivers are rarely assessed within a unified framework. This study presents a reproducible, basin-scale framework integrating multi-season (monsoon–dry) land-use dynamics (2000–2020), hydrochemical assessment (including nutrients and trace metals), and GIS-based Multi-Criteria ecological modeling to delineate fish sanctuary suitability across the Ganges–Padma, Brahmaputra–Jamuna, and Barak–Meghna basins of

title: The Empire Under One Umbrella: Espionage, Reporting and the Communications System of the Mauryan State in the Aśokan Edicts, the Contemporary Textual Sources and Recent Scholarship
abstract: This paper argues that the Mauryan empire could not have been held together under a single authority without a system for acquiring, moving and verifying information, and that this proposition — which no surviving document states in so many words — can be established by correlating four independent bodies of evidence: the Aśokan inscriptions, the Arthaśāstra, the Greek testimony as transmitted by later authors, and the Buddhist literary tradition. title: Instantaneous heating rate forcing differentiates tropical high-cloud adjustments across greenhouse gases
abstract: Tropical high clouds are central to large-scale circulation and the hydrological cycle. The consensus expectation is that they rise and contract under surface warming, but their fast adjustment to greenhouse gas (GHG) concentrations is diverse. All GHGs reduce atmospheric longwave loss, yet tropical high clouds can increase or decrease depending on the gas. Using a model hierarchy with unchanged sea surface temperature, we find increased tropical high cloud for CO2 and decreased tropical high cloud for CH4 and N2O. These diverging responses are primarily driven by changes in the vertical struc
publisher: American Association for the Advancement of Science

title: Emergence of nonequilibrium Lieb excitations in periodically-driven strongly-interacting bosons
abstract: We study the exact nonequilibrium spectral function of a gas of strongly correlated Tonks-Girardeau bosons subjected to a strong periodic drive. Utilizing the theory of Floquet spectral function in conjunction with the Bose-Fermi mapping theorem, we show that nonequilibrium Lieb modes emerge if the underlying mapped fermions form a Floquet-Fermi sea. In the low-frequency regime, the exact analysis reveals the emergence of characteristic linear Lieb excitations for the bosonic system, while the underlying mapped fermions displays the wide Dirac-like linear dispersion.

title: Global patterns are key to understanding macroevolution
abstract: Regional diversification patterns are increasingly being used to investigate spatial heterogeneity in biodiversity evolution and its drivers. However, estimating and interpreting regional diversification rates is complicated by the fact that regional diversity fluctuations reflect multiple biological processes and may be more sensitive to temporal sampling bias than global patterns. Here, we assess the biological fidelity and sampling sensitivity of regional diversification rates using fossil occurrences of marine invertebrates. title: RANCANG BANGUN SISTEM MONITORING KETINGGIAN AIR PADA BANJIR ROB MENGGUNAKAN TEKNOLOGI IOT BERBASIS WEBSITE
abstract: Wilayah pesisir Muara Angke, Jakarta Utara, sering mengalami banjir rob yang mengganggu aktivitas sosial dan ekonomi masyarakat, sementara informasi peringatan dini yang tersedia masih bersifat umum dan belum menggambarkan kondisi ketinggian air secara langsung di lokasi terdampak. title: Using spatio-temporal models to assist ecosystem-based fisheries management: a New Zealand case study
abstract: Tools to understand or predict ecosystem changes (e.g., fish community analyses) and the impacts of management measures on ecosystem components (e.g., ecosystem simulation models) are instrumental to the success of ecosystem-based fisheries management (EBFM). We developed a workflow using vector autoregressive spatio-temporal (VAST) models to assist EBFM in the Chatham Rise middle depth (CHAT MD) region, located in New Zealand waters. journal: Reviews in Fish Biology and Fisheries

title: Smartphone-based mapping of home ignition zone attributes for wildland–urban interface fire risk assessment
abstract: Background Assessing home ignition zone attributes is essential for reducing wildfire risk in wildland–urban interface (WUI) communities; however, traditional satellite imagery often lacks sufficient spatial resolution and timely updates to capture localized fuel conditions near structures. Aims This study develops and validates a smartphone-based framework for real-time detection, mapping and 3D visualization of building features and defensible space fuel to support wildfire risk assessment and mitigation in WUI environments. title: Population genetic structure and connectivity of Enhalus acoroides along the Southern Vietnamese coastline
abstract: Introduction Seagrass meadows have undergone substantial declines in Vietnam over recent decades owing to habitat loss, climate change, nutrient enrichment, and other anthropogenic disturbances. Enhalus acoroides , a dominant large tropical seagrass, has experienced marked reductions in distribution and abundance, yet information on its population genetic structure remains limited. title: SAFEBORDERS (DIGITAL CONVERSATIONAL AGENT): PREVENTION OF SMUGGLING OF CIGARETTES, DRUGS AND CONTROLLED GOODS AT MALAYSIAN BORDERS
abstract: This study presents the design, development, and usability evaluation of SafeBorders, an AI-powered bilingual digital conversational agent developed to support public advocacy and community engagement in preventing the smuggling of cigarettes, drugs, and controlled goods at Malaysian borders. Grounded in Mayer’s Cognitive Theory of Multimedia Learning, Social Agency Theory, and Conversational Design Principles, and guided by user-centered design, SafeBorders delivers general safety information, emergency guidance, and a structured incident reporting mechanism across web and mobile platforms in

title: Industrial Development in Protected Zones: A Four-Gate Legal Assessment of the Tahura Ngurah Rai Factory Case in Bali
abstract: The reported construction-material factory linked to Russian investment near Bali's Tahura Ngurah Rai highlights a recurring difficulty in environmental governance: the coexistence of land certificates, business registrations, spatial restrictions and conservation boundaries. This article examines the legal consequences of that overlap through normative legal research using statutory, conceptual and documentary case approaches. journal: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF MULTIDISCIPLINARY RESEARCH AND ANALYSIS

title: Spatiotemporal analysis of land use change in the Eastern Slopes of the Jerusalem Area
abstract: Abstract Urban expansion is one of the main drivers of land use changes in the Central Palestinian Mountains. It influences the basic environmental components, including water, soil, and specifically vegetation cover. In the present study, the study area has experienced noticeable land use changes over the past three decades, resulting in many adverse impacts on the environment. This study aims to examine land use changes and identify the main drivers and consequences of these changes on vegetation cover during the period 1997 and 2022. title: Complete mitochondrial genome of Arcuatula japonica (Mollusca: Mytilidae: Crenellinae) and its phylogenetic analysis
abstract: Arcuatula japonica (Dunker, 1857) (Mollusca: Mytilidae: Crenellinae) is a marine mussel distributed primarily in the northwestern Pacific. To clarify its evolutionary position and evaluate the taxonomic status of Crenellinae, we sequenced and characterized the complete mitochondrial genome of A. japonica. The mitogenome is 16,198 bp in length and contains 13 protein-coding genes (PCGs), 22 transfer RNA genes (tRNAs), 2 ribosomal RNA genes (rRNAs), and 1 non-coding control region (CR), with an A + T bias (68.7%). title: Analysis of Fin Stabilizer Effects on 100 GT Fishing Vessel Resistance Using Computational Fluid Dynamics
abstract: Fishing vessels require good hydrodynamic efficiency to limit propulsion power and energy consumption. Adding a fin stabilizer can modify the flow pattern, pressure distribution, wetted area, and consequently the total resistance; however, studies specifically addressing its resistance effect on a 100 GT fishing vessel remain limited. This study compares the flow characteristics and ship resistance before and after fin-stabilizer installation using Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD). title: Isolation and characterization of human skin-derived bacteriophages with antibacterial and antibiofilm activity against coagulase-negative staphylococci
abstract: Abstract Coagulase-negative staphylococci (CoNS), particularly Staphylococcus epidermidis and Staphylococcus capitis , are significant opportunistic pathogens associated with biofilm-related infections and antimicrobial resistance. Although bacteriophage therapy is a promising alternative to antibiotics, human skin-derived phages targeting clinically important CoNS remain poorly characterized. Four bacteriophages were isolated from facial skin swabs of healthy volunteers, and two (phages Se_20 and Se_42) were selected for detailed characterization. title: Recurrence lacunarity of spatial data
abstract: Abstract Quantifying the structure and heterogeneity of complex spatial patterns remains a key challenge in spatial data analysis. Recurrence plots (RPs) offer a powerful method for visualizing the recurrent spatial patterns in such data. To quantify the structure of spatial recurrences, we extend the normalized recurrence lacunarity (nRL), a measure of the homogeneity of an RP, to the analysis of spatial RPs. title: The Evolutionary History of Early Ray‐Finned Fishes (Pan‐Actinopterygii)
abstract: One out of every two vertebrate species is a ray-finned fish (Actinopterygii). The ~380-million-year fossil record of ray-finned fishes provides a window into the evolutionary history of actinopterygian diversity in deep time. The actinopterygian fossil record shows that the ray-finned fish crown group (Actinopterygii) lived alongside speciose members of now extinct lineages, collectively referred to as early actinopterygians. title: Circulating in the oyster immune system: multi-compartment modeling reveals dynamic intercellular trafficking of biodegradable nanoplastics
abstract: Studies of the cellular fate of nanoplastics (NPs) in bivalves commonly overlook the dynamic trafficking of particles among immune cells. Here, we established a multi-compartment kinetic framework using time-resolved measurements of hemocyte populations for 2-h following a 1-h in vitro exposure to polylactic acid biodegradable nanoplastics (PLA-NPs). title: Biofilm-host immunometabolic crosstalk in Staphylococcus aureus orthopedic implant infection: mechanisms and translational constraints
abstract: Orthopedic implant biofilms are not only antibiotic-tolerant bacterial communities but metabolically active niches that reshape host immunity. Compared with planktonic infection, mature biofilms impose spatial and metabolic constraints that can uncouple leukocyte recruitment from sterilizing activity. Neutrophils can penetrate and phagocytose portions of Staphylococcus aureus biofilms, but clearance becomes incomplete as biofilms mature and may coexist with degranulation and neutrophil extracellular trap-associated tissue injury. title: Spatial Analysis of Atmospheric Pollutants in An-Najaf Governorate Based on Sentinel-5 Satellite Observations
abstract: Sentinel-5P satellite imagery, in combination with Geographic Information Systems (GIS), was utilized to analyze the spatial distribution of the atmospheric pollutant gases—ozone (O₃), sulfur dioxide (SO₂), and carbon monoxide (CO)—across An-Najaf Governorate in central Iraq. The study aimed to assess patterns of pollutant concentration and identify the anthropogenic and environmental factors influencing their distribution. title: Chemical stress drives opposing bacterial biomass responses at the single-cell level
abstract: Abstract Microbial biomass is a central functional trait governing nutrient turnover and trophic transfer in aquatic ecosystems, yet how chemical stress reshapes biomass at the level of individual cells remains poorly resolved. Conventional toxicity assays primarily detect population-level growth inhibition and overlook sublethal physiological responses and heterogeneity within microbial populations. title: A Comprehensive Methodology for the Integrated Assessment of Road Safety of Transport and Technological Vehicles Based on Fuzzy Logic
abstract: In conditions of increasing complexity and intensity of transportation systems, ensuring road safety requires a transition to proactive and predictive methods of integral risk management. In this work a hierarchical model based on fuzzy logic has been developed to assess the safety of vehicle fleets by aggregating heterogeneous real-time data. To implement a comprehensive assessment, an algorithm has been proposed that performs automated multi-criteria analysis by merging key safety indicators related to technical condition, driver behavior, and operational factors. title: Feasibility study of using magnetic and thermoelectric methods for the assessment of storage-induced changes in flux-cored welding wires
abstract: The lack of knowledge regarding whether a welding consumable remains suitable for the welding process or has undergone degradation that precludes its further use constitutes a significant challenge. Appropriate control procedures and effective evaluation methods may contribute to addressing this issue. This study presents the results of investigations concerning the applicability of magnetic and thermoelectric methods for such an assessment. journal: The International Journal of Advanced Manufacturing Technology

title: Development of a city level nitrogen dioxide exposure (CLeNE) intelligence platform for West Africa
abstract: Abstract Nitrogen dioxide (NO 2 ) is a major urban air pollutant, yet assessment of population exposure remains challenging across West Africa due to lack of uncoordinated sparse monitoring infrastructure. We present the City-Level Nitrogen Dioxide Exposure (CLeNE) platform, an interactive exposure intelligence system that integrates Sentinel-5P TROPOMI NO 2 observations, population data, and city boundaries to quantify and visualize urban exposure burden. title: Macroevolutionary dynamics and predictors of tropical rain forest plant diversity
abstract: Tropical rain forest is the most diverse terrestrial biome, yet the drivers of its diversification across space and time remain poorly understood. Although heterogeneous diversification rates, including both ancient and recent radiations, have been reported, these dynamics have rarely been examined within a single lineage across deep evolutionary timescales. Here, we reconstruct a dated phylogenomic tree of the pantropical plant family Annonaceae, sampling 2045 species (∼82% of its diversity) and spanning ∼100 million years of evolutionary history. title: From Content Coverage to Competence Development: Shifting Mechanics Education Toward Modeling and Reflection
abstract: ABSTRACT Many engineering courses are still organized according to a predominantly deductive and content‐oriented approach: theoretical foundations are introduced first, while authentic disciplinary activity is often postponed to later stages of the curriculum. This contribution argues that such an approach is insufficient for sustainable competence development in mechanics education. Instead, courses and problem statements should be designed from intended capabilities and observable learning outcomes. title: Nanocomposite of TiO2 and Phase-transition-derived α-Fe2O3 for Enhancing Photocatalytic Dye Degradation
abstract: Although a-Fe2O3 is a promising photocatalyst for Advanced Oxidation Processes in dye-polluted wastewater treatment, its practical efficiency is limited by inherent drawbacks including rapid electron-hole recombination and poor electron mobility. This study proposes a TiO2/a-Fe2O3 nanocomposite system to enhance dye removal efficiency of a-Fe2O3, specifically Methylene Blue (MB), in which hierarchical porous, coral-like a-Fe2O3 was prepared via a thermal phase transition process from g-Fe2O3. title: Antioxidant Activity of Unsaturated Fatty Acid Isolated From The Green Algae (Halimeda opuntia)
abstract: Halimeda is a genus of green macroalgae found in Indonesian waters, including the waters around Ternate Island. Coastal communities typically consume algae as a food source. However, over time, knowledge about algae has expanded, and people have become more aware of their nutritional content. This study aimed to determine the antioxidant activity and fatty acid composition of green algae from waters off Ternate Island. journal: Journal of Marine Biotechnology and Immunology

title: Standardized Ophthalmic Examination Protocol For Fish Developed During Assessment of 274 Eyes in Rockfish (Family Sebastidae)
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To develop and evaluate a practical, standardized ophthalmic examination protocol for teleost fish using captive rockfish (Family Sebastidae) as a pilot population. METHODS: One hundred twenty-seven captive rockfish housed at Hatfield Marine Science Center and 11 newly acquired rockfish at the Oregon Coast Aquarium, representing 9 Sebastes and 1 Sebastolobus species. title: Diseño de una propuesta de gestión y preservación digital basada en TIC para los proyectos académicos estudiantiles de la sede regional Chorotega de la Universidad Nacional de Costa Rica
abstract: The primary objective of this article is to present the design of an Information and Communication Technology (ICT)-based web application for the management and preservation of academic projects created by students at the Chorotega Regional Campus of the National University of Costa Rica. The study employed a descriptive design to identify the characteristics of the phenomenon, subjects, and population under study, using a mixed-methods research approach that integrated both qualitative and quantitative perspectives. title: From Passive Participation to Self-Reliance: Community Empowerment through the INSPIRASI Program in Binor Village
abstract: Binor Village, a coastal village in Ring 1 of the Paiton Power Plant (PLTU Paiton), has diverse economic potential, yet residents’ livelihoods remain vulnerable to seasonal and market fluctuations, while community participation in social activities needs strengthening. Social mapping data show 57% of families earn below the district minimum wage, 90% have no savings, and individual participation is nearly zero, despite active village institutions (PKK, Posyandu, BUMDes, Karang Taruna). title: Probabilistic Seismic Hazard Assessment of Southern Offshore East Java Using Poisson and Gutenberg–Richter Models
abstract: The southern region of East Java is part of the Sunda Subduction Zone, which has high seismic activity due to the convergence of the Indo-Australian and Eurasian Plates. This study aims to analyze the probability of earthquake occurrences in the southern offshore of East Java using the Poisson distribution and the Gutenberg–Richter law. Earthquake catalog data from the International Seismological Centre (ISC) for the period 1996–2025 were used. title: Improving Housing Quality of the Bajo Tribe through a Self-Help Approach: A Case Study in Muna Regency, Indonesia
abstract: This study explains the living conditions of the coastal Bajo tribe in Muna Regency, Indonesia, and examines their potential for improving housing quality through a community-led self-help approach. Adopting a convergent parallel mixed-methods design, fieldwork was conducted across three purposively selected vulnerable settlements: Tapitapi, Lagasa, and Pasikuta villages (N = 259). Quantitative housing evaluation against PUPR/BPS standards reveals severe structural and environmental deprivation. title: Hymenoptera of Galápagos: diversity and distribution of one of the most species-rich insect orders in the archipelago
abstract: Despite the importance of the Galápagos archipelago as a key site for the study of biodiversity and evolution, significant components of its invertebrate biodiversity, particularly Hymenoptera, remain insufficiently documented. Occurrence records of Hymenoptera from 1959–2025 were combined from structured surveys of non-formicid Hymenoptera, long-term ant sampling, museum collections, literature, and online sources to assess the richness, distribution, and species composition of hymenopterans across the archipelago.
