title: Spatiotemporal evolution and influencing factors of regional resilience in China: evidence from provincial panel data using Spearman-CRITIC and XGBoost-CatBoost-SHAP
abstract: Regional resilience is closely related to sustainable development because it reflects the capacity of a region to maintain stable economic, social, ecological, and infrastructural functions under long-term transformation. Based on provincial panel data for China from 2007 to 2024, this study constructs a regional resilience evaluation system covering economic resilience, social development resilience, ecological and environmental resilience, and infrastructure resilience. title: Head-to-tail assembled borphyrins for solid-state lithium extraction
abstract: Abstract Lithium is a critical mineral for advancing greener technologies. Extraction of lithium ions (Li⁺) from sea salt, minerals, and waste is important, but has been hindered by the lack of extraction methods that offer both high selectivity and strong lithium affinity. Here, we report a dioxaborole-linked, head-to-tail assembled macrocycle – termed borphyrin – featuring a rigid cavity with a 16-crown-4-like configuration. title: Solar resource assessment and performance forecasting of a utility-scale photovoltaic plant in Bhutan: A high-altitude Himalayan case study
abstract: High-altitude solar photovoltaic (PV) deployment can diversify electricity supply in hydropower-dominated Himalayan regions, particularly during the dry season. This study evaluates the technical feasibility, site suitability, solar resource, and forecast performance of a proposed utility-scale plant at Ladrong, Bhutan. The method integrates GIS terrain screening, slope and aspect classification, horizon and near-shading analysis, grid connectivity, and PVsyst simulation. abstract: Epizootic Ulcerative Syndrome (EUS) is a fish disease caused by the fungal pathogen Aphanomyces invadans and is responsible for significant economic losses in fisheries. This study aimed to detect the presence of Aphanomyces invadans in marble goby (Oxyeleotris marmorata) using the Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) method at the West Sumatra Animal, Fish, and Plant Quarantine Center (BKHIT) Laboratory. title: Nicotinium-based surface-active ionic liquids as antimicrobial surfactants: Micellization properties, antibiofilm activity, and biocompatibility
abstract: A new family of nicotinium-based surface-active ionic liquids (CₙNicBr, n = 10-16) was synthesized by N-alkylation of nicotine and characterized by NMR, MS and thermogravimetry (stable to 215 °C). Aqueous association, assessed by conductimetry, fluorescence, tensiometry and dynamic light scattering, gave critical micelle concentrations of 0.58-36 mM and a chain-length-independent apparent monomeric pKa of 5.6 ± 0.1 for the pyrrolidinium nitrogen. title: Relay Architectures and Ecological Strategies of Quorum Sensing Effects on Microbial Interactions
abstract: Microbial communities assemble in heterogeneous habitats, where quorum sensing (QS) influences interactions beyond signalling populations. Yet QS studies are commonly organized by signal type, circuit, or phenotype, obscuring the routes by which a QS event reaches neighbouring populations and why they prevail in particular settings. title: A new teleosauroid (Crocodylomorpha, Thalattosuchia) with a unique dentition from the Middle Jurassic of eastern Morocco
abstract: The Mesozoic and early Paleogene of Morocco provides a rich and extensive record of crocodylomorphs encompassing a wide range of skull, dental morphologies, and paleoecologies. Here we describe a new longirostrine teleosaurid thalattosuchian, Ctenosuchus tenuidens, gen. et sp. nov. with a needle-like dentition from a Middle Jurassic fluvio-lacustrine sequence of the Talsint–Anoual area of Figuig Province, southeastern Morocco. title: Introgression Shapes Genetic Variation Associated With Humid Environments in Aedes aegypti Mosquitoes From Saudi Arabia
abstract: Introgression between genetically distinct populations generates variation that may promote adaptation to diverse environmental conditions. In the mosquito Aedes aegypti, the forest-associated subspecies Aedes aegypti formosus (Aaf) underwent a domestication process approximately 5000 years ago, giving rise to the globally invasive, human-associated arbovirus vector Aedes aegypti aegypti (Aaa). Despite extensive human-mediated transport, the two subspecies remain largely distinct, with admixture documented mainly in coastal Africa and Saudi Arabia. title: Where Menstrual Education and Environmental Justice Converge
abstract: When discussed together, menstrual and socioenvironmental health often focus on questions of hygiene and risk management, centering the materialities, distribution, and disposal of menstrual products. The toxicity of disposable menstrual products has long been a matter of concern, with growing public attention to endocrine disruptors (EDs) accompanying the expansion of a marketplace for “eco-friendly” options. title: A Comparative Analysis of Open Data Portals: The Cases of Ordu and Tampere
abstract: Open data has become an important component of contemporary urban governance, contributing to transparency, accountability, and data-driven decision-making. However, the effectiveness of open data systems depends not only on data availability but also on interoperability, standardization, and the ability of data infrastructures to support reuse and integration within urban service ecosystems. title: Flood Risk Assessment and Vulnerability Analysis in Ogbese, Ondo State, Nigeria: Implications for Sustainable Urban Planning
abstract: Flooding has become one of the most frequent and destructive environmental hazards in Nigeria, with increasing impacts on lives, livelihoods, and infrastructure, particularly in rapidly expanding peri-urban communities. Despite the recurrent occurrence of flood events in Ogbese, limited empirical information exists on the combined influence of physical and socio-economic factors that shape flood vulnerability and risk. title: A case study on SWMM based evaluation of rain barrel and downspout disconnection scenarios for urban stormwater management
abstract: Colombo, the executive and judicial capital of Sri Lanka, is located on the southwestern coast of the country and has experienced rapid urbanization in recent years, driven by infrastructure development, land use changes, and the growing impacts of climate change. These factors have significantly increased the frequency and severity of urban flooding. Therefore, this study explores the stormwater management problems in the 686.3-hectare study catchment, adjacent to the Kelani River in suburban Colombo, and proposes effective stormwater management strategies to avoid flooding in the area. title: Repolitisasi Bencana Pesisir: Sintesis Pedagogi Ekologi Politis pada Pembelajaran Geografi di Kurikulum Merdeka
abstract: Kawasan pesisir utara Jawa menghadapi krisis sosial-ekologis akut berupa amblasan tanah, abrasi, dan banjir rob. Namun, pendidikan geografi sering kali mendepolitisasi rentetan bencana tersebut dengan membingkainya semata-mata sebagai fenomena alamiah. title: Arbuscular Mycorrhizal fungi alleviate salinity stress in Avicennia marina through morphophysiological and biochemical modulation
abstract: Increasing salinity threatens coastal mangrove ecosystems worldwide by impairing plant growth, physiological function, and biochemical processes, ultimately reducing productivity and survival. The present study was conducted to examine the impact of arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) on Avicennia marina under different salt concentrations (9, 14, and 19 dS/m). This study included four treatments i.e. negative control (only salt: T1), species consortium of Glomus (T2), species consortium of Gigaspora (T3), consortium of both Glomus and Gigaspora spp. (T4) along with positive control (T0). title: Low-cost Efficient Wireless Intelligent Sensors (LEWIS) IoT-Based Rainfall Monitoring
abstract: Rainfall measurement with high spatial and temporal resolution is critical for flood forecasting, drought mitigation, and disaster preparedness. Rainfall patterns are highly variable, both geographically and over time. This variability presents a significant challenge for monitoring, as rain gauges can accurately capture temporal patterns only at a single location. Furthermore, the high cost of commercial instruments restricts their widespread deployment, and rain gauge networks often fail to adequately capture the spatial heterogeneity of precipitation patterns. title: Land-Use Change and Socio-Economic Impacts on Food Security in Aimas District, Sorong Regency
abstract: This study examines agricultural land-use change, socio-economic transformation, and food security implications in Aimas District, Sorong Regency, Indonesia. The study integrated GIS-based spatial analysis of land-cover data for 2014, 2019, and 2024 with a socio-economic survey of 210 households, complemented by direct field observation. title: Digital transformation and third places: Mapping public spaces in Bekasi Regency
abstract: As an urban and industrial area, Bekasi Regency faces challenges in providing inclusive and multifunctional public spaces that support social interaction, community cohesion, and economic activities. The limited availability of formal public spaces has encouraged the informal use of vacant spaces by local communities, indicating a need for both formal and informal “third places.” This study aims to develop a spatial database of third places in Bekasi Regency, identify their distribution patterns, and evaluate user experience through a phenomenological approach. abstract: This study examined the role of pre-boarding training in enhancing the mental health preparedness, safety awareness, and professional preparedness of Filipino seafarers who entered maritime service after March 2020. A convergent parallel mixed-methods design was employed involving 390 purposively selected seafarers who had completed at least one sea contract and participated in a manning agency pre-boarding training program. abstract: A GPS-GIS based soil survey of the Agronomy Research Farm, College of Agriculture, Dapoli, Maharashtra was carried out during 2024-25 to characterize the physical and morphological properties of the soils. Geo-referenced surface (0-30 cm) and sub-surface (30-45 cm) soil samples were collected from 91 locations (182 samples) using a differential GPS and analysed for soil colour, bulk density, particle density and texture. abstract: The current study evaluated the genetic characterization and differentiation of oil families in the units of the Yamama, Nahr Umr, and Mishrif reservoirs of the Ratawi oil field, south of Iraq. The combination of bulk properties, stable carbon isotopes, and molecular biomarkers reveals a distinct pattern of hydrocarbon generation, migration, and accumulation, influenced by salt-induced tectonics in the studyarea. title: Floristic Diversity, Habitat Preference, and Ecological Distribution of Zingiberaceae Species in Different Regions of West Bengal
abstract: The Zingiberaceae, a family of aromatic, rhizomatous herbs with its principal centre of diversity in tropical and subtropical Asia, is well represented in the state of West Bengal, which spans an unusually steep environmental gradient from the humid Eastern Himalayan foothills to the saline Sundarbans delta within a comparatively small area. title: Optimization of the Certification Process for Indonesian-Flagged Ships to Enhance Maritime Safety and Security at the Tanjung Priok Main Port Authority and Harbor Master Office (KSOP Utama Tanjung Priok)
abstract: This study aims to analyze the implementation of certification for Indonesian-flagged ships at the Tanjung Priok Main Port Authority and Harbor Master Office (KSOP Utama Tanjung Priok), identify the constraints encountered, examine its contribution to maritime safety and security, and formulate optimization efforts. The study employs a qualitative descriptive approach. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, direct observation, and documentation involving relevant parties in the certification process. title: Towards an integrated approach to evaluating biodiversity‐ and water‐sensitive urban design: A review of popular software tools
abstract: Abstract Globally, cities are recognising a need to incorporate blue‐green infrastructure and ecosystem‐based approaches into urban design and development. With this recognition comes the need to design for biodiversity and water together—though current approaches typically consider these systems independently. The consequences of this are that relationships between biodiversity and water are overlooked, leading to a reduction in system resilience and functionality. title: Beyond Basic ICT Access: Pedagogical Integration of Geospatial Technologies in Geography Teaching in Temeke Municipality, Tanzania
abstract: Digital technology is now central to competence-based Geography education, yet access and pedagogical use remain uneven in Tanzanian public schools. This study examined how ICT integration supports Geography teaching and learning in Temeke Municipality. Its main objective was to assess whether available technology was being converted into subject-specific, learner-centred practice. A mixed-methods approach and cross-sectional survey design were used. The sample comprised 120 participants: 100 students, 16 Geography teachers, and four Ward Education Officers. title: Materialidades efímeras de las artes escénicas: el caso chileno-costarricense en la colección Huellas del exilio de Proyecto Arde y LaMAE
abstract: The purpose of this article is to analyze the theater posters and playbills that form part of Huellas del exilio collection, housed within the digital archives of Proyecto Arde in collaboration with LaMAE, and produced during the Chilean exile in Costa Rica. To this end, this study approaches these materials through the documentary typology of ephemera, investigating core axes related to: their participation within print culture, their modes of circulation and deployment across subjects and surfaces for public display, the forms of reading they elicit and their materiality. title: The Role of Geographical Indications in Sustainable Coffee Tourism in Forest Areas: Lessons from Lemukih Coffee
abstract: Geographical Indications (GIs) protect distinctive local products while supporting community development and sustainable tourism. However, their effectiveness depends on regional government capacity to integrate product protection, economic development, environmental conservation, and tourism. This study examines the potential of Lemukih Robusta Coffee as a regional flagship product, evaluates the effectiveness of the Buleleng Regency Government’s policies in managing and protecting its GI in areas adjacent to forests, and explores how GI protection can support sustainable coffee tourism. title: Evaluating Carniolan honey bee (Apis mellifera carnica) lines under contrasting ecological zones
abstract: This study evaluates four breeding lines of the Carniolan honey bee, Apis mellifera carnica, across distinct ecological zones of Serbia and Montenegro. The objective was to assess phenotypic, morphometric, and isoenzyme polymorphism of local populations adapted to contrasting climatic and altitudinal conditions. Two Serbian lines (lowland Vršac and mountainous Vranje) and two Montenegrin lines (mountainous Bijelo Polje and coastal Sutomore) were examined. title: Fabrication of a citric acid-crosslinked β-cyclodextrin/silica composite and its selective adsorption of cholesterol from crude fish oil
abstract: A novel β-cyclodextrin-modified silica composite (β-CD-SiO 2 ) was prepared by in situ thermal esterification for selective elimination of cholesterol in tuna oil refining. Characterisations revealed the effective immobilisation of β-cyclodextrin (β-CD) onto mesoporous silica (mean pore size 24.40 nm). title: Improved estimation of lake storage variation via DEM reconstruction integrating elevation and morphological constraints
abstract: High-quality Digital Elevation Models (DEMs) are essential for accurately estimating lake storage variations, but the high cost of in-situ measurements limits their large-scale application. Reconstructing DEMs from remote sensing-derived lake contours is a promising low-cost alternative. However, most existing methods primarily rely on elevation-matched contours and discard those without elevation data. title: Photosynthesis of Zinc Oxide Nanoparticles from Portieria hornemannii: Multifunctional Biological Activities and Molecular Docking Insights for Cervical Cancer
abstract: Red seaweed is regarded as an environmentally friendly and safe material for the biosynthesis of nanoparticles. Biomass of seaweeds is a renewable and commercial source of marine resources. In this research, zinc oxide nanoparticles were produced exploiting the red alga Portieria hornemannii. The formation of zinc oxide nanoparticles was indicated through the change in color of the test mixture recorded with the assistance of the UV-visible spectrophotometer. title: The Mediating Role of Spatial Skills in Learning Kinematic Graphics Assisted by Vector Animation Videos
abstract: Kinematic graph interpretation is a basic physics competency that often challenges students because of abstract vector representations and weak geometric transformation skills. This study analyzes the influence of vector animation videos on kinematic graph learning, with spatial skills as a mediating variable. A quantitative approach with a quasi-experimental design was applied to 60 Grade X students of SMAS Ta’miriyah Surabaya. abstract: ABSTRACT Fifteen new actinomycin analogs were obtained from the marine‐derived Streptomyces polyantibioticus S4D258. title: The Impact of Virtual Dental Clinic Color and Image Modifications on Anxiety Reduction in Undergraduate Dental Students
abstract: Dental students often experience stress due to the curriculum’s theoretical and practical demands, whichcan negatively affect their well-being. Previous research suggests that room colors and images can reduceanxiety in certain populations. However, no studies have examined this effect among dental students. title: Culturas académicas e internacionalización de la educación geográfica: EUROGEO y la Unión Geográfica Internacional en la intersección de los enfoques global, anglosajón, continental e iberoamericano
abstract: La creación de la Comisión de Educación Geográfica, de la Unión Geográfica Internacional, en 1952, y de EUROGEO, la Asociación de Geógrafos Europeos, en 1979, ha permitido durante varias décadas la colaboración internacional entre didactas de la geografía y, consecuentemente, el intercambio, la difusión y la innovación de ideas, concepciones y métodos para la enseñanza de la geografía y de un mundo cada vez más integrado por los procesos de globalización territorial: política, económica, social y cultural.A pesar de la gran influencia de la geografía anglosajona en la producción científica de

title: Mobilizing Dynamic‐Capability Microfoundations for Sustainability‐Oriented Innovation: The Role of Innovation Champions
abstract: ABSTRACT Organizations face growing pressure to respond to environmental and social challenges, yet research has not sufficiently explained how organizational actors mobilise dynamic‐capability microfoundations across the development of sustainability‐oriented innovations. Drawing on 68 semistructured interviews conducted between March and November 2024 across 18 EU and UK marine firms, this qualitative study examines how innovation champions and related actors support sensing, seizing, and reconfiguring. title: Multiple introductions and spread of novel reassortant highly pathogenic avian influenza A (H5N1) clade 2.3.4.4b viruses via wild birds, South Korea, 2024–2025
abstract: Between 14 October 2024 and 24 March 2025, 43 cases of clade 2.3.4.4b highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) type A (H5N1) infections in wild birds and 1 case in a leopard cat were detected through the national HPAI surveillance program. title: Aramid inserts to reduce shear fracture in GFRP composite materials for aeronautical and naval use
abstract: Delamination is a critical failure mode in glass fiber reinforced polymer (GFRP) laminates used in artisanal boatbuilding, particularly under dynamic loading associated with slamming phenomena. This study evaluates the effectiveness of interlaminar aramid fiber stitching as a reinforcement technique to improve the interlaminar shear strength and damage tolerance of GFRP laminates manufactured using traditional hand lay-up processes. title: Far-Red Turn-On Fluorogenic Probe for Versatile Detection of Inorganic Polyphosphates
abstract: Abstract Inorganic polyphosphate (polyP) is a ubiquitous phosphate biopolymer involved in diverse cellular processes. Despite its significance, selective detection of polyP remains challenging because of its simple and highly charged structure. Here, we report a far-red fluorogenic turn-on chemosensor for selective polyP detection and imaging, SiX-DPA-Zn. title: Favorable habitats of endangered halophytes harbor unique soil properties and bacterial communities, with a dominant root-associated genus promoting host plant growth
abstract: Understanding how edaphic factors and root-associated bacterial communities interact to shape plant growth is essential for effective conservation of halophytic species in coastal ecosystems. We investigated relationships among bulk soil, rhizosphere, and root bacterial microbiota; soil physicochemical properties; and Salicornia europaea growth spanning three distinct areas (Lakeside Park, Ubaranai and Misaki) within a brackish lake in Japan. title: Integrative transcriptomic and lipidomic analysis of the effects of Eucommia ulmoides on growth performance and lipid metabolism in Larimichthys crocea
abstract: Introduction Larimichthys crocea is an economically important marine aquaculture species, and improving growth performance while maintaining lipid metabolic homeostasis is important for its sustainable production. This study investigated the effects of dietary Eucommia ulmoides supplementation on growth performance and lipid metabolism in L. crocea and explored the underlying molecular basis using integrated transcriptomic and lipidomic analyses. title: MerR-type regulator ZccR links zinc homeostasis to biofilm formation and interspecies competition in Streptococcus mutans
abstract: Objectives Zinc is widely present in the oral microenvironment and can influence the growth of oral bacteria. ZccR is a MerR-type transcriptional regulator that controls zinc efflux in Streptococcus mutans ( S. mutans ), but its role in biofilm virulence and interspecies competition with oral commensals remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the role of ZccR in the formation of single-species biofilms of S. mutans and dual-species biofilms with oral commensal streptococci, and its underlying regulatory mechanisms. abstract: Abstract Mountainous transport corridors are increasingly exposed to interacting natural hazards that intensify infrastructure, socio-economic, and land-use risks. However, most susceptibility assessments for high-mountain corridors still focus on single hazards or rely heavily on expert-based weighting, which can introduce subjectivity into spatial decision-making. abstract: The Wazwaz–Kaur equation is a significant nonlinear partial differential equation. This equation is used to describe nonlinear wave propagation in fields including fluid dynamics, plasma physics, and other areas of mathematical physics. In this study, we investigate analytical solutions of the $(3+1)$-dimensional Wazwaz–Kaur Boussinesq Equation (WKBE). title: Nature-based flood assessment for vulnerable educational infrastructure under tropical urban conditions
abstract: Worldwide, urban rainwater flooding is increasingly affecting small-scale public infrastructure in tropical cities. Consequently, drainage decisions are often made with limited hydrometric data. Therefore, this study aims to evaluate flood control alternatives using the Nature-based Solutions (NBS) approach through participatory assessment and modeling with the Stormwater Management Model (SWMM) at a vulnerable educational infrastructure (VEI) in Durán, Ecuador. abstract: Debates on the future of smallholder farming in sub-Saharan Africa often interpret rural youth mobility and non-farm work as withdrawal from agriculture. This article examines how rural youth in coastal Guinea-Bissau engage with labour- and knowledge-intensive, climate-vulnerable mangrove swamp rice farming, and the conditions under which agriculture remains part of their imagined futures. title: From tourism pressure to overtourism vulnerability regimes: A municipal impact assessment framework for sustainable destination governance
abstract: Overtourism is increasingly understood as a multidimensional sustainability challenge, yet local decision-makers still lack replicable tools for assessing where tourism pressure may translate into territorial vulnerability. This paper develops a municipal impact-assessment framework for diagnosing overtourism vulnerability regimes. The analysis follows a two-step logic. abstract: This study examines how Chinese high school students perceive and respond to online misinformation and how their responses are shaped by school, family, and wider social contexts. Four focus group discussions were conducted with 24 students aged 15-17 from two public high schools in a southeastern coastal city. abstract: Ti 6 Al 4 V components in aerospace and marine applications frequently suffer from coupled mechanical wear and corrosive degradation across severe temperature regimes. While TiAlN-based systems offer good wear resistance, tailoring Cr incorporation to concurrently enhance passivity without triggering microstructural embrittlement remains underexplored. abstract: ABSTRACT Tumor microenvironment (TME) interactive platforms are promising for accurate diagnostics and therapeutics. title: Passive acoustic monitoring for the estimation of density of the singing lemur ( Indri indri )
abstract: Abstract Passive acoustic monitoring (PAM) has emerged as a valuable tool for estimating animal density and abundance, particularly in challenging environments where traditional methods face limitations. In this study, we applied PAM techniques to study the indri ( Indri indri ) in the Maromizaha New Protected Area, a tropical forest in Eastern Madagascar. title: Facade and Opening Design Strategies for Enhancing Natural Lighting Efficiency in Classrooms at SD Labschool UPI
abstract: Natural lighting is an essential aspect of elementary school building design, as it significantly influences visual comfort and learning effectiveness. However, many classrooms in Indonesia do not meet the minimum illuminance standard of 350 lux specified in SNI 03-6197-2020. This study aims to evaluate and optimize facade and opening design strategies to improve the performance of natural lighting at SD Labschool UPI. title: Public Health Emergencies in Jordan: appraising multi-agency preparedness
abstract: Jordan faces a complex landscape of public health threats arising from infectious disease outbreaks, environmental hazards, technological incidents, humanitarian crises, and regional instability. These risks place sustained pressure on national institutions responsible for preparedness, response, and resilience. While multiple governmental and non-governmental agencies contribute to public health emergency preparedness and response (PHEPR), coordination gaps, overlapping mandates, and fragmented governance structures continue to challenge the effectiveness of a unified national response. title: Roblox-Based Immersive Learning for Environmental Literacy in Online Science Education
abstract: Environmental literacy requires learning environments that enable students to explore complex ecosystem interactions and evaluate the consequences of environmental decisions, yet conventional online science learning often provides limited opportunities for such experiences. This study developed and evaluated a Roblox-based immersive learning system designed to support environmental literacy, particularly in the context of peatland conservation. abstract: This study aims to analyze the development, trends, and patterns of research related to the Halal Assurance System (SJH) in Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in the Southeast Asian region using a bibliometric approach. A total of 101 articles indexed in Scopus for the period 2010–2023 were collected through the Publish or Perish application, then analyzed and mapped using VOSviewer software. abstract: With the rapid advancement of drone technology, aerial photogrammetry has been increasingly applied to morphometric research, particularly for endangered species, owing to its fully non-invasive nature. Photogrammetry-derived morphometric models (e.g., three-dimensional reconstructions) provide critical insights into individual health conditions and population demographic characteristics. abstract: Yongsu Sapari Village occupies a narrow coastal corridor on the northern flank of the Cycloops Mountains, where steep relief, developed lineaments, and limited flat land place roads, settlements, and cultivation activities close to potentially unstable rock slopes. This study integrates regional spatial information and site-scale rock-mass characterization to formulate landslide-mitigation-oriented land-use directions. abstract: Subtidal oyster reef restoration presents greater challenges for implementation and monitoring than intertidal restoration, and evaluations of relatively large-scale ecological restoration projects remain limited. This study evaluated the restoration project of Dashengtang using monitoring data from five field surveys collected from 2022 to 2026, and evaluated stage-specific ecological changes in oyster populations, aquatic environments, and macrobenthic communities. title: Joint determination of factors influencing adoption of climate smart agricultural practices in modern rice production in Southwest Bangladesh: a multivariate probit approach
abstract: Climate change and environmental degradation are increasingly threatening rice production in the coastal regions of the developing world, where the goals of raising productivity and building resilience became a joint priority. Climate smart agriculture offers a portfolio of practices that serve both goals, yet knowledge on how farmers in saline rice systems combine these practices, and why adoption remains often partial, is still limited. title: Cyanobacterial blooms at Canadian freshwater beaches: A prospective cohort study of exposure, health outcomes, and One Health implications
abstract: Cyanobacterial blooms are an emerging One Health concern in freshwater environments, yet limited evidence exists on how humans and companion animals interact with bloom-prone waters or how these exposures align with water-quality indicators. This study characterizes recreational behaviours, environmental conditions, and illness patterns across multiple Canadian beaches to inform integrated monitoring and risk-management approaches. abstract: This study examines the effects of optimized stacking sequences and NaOH surface treatment on the mechanical and dielectric performance of hybrid polyester composites reinforced with natural fibers (flax, sisal) and synthetic fibers (carbon, glass). title: FORMATION OF A SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT STRATEGY FOR AN ENTERPRISE BASED ON BUSINESS ANALYTICS TOOLS
abstract: The article explores the theoretical and applied aspects of forming a corporate sustainable development strategy. The purpose of the article is to substantiate the role of business analytics as a tool for information and analytical support in the process of strategic management of an enterprise's sustainable development. abstract: Seaweed has potential to be a sustainable food ingredient, yet its sensory properties are poorly understood, and previous research has focused on species differences, with less attention given different post-harvest processing formats. To characterize sensory properties across different post-harvest processing formats, 15 seaweed ingredients were profiled by Quantitative Descriptive Analysis. abstract: The European nightjar (Caprimulgus europaeus) is a long-distance migrant that also uses slow, hovering, flight as part of its feeding ecology. This reflects complex tradeoffs in aerodynamic mechanisms and makes studies of their flight performance, in relation to their wing shape, particularly interesting. abstract: Spontaneous isolated celiac artery dissection is uncommon and is usually confirmed with computed tomography angiography (CTA). A 56-year-old woman with untreated hypertension presented with acute persistent epigastric pain radiating to the back. abstract: Background: Early diagnosis of Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma (OSCC) from histopathological images is challenging because of limited and imbalanced datasets, variations in image magnification (100× and 400×), and calibration degradation associated with site-specific staining and scanner shifts. This study proposes CLARA-OSCC, a magnification-aware framework designed to improve robust classification, calibration, and clinically relevant triage of OSCC under heterogeneous imaging conditions. abstract: The freight and logistics sector is experiencing significant growth in Lubumbashi, with an increase in imports from China and other countries. The agency Sky Nine Cargo, specialized in freight transport and consolidation, faces a recurring problem: many clients do not collect their packages within the allotted 14-day period, resulting in an accumulation of goods, higher storage costs, tied-up capital, and slower inventory turnover. title: Assessing Habitat Suitability and Exposure of the Endemic Vasconcellea candicans Under Climate Change and Urban Growth in Lima, Peru
abstract: ABSTRACT Fog oases (lomas) are vegetation islands that support unique biodiversity in the coastal deserts of South America by capturing moisture from seasonal fog. Despite their ecological importance, they are among the region's most threatened ecosystems, particularly around Lima, where informal urbanisation and climate change drive their degradation. abstract: Following its emergence in China, pine wilt disease (PWD) has continuously expanded, creating substantial risks to regional forest ecosystems. abstract: Abstract Mangrove ecosystems are crucial to the ecological and climatic dynamics of the Asia–Pacific coastline. However, the ability to predict long-term changes is limited, hindering evidence-based resilience and adaptation strategies. The study presents a remote-sensing framework that integrates data from multiple sensors with time-series analysis to predict changes in mangrove ecosystems along India’s coastlines, aiding in conservation planning. abstract: The breakthrough of aDNA research during the mid-2010s fundamentally shifted the dominant focus of research on the Corded Ware period in Europe, redirecting attention to questions about migration and the interdisciplinary integration of new and older approaches. title: How Visual Resources Support Reading Comprehension: A Multimodal Analysis of English for Nusantara for Grade VIII
abstract: This study examines how visual resources accompanying reading materials in English for Nusantara for Grade VIII may support reading comprehension. A qualitative textbook content analysis was conducted on all 18 explicit Reading and Your Turn: Reading sections in Chapters 1-5. abstract: Cryogenic Electron Tomography (cryo-ET) is an emerging experimental technique used to visualize cell structures and macromolecules in their native cellular environment. Accurate segmentation of cell structures in cryo-ET tomograms, such as cell membranes, supports the study of cellular organization and function. title: Animal collagen as a source of antihypertensive bioactive peptides: production technologies, structural characteristics, and molecular mechanisms
abstract: Hypertension affects approximately 1.4 billion adults globally, yet nearly 80% of hypertensive individuals remain inadequately controlled, underscoring the urgent need for safe, food-based interventions. Collagen-derived bioactive peptides from animal sources represent promising functional food ingredients for blood pressure management through controlled enzymatic hydrolysis. abstract: Batu City was one of the main centers of cut flower production in East Java, particularly for roses (Rosa sp.), where favorable climatic conditions support floriculture development. However, rose productivity has fluctuated in recent years, potentially linked to rainfall variability and meteorological drought influenced by global climate phenomena such as the El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO) and the Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD). abstract: Abstract The rapid development of smart ports has revolutionized the maritime industry, leveraging advanced technologies and data analytics to enhance efficiency, productivity, and sustainability. However, assessing and optimizing the performance of smart ports remains a complex challenge. This study proposes a comprehensive framework for evaluating and improving smart port efficiency using a Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA) approach. title: Degradation-aware co-design and multi-level energy management of fuel cell–battery powertrains for hybrid-electric aircraft
abstract: Integrating proton exchange membrane fuel cell systems (PEMFCSs) with batteries can reduce aircraft emissions, but degradation must be addressed during design and operation. This study proposes a degradation-aware co-design framework determining the beginning-of-life PEMFCS rating to meet an end-of-life (EoL) power target, accounting for stack degradation, altitude-induced losses, and balance-of-plant (BoP) parasitic consumption. abstract: Meromictic lakes serve as natural laboratories for investigating microbially mediated biogeochemical cycling because their stable redox stratification supports diverse metabolic processes. Lake Suigetsu is a typical meromictic lake in Japan characterized by a permanent oxycline separating the oxic brackish mixolimnion from the anoxic saline sulfidogenic monimolimnion. abstract: This study investigates the development of digital solidarity within disaster-related online communities by conducting a netnographic analysis of the 2025 Aceh–Sumatra flood response campaign on Ferry Irwandi's YouTube channel. Although previous research has investigated the interconnections between mobilization, collective identification, trust, accountability, and sustained civic engagement during disaster response, it has given less attention to the topics of crowdfunding, trust, and digital donations. abstract: Despite the growing availability of customer feedback data, restaurant chains often face challenges in translating customer feedback into actionable quality improvements. To address this problem, this research aims to investigate operational process inefficiencies and food quality–related aspects of customer satisfaction. For this purpose, customer review data and operational activity data are collected from the central kitchen of a Malaysian restaurant chain. abstract: Soil salinization and phosphorus (P) deficiency often co-occur in coastal saline-alkali soils, severely limiting crop productivity. abstract: Extreme basin floods can strongly reshape tide-dominated estuaries, but their effects are often conditioned by antecedent channel geometry and human-induced river-bed incision. Here, we investigated the annual-scale morphodynamic response of the North Branch of the Changjiang (Yangtze) Estuary to the 2020 extreme basin flood using hydrological records, bathymetric surveys, surficial sediment samples, and Delft3D scenario experiments. abstract: Chemical composition and source contributions of PM 2.5 were investigated at a public-restricted bus depot in Valladolid (Spain) and two metro stations (Alto dos Moinhos and Quinta das Conchas) in Lisbon (Portugal) using positive matrix factorization (PMF). abstract: Due to growing resource demands in sustainability transitions, multi-system interactions (MSI) increasingly extend into extreme environments, such as the deep sea, outer space, and the underground, which harbour vast but largely untapped resource reservoirs. abstract: Conservation of plant biodiversity in national natural parks of Ukraine is becoming particularly relevant in the context of climate change, which transforms the temperature and humidity regime, increases the risks of droughts, fires, habitat degradation and species range shifts. abstract: A new species of the ostracod genus Polycopsis G. W. Müller, 1894 (Myodocopa: Halocyprida: Polycopidae), P. higejii sp. nov., is described from the interstitial habitat of a sandy beach in Miura City, central Japan. abstract: Este artículo analiza críticamente las limitaciones estructurales, normativas y políticas que enfrenta la libre circulación de personas en el espacio CEDEAO-ECOWAS, subrayando su relevancia como pilar fundamental para una integración regional que sea no solo operativa, sino también justa, democrática y centrada en las personas. abstract: The environmental behavior of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in tropical nearshore sediments remains poorly understood, particularly with respect to the contamination characteristics of emerging PFAS and precursor-related compounds. abstract: Abstract The Awassi is a native sheep breed of Lebanon with high historical and economic value. Despite its importance, its genetic background has not been characterized, leaving limited understanding of its origins, diversity, and regional connections. abstract: Abstract Populations of seagrasses such as eelgrass ( Zostera marina ) have been declining worldwide within the last century. This loss has partly been attributed to mechanisms associated with increases in nutrient loading from anthropogenic sources. Furthermore, the systems are kept in a degraded state through feedback mechanisms caused by loss of the eelgrass habitat’s nutrient-related ecosystem functions. abstract: Plant–microbe interactions are increasingly recognised as drivers of plant invasion and adaptation, via their capacity to modulate phenotypic plasticity. abstract: Background and Aim. Malus sieversii (Ledeb.) M. abstract: Abstract Algal blooms pose significant environmental and economic challenges worldwide. As their impact increases, there is an urgent need to improve forecasting models that predict their occurrence, development, and trends. Understanding recent research developments in satellite-based monitoring of algal blooms in the African Great Lakes provides a vital foundation for creating effective early warning systems and improving both short- and long-term prediction accuracy. abstract: Abstract The identification and classification of new taxa are crucial for understanding biodiversity. However, assigning samples to new taxa requires cautious and rigorous approaches. abstract: Abstract Urban and economic expansion across Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) may be shifting the relative contributions of dominant ambient air pollution sources, influencing both pollutant concentrations and composition, along with their associated health risks. abstract: Microplastics (MPs) have transitioned from a predominantly marine concern to a defining threat facing terrestrial agroecosystems, where croplands now function as one of the largest global reservoirs of plastic particles. abstract: Environmental robotic sampling requires considering the dual influence of water currents on robotic motion and particle transport. abstract: A combination of remote sensing techniques, open space data and field testing was developed to derive astronomical and meteorological parameters and assess Dark Sky brightness of the hitherto unstudied Schist Villages region in the mountainous Interior Center of Portugal. abstract: LLM-guided evolutionary methods, such as AlphaEvolve, have emerged as powerful approaches for challenging computational optimization problems, such as circle packing. abstract: We investigate soliton formation and interactions in the non-integrable Gardner-Ostrovsky equation (alias the rotation-modified Gardner equation) with anomalous (positive) dispersion. title: Visibility on Terrains
abstract: This chapter surveys terrain visibility models, algorithms, and applications. It introduces basic definitions, from line-of-sight, single-viewpoint viewsheds to cumulative and total viewsheds, on both Triangulated Irregular Network (TIN) and regular grid terrains. Reviews exact and approximate algorithms and highlights key application domains including archaeology, visual exposure to greenery, scenic route management, and land conservation.

abstract: LLM-based agents are increasingly capable of generating complex 3D structures, with the potential to reshape how objects are designed and realized in the physical world. abstract: Human and natural systems are deeply interconnected, influencing one another for centuries. abstract: Transitional waters are dynamic coastal ecosystems located at the interface between freshwater and marine environments. They are characterized by pronounced environmental variability resulting from the interaction between geomorphology, freshwater inputs, tidal exchanges, climatic variability, and human activities. abstract: Abstract Coastal extreme sea level is conventionally characterized by exceedance frequency or height, with the seasonal cycle removed as a nuisance. title: Socio-Ecological Resilience of a Coastal Community Facing Coastal Erosion in Bangboler Hamlet, Sikka Regency, Indonesia
abstract: Coastal erosion continues to recur and threatens the sustainability of coastal communities' living spaces, yet how social capital (trust, networks, and cooperative practices within broader social response capacity) interacts with ecological conditions and institutional support in building socio-ecological resilience remains insufficiently explained. This study aims to analyze the impacts of coastal erosion, community adaptation strategies, and the relationship among social response capacity, ecological recovery, and institutional support. abstract: Overland corridors offer alternatives to ocean freight, but rising railway traffic does not by itself demonstrate maritime substitution. This study evaluates the scale, direction, and commodity composition of reported modal reallocation in China–European Union trade. abstract: This study investigated the morphological and molecular characteristics of Scomberoides commersonnianus and Scomberoides lysan from the Sudanese Red Sea. abstract: Abstract. abstract: Sea urchins (Echinoidea) play important ecological and economic roles in coastal ecosystems, but morphological identification is often unreliable due to overlapping diagnostic traits among closely related taxa. abstract: Introduction Polystyrene nanoplastics (PS-NPs) represent persistent environmental contaminants derived from the degradation of plastic debris and are increasingly detected in biological systems, raising concerns regarding their potential effects on human health. title: Harnessing macrogenomics to study changing marine ecosystems under global climate change
abstract: Climate change is reshaping marine ecosystems at an accelerating pace. Predicting its impacts on biodiversity and ecosystem functions is therefore crucial to developing effective conservation strategies. Integration of genomic tools, habitat modelling and simulations offers a transformative approach to forecast these impacts. Yet, current frameworks remain limited to single-species analyses. abstract: Abstract Coconut ( Cocos nucifera L.) supports coastal value chains, yet compositional variation across varieties and production landscapes remains insufficiently characterized. abstract: Global biodiversity is declining rapidly as anthropogenic climate change interacts with habitat loss, disease emergence and overexploitation to reshape species distributions and population viability. This study examines the constitutional and criminal law protection of national symbols, their history and changes, presenting their role in expressing national identity. title: CG Fire Simulation in Films and Games: A Comparative Study
abstract: Fire shows up constantly in film visual effects and in video games, which makes it one of the most widely used - and hardest to get right - effects in computer graphics. This survey covers fire simulation work published between 2006 and 2026, picking out 54 papers that we think are broadly representative of the field. We sort these methods into six families: physics-based simulation, particle systems, procedural and data-driven approaches, neural style transfer, neural reconstruction, and AI-based video generation. abstract: The rising popularity of skin-whitening creams in Nigeria raises alarms about potential exposure to harmful metals that may occur either as impurities or as intentionally added ingredients. This study assessed the levels of cadmium, chromium, copper, iron, and lead in various skin-whitening creams available in Lafia Town. abstract: Hardness testing is one of the most widely applied methods for evaluating the mechanical properties of metallic materials in manufacturing and quality control. Among standardized techniques, Brinell, Vickers, and Rockwell are most commonly used, all relying on precise measurement of indentation geometry. abstract: Introduction Potentially hazardous element (PHE) contamination threatens agroecosystem sustainability and food security, particularly in irrigated regions. title: The Legal and Socio-Economic Implications of Maritime Crimes in Nigeria: Challenges and the Way Forward
abstract: Maritime crimes constitute a significant threat to Nigeria’s national security, economic stability, and regional maritime governance. These crimes include piracy, armed robbery at sea, illegal oil bunkering, human trafficking, drug trafficking, illegal fishing, and environmental pollution. title: In the World of Aquatic Parasites, Microsporidia Matter!
abstract: Microsporidia are highly diverse, widespread parasites related to fungi and several groups of zoosporic protistan parasites. They infect a broad range of hosts, from protists to vertebrates, in many environments including most, if not all, aquatic habitats. Their genomes range from relatively conventional to highly reduced, yet they share key cellular structures and traits underlying infection and host association. abstract: The problem of detecting anomalies in processed images acquired from visual monitoring equipment becomes particularly relevant in the context of ecological monitoring of the world ocean's water areas, specifically when searching for the consequences of technogenic catastrophes caused by oil spills. abstract: Abstract Future imaging spectrometers will expand contemporary data volumes by orders of magnitude, requiring automated methods to upscale labor-intensive detection of trace gas point sources. Here we present a fully-automated approach that achieves operational performance for plume detection and labelling without human participation. abstract: Automated snow depth retrieval from time-lapse cameras is constrained by site-specific annotation and manual image quality screening, thus limiting scalability across deployments. abstract: Microplastics (MPs; plastic particles smaller than 5 mm) are widely reported in the surface water and sediment of the Vietnamese Mekong Delta, but their ecological hazard has not been synthesised across the Delta. title: Construction of Urban Functional Zones Identification Model Based on TF-IDF and Public Perception-Weighted Algorithms
abstract: Urban neighborhoods used to be fairly straightforward—residential here, commercial there. That is less and less true, and planners need ways to keep up. abstract: Abstract Fish-killing harmful algal blooms (HABs) continue to inflict severe economic losses on marine aquaculture worldwide, yet monitoring systems designed around microalgal cell counts frequently fail to anticipate acute mortality events. abstract: Abstract. abstract: The Maritime Labour Convention (MLC, 2006) was designed to harmonise minimum standards of working and living conditions at sea across jurisdictions. Despite its near-universal ratification, significant disparities in labour conditions persist, indicating limited effectiveness in the implementation of the regulatory framework. abstract: Toxic trace elements in edible oils pose public health risks because of their persistence, bioaccumulation, and, for some elements, carcinogenic potential. abstract: Microplastics (MPs) are increasingly reported in foods, yet comparative data across commonly consumed dairy products remain limited in South Asia. abstract: Direct lithium extraction (DLE) from geothermal and oilfield brines is supported by many technology reviews, yet an operator holding a brine analysis still lacks a structured route to a defensible choice of technology. abstract: Satellite retrieval of chlorophyll-a (Chl-a) is central to monitoring eutrophication in inland reservoirs, yet the atmospheric-correction processors it depends on, trained on oceanic and large-lake conditions, are systematically biased over small water bodies. abstract: Access to safe and reliable water remains a persistent challenge for rural communities in Malaysia, where infrastructural limitations, spatial constraints, and governance fragmentation continue to undermine water security. abstract: Background. Ginger is a horticultural commodity and a biopharmaceutical crop with many benefits and high economic value. abstract: Abstract To further constrain the lunar Li isotopic composition and its behavior during lunar magmatic differentiation, we measured twelve lunar meteorites, including mare basalts, Mg‐suite rocks and anorthosites. title: Spread dynamics of invasive species in the Iberian Peninsula
abstract: The continued spread of invasive species represents a major threat to biodiversity and ecosystem functioning, yet the extent to which invasive species are approaching spatial saturation remains poorly understood. Quantifying invasion dynamics across taxa and regions is therefore critical for understanding ongoing range expansion and identifying species at different stages of invasion so that management actions are applied efficiently. title: Enhancement of the Properties of Libyan Concrete through the Incorporation of Natural Additives Derived from Palm Waste or Local Limestone: A Comparative Data-Driven Assessment
abstract: The concrete manufactured in Libya is subject to hot-dry weather conditions, variability in the quality of aggregates used, and quality control, whereas the agricultural waste from date palm (Phoenix dactylifera L.) and common carbonate rocks can be considered underutilized sources of additives to concrete. This work provides a comparative and evidence-based analysis of natural additives based on palm waste (fibers and ash) and limestone (powder) for improving the characteristics of Libyan concrete. title: Physiological basis of altitude-adjusted hemoglobin thresholds and anemia misclassification at moderate altitude
abstract: ABSTRACT Residence at moderate altitude reduces oxygen availability and stimulates hematological adaptations, but the contributions of erythropoiesis and plasma volume shifts are not clear and complicate interpretation of hemoglobin and anemia classification. This study examined whether residence at moderate altitude (∼1,800m) was associated with elevated hemoglobin mass (HbMass), independent of plasma volume fluctuations, and its implications for anemia prevalence. title: Goldfish, gibel carp, or crucian carp? Testing public recognition of Carassius species
abstract: Crucian carp ( Carassius carassius ) has declined across much of Europe and is listed as critically endangered in the Czech Republic. A major threat is the spread of non-native congeners, especially gibel carp ( Carassius gibelio ) and goldfish ( Carassius auratus ), which overlap in habitat use and can hybridise with crucian carp. Because these taxa are morphologically largely similar, public misidentification may bias citizen science monitoring and lead to counterproductive freshwater management by hobbyists or stakeholders. abstract: This article draws on the authors’ more than 17 years of experience in transcriptomic research, beginning with the introduction of high-throughput sequencing in Mexico in 2009. Here, we provide a critical review of bioinformatics pipelines for different RNA classes, ranging from small RNAs to long non-coding RNAs. Our analysis encompasses a range of scenarios, from de novo transcriptome assembly for organisms lacking a closely related and adequately annotated reference genome to differential expression analysis based on a well-annotated reference genome. title: Effectiveness of Planting Pattern Systems and Types of Varieties on the Growth and Production of Rice Plants (Oryza sativa L.)
abstract: Jajar Legowo planting pattern technology is a planting technique designed to arrange the planting pattern in order to increase production. The purpose of this study is to analyze the Jajar Legowo planting system and different varieties on post-harvest rice production and proximate content. There are 2 types of research methods: quantitative analysis of post-harvest rice, which includes proximate content, and rice cultivation using a Randomized Block Design (RBD) with 5 repetitions. title: Contribution of Ship Berthing to Surface Water Pollution in Selected Harbours in Rivers State
abstract: This research focused on the impact of ship docking operations on the contamination of surface waters in specific ports in Rivers State, Nigeria, utilizing both physicochemical and biological metrics. A descriptive research methodology was used, encompassing repeated sampling conducted over a span of three months. Five primary ports—Okrika, Kidney Island, Macobar, Abonnema, and Onne—were chosen, resulting in the collection of 120 water samples along with ballast water from ten vessels. title: A framework for understanding automatic identification system (AIS) manipulation: purposes, goals, and strategies
abstract: Abstract There is increasing attention paid to the manipulation of ships’ Automatic Identification System (AIS) signals, with implications for maritime safety, law enforcement, and security. Based on the literature and narrative reports, this paper proposes a framework that answers why and when ships engage in AIS manipulations by tracing the purpose, goals, and strategies of their operators. title: Heavy metal contamination in branded and non-branded turmeric powder from Khulna, Bangladesh: Exposure assessment and potential carcinogenic risk
abstract: Turmeric is vulnerable to heavy metal contamination due to metal uptake from contaminated soils, irrigation water, post-harvest processing or via adulteration. This research assessed the concentrations of heavy metals (Pb, Cr, Cd, Mn, Cu) alongside non-carcinogenic and carcinogenic risks in fifteen non-branded and five branded powdered turmeric samples acquired from eight sampling locations in Khulna, Bangladesh. title: Hepatoprotective effects of natural polysaccharides: molecular mechanisms, structure–activity relationships, sources, applications in functional foods, and prospects
abstract: Natural polysaccharides from plants, fungi, algae, microorganisms, and animals have attracted increasing interest as food-derived candidates for liver protection. This critical review integrates preparation identity, structural attributes, mechanistic evidence, disease-model specificity, and translational readiness rather than treating these dimensions independently. title: Protein homeostasis and inter-organellar signaling under salt stress
abstract: Salinity is a major abiotic constraint on plant growth, productivity, and global food security. It disrupts cellular protein homeostasis (proteostasis) at every step, from synthesis to degradation. Plant survival under salt stress therefore depends on the coordinated regulation of protein synthesis, folding, post-translational modification, trafficking, quality control, and turnover. title: Trade-offs in the environmental and social sustainability of conventional and alternative pig production systems
abstract: Sustainability assessments of livestock systems have largely prioritized environmental and economic outcomes, with comparatively limited attention to social performance or the trade-offs that emerge when multiple objectives interact. We advance a more holistic perspective by jointly evaluating environmental and social sustainability across conventional indoor and alternative pig production systems on the island of Ireland, the latter encompassing outdoor and agroforestry-based systems. title: Evaluation of micro-litter pollution in the Antarctic asteroid Odontaster validus Koehler, 1906 at Deception Island (South Shetland Islands)
abstract: Micro-litter (ML) pollution is increasingly being reported in Antarctic benthic ecosystems and the organisms inhabiting them. In this study, we assessed ML abundance and characteristics in the Antarctic asteroid Odontaster validus at Deception Island (South Shetland Islands), an area with significant human presence. Additionally, we considered the potential influence of local factors, including proximity to research stations and the bay entrance, as well as depth (5 and 15 m), on ML pollution. title: A Scalable Low-Supervision Framework for Longterm Land Cover Mapping: Automated Training Sample Generation and Independent Validation
abstract: Reliable long-term land cover information is essential for environmental monitoring, yet many regions still lack dedicated datasets. Main obstacles are assembling training labels at national scale without extensive manual annotation and obtaining reference data sufficiently independent of the mapping process to support credible accuracy assessment. Here, we present a scalable, low-supervision framework for national land cover mapping addressing both limitations. abstract: : This study presents an integrated evaluation of tight sandstone gas reservoirs in the Yan 439 Block, Yan'an Gas Field, through secondary fine-scale well logging interpretation and rock mechanical analysis. title: Polychaete (Annelida) diversity in the impacted Berg River Estuary, South Africa
abstract: Abstract Although Ramsar-listed, the Berg River estuary (South Africa) is anthropogenically impacted and severely understudied. Four studies conducted between the 1950s and 2000s found that polychaetous annelids in the estuary are represented predominantly by capitellid, spionid and nereidid species. This study provides an updated taxonomic inventory of polychaetous annelids in this estuary, with COI, cytb and 16S DNA sequence data to facilitate future molecular-based biodiversity studies. 3840 specimens (16 species from seven families) were collected from 9 sites from the mouth of the estuary

title: An update on freshwater gastropods serving as intermediate hosts of amphistomes infecting livestock in South Africa
abstract: Improved surveillance of amphistome parasites and their intermediate hosts is crucial for comprehending their epidemiology and developing effective prevention and control measures, since amphistomosis is among the neglected parasitic diseases of ruminants, alongside schistosomiasis and fasciolosis. This study characterized the diversity of freshwater gastropods collected from six South African provinces and assessed their potential in the transmission of amphistomes infecting livestock. title: An Analysis-Ready Dataset of Sentinel-2 Water and Vegetation Indices for River Basin Monitoring: STAC and COG Based Data Access and Cloud-Native Organization
abstract: River basins integrate hydrological, water-quality, and vegetation processes, requiring consistent observations of surface water and surrounding vegetation. Sentinel-2 Multispectral Instrument imagery provides frequent observations at spatial resolutions of up to 10 m. However, long-term basin-scale analysis requires repeated data discovery, retrieval, preprocessing, and quality control. This study presents an analysis-ready, cloud-native dataset of Sentinel-2-derived environmental indices for the Hwangnyonggang River Basin, South Korea (674.8 km2), covering January 2017 to August 2026. abstract: The present study examined Perceived Influence of Indoor and Outdoor Air Quality on Active Sawmills in Port Harcourt Metropolis Rivers State focusing on Air Quality Status, Human Health Risk and Seasonal variations. An experimental design was used with cross-sectional observation, combining field measurements with lab analysis. The areas with different levels of sawmill activity and equipment are monitored at the four main sites and the units deployed are the Aeroqol, Kestrel and Air volume mini sampler. abstract: Little is known about the behaviour and stress responses of animals captured by longline gear from hooking until retrieval at the vessel, despite the importance of this process for bycatch mitigation and post-release survival. Most existing studies have relied on physiological sampling at haulback, which provides only a snapshot of stress at retrieval and requires invasive handling. title: DIVERSIFICATION STRATEGIES ON NON-FINANCIAL PERFORMANCE OF CASHEW NUT COMPANIES IN KILIFI COUNTY
abstract: Cashew nut companies in Kilifi County play a vital role in supporting rural livelihoods, generating employment, and contributing to economic development in Kenya's coastal region. However, these companies continue to encounter persistent difficulties in achieving optimal non-financial performance outcomes, including consistent product quality, reduced post-harvest losses, and sustained customer satisfaction. title: Plasmodium falciparum parasite density and its association with malaria rapid diagnostic test positivity among school-aged children across diverse malaria transmission settings in mainland Tanzania
abstract: Malaria rapid diagnostic tests (mRDTs) are widely used for malaria diagnosis and surveillance; however, their performance is influenced by parasite density. This study assessed the relationship between parasite density and mRDT positivity among school-aged children (SAC) across diverse malaria transmission settings in mainland Tanzania. Data were obtained from 17,131 school-aged children participating in a nationwide malaria survey. Malaria infection was assessed using mRDT and quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) targeting the Plasmodium falciparum lactate dehydrogenase (PfLDH) gene.

abstract: This study aimed to identify the environmental determinants influencing the distribution of lumpy skin disease and to predict changes in its spatial distribution risk and potential geographic range across Iran under future climate change scenarios using ensemble Species Distribution Models (SDMs). title: Do large language models keep the hedge? Uncertainty preservation when large language models summarize aviation and maritime incident reports
abstract: Safety-incident reports are written with deliberate epistemic caution: A reporter marks what was seen, what was inferred, and what remains unsure, and a dropped hedge can turn a tentative observation into an apparent cause. As large language models take over summarizing such reports for triage, indexing, and search, whether they preserve that caution becomes a property of the safety record itself. title: Occurrence characteristics of plastic waste on beaches and the influencing factors of mercury enrichment: a case study of Qingdao
abstract: Abstract Plastic pollution has become a research hotspot. To explore the occurrence characteristics and influencing factors of mercury (Hg) in plastic waste on beaches, plastic debris samples were collected from the intertidal and supratidal zones of four typical beaches in Qingdao. Polymer types of the plastics were identified, and Hg concentrations in the plastics were determined to investigate the effects of physicochemical properties (plastic color, polymer type, and degree of aging) on Hg enrichment. abstract: Identifying climatically suitable areas for cacao cultivation (Theobroma cacao L.) is essential to guide sustainable intensification, territorial planning, and compliance with emerging environmental standards in tropical regions. abstract: Abstract Northeast Atlantic spurdog ( Squalus acanthias ) has recently shown signs of recovery from overfishing following international conservation measures. As the fishery slowly reopens, ensuring its sustainable long-term trajectory will require an understanding of its contemporary population structure, habitat use, and life-history traits across its distribution range. abstract: Introduction Alpha-thalassemia is a common genetic disorder in southern China. The - α 3.7 deletion has three subtypes (I, II, III), among which type III has been rarely reported in the Chinese population. This study aimed to investigate the prevalence, genotypic distribution, and hematological phenotypes of the - α 3.7III subtype in Sanya, Hainan. title: Distant water fishing and its effects on domestic food security
abstract: Governments around the world have identified distant water fleets (DWFs) as a key threat to ecosystem health, domestic economic opportunities, and food security. With a high prevalence of undernutrition and micronutrient deficiencies in countries where DWFs operate, the aquatic foods caught by DWFs represent a vital opportunity to shift policy and improve nutrition outcomes. abstract: This article examines conflict dynamics in the Arctic using a framework that includes the state, regional, and systemic (international) analysis levels. While public and political narratives often depict the Arctic as an emerging arena of geopolitical rivalry, these interpretations often overlook the analytical complexity of conflicts in the region. abstract: Understanding the bioaccumulation and trophic transfer of naturally occurring radionuclides is essential for assessing ecological risk in freshwater systems. This study provides a large-scale assessment of polonium-210 ( 210 Po) and lead-210 ( 210 Pb) bioaccumulation, trophic transfer and tissue-specific biodistribution in freshwater food webs across Canada. title: Effects of Antibiotic and Temperature Treatments on Phycosphere Bacterial Communities of Kelp Gametophytes
abstract: Microbiome dysbiosis represents a critical bottleneck in sustainable kelp aquaculture, yet the distinct regulatory mechanisms of antibiotics and temperature remain poorly characterized. This study systematically elucidates the divergent effects of penicillin-streptomycin exposure and temperature gradients on Saccharina japonica gametophytes and their epiphytic microbiota. abstract: ABSTRACT The global fisheries sector is undergoing a structural transformation, with aquaculture surpassing capture fisheries in 2022 (51% of global aquatic animal supply) and reaching 53% by 2024, when aquaculture production topped 100 million tonnes for the first time. Despite vast aquatic resources, Africa produces only approximately 1.9% of global aquaculture output and remains dependent on declining capture fisheries. abstract: Abstract Sediment color is a valuable proxy in paleoceanography, reflecting chemical and mineralogical composition influenced by biogeochemical processes and depositional environments. This study investigates the relationship between sediment color (RGB and CIE L*a*b*) and metals in three radiocarbon-dated sediment cores from the Santos Basin continental slope (SW Atlantic). abstract: The maritime industry is undergoing a paradigm shift driven by stringent decarbonization regulations, such as the Carbon Intensity Indicator (CII) and Energy Efficiency Existing Ship Index (EEXI). Despite the proliferation of technical solutions, a conceptual divide persists between emission compliance and the established safety management culture governed by the International Safety Management (ISM) Code. title: A reproducible baseline framework for landsat satellite-based water quality modeling
abstract: Remote sensing can monitor water quality at a large scale and low cost, but many existing models are narrowly tuned and hard to generalize. To the best of our knowledge, this study introduces a reproducible, end-to-end evaluation framework for Landsat-based water quality modeling. It compares machine learning algorithms, water quality indicators, cloud-cover thresholds, temporal matching windows, and water body types using a single standardized dataset. title: Assessment of microplastics occurrence and abundance in water and sediment from Lekki Lagoon, Ogun State, Nigeria
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) are ubiquitous sources of pollution in aquatic habitats, which have proven to be a source of concern to the world because of their consumption by aquatic animals and the risk of their introduction into the food web. abstract: Abstract Tire rubber-derived chemicals (TRCs) are known to be highly toxic to fish, but understanding of their environmental levels and fate is still limited. This study presents a new method for the analysis of 18 TRCs, including phenylenediamines (TRC-PDs), their quinone derivatives (TRC-Qs), and rubber vulcanizing and curing-related chemicals (TRC-VCRs) in fish bile and plasma samples. abstract: Abstract We assessed the leaching potential of dissolved carbon (DC) from polyvinyl chloride (PVC) and polyethylene terephthalate (PET) microplastics (MPs), selected for their differing polymeric structure and response to thermal oxidation. title: Assessment of Groundwater Quality from Tombia Community in Degema Local Government Area of Rivers State, Nigeria
abstract: Groundwater is the primary source of drinking water for rural communities in the Niger Delta, yet its quality is increasingly threatened by natural geochemical processes and anthropogenic activities. This study evaluated the quality of groundwater in Tombia community in Degema Local Government Area, Rivers State, Nigeria, with the aim of assessing its suitability for domestic consumption and identifying potential health risks. title: Underestimation of plastic pollution and implications for water quality assessments in urban lakes
abstract: Plastic pollution is increasingly recognized as a pervasive threat to water quality, yet most studies quantify only microplastics (<5 mm), potentially biasing estimates of environmental contamination. Here, we formally evaluated the underestimation bias associated with the intentional exclusion of plastics >5 mm from samples collected across a system of urban freshwater lakes (n = 20). title: Nutritional and Economic Potential of Needle Cuttlefish (Sepia aculeata): Unlocking an Underutilized Seafood Resource in Bangladesh
abstract: Needle cuttlefish ( Sepia aculeata ), an abundant yet underutilized cephalopod species in Bangladesh, remains a non-conventional seafood resource with limited nutritional information. This study evaluated the proximate composition, amino acid profile, fatty acid composition, micronutrients, and heavy metals of both edible and non-edible portions of S. aculeata , while recommended nutrient intake (RNI) contribution and economic efficiency were assessed using edible portions only. Using monitoring data from 2020 to 2024, this study examined six water quality indicators: total organic carbon (TOC), total nitrogen (TN), total phosphorus (TP), dissolved oxygen (DO), pH, and electrical conductivity (EC) across 67 mid-basins in South Korea. Forty-nine water column samples were collected bimonthly over an annual cycle (September 2024–September 2025) from a stream in southeastern Pennsylvania, USA. title: Effects of Saccharomyces cerevisiae Supplementation on Growth, Survival and Fatty Acid Composition of Anadara tuberculosa Spat
abstract: ABSTRACT This research assessed the feasibility of using the yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae as a complementary feed for the mangrove cockle Anadara tuberculosa spat. The nutritional impact of five mix diets was tested: (1) Tisochrysis lutea + Chaetoceros gracilis , (2) C. gracilis + S. cerevisiae , (3) S. cerevisiae , (4) T. lutea + S. cerevisiae and (5) T. lutea + C. gracilis + S. cerevisiae . In addition, fatty acid (FA) profiles of the diets and of spat tissues were analysed. title: Reconciling Competing Natural Resource Interests for Sustainable Development: The Role of Law in Balancing Oil Exploitation, Water Resource and Ecosystem Services in Nigeria
abstract: Oil exploitation remains important to the economy and development of Nigeria, but its interaction with the ecosystem and interconnected water resources create conflicts between competing forms of resource use. This paper examines whether Nigerian law provides a coherent and balanced framework for reconciling oil development with the continued impairment on water resources and associated ecosystems. journal: JOURNAL OF LAW AND GLOBAL POLICY

title: Effect of storage time on release of microplastics (MPs) from different milk packaging
abstract: The growing detection of microplastics (MPs) in the human body has raised concerns about the potential entrance of MPs into the food chain and subsequently into humans. Due to wide consumption of milk by different age groups, investigating the MPs release into milk during storage time from different commercial milk packaging materials is crucial. MPs release in three common packaging types of ESL milk (bottles and packets) and sterilized milk (multi-layer carton) during storage periods (expiration date) was studied. title: Toxicological impacts of sulfamethoxazole on freshwater organisms – toxicity and oxidative stress
abstract: The continuous expansion of the pharmaceutical sector has intensified aquatic contamination, as persistent active compounds enter water bodies through urban, industrial, and agricultural runoff. Among these contaminants, sulfamethoxazole (SMX)—a widely used sulphonamide antibiotic—raises ecological concerns due to its persistence and potential for bioaccumulation. institutions: National Institute for Research and Development for Industrial Ecology

title: Integrating the economic valuation of ecosystem services for sustainable futures: methodological variability, scale effects, and policy implications
abstract: This study analyzed how valuation methods and spatial scale influence reported ecosystem service values. A systematic literature review following PRISMA guidelines and the PICO approach screened 222 articles from the Scopus database (2016–2025); after applying rigorous inclusion criteria, 38 studies were selected. Results reveal substantial methodological variability. Sum-based Total Economic Value (TEV) aggregation assigns 71.45% of total value to forests and vegetation; however, sensitivity analysis shows that this dominance is driven by a single macro-scale outlier.
