title: Implementation Of The Indonesian Government's Policy In Supervising The Seaworthiness Of Ships Based On George Edward III's Policy/Module At The Tanjung Priok Main Port Authority And Harbor Master's Office
abstract: This study examines the implementation of the Indonesian Government’s policy in supervising ship seaworthiness at the Tanjung Priok Main Port Authority and Harbor Master’s Office (KSOP Utama Tanjung Priok). The study aims to analyze policy implementation based on George C. Edwards III’s four dimensions: communication, resources, disposition, and bureaucratic structure; identify supporting and inhibiting factors; and examine efforts to overcome implementation barriers. title: Variability of toxic Microcystis blooms and bacterial communities in freshwater bodies with different anthropopressure and climate zones: a novel comparative study in Guatemala and Poland
abstract: Abstract The global rise of harmful cyanobacterial blooms (HCBs) in freshwater systems is driven by anthropogenic pressure and climate change, yet limited information exists on how these factors shape HCBs and their phycosphere-associated bacterial communities (PBCs). We examined the influence of eutrophication (nutrient concentrations and land use), climate zone, and seasonality on phytoplankton and PBCs across three freshwater bodies: hypertrophic Lake Amatitlán with urban and agricultural catchments, mesotrophic Laguna del Pino with a forested/agricultural catchment (both tropical, Guatemal

title: Landscape spatial configuration determines seasonal nitrate transport rather than land-use proportions in mountainous rivers
abstract: Identifying seasonal nitrate (NO 3 − ) transport pathways remains a challenge in complex mountainous watersheds. This study integrated hydrogeochemistry, dual isotopes (δ 15 N-NO₃ − and δ 18 O-NO₃ − ), and the MixSIAR model with landscape metrics to investigate nitrate dynamics in the Chao River Basin. Spatial analysis categorized the watershed into upstream, midstream, and downstream zones. title: Method of meal delivery influences estimates of postprandial metabolism and alkaline tide in a benthic fish
abstract: Intragastric gavage is widely used in studies of digestive physiology to deliver standardised meals, yet it remains unclear whether it elicits postprandial metabolic and acid-base responses comparable to voluntary feeding. Here, we tested whether the method of meal delivery affects the magnitude and timing of the postprandial rise in metabolic rate known as specific dynamic action (SDA) and the associated alkaline tide (transient rise in blood pH and bicarbonate following feeding) in sand flathead (Platycephalus bassensis) using a standardised 1.5% body-weight ratio either as intact pellets (v

title: Resveratrol in Microplastic‐ and Nanoplastic‐Induced Toxicity: Current Evidence, Mechanistic Insights, and Future Directions
abstract: Microplastic (MP; MPs) and nanoplastic (NP; NPs) pollution poses a growing threat to global health. Their small size and large surface area facilitate ingestion, accumulation, and interactions with biological systems, leading to toxicity through oxidative stress, inflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and cell death. These effects may occur directly or through the release of adsorbed pollutants and plastic additives. title: Hong Kong’s Water Quality Governance: A Historical PerspectivePolicy Instruments and Priorities
abstract: Based on 112 water quality-related proceedings of the Hong Kong Legislative Council from 2014 to 2025, this study employed an analytical framework of policy tools, policy issues, and time evolution to investigate Hong Kong’s water-quality governance agenda. The findings indicate that command and control were mentioned most frequently, followed by public information, participation and collaboration, public investment, and economic incentives. institutions: Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen

title: Environmental fate and ecotoxicological impacts of antibiotic transformation products: Microbial reactivation, resistance selection, and ecosystem risks
abstract: Antibiotics and their transformation products (TPs) make up a critical class of emerging contaminants. While parent compounds are frequently monitored, their metabolic derivatives often bypass detection due to analytical gaps and a lack of systematic risk assessments. This review evaluates the persistence, bioactivity, and ecological impact of antibiotic TPs across ecosystems. Our review illustrates the biotic and abiotic pathways of TP formation, showing that these metabolites often retain or amplify the bioactivity of their parent compounds. journal: Asian Journal of Water Environment and Pollution

title: An AI-Enabled Predictive Procurement Model for Forecasting and Inventory Optimization
abstract: This paper presents an AI-enabled predictive procurement model that integrates probabilistic demand forecasting, supplier lead-time prediction, and multi-echelon inventory optimization to secure target service levels while lowering working capital. The framework couples hierarchical time-series forecasting with gradient-boosted trees and lightweight sequence models, capturing seasonality, promotions, and regime shifts. title: Artificial light at night and apparent predation on juvenile Neohelice granulata during two deployment periods at Mar Chiquita, Argentina
abstract: Over the past decade, artificial light at night (ALAN) has become one of the most spatially extensive anthropogenic disturbances along coastlines worldwide, yet whether its capacity to alter predation is a fixed property of illumination intensity or depends on the ecological context in which it occurs has received little attention. title: Multi-Isotope Analyses of Colonial Sheep from the Sydney Region, Australia: Implications for Husbandry Strategies
abstract: Abstract Stable isotope analyses of faunal remains have demonstrated significant potential to enhance understandings of human-animal relationships during periods of European colonization. Isotopic analyses enable reconstructions of historical livestock management practices, including diet, provenance, and mobility, while also providing insights into past climatic and environmental conditions. title: Solid waste management practices in riparian communities are a key driver of microplastic concentrations in the Mekong River, Cambodia
abstract: Rivers are major conduits of plastic pollution, however the role of community level waste collection on riverine microplastic concentrations remains poorly understood. We investigated seasonal patterns and drivers of microplastic pollution along the Lower Mekong River, Cambodia, with a focus on riparian waste collection services. Surface water samples were collected during dry and wet seasons using a pump and filter method (100 µm minimum aperture), and more than 15,000 particles were chemically identified using Fourier Transform Infrared spectroscopy (FTIR). title: Source apportionment and health risk assessment of PAHs in commercial fish from Al Jubail, Saudi Arabia
abstract: Abstract This study measured polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) contamination in ten commercially important fish species from the Al-Jubail industrial coastline, Arabian Gulf, Saudi Arabia. Muscle tissue concentrations were quantified by GC-MS. Source apportionment used diagnostic molecular ratios, positive matrix factorization (PMF), and hierarchical clustering, and health risk was assessed separately for adults and children. title: Redox distribution of Asgard archaea and co-occurring taxa in microbial mats from an early Proterozoic ecosystem analog
abstract: Abstract Increasing evidence supports that eukaryotes originated from the symbiosis of an Asgard archaeon, the alphaproteobacterial ancestor of mitochondria, and possibly additional bacterial contributions. Eukaryogenesis likely occurred in redox-transition environments such as microbial mats or shallow sediments ~2 billion years ago, when atmospheric oxygen was far lower than today. abstract: This study was conducted to determine the effect of foliar spraying with different concentrations of the Kelpmax seaweed extract on the growth and chemical composition of two barley varieties (Hordeum vulgare L.), namely Al-Jazira 1 and Rayhan, under greenhouse conditions. The plants were sprayed with three concentrations of the extract (0.0, 2.5, and 5) mL L⁻¹ at three growth stages. title: Corrosion-induced degradation of rock bolt–grout systems in subsea tunnel primary support
abstract: Rock bolt–grout systems are critical load-transfer components in the subsea tunnel primary support, but its material deterioration and structural damage under aggressive groundwater remain insufficiently understood. In the article, the properties of rock bolt–grout specimens exposed to chloride, sulfate and chloride–sulfate environments were tested. title: The Multiplying Worlds of Ma Joie
abstract: This essay explores the environmental and spatial afterlives of plantation colonialism in the Seychelles through an ecofeminist auto-theoretical approach. Drawing on family archives and field philosophical research, the author reflects on her position as the granddaughter of a former plantation owner while tracing the material and spatial legacies of the Plantationocene. title: Gene expression, Antioxidant Responses, and metabolomic Profiling Reveal Chlorella vulgaris Mediated Protection against acetaminophen and microplastic Co-toxicity in Oreochromis niloticus
abstract: Abstract Emerging water pollutants such as pharmaceutical (PhACs) and microplastics (MPs) are progressively detected in aquatic environments, raising alarms about their mutual toxicological effects on non-target biota, particularly fish. Although the individual effects of these pollutants have been investigated, there is little data available on their interactions and potential strategies to reduce toxicity. title: Sri Lankan ethnic cuisine on YouTube: a computational netnographic study of food-neophobic and food-neophilic audience reactions and the digital transmission of culinary heritage
abstract: Abstract Sri Lankan cuisine is a layered ethnic food heritage shaped by tropical agriculture and by centuries of Arab, Portuguese, Dutch, and British contact atop a South Indian rice-and-curry foundation, and it is increasingly encountered by global audiences not at the destination but on digital platforms. This paper analyses 21,984 English-language comments posted on 45 YouTube videos about Sri Lankan ethnic cuisine, using VADER sentiment analysis, LDA topic modelling, and a purpose-built keyword lexicon for phobic and philic markers. title: The prospects of Vietnam’s niche diplomacy in the era of national advancement
abstract: Niche diplomacy is a notable characteristic of the foreign policy of middle powers - states that have the capacity to play a prominent role on the international stage, but are not powerful enough to impose their will on others. Therefore, middle powers need to rely on their ability to identify and fill in “niche spaces” through diplomatic methods and skills, that is, choosing a few specific issues, institutions or areas to specialize in and orient them as important foundations in its foreign policy. title: Estimating the completeness of large-scale single-cell sequencing projects
abstract: During embryonic development, cells undergo differentiation into highly specialized cell types. Capitalizing on single-cell RNA sequencing, many initiatives and substantial resources are cataloguing these differentiated cell types by their transcriptomic profiles. Despite the extensive efforts to profile various organs and their cellular compositions, we lack metrics to assess the completeness of the sequencing projects. title: Robust trajectory tracking of an underactuated ROV under compound flow disturbances using ADRC-GISMC
abstract: Abstract Trajectory tracking of remotely operated vehicles (ROVs) remains difficult when hydrodynamic coupling, plant uncertainty, actuator constraints, and spatially varying flow disturbances act simultaneously. This study presents a simulation-based evaluation of an ADRC-GISMC strategy for an underactuated ROV under an engineering-oriented compound disturbance model combining background-current and local outfall-plume components. title: Integrating free-living amoebae into climate-microbiome and One Health frameworks
abstract: Climate change is altering microbial ecosystems at a global scale, yet the role of free-living amoebae within these shifting microbiomes remains incompletely understood. Free-living amoebae occupy soil, water, air, and built environments, where they contribute to microbial diversity, regulate nutrient cycling, and host diverse bacterial, fungal, and viral microorganisms. title: ANALYSIS OF THE IMPACT OF PRESSURE RELIEF VALVE FAILURES ON FLEXIBLE PIPELINE CONNECTORS IN OFFSHORE OIL PRODUCTION
abstract: Oil plays a significant role in the Brazilian and global energy matrices. Brazilian oil production is predominantly offshore, particularly in pre-salt fields. In oil and gas production systems, both rigid and flexible pipelines are employed. During retrieval operations, special attention must be given to permeated gas trapped within the annular space of the flexible pipeline. Controlled gas release, as required by API 17B, is performed by opening pressure relief valves installed in the end connectors. title: From lab to field: case study of predicting the capability of accelerated weathering for protective coatings in Qatar
abstract: This study evaluates the ability of accelerated laboratory testing to represent the field performance of four commercial multilayer protective coating systems. Coated carbon-steel panels were exposed to 4,200 h of ISO 12944-9 cyclic aging and compared with panels subjected to two years of natural exposure at a C2 corrosivity site in Qatar. title: Stakeholder perceptions of seafood supply chain resilience and sustainability: an Australian case study
abstract: Abstract Seafood supply chains face increasing disruption from climate change, pandemics, and changing market conditions, creating challenges for maintaining both resilience and sustainability. Understanding the perspectives of people working in the industry and supply chain (i.e. stakeholders) are crucial to developing context-specific and practical pathways for supporting continued seafood supply, livelihoods and profitability. title: Compliance and non-compliance patterns among listed and non-listed ship recycling facilities: a comparative assessment of 22 facilities evaluated for the EU List
abstract: Ship recycling plays a central role in the circular economy of the maritime industry, yet significant disparities persist in safety, environmental performance, and regulatory compliance across global Ship Recycling Facilities (SRFs). This study analyzes 22 official inspection reports conducted by DNV for the European Commission under the EU Ship Recycling Regulation (EU SRR 1257/2013), comparing listed and non-listed facilities. title: Monitoring and Assessment of Aquatic Ecosystems in the Yangtze River Basin
abstract: ABSTRACT Monitoring and assessing aquatic ecosystems are essential for diagnosing ecological conditions and supporting ecosystem management at the basin scale. In response to the strategic transition from a focus on water quality standards to a broader focus on aquatic ecosystem health in the Yangtze River Basin, China implemented a pilot program for aquatic ecosystem monitoring and assessment. title: Physicochemical and microbiological qualities of shrimp (Litopenaeus vannamei) coated with pectin incorporated with green tea spent extract during refrigerated storage
abstract: This study developed and characterized a pectin (PEC) based coating incorporated with green tea spent extract (GTSE) and/or nisin. Further, Pacific white shrimp were treated with the developed coating and investigated for physicochemical, textural, microbial, and melanosis formation during refrigerated storage for 12 days. Among the four coating solutions, PEC-2 had higher homogeneity (583.6 nm) and antioxidant activity (DPPH: 76.73% and ABTS: 70.95%). title: From supporting roles to leaders: women driving change in Odisha’s fisheries sector
abstract: Women are involved across all parts of the fisheries and aquaculture value chains; however, their access to productive assets, technical skills, capital, markets, and decision-making remains unequal. This study investigates changes in women's participation and enterprise performance among women self-help groups (WSHGs) engaged in fisheries and aquaculture in Balasore District, Odisha, India. title: Reviews and syntheses: Snow algae on the move – biased motility and snowpack interaction from a biophysics perspective
abstract: Abstract. Snow algae are psychrophilic and psychrotolerant photosynthetic microorganisms found on every continent, predominantly in polar and alpine environments. Along with contributing to terrestrial carbon cycling and food webs, colourful snow algal blooms formed on snow surfaces can substantially reduce albedo and accelerate snowmelt. Despite their ecological importance, the mechanisms governing snow algae motility and migration within snow remain poorly understood. title: Design and Characterization of Passive Managed Aquifer Recharge Desalination: Multilayer Material Optimization and Techno-Economic Modelling
abstract: Advancing managed aquifer recharge (MAR) is critical towards tackling global freshwater shortages. In this study, layered geological horizons and engineered sorbent sinks were upscaled into a multilayer model to optimize passive underground desalination, using saline groundwater ( C 0 = 35000 mg/L) extracted from depleted hydrocarbon reservoirs. abstract: The increasing activity of armed attacks, pirate raids and military operations in waters where pass key shipping routes conditions actuality to ensure safety of life and health of crew members of merchant navy. Such threats are accompanied with use of various types of weapons and infliction of injuries of varying severity to crew members, that, under absence of timely medical care results in complications and risk to life. title: Rhizosphere-driven desorption-biodegradation coupling reduces pore-water phenanthrene exposure in aged sediments
abstract: Abstract Purpose Sequestration of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) into slowly desorbing pools in sediments constrains their bioavailability and biodegradation. This study evaluated the phytoremediation potential of the submerged macrophyte Potamogeton crispus L. ( P. crispus ) for aged phenanthrene-contaminated sediments and investigated the underlying mechanisms. title: 3D Reconstruction of Dinoflagellate Chromosomes from Hi-C Data Challenges the Cholesteric Liquid Crystal Hypothesis
abstract: Dinoflagellates have permanently condensed chromosomes that are often described as cholesteric liquid crystals (CLCs). The CLC model proposes that DNA is organized into parallel fibers within stacked discs, such that the fiber orientation rotates between adjacent discs. Extrachromosomal loops extending from the discs are hypothesized to be more accessible and thus to contain transcriptionally active genes. title: The 2026 U·S·–Iran War and Its Implications for Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) Exports and Global Energy Markets: The State of Qatar as a Case Study
abstract: This study analyzed the 2026 United States–Iran War and its impact on global LNG exports, using Qatar as a case study. Qatar was chosen because it is a major exporter of liquefied natural gas and depends heavily on the Strait of Hormuz to export LNG to other countries. The study also examined the political and geopolitical aspects of military conflict and its consequences for LNG production and exports, as well as its broader impact on global energy security and energy markets abroad. title: Rainfall homogeneity, variability, and trends across unimodal and bimodal regimes in the Wami Basin, Tanzania
abstract: ABSTRACT The graphical abstract links rainfall data, statistical tests, spatial outputs, and hydrological implications for the Wami basin. Rainfall regime coexistence influences hydrological variability in semi-arid regions, but is rarely treated explicitly in basin-scale assessments. This study evaluates rainfall homogeneity, variability, anomalies, seasonality, and trends across unimodal and bimodal regimes in Tanzania's Wami basin from 1985 to 2014. title: Assessing the Socioeconomic Challenges Affecting Economic Development in Puntland
abstract: Puntland, a self-governing federal member state in north-eastern Somalia, occupies a distinctive position within one of the world's most fragile economies. Since declaring autonomy in 1998, Puntland has built functioning public institutions, a working seaport at Bosaso, and a livestock-led export economy, even as it has remained exposed to drought, clan-based insecurity, weak public revenue, and limited access to international finance. title: Microplastics at the ‘roof of the Americas’: widespread presence in snow on Mount Aconcagua, Central Andes, Argentina
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) pollution has emerged as a pervasive contaminant in remote environments; however, its occurrence in high-altitude snow remains poorly constrained. Here, we provide baseline evidence of MP contamination in snow from four mountaineering camps on Mount Aconcagua (6,962 masl), the highest peak in the Americas and in the entire Western and Southern Hemispheres. Microplastics were identified using µFTIR-ATR spectroscopy. title: Integrated adaptations of muscle structure and mitochondrial function to locomotion demands in teleost fishes
abstract: Abstract Teleost fishes display diverse swimming modes supported by functional specialization of skeletal muscle. However, the ultrastructural adaptations and molecular mechanisms regulating mitochondrial homeostasis in relation to divergent locomotion remain unclear. We compared muscle fiber composition, mitochondrial ultrastructure, and regulatory pathways in two teleosts with contrasting swimming strategies: the sustained swimmer Pseudocaranx dentex and the burst swimmer Paralichthys olivaceus. title: Evaluating the Courier and Delivery Services Company's Efficiency Using an EBM Model
abstract: The market for courier and delivery services is changing favorably as a result of the most recent and continuous technical developments in logistics. Thanks to real–time monitoring technology, which provides transparency and peace of mind, customers can now effortlessly keep a watch on their deliveries at every stage. This study aims to assess the efficiency of nine significant delivery and courier services. title: Sexual dimorphism shapes the plasma metabolome of the endangered Iberian lynx
abstract: Sexual dimorphism is a key but still incompletely resolved determinant of mammalian systemic metabolism, particularly in endangered species where physiological organization remains poorly characterized. Here, we integrate untargeted plasma metabolomics to dissect hierarchical determinants of systemic metabolic organization in the Iberian lynx ( Lynx pardinus ), one of the world’s most endangered felids. title: 16S rRNA amplicon profiling of Salvadora persica -associated rhizosphere bacterial communities under saline agricultural conditions
abstract: Salvadora persica (Arak) is a facultative halophyte adapted to arid and saline environments, yet its rhizosphere microbiome remains poorly characterised. We profiled bacterial communities associated with S. persica at Arak Farm, Rabigh, Saudi Arabia, using Illumina MiSeq sequencing of the V3–V4 16S rRNA region and ASV-based analysis. Three rhizosphere composites and one adjacent bulk-soil composite were analysed. title: Beneficiation and metallurgical challenges of ilmenite-bearing heavy mineral sands: A comprehensive review
abstract: Ilmenite-bearing heavy mineral sand deposits constitute a primary source of titanium feedstock for pigment and metal production. Deposit evaluation and mineral processing flowsheet development are commonly based on total heavy mineral content and bulk titanium dioxide grade, parameters that do not capture the constraints imposed on downstream metallurgical processing. This review examines the physical beneficiation of ilmenite-bearing heavy mineral sands. abstract: ABSTRACT Global warming and environmental pollutants represent escalating threats to crustaceans, with serious implications for aquaculture sustainability and ecosystem stability. abstract: Water is very essential and widely used by humans, animals and for the success of agricultural products. There is paucity of information on bacterial contamination and phytochemical properties of drinking water sources in major slums of Lagos city. abstract: Addressing the interconnected challenges of climate change, biodiversity loss, and human health requires a shift from fragmented governance toward integrated actions. This study applies an analytical framework combining Latent Dirichlet Allocation topic modelling and network analysis to systematically map the Biodiversity, Climate, and Health (BCH) nexus within the Horizon 2020 and Horizon Europe research portfolios. abstract: The in situ relevance of biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) remains poorly understood. We apply meta-omics to characterize BGC diversity and activity along a peatland redox gradient. abstract: Scientific data sharing is central to open science, yet its development is constrained by fragmented data resources, heterogeneous stakeholder incentives, privacy risks, and limited regulatory capacity. This study develops a bounded-rationality, four-population evolutionary game framework involving data providers, data users, government agencies, and sharing platforms. abstract: Water scarcity threatens earthen pond aquaculture's viability and profitability. Drought, variable rainfall, rising air and water temperatures, decreased groundwater availability, and inadequate pond soils deplete stored water through evaporation, seepage, and operating losses. This review synthesises drought-prone pond water retention solutions from engineering, hydrological, aquaculture, and climate-adaptation literature. abstract: This study aimed to determine the concentrations of heavy metals (As, Cr, Cd, Pb, and Hg) in Macrobrachium rosenbergii from prawn farms in Khulna division, Bangladesh, and to assess the associated human health risks. Twenty-four farms in different upazilas of Khulna division were selected for sampling, and heavy metal concentrations in prawns were determined using inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS). abstract: Reliable fault detection and health monitoring of industrial robots are important for smart manufacturing in Industry 4.0. However, robotic platforms differ in their mechanical design, sensing characteristics, and operating conditions. These differences make it difficult for data-driven models to generalize to unseen robots and working conditions. abstract: Well log interpretation faces significant challenges due to data scarcity, distribution shift across geological basins, and a lack of physics-informed representations in current foundation models. abstract: Abstract. Most existing datasets that could support dam and reservoir management and assessments of their impacts in West Africa are limited by inaccurate georeferencing, inconsistent accessibility, heterogeneous data records, and a lack of validation against field observations. In this study, we review and assess existing datasets containing information on dams and reservoirs in West Africa and subsequently integrate them into a harmonized and consolidated regional dataset. abstract: Abstract Purpose Microbially induced carbonate precipitation (MICP) is increasingly applied as an environmentally oriented soil-improvement technique; however, its ecological effects on native soil microbial communities remain insufficiently understood. This study investigated injection-based MICP for soil improvement and the associated restructuring of soil microbial communities. abstract: Abstract This paper presents the results of a new radiocarbon dating program for the Upper Palaeolithic site of Badanj, Bosnia and Herzegovina. After putting together older dates originating from the 1970s and 1980s with recent ones acquired as part of new fieldwork, we then combine the available radiocarbon record with the present understanding of the stratigraphy to create two alternative Bayesian models. abstract: ABSTRACT In the 1980s, the Laysan Albatross ( Phoebastria immutabilis ) expanded its breeding range into the eastern Pacific and established colonies on several islands off the coast of Mexico. Colony growth has varied widely among these islands, likely reflecting differences in immigration rates and local conditions, such as food availability and predation risk, which can influence breeding success and population dynamics. abstract: In recent years, fruit juice consumption has increased worldwide due to its potential health benefits. However, there is concern regarding heavy metals (HMs) in commercial fruit juices, posing significant health risks to their consumers. abstract: Using novel technology and dedicated algorithms, the FLuorescence EXplorer (FLEX) will yield information about the health of the world’s plants. abstract: The anthropocentric consciousness of human beings has induced the belief that humans are the most significant and only important entity in the ecosphere. title: High-resolution mangrove mapping in Guatemala using PlanetScope imagery and a SWIR-free moisture index
abstract: Mangrove forests are ecologically and socioeconomically important ecosystems that require accurate and timely monitoring. This study presents a high-resolution mangrove mapping approach along the Pacific coast of Guatemala using PlanetScope imagery integrated with a machine-learning framework. abstract: Abstract The Urban Heat Island effect intensifies urban temperatures and exacerbates climate-related warming, yet how land cover (LC) buffers or amplifies this warming remains poorly quantified. This study analyzed satellite-derived land surface temperature (LST) across 100 cities from 2000 to 2020 using summer Landsat imagery at five-year intervals, evaluating LC–LST relationships through a three-level framework: net compositional change, pixel-level transition-specific pathways, and a Relative Temperature Index (RTI) revealing cross-city thermal signatures. abstract: Remote ecosystems are often assumed to be insulated from chemical contamination; however, increasing human visitation may compromise this perception. abstract: Environmental DNA (eDNA) metabarcoding is the most recent advancement in freshwater biodiversity monitoring, rapidly identifying aquatic organisms without invasive sampling, but is not able to discriminate between dead and living communities. The fast decaying environmental RNA (eRNA) gives complementary information of metabolically active organisms. abstract: Abstract Brazil’s vast territory and favorable wind conditions have positioned it as a global leader in wind energy development. This study assessed the bacteriological and physicochemical quality of drinking water along the supply chain and evaluated household water handling practices in Dabat Town, northwest Ethiopia. abstract: The Galapagos Islands face significant environmental challenges associated with increasing urbanization and the generation of Construction and Demolition Waste (CDW) from residential buildings. title: Influence of thermal stratification on aquatic community structure and water quality across freshwater ecosystems
abstract: Climate change intensifies thermal stratification in lakes, altering oxygen, nutrients, and habitats, which reduces aquatic biodiversity, modifies biological communities, and compromises the ecological resilience of these ecosystems. In this context, the objective was to evaluate, through a systematic review, the impact of thermal stratification on aquatic biodiversity in lake systems, analyzing changes in richness, abundance, and biological composition associated with thermal stratification. title: Transportation Safety, and Supply Chain Resilience in Road-Based Crude Oil Logistics: Evidence from a Conflict‐Affected Region
abstract: Abstract Crude oil transport is a vital component of global energy supply chains; however, it is riddled with systemic risks, including human error, infrastructure fragility, security vulnerabilities, and regulatory deficiencies. This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of crude oil transport, with particular emphasis on the Kurdistan Region of Iraq (KRG), a semi-autonomous territory that has emerged as a significant oil producer despite enduring geopolitical instability. abstract: The study presents the results of ground deformation monitoring in Almaty for the period 2017–2023 using the SBAS-InSAR method and Sentinel-1 satellite data. The scientific novelty of the research lies in the application of the Small Baseline Subset (SBAS) algorithm for the quantitative assessment of vertical and horizontal displacement rates under conditions of complex terrain and dense urban development. Missing values, attribute noise, and imbalanced classes are some of the significant factors that can impact the quality of input data. title: Technological evolution and emerging research hotspots in earthquake monitoring from 1990 to 2024 revealed by bibliometric evidence
abstract: Earthquake monitoring has changed substantially over the past three decades, yet its technological evolution has rarely been examined through a systematic bibliometric lens. Existing review and scientometric studies have mainly focused on overall publication trends or adjacent disaster domains, with limited attention to how advances in sensing and analysis have reshaped earthquake monitoring itself. title: Non-sewered sanitation systems reshape microplastics into chemically complex and reactive contaminants
abstract: Non-sewered sanitation systems (NSSSs) are gaining global attention as decentralized solutions, yet the transformation of microplastics (MPs) within these systems remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate MP characteristics in the influent and effluent of two NSSSs using laser direct infrared spectroscopy, Fourier transform ion cyclotron resonance mass spectrometry (FT-ICR MS), and liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS). title: Physical controls dominate stream metabolism and carbon cycling over nutrients and stoichiometry
abstract: Abstract Streams process and transport vast carbon quantities along the aquatic continuum. The balance between processing and downstream export is governed by metabolism, which in turn is regulated by distinct physicochemical controls that vary through space and time. However, macronutrient stoichiometry is rarely considered over absolute concentrations. Here, we examined physical, chemical, and stoichiometric controls on stream metabolism, organic carbon mineralization, and carbon spiraling over 2 years. title: Metagenomic insights into viral community restructuring and microbial interactions in waste stabilization ponds
abstract: Abstract Waste stabilization ponds (WSPs) operate as sequential ecological compartments in which physicochemical gradients, microbial succession, and trophic interactions increase toward the final polishing stage. Among these units, the maturation pond represents the terminal control point for pathogen attenuation and effluent quality; however, its role in shaping viral community structure remains insufficiently resolved. Here, we applied shotgun metagenomics to characterize DNA viral communities across the full treatment train of a full-scale WSP system in Giza, Egypt, with particular emphasi

title: Future of edge AI in biodiversity monitoring
abstract: Abstract Many ecological decisions are slowed by the gap between collecting and analysing biodiversity information. Edge computing moves data processing closer to the sensor, with edge artificial intelligence (AI) using AI models for data processing and selective data transfer. edge AI extends the scope of biodiversity monitoring by complementing retrospective ecological analysis with real‐time sensing, enabling responsive and adaptive decision‐making. However, the adoption of edge AI systems in ecological research remains fragmented because deploying efficient and reliable systems is complex.

title: Spatial And Temporal Assessment of Atmospheric Nitrogen Using Hypnum Cupressiforme Mosses and Kjeldahl Analysis
abstract: This study aimed to explore the experiences of Palestinian Nitrogen content in mosses was investigated in a semi-rural area in Lebanon. CALPUFF dispersion model was used to estimate the annual average NOx and NH3 concentrations. Three sampling campaigns were conducted over the course of a year where 33 samples of the moss Hypnum cupressiforme were collected during each campaign. Kjeldahl method was used to determine the total nitrogen content in the collected samples.

title: Groundwater sustainability in hard rock terrains and related health risks assessment in semi-urban Nigeria
abstract: Ten representative groundwater samples were randomly collected from public hand dug wells in the Igarra Town and analyzed to assess their quality for drinking purpose and associated health risks following established methodological standards. The results revealed that pH values ranged from 5.25-6.63, indicating slightly to moderately acidic conditions and deviation from World Health Organization (WHO) and Nigeria drinking water standards (NSDWQ). title: Molecular shape evolution of cyanobacterial circadian clock protein KaiC
abstract: A primitive form of clock protein KaiC has diverged into autonomous or passive time-measuring system. Here we traced molecular shape evolution of ancestral KaiCs using X-ray solution scattering and structure prediction techniques to date this diversification. The results show that the oldest KaiC emerged approximately 3.5–2.8 billion years ago as a moderately expanded and asymmetric double-ring hexamer, and subsequently evolved over approximately 1 billion years into a compact and symmetric form essential for the self-sustained rhythmicity in extant cyanobacteria. institutions: The Graduate University for Advanced Studies, SOKENDAI

title: BUILDING THE RESILIENCE OF LOGISTICS COMPANIES THROUGH SELECTED STAKEHOLDER GROUPS
abstract: Motivation: Logistics companies are a vital link in most global supply chains and improve the performance of their partners by optimising costs, increasing delivery reliability and flexibility of operations, and improving logistics organisation. It is important to note that the logistics industry, through its role in serving other sectors of the economy, is susceptible to any disruption that causes the slowdown in those sectors. title: Quantifying metal transferability in soil and its relationship to metal-related health risks in the strawberry (Fragaria × ananassa)-human food chain
abstract: Understanding metal transfer in soil-strawberry systems is indispensable for sustainable strawberry production. To date, much attention has been paid to metals in strawberries, while metal transferability in strawberry-growing soil has been ignored. In this study, the availability, mobility, and bioavailability indices established based on BCR-extracted metal fractions and previously used for metal bioavailability evaluation in sediments were utilized to estimate metal transferability in soil sampled from strawberry orchards in the Yangtze River Delta, China, and predict metal-related health r

title: Persistent carcinogenic risk from PM2.5-bound metals despite substantial concentration reductions: Evidence from a Chinese megacity during the COVID-19 lockdown
abstract: Health benefits from emission controls are often inferred from reductions in fine particulate matter (PM 2.5 ) mass, yet this metric can underrepresent toxicity from PM 2.5 -bound metals. Using the COVID-19 lockdown as an intervention-like natural experiment, this study quantified how PM 2.5 -bound metals, emission sources, and inhalation health risks changed in Guangzhou, China. Hourly measurements of 16 metals were coupled with positive matrix factorization and source-specific risk apportionment for pre-lockdown, lockdown, and post-lockdown periods. title: Deer disturbance influences avian acoustic activity across functional groups in temperate forests
abstract: Cervid overpopulation is increasingly altering temperate forest ecosystems worldwide, when browsing pressure exceeds ecosystem resilience, with consequences that extend beyond individual species to the structure and functioning of entire communities. While the impacts of deer ( Cervidae ) on specific bird species are well studied, there remains a critical gap in understanding how deer influence avian communities across a spectrum of functional traits. title: Pedological and geochemical characteristics of highly weathered soils derived from ophiolitic rocks in Samar, Philippines
abstract: Limited information is available on the pedology of highly weathered soils derived from ophiolitic rocks in the Philippines. This study evaluated red, highly weathered soils across the ophiolitic landscape of Eastern Samar. Five soil profiles were described and sampled for laboratory analysis. The geochemical composition of the parent materials ranged from mafic to ultramafic. abstract: SThe application of live probiotics in food preservation is often limited by the risk of horizontal gene transfer. In this study, cell-free supernatant (CFS) from Lactobacillus johnsonii KD1 was characterized for its antimicrobial efficacy through minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) and minimum bactericidal concentration (MBC) assays against Vibrio parahaemolyticus, Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium, and Listeria monocytogenes . title: Localization in the internet of things based on game theory with applications in the healthcare
abstract: Accurate indoor localization is critical for healthcare Internet of Things (IoT) applications such as patient tracking and asset management. However, maintaining localization accuracy under node mobility, signal attenuation, and faulty or adversarial behaviors remains challenging. Existing schemes either assume benign environments or employ rigid filters that permanently exclude noisy nodes, causing unacceptable losses in patient monitoring coverage. title: MycorrhizaTracer: A bioinformatic pipeline for fungi and plant classification of Sanger DNA sequences
abstract: Abstract Processing Sanger DNA sequences remains a routine yet technically demanding step in many biodiversity and ecological studies, particularly when barcoding large numbers of environmental samples. Manual inspection and editing of trace files, DNA sequence alignment, and classification using taxonomic reference databases is time-consuming, inconsistent, and prone to error. These challenges are compounded in studies involving degraded samples, in-house DNA sequencing, under-described taxa, or when investigators have limited access to computational tools. title: Identification of Critical Water-Quality Parameters in an Abattoir-Impacted River Using Principal Component and Multivariate Statistical Analyses
abstract: Abattoir wastewater introduces organic matter, nutrients, suspended solids, microorganisms and potentially toxic metals into receiving rivers, producing complex water-quality responses that are difficult to interpret using single-parameter assessments. This study identified the critical variables and dominant pollution processes controlling water quality in the Effurun River, Delta State, Nigeria, using principal component analysis (PCA) and multivariate statistical analysis. title: Development of a Jamʿ al-Āyāt Procedure in Mawḍūʿī Tafsir: An Integrated Model of Syntagmatic Analysis, Tafsir Verification, and Corpus Selection
abstract: Verse collection (jamʿ al-āyāt) is the second of seven steps in al-Farmāwī's mawḍūʿī tafsir, but the step does not specify how the thematic relevance of an individual candidate verse is to be assessed once it has been identified. This article develops a four-stage procedure — textual and syntagmatic analysis, preliminary thematic evaluation, tafsir verification, and synthesis and position determination — that operationalizes this step while keeping it within al-Farmāwī's seven-step framework. title: The investor gaze: recognition heuristic, social liability and legal disillusionment among foreign tourism entrepreneurs on Sri Lanka's southern coast
abstract: This study examines investment failures among foreign visitors and tourism entrepreneurs on Sri Lanka’s southern coast, exploring what can go wrong after tourism-related familiarity encourages investment. It introduces the “investor gaze” as the epistemic position emerging when tourists become resident investors, distinguishing it from familiarity-based confidence and “substitutional collapse,” a specific failure mechanism. abstract: Purpose – This study examines the direct and mediated effects of technical competence and technology mastery on ship pilot performance through the effectiveness of the Pilotage Information System (SIPANDU) at the Class II Harbormaster and Port Authority Office of Bontang. Methodology – An explanatory cross-sectional survey involved 52 active ship pilots. The four-construct model was analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling. title: Muslim-Friendly Tourism Facilities, Tourism Services, and Government Support as Determinants of Indonesian-Tourist Visit Intensity
abstract: The growth of halal tourism underscores the need to understand tourist behavior in multicultural destinations. This study contributes to halal tourism literature by examining how Muslim-friendly facilities, tourism service quality, and government support influence tourist visit intensity in Singkawang, Indonesia, a culturally diverse destination. Grounded in Demand Theory, Customer Satisfaction Theory, and the Theory of Planned Behavior, the study employed a quantitative design involving 550 Muslim tourists with at least two prior visits. title: Groundwater Contamination in India: Regional Variations, Hydrogeochemical Controls, Health Risks, and Integrated Management Strategies
abstract: Groundwater plays a critical role in meeting drinking and agricultural water demands in India. This review focuses on regional variations in groundwater quality, contamination sources, and remediation strategies. The evaluation encompasses pH, electrical conductivity, total dissolved solids, hardness, major ions, and contaminants including fluoride, arsenic, nitrate, and heavy metals. Results reveal significant regional variations, with contamination driven by intensive agriculture, industrial activities, mining, urbanization, and geological factors. title: A comparison of consumer preferences for cell-based seafood across European countries
abstract: Global seafood consumption has been increasing and is expected to continue rising, driven by population growth and evolving dietary patterns. Cell-based seafood has the potential to complement capture fisheries and aquaculture in meeting this growing demand. However, the long-term viability of this emerging sector will depend largely on consumer acceptance. This study examines consumer preferences and acceptance of cell-based seafood in four European countries—Italy, the Netherlands, Portugal, and Hungary. title: Engineering PET surface colonization with a synthetic bacterial consortium
abstract: Introduction Polyethylene terephthalate (PET) is a widely used synthetic polymer that persists in the environment because of its resistance to biological degradation. Although engineered PET hydrolases have shown improved catalytic performance, translating these advances into effective whole-cell degradation remains challenging because cells and enzymes must interact with an insoluble polymer surface. title: Human-validated LLM-assisted assessment of a large-scale online precision medicine course in diabetes
abstract: Precision medicine increasingly relies on multimodal data and artificial intelligence, creating a need for scalable education and assessment. We developed an online diabetes precision medicine course and conducted an observational single-group pre–post evaluation of knowledge, confidence, and rubric-scored open-ended responses among 435 learners who completed the course. Because manual scoring of open-ended responses is time-consuming and subject to variability and human judgment, we developed a human-validated, large language model (LLM)-assisted scoring workflow. abstract: The initial assessment of 43 Indonesian migrant workers (IMWs) in Malaysia revealed that 26 participants were unable to identify at least two official assistance channels, 17 lacked complete copies of essential documents, and 21 expressed concerns about the potential consequences of reporting risky situations. This community engagement program aimed to strengthen IMWs’ capacity to recognize human trafficking schemes, assess risks, determine preventive actions, and access official assistance. title: Not So Stories
abstract: Three short autobiographical stories introduce a host of characters (human and beyond), places, and objects that bridge worlds – worlds of fact and fiction, past and present, Africa and Europe. The three autobiographical reflections, How the Outside Got In, Of Migrants and Music, and New Transvaal Stories, serve as points of departure for diffractive engagements with relational ontologies, histories, and cultures. title: Technical–ethical–governance circuit–breaker framework for safe and sustainable AI governance
abstract: The growing use of large language models and autonomous AI systems in high-risk settings has created safety risks that cannot be addressed through technical safeguards alone. Existing approaches often treat technical failure control, ethical oversight, and institutional governance as separate domains, making coordinated intervention difficult when risks escalate across these boundaries. This study proposes the technical–ethical–governance (TEG) framework as an integrated circuit-breaker architecture for managing risks in high-risk AI systems. title: Crude Oil Theft and Environmental Degradation in Oil-Producing Communities of Rivers State, Nigeria: Evidence from Bodo And Rumuekpe
abstract: This study examines crude oil theft as a direct driver of environmental degradation in Bodo (Gokana LGA) and Rumuekpe (Emuoha LGA), two oil-producing communities in Rivers State, Nigeria, using a descriptive survey design anchored on Strain Theory, Resource Curse Theory, and Environmental Justice Theory. Two communities were purposively selected for their contrasting exposure profiles; within them, 200 respondents were drawn through stratified random sampling across six occupational categories. title: Evaluation of Water Quality from Atmospheric Water Generators Deployed Across Multiple Indian Cities: A Comparative Study
abstract: Atmospheric Water Generators (AWGs) represent an emerging decentralized water solution that extracts moisture from ambient air to produce potable water without reliance on conventional freshwater sources. This study evaluates AWG-produced water quality at three Indian deployment sites — Pune (October 2025), Sringeri (November 2025), and Chennai (October 2025) — against IS 14543:2024, the Indian Standard for packaged drinking water, and benchmarks results against the WHO Guidelines for Drinking-water Quality. title: Locking Down Science Gateways with Landlock and Seccomp
abstract: Abstract The most recent Linux kernels have a new feature for securing applications: Landlock. Like Seccomp before it, Landlock makes it possible for a running process to selectively relinquish access to certain system resources including network and filesystem access. Rather than being a proper successor to Seccomp, Landlock has different and somewhat complementary capabilities. title: Beyond cichlid diversification: environmental drivers of biodiversity across the Nicaraguan lake system
abstract: Abstract The Nicaraguan lake system, comprising two Great Lakes and several isolated crater lakes, is a natural laboratory for investigating how environmental heterogeneity and isolation shape biodiversity and a classic model for Midas cichlid diversification. We asked whether lake characteristics associated with cichlid diversification are also linked to prokaryotic and eukaryotic diversity patterns. title: What matters when? Temporal development of drivers and sources of nitrous oxide emissions in winter wheat
abstract: Abstract. Agriculture is the largest anthropogenic source of nitrous oxide (N2O), primarily due to nitrogen (N) fertilization. Understanding how the influence of key drivers and the relative contribution of source processes change throughout the cropping season is crucial for developing effective strategies to mitigate N2O emissions. In this study, we combined high-resolution eddy covariance flux measurements and stable isotope analyses over one winter wheat cropping season and the subsequent summer cover crop season. title: A validation framework for translating ethnomicrobiology into microbiome-enabled desert restoration
abstract: Microbiome-based dryland restoration is promising but weakly validated. We develop ethnomicrobiology, the study of how human communities manage microbial processes, as a discovery-and-validation framework. A structured evidence map of 42 systems shows food fermentation is most mature, whereas restoration practices lag. We propose a five-level evidence-maturity ladder, from traditional observation to governed field deployment, and apply it to waste-biomass valorization, converting traditional practices into mechanistically tested, ethically governed restoration interventions.

title: Maintenance of bone health by osteoblasts in the absence of osteocytes: comparative analysis of gene expression in medaka and zebrafish vertebrae
abstract: Osteocytes are regarded as the strain-sensing bone cells, their capacity to sense and convert mechanical loads into biological signals underpins our current understanding of how bone is (re)modelled to normalise local strains. However, most extant fish are anosteocytic and lack osteocytes, yet their bone structure and (re)modelling abilities remain unimpeded, sitting uncomfortably with this paradigm. title: Recommendations for microbiological sampling in infected hard-to-heal wounds: an Italian association for cutaneous ulcers (AIUC) perspective
abstract: Chronic and hard-to-heal wounds represent a significant and growing healthcare burden, frequently complicated by infection and impaired healing. Despite the availability of international guidelines, microbiological assessment in clinical practice remains highly heterogeneous, with substantial variability in sampling techniques, timing, and interpretation of results. This variability occurs within a broader One Health context, where antimicrobial resistance and microbial ecology are shaped by interconnected human, environmental, and healthcare factors. title: Analysis of Vessel Clearance in and Clearance Out Procedures at PT Eleanor Pradana Shipping
abstract: This study aims to analyze the procedures for ship clearance in and clearance out services at PT Eleanor Pradana Shipping, identify operational bottlenecks, and evaluate strategic efforts to optimize service efficiency. A descriptive qualitative method was employed, utilizing primary data gathered through field observation, semi-structured in-depth interviews with key personnel on General Manager, Head of Operations, and Operational Staff, and administrative documentation. title: ORGANIC-TAINTED MINERAL SOILS PART II: NEUTRALISATION-FIRST STABILISATION FROM LABORATORY TO FIELD
abstract: Organic-tainted mineral soils remain predominantly mineral and physically compactable, yet reactive organic matter can interfere with conventional lime- and cement-based treatment. Building on the mechanistic framework established in Part I, this companion paper translates neutralisation demand into a laboratory-to-field validation procedure. The approach determines whether preliminary chemical conditioning can reduce organic interference, improve binder activation, and produce more consistent engineering performance than direct binder addition. title: Innovation in health tourism: a service innovation perspective and research agenda
abstract: Health tourism (HT) is an umbrella domain encompassing medical tourism and wellness tourism. While these subdomains have developed substantial research, service models increasingly connect hospitals, clinics, hotels, resorts, and wellness providers, creating overlaps between healthcare, hospitality, and travel. This study uses innovation to connect these subdomains and explain the development of HT and identify future directions. title: A novel multivariate vine-copula–based drought index with application to high-elevation catchments
abstract: Abstract Drought is a complex, slowly evolving hazard governed by multiple interacting hydro-climatic factors, making it difficult to monitor, characterize, and predict. Conventional single-variable indices fail to capture the nonlinear, asymmetric dependence between precipitation and temperature—a limitation that is particularly critical in data-scarce, high-mountain catchments, where incomplete drought characterization undermines the reliability of early-warning systems. title: Identification of rainfall-activated multi-indicator pollution pulses and lagged responses in Erhai Lake based on continuous water quality monitoring
abstract: Abstract Rainfall runoff can activate non-point source pollution and generate short-term water-quality anomalies in plateau lake basins, but event-scale multi-indicator responses remain difficult to identify using conventional mean-based assessments. Here, continuous water-quality records from the Lake Center, Jiangwei, Xiaoguanyi, and Jinhe sections of Erhai Lake from June 2021 to December 2024 were combined with daily precipitation data to identify 127 rainfall events. title: Flow Tree: a model for navigator dynamics and environmental complexity
abstract: Navigation is a dynamic process, involving learning new environments and manoeuvring through them. Individuals differ widely in their abilities and strategies. Prior research often uses static measures, such as total distance travelled or location tallies, which overlook the variability and asymmetry in how trajectories unfold. To address this, we introduce the Flow Tree, a novel data structure that encodes how trajectories evolve relative to each other through time and space. title: Combination of instrumental and biomonitoring approaches elucidate the contributions of multiple and contrasted sources of atmospheric exposure to polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons
abstract: A combined approach was implemented to investigate the origins of elevated PAH concentrations in a complex urban environment where numerous emission sources coexist. This approach integrated one year of atmospheric measurements PM10 filters and continuous atmospheric monitoring), alongside lichen biomonitoring and soil analyses. title: SYSTEM FOR LAND-BASED EMISSIONS ESTIMATION IN KENYA(SLEEK) AND LAND-SECTOR CARBON ACCOUNTING IN KENYA: EVIDENCE FROM EMISSIONS AND REMOVALS ACCOUNTING, 1990-2015
abstract: Developing countries face persistent constraints in producing transparent, consistent and nationally owned greenhouse-gas inventories for the land sector. Kenya responded through the System for Land-based Emissions Estimation in Kenya (SLEEK), a national programme designed to integrate activity data, country-specific parameters, spatial modelling, reporting tools and institutional capacity. title: Two decades-long NDVI anomalies to understand Mediterranean forests ecosystem shifts
abstract: Abstract Mediterranean forest ecosystems are increasingly exposed to climate change, land-use transformations and altered disturbance regimes. Understanding vegetation shifts across these complex landscapes requires scalable, high-resolution tools. In this study, we analyzed a 24-year NDVI time series (2000–2023) from Landsat imagery over the Gargano National Park (Southern Italy) to identify anomalous vegetation dynamics and assess their potential drivers. title: A first, provisional, annotated checklist of the microlepidoptera of Albania (Insecta: Lepidoptera)
abstract: All available published data on the microlepidoptera fauna of Albania are collated and combined with the results of modern sampling to form the first known checklist of Albanian microlepidoptera. Published data are minimal as a consequence of the political history of the country; these historic reports are supplemented by active sampling during the present millennium. abstract: Abstract The increasing atmospheric burden associated with firework manufacturing requires intelligent environmental monitoring frameworks capable of integrating heterogeneous pollution indicators. This study presents an IoT-driven multimodal surveillance architecture designed for industrial air quality assessment in Sivakasi. abstract: This research is based on forecasting the net demand for electricity by considering the previous trends. Considering the overall increase in demand for electricity year by year, predicting such a trend plays a crucial role in a country’s development, as it helps make an accurate prediction of future energy consumption and prepare accordingly. title: Spatiotemporal wildfire occurrence, burn severity and early post-fire vegetation recovery in a tropical Andean landscape: Quilanga, southern Ecuador
abstract: Wildfires are recurrent environmental hazards in tropical Andean landscapes, where limited spatial records can constrain prevention, impact assessment, and post-fire management. This study presents an integrated assessment to characterize wildfire occurrence, burn severity, and early vegetation-greenness recovery in Quilanga, southern Ecuador. abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding the mechanisms driving genetic differentiation—and ultimately, speciation—is central to evolutionary biology, particularly in widespread species inhabiting environmentally complex landscapes. Homonota darwinii , a member of the H. whitii group, is the southernmost gecko in the world, distributed across the Patagonian Steppe—a vast, heterogeneous landscape with a complex geoclimatic history. abstract: Global maritime trade increasingly depends on efficient and safe port operations, where crane operators play a vital role in container handling. Although traditional training methods are effective, they require considerable time and may involve operational risks. Simulation-based training offers a risk-free, cost-effective, and performance-oriented alternative. abstract: General Background Floating power station construction requires highly structured manufacturing workflows to deliver clean energy infrastructure reliably. abstract: Climate services for tourism (CST) face challenges in implementation and long-term continuity because policy coordination and governance mechanisms remain poorly documented. This study assessed whether the CST evidence base reflects a transition from climate-information products to mature service chains supported by policy coordination arrangements. abstract: DNA metabarcoding of freshwater macroinvertebrate samples can provide rapid and accurate identification of species diversity. Processing samples where macroinvertebrates are not separated from net contents can substantially reduce time and cost. We devised and tested a standardised method for processing combined kick/sweep samples using DNA metabarcoding to provide accurate estimates of macroinvertebrate species diversity. abstract: Snakehead fish albumin is a product based on South Kalimantan fishery resources that has the potential to be developed as a value-added agro-industrial product, but its development still faces various strategic obstacles. This study aims to formulate a strategy for developing snakehead fish albumin through an analysis of internal and external factors using the SWOT approach combined with the IFAS, EFAS, and IE matrices. abstract: Large dam vibrations will be assessed by using a sensor network as part of the proposed protocol. abstract: The growing demand for self-powered systems in distributed sensing, Internet-of-Things devices, and structural health monitoring has stimulated increasing interest in flow-induced piezoelectric energy harvesting. abstract: The transition from conchocelis to conchosporangial branches is not only a key stage in the life cycle of Pyropia/Porphyra but also directly affects the yield and quality of economically important species such as Pyropia haitanensis . abstract: This research investigated the multi-sectoral readiness of Barcelona, Sorsogon, to implement the Department of Science and Technology (DOST) Smart and Sustainable Communities Program (SSCP). title: Assessment of post-construction quality of projects: cases from Sinja valley of Nepal
abstract: Post-construction quality determines whether public investment is converted into durable and usable service, yet small public works in remote mountain municipalities of Nepal are rarely assessed after handover. This study assesses the post-construction quality of completed projects in Sinja Valley of Jumla district, Karnali Province. abstract: Background: Envenomation by snakes, scorpions, spiders, and caterpillars remains a major but unevenly addressed public health challenge in Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC). Environmental change, urbanisation, and ecological disruption are changing the distribution of medically important species, while persistent gaps in surveillance, clinical management, and antivenom availability limit prevention and care. title: Decoding individual dairy cow behavioral profiles through electronic feeder and drinker data
abstract: Individual animals can differ considerably in how they feed, drink, and compete for resources, yet much data analysis still relies on group-level comparisons that obscure these individual differences. Electronic feeding and drinking systems make it possible to characterize individual behavioral profiles within groups. title: Changes in arbovirus risks and responses from 2020 to 2026
abstract: Abstract Since 2020, viruses spread by mosquitoes and biting midges have become a larger and less predictable public health challenge. Dengue continues to cause the greatest burden, but chikungunya, Oropouche, and other viruses are re-emerging or spreading into new areas. In this narrative review, we summarize major changes in arbovirus epidemiology, surveillance, diagnosis, vaccination, treatment, vector ecology, and mosquito control from 2020 to 2026. abstract: Hourly precipitation products are often assembled from station records with heterogeneous sub-hourly reporting cadences, yet users rarely know how much of the resulting difference in extreme diagnostics reflects temporal support, clock-hour alignment, the aggregation implementation, or the temporal structure of the rainfall. abstract: This study was conducted to determine the effect of the implementation of the occupational safety and health management system (SMK3) on employee work productivity at KSOP Utama Makassar. The results of this study indicate that, simultaneously (F-test), occupational safety and occupational health have a significant positive effect on employee work productivity, accounting for 87.6%. abstract: En la actualidad, los dilemas éticos y bioéticos existen en todos los ámbitos, especialmente en los laboratorios clínicos. El objetivo de este estudio fue analizar la ética y bioética en el laboratorio clínico mediante una revisión bibliográfica documental de tipo narrativo, utilizando PubMed y Google Académico como fuentes de consulta científica, considerando documentos publicados entre 2015-2026 en inglés y castellano. title: Bioash amendments from biomass energy systems reshape rhizosphere bacterial communities and reduce metal bioavailability in contaminated soils
abstract: Biomass-derived ashes (bioash) from energy production are increasingly promoted within circular bioeconomy frameworks as soil amendments that recycle nutrients and mitigate soil acidity. However, their impacts on rhizosphere bacterial communities in metal-contaminated soils (MCS) remain poorly understood. abstract: Abstract Bats are hosts to diverse zoonotic viruses which can cause high case fatality rates in humans. Since detecting viruses in bats is difficult, antibodies are often used for surveillance, though their significance remains unclear in the absence of in vivo immunological studies. title: A supergene and genomic mosaicism are associated with phenotypic evolution in Galápagos tree finches
abstract: Adaptive radiations provide powerful models to study the origins of phenotypic novelty and species diversity. Darwin's finches constitute a classic example of adaptive radiation, in which beak morphology is a key trait related to fitness. Here, we focus on Camarhynchus tree finches by analyzing whole genomes in combination with morphological data to revisit long-standing questions regarding their origins raised before genetic evidence became available. abstract: Finding the appropriate supplier is becoming increasingly difficult because of the complexity in evaluation criteria. abstract: In estimating rainfall over the composite coverage area of the Takhli and Sattahip radars, the use of a composite Z–R relationship may still result in residual errors due to differences in the physical characteristics of rainfall. title: When Clades Collide: Genomic Admixture in Blacklegged Ticks ( Ixodes scapularis ) From the Great Plains
abstract: Ixodes scapularis ticks transmit a number of pathogens important to human health, including Borrelia burgdorferi sensu stricto, the causative agent of Lyme disease. While I. scapularis is found across the Eastern United States, Lyme disease transmission is largely limited to the Northeast and Upper Midwest and is nearly absent in the South. Although puberty represents a critical window of susceptibility to toxic insults, the effects of DON exposure during this period remain poorly understood. This study evaluated the effects of DON on testicular structure, oxidative status, inflammatory responses, and sperm parameters in prepubertal and adult mice. title: Occurrence and hydrolytic stability of emerging tire wear contaminants in environmental waters and soils: A case study from northern Poland
abstract: Background Tire wear particles release additives and transformation products into the environment. Among these, p -phenylenediamines (PPDs) and their quinone transformation products (PPD-Qs), including 6PPD-Q, have attracted increasing attention. However, data on tire wear contaminants (TWCs) in Central and Eastern Europe remain limited, and their hydrolytic stability is poorly characterized. This study investigated the hydrolytic stability of 16 TWCs, optimized sample pre-treatment, and assessed their occurrence and preliminary ecological risks in water and soil samples from northern Poland.

abstract: Auxotrophy, the inability of bacteria to synthesize one or multiple essential metabolites, is thought to be common among bacteria. However, studies often rely on either bioinformatic genome-based prediction of auxotrophies or on experiments with low strain numbers. Here, we combine experimental and bioinformatic approaches to assess amino acid auxotrophies among 315 co-isolated natural Pseudomonas strains from pond and soil habitats. title: Estacionalidad y variabilidad espacial de las lluvias en la Patagonia Austral Continental
abstract: La precipitación es uno de los fenómenos meteorológicos con mayor variabilidad espacial y temporal, y su estacionalidad influye de manera directa en la provisión de servicios ecosistémicos y en la productividad primaria neta de pastizales y cultivos, especialmente en ambientes áridos y semiáridos. En este estudio se analizó la estacionalidad de la precipitación para el período 1995-2014 y su variabilidad espacial y temporal en la Patagonia Austral Continental. abstract: This article examines the functioning of proper names from a sociolinguistic and political perspective, focusing on the name of the Republic of Belarus across languages. The aim of the study is to explain why the form Belarus (Byelarusʹ) is promoted by Belarusian authorities and communities, and why traditional exonyms continue to be used in other languages. abstract: Solar power is a rapidly growing renewable energy source that converts sunlight into electricity using photovoltaic (PV) cells. Global solar capacity has grown exponentially over the past decade, driven by plummeting technology costs and aggressive government climate targets. abstract: Antibiotics are among the most widely distributed contaminants of emerging concern in aquatic systems, entering water from hospital effluent, pharmaceutical manufacturing, livestock production, aquaculture and municipal sewage. Drawing on the concept of social harmony, this study aims to understand the factors shaping local acceptance and the dynamics of interaction between Indigenous peoples and migrants. abstract: Abstract This study investigates the combined effects of geology, land use and land cover, hydrological seasonality, and disturbance history on the hydrogeochemistry of surface waters in the Paraopeba River Basin (PRB), located in Minas Gerais State, southeastern Brazil, and forming part of the São Francisco River Basin, a region characterized by high lithological complexity and intense anthropogenic pressure. abstract: Background Air pollution has been linked to adverse COVID-19 outcomes. abstract: Tourism growth in emerging destinations has intensified competition among leisure venues, particularly in Bali’s beach clubs, which have become a distinctive attraction for domestic and international tourists. Sustaining revisit intention is critical for the long-term success of these establishments, yet little is known about the determinants of loyalty in this context. This study investigates the mediating role of satisfaction in the relationship between perceived value, hedonic value, and revisit intention, drawing upon the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB). title: Photoaging-driven amplification of polystyrene microplastic toxicity in wheat: physiological and multi-omics insights
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) in agroecosystems displayed phytotoxicity; however, the differential effects of pristine and photoaged MPs remain unclear. abstract: ABSTRACT This study aimed to investigate whether the degree of polymerization (DP) influences intestinal health benefits of pectic oligosaccharide (POS) in broilers. title: Smart Multi-Species Milk Bank System (SM²BS) Integrating Cold Chain Management, Digital Traceability, and Nutritional Profiling of Cow, Goat, Sheep, Mare, and Buffalo Milk
abstract: The Smart Multi-Species Milk Bank System (SM²BS) is proposed as an integrated digital platform to improve milk supply chain management through cold chain management, digital traceability, and nutritional profiling. This study adopts a qualitative approach involving literature review, observation of milk handling processes, and stakeholder discussions to identify operational challenges and develop a conceptual framework for managing cow, goat, sheep, mare, and buffalo milk. abstract: This study aimed to determine heavy metal contents in the fish of Nguru Local Government Area (LGA), Yobe State, Nigeria, and assess the potential health risks associated with their consumption. The work seeks to enhance public health awareness and promote environmental sustainability in the region. Heavy metals, including Lead, Cadmium, Chromium, Arsenic, and Copper, pose significant threats to aquatic ecosystems and human health. title: Floods Early Warning Messages in a Rural Province in South Africa
abstract: ABSTRACT Floods remain among the most frequent and damaging natural hazards globally, with effective flood early warning messages (FEWMs) playing a critical role in reducing disaster risk and enhancing community preparedness. Despite advances in early warning systems, many rural communities in developing countries continue to experience challenges in accessing, understanding, and responding to warning information. title: Uncertain consequences of releasing game‐farm mallards: further insights and implications
abstract: Abstract Mallards ( Anas platyrhynchos ) have been domesticated and released in Europe and North America for centuries to supplement hunter harvest and in attempts to increase populations. They have interbred with wild mallards, most notably in the Atlantic Flyway of North America. Published research indicates that >90% of mallards harvested in the Atlantic Flyway are hybrids, and the species has formed a hybrid swarm of wild‐strain and game‐farm (GF) birds. title: A STATISTICAL APPROACH TO DCPT DATA IN DETERMINING SUBGRADE PARAMETERS FOR ROAD PAVEMENTS
abstract: This study examines the characteristics of the road base layer in pavement construction using a statistical method based on Dynamic Cone Penetration Test data. The subgrade condition must be accurately assessed to avoid premature pavement failure, such as cracking and settlement. Field investigations were conducted at a number of sites with various types of soil. However, due to access restrictions, only two main sites were tested. title: Greenwashing and the Erosion of Consumer Trust: A Critical Analysis of Communication Ethics in Tourism
abstract: The discrepancy between sustainability claims and actual practices in tourism and hospitality has brought forth the "greenwashing" phenomenon. This conceptual study analyzes the multi-dimensional effects of greenwashing perceptions on consumer trust through legitimacy theory, signaling theory, and attribution theory. The study argues that greenwashing represents not merely an ethical violation, but also a strategic risk and market failure. title: Glacier change at the ISM-MLW transition: multi-decadal evidence of spatial heterogeneity from the Sara Umga watershed, western Himalaya
abstract: This study presents a multi-decadal assessment of glacier change in the Sara Umga Watershed (SUW), between the Parvati and Chandra basins. The region receives a majority of its annual precipitation from Indian Summer Monsoon (ISM) and a comparatively lower share contributed by winter Mid Latitude Westerlies (MLW). Using multi-temporal satellite data, we quantify changes in glacier length, area, surface velocity, elevation, debris cover, ice cliff dynamics, and high-faltitude lakes, supplemented by long-term climate trend analysis.
