title: Evaluation of larvicidal efficacy of Clerodendrum infortunatum Linn extracts against Culex quinquefasciatus Say (Diptera, Culicidae)
abstract: Clerodendrum infortunatum Linn (Family, Lamiaceae), extracts of acetone, methanol and aqueous evaluated against larvae of Culex quinquefasciatus Say, showed promising results. Acetone leaf extract recorded an LC50 value of 345.41ppm, and was found effective for the management of Cu. quinquefasciatus. In vitro cytotoxic analysis of L929 mouse cell lines using the plant extract proved safe for non-target organisms, higher vertebrates. Phytochemical screening of the acetone extract revealed the presence of secondary metabolites that may have contributed to its insecticidal activity.

abstract: Reliable sensor data is essential for understanding process dynamics and enabling data-driven monitoring in machining processes. However, experimental data acquisition is typically subject to resource constraints in data collection under controlled conditions, leading to a scarcity of characteristic data that hinders the development of robust data-driven models. This study introduces a diffusion-based generative AI-framework for synthesizing machining power data in end milling to support the development of machined surface integrity evaluation methodologies. abstract: Decompiling stripped binaries to assist human reverse engineers remains a critical yet highly challenging task in software security. Prior work has developed various neural networks and even dedicated large language models (LLMs) to improve function and variable name recovery in decompiled code. title: Morocco's grand strategy: Pillars and limitations
abstract: The Grand Strategy aims to align a state’s means and resources with its strategic priorities in pursuit of national interests, while taking into account internal and external constraints. For Morocco, the Grand Strategy provides a key framework for achieving national interests and redefining the country’s position within the international community. abstract: Our research addresses the limited applicability of traditional reliability assessment methods by implementing a hybrid framework for the Branson 2000X AED ultrasonic welding system in mass production. We aimed to align the quantitative technical framework with the causality and financial impacts of identified failures. title: Molecular basis of sphingosine-1-phosphate transport by MFSD2B provides insights for selective inhibitor screening
abstract: Sphingosine-1-phosphate (S1P) regulates immune cell trafficking, vascular homeostasis, and platelet function. Major facilitator superfamily domain-containing protein 2B (MFSD2B) maintains plasma levels of S1P by exporting it from erythrocytes and platelets, but how MFSD2B recognizes and transports S1P remains unclear. Here, we determined the structure of Sus scrofa MFSD2B by cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM). title: Fungus above us: exploring the atmospheric mycobiome by aircraft
abstract: Fungi play a key role in ecosystems, influencing the global bioaerosol budget and pollution dynamics even when metabolically inactive. Despite this, diversity and transport of fungi in the atmosphere are not well explored. This study shows that the atmosphere contains diverse fungi with varied ecological classifications and recruitment patterns reflecting underlying terrestrial habitats. Abundant genera include Neoascochyta , Cladosporium , Alternaria , Coniothyrium , Penicillium , Hymenochaetopsis , Lachnum , and Fonsecazyma . abstract: ABSTRACT To examine the influence of diet on fish gut microbiota in channelized rivers, we characterized the gut microbial communities of fish with different feeding habits in the midstream of the Jialing River. The main findings are as follows: (1) 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing identified Firmicutes and Proteobacteria as the dominant phyla, with their relative abundances differing significantly among fish of distinct feeding habits. abstract: Data on microplastics in Central African inland waters remain limited. This study assesses contamination in the surface waters and surficial sediments of four Pool Malebo sites: Maluku, Kinkole, Kingabwa-Baramoto, and Kinsuka, Democratic Republic of the Congo. Sampling was conducted in June 2024, with three independent replicates per site. Water samples were vacuum-filtered, and sediments underwent KOH digestion followed by vacuum filtration. abstract: Ambient fine particulate matter (PM₂.₅) has emerged as one of the most pressing environmental health challenges in East Africa, where rapid urbanization, industrial expansion, and reliance on biomass fuels converge to elevate exposure levels. Despite its recognized role in respiratory and cardiovascular morbidity, monitoring of PM₂.₅ across the region remains fragmented, with limited reference-grade stations and growing reliance on low-cost sensors and satellite-derived estimates. abstract: Abstract What can the United Nations do to strengthen the protection of civilians when it fails? When missions struggle to protect civilians, high‐level naming and shaming of non‐responsive units within the operation can occur to reorient the operation. Shaming helps rehabilitate the operation and achieve the protection of civilians. abstract: Urinary tract infections (UTIs) represent one of the most common bacterial infections worldwide and are increasingly complicated by the emergence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) uropathogens. The present cross-sectional study aimed to investigate the incidence, microbial diversity, and antimicrobial resistance profiles of uropathogens isolated from clinically diagnosed UTI patients belonging to different high-risk groups. abstract: Abstract Most biological control programmes against invasive alien plants (weeds) utilise agents collected from indigenous populations of the target weed that are thought to have a long coevolution history between the target weed and the agent. These biocontrol agents are referred to as old associations. abstract: Objectives Candida albicans ( C. albicans ) biofilm serves as a major cause of Candida-related infections. However, the available antifungal agents are limited in variety, and the emergence of drug resistance has complicated clinical treatment. abstract: This study addresses osteoarthritis (OA), in which dysregulated chondrocyte cholesterol homeostasis and cellular senescence contribute to cartilage degeneration, by developing an inflammation-responsive injectable QCG hydrogel for local delivery of miR-106a-enriched M2 macrophage-derived small extracellular vesicles (sEVs). abstract: Acrossocheilus fasciatus is an economically important freshwater fish species in China. In recent years, Citrobacter freundii infection has caused significant harm to the aquaculture industry. abstract: Fruits such as cranberry (Vaccinium macrocarponAiton), that contain several phenolic substances, are processed commercially as juices, requiring treatments to extend shelf-life. abstract: The Miskito constitute Honduras’s largest indigenous population (~ 80,000 individuals), yet population-specific genetic databases essential for accurate forensic analysis remain unavailable. Allele frequencies for 23 autosomal short tandem repeat loci were determined from 100 unrelated Miskito individuals (52 females, 48 males) from four settlements in Gracias a Dios department. abstract: As spatial molecular data grow in scope, there is a pressing need to identify disease-associated spatial structures. Current approaches typically make restrictive assumptions such as representing tissue regions by abundances of discrete cell types and samples by abundances of discrete niches; this risks overlooking important signals. abstract: Plastic-waste combustion in small-scale food production may create particle-rich environments with potential for deposition onto exposed foods, yet paired environmental–food evidence remains limited. abstract: Close-kin mark-recapture (CKMR) offers a promising alternative to traditional mark-recapture methods for estimating wildlife population parameters. CKMR estimates demographic parameters by identifying genetic relationships between individuals, effectively "recapturing" parental genotypes through their offspring's genetic profiles. abstract: 1. Phylogenetic comparative methods require species names in a trait dataset to match tip labels in a phylogenetic tree. Names may differ because of, for example, formatting, taxonomic revisions, synonyms, or spelling errors. abstract: Background: Environmental factors such as air pollution and urban greenness are important in influencing pediatric asthma, yet their individual effects remain unclear across industrial and non-industrial settings. This study examined whether urban greenness modifies the link between air pollution and pediatric asthma in Kaohsiung (industrial) and Taipei (non-industrial), Taiwan, by highlighting differential environmental impacts on children’s health. title: Spatiotemporal Assessment of Climatic Water Scarcity in Nigeria Using an Integrated Standardized Precipitation Index–Temperature Anomaly Index (SPI–TAI) Framework
abstract: Climate change is increasing water scarcity in Nigeria through rising temperatures and declining rainfall, and most of the drought evaluations depend on precipitation only. The study examined the climate-induced water scarcity situation in Nigeria using the Standardized Precipitation Index (SPI) and the Temperature Anomalies Index (TAI). Monthly precipitation and temperature data for 1901–2024 were extracted from the Climatic Research Unit Time Series (CRU TS v4.09) dataset through the Google Earth interface. title: FROM LUXURY TO RESPONSIBLE CONSUMPTION: NUTRITIONAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL PERSPECTIVES ON THE PRODUCTION OF SIBERIAN STURGEON CAVIAR (ACIPENSER BAERII, BRANDT, 1869)
abstract: Caviar is a fish-based food product of high gastronomic and economic value, traditionally associated with luxury cuisine, but increasingly examined in the context of sustainability and responsible aquaculture. This review paper summarizes current information on the consumption of caviar derived from the Siberian sturgeon (Acipenser baerii Brandt, 1869), from nutritional, technological, and ecological perspectives. title: Cognitive and institutional barriers to effective natural resource management under global change
abstract: Many of the most challenging decisions facing natural resource managers today can be understood as time dependent. The concept of time-dependent decisions is useful when considering natural resource management decisions that are characterized by nonstationarity in the underlying ecological system, uncertainty surrounding key ecological relationships, efficacy of management interventions, and difficult trade-offs between the present and the future. abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) is one of the important cancers that are responsible for considerable morbidity all over the world. Recent studies reveal that changes in the oral microbiome are linked with HNSCC, but the exact microbial signatures according to the presence of disease need further research. In this study, metagenomic analysis was done on the oral microbiome of 210 HNSCC patients and 180 healthy controls based on the whole-genome shotgun metagenomic sequencing technique. This study developed an evaluation system comprising five criterion-level dimensions, 12 sub-criteria, and 26 indicators. abstract: Among the human-associated Aeromonas species, A. dhakensis is increasingly implicated in systemic infections and high rates of antimicrobial resistance. Two strains of A. dhakensis were recently isolated from separate clinical cases of fatal, monomicrobial bacteremia and we aimed to define the genes and pathways utilized by these isolates during infection. abstract: Contributing to the burgeoning interdisciplinary literature on affective and emotional governance of borders, this paper explores recently emerging strands of affective border governance literature to contextualize Middle Eastern borders. This contextualization highlights areas where Middle Eastern border studies are developed and where they remain underdeveloped in relation to the affective governance of borders. title: The evolving role of liver biopsy in chronic liver disease: a pathological and clinical perspective
abstract: Abstract Background Liver biopsy has traditionally been regarded as the reference standard for evaluating chronic liver disease because it provides direct tissue-level assessment of necroinflammatory activity, fibrosis, architectural remodeling, and disease-specific patterns of injury. However, its role has changed substantially with the widespread use of serum-based biomarkers, elastography, imaging, and other non-invasive tests that now guide risk stratification and follow-up in many clinical settings. title: Abnormal ingestive behavior in male zoo gorillas: investigating the dietary and activity patterns associated with regurgitation and reingestion
abstract: Introduction Regurgitation and reingestion (R&R) is a widely observed, yet poorly understood, abnormal ingestive behavior among zoo-housed apes, including gorillas. While frequently characterized as a stereotypical behavior, emerging hypotheses suggest R&R may serve metabolic or self-regulatory functions in response to altered feeding patterns in captivity. abstract: ABSTRACT Established under the Disability Inclusion Act 2014 (NSW), Disability Inclusion Action Plans (DIAPs) are public accountability instruments through which New South Wales (NSW) councils translate statutory disability inclusion obligations into place‐based inclusion planning. Many of the local environments, services and systems through which inclusion is experienced fall within council responsibilities. abstract: Many animal species replace histones with protamines during spermatogenesis. Although essential for sperm function, protamines evolve rapidly for reasons that remain unknown. abstract: Modern microbiological research generates vast quantities of data, particularly from high-throughput "omics" technologies. These datasets promise unprecedented insights into microbial diversity, function, and interactions, yet they are often deposited in unstructured formats with inadequate metadata, significantly hampering their discoverability, interoperability, and long-term reusability. abstract: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA) is a multisystem immune-mediated disease characterized by adult-onset asthma, eosinophilic inflammation, and necrotizing vasculitis of small-to-medium-sized vessels. Diagnosis is frequently prompted by clinically overt neurological, cardiac, renal, cutaneous, or gastrointestinal involvement. abstract: The construction industry is among the most resource-intensive sectors, contributing substantially to global resource consumption. In light of the escalating scarcity of natural resources, the circular economy (CE) paradigm offers a promising avenue for the recovery and reuse of raw materials. In order to achieve this objective, it is essential to establish a reliable information base that encompasses both semantic and geometric building data throughout the entire life cycle of a building. title: Genome reorganisation and expansion shape 3D genome architecture and define a distinct regulatory landscape in coleoid cephalopods
abstract: How genomic changes translate into organismal novelties is often confounded by the multi-layered nature of genome architecture and the long evolutionary timescales over which molecular changes accumulate. Coleoid cephalopods (squid, cuttlefish, and octopus) provide a unique system to study these processes due to a large-scale chromosomal rearrangement in the coleoid ancestor that resulted in highly modified karyotypes, followed by lineage-specific fusions, translocations, and repeat expansions. title: Geochemical assessment of soil and water around abandoned gold mine tailings dams: evidence from the Welkom Goldfield, South Africa
abstract: Abstract Gold mining in Welkom, South Africa, has generated abandoned mine tailings containing potentially toxic elements, some located near residential and agricultural areas. This study evaluated soil and water geochemistry around abandoned tailings, emphasising ecological and human-health risks. Soil and water samples were collected near and away from abandoned mine tailings and analysed using Inductively Coupled Plasma Mass Spectrometry (ICP-MS) and Inductively Coupled Plasma Optical Emission Spectrometry (ICP-OES). Soil samples were assessed for total and leachable element concentrations.

title: Weeds as teachers on country: Management through seasonal story calendars
abstract: This paper reconceptualises weeds through Australian Indigenous knowledge systems, presenting them not as invasive threats, but as teachers; living beings that offer ecological insight, support restoration, and contribute to cultural renewal and resurgence. Drawing on relational governance theories, the study employs Indigenous methodologies, including yarning with Country and the development of a storying seasonal calendar, to examine the behaviours and teachings of Fireweed (Senecio madagascariensis), African Lovegrass (Eragrostis curvula ), and Lantana (Lantana camara). title: Drawing Out Hilbre: Tidal Event-Scores Between the Cartographic and the Choreographic
abstract: Drawing Out Hilbre is a practice-based enquiry on Hilbre Island where access is timed, ground is temporary, and orientation is continuously re-made through weather, tide, and group behaviour. Following Sarah Rubidge's (2012) proposition that movement generates dynamic systems that shape perception, I treat the crossing not as a route to be documented but as a space-producing force: the island seems to fill and empty, attention is pulled and re-pulled, and intensities accumulate where bodies cluster, disperse, hesitate, or reroute. title: Sentinel-2 NDVI as an indicator of apple orchard yield
abstract: Satellite data is increasingly being used as a basis for operational crop monitoring. However, satellite technologies for monitoring perennial crops remain underdeveloped. The aim of this study was to assess the relationship between apple yield and NDVI calculated using all available Sentinel-2 data for the growing seasons (March-November) from 2017 to 2024. abstract: The increasing availability of spaceborne imaging spectroscopy data requires validation approaches capable of linking measurements acquired at different spatial scales. This study examines the temporary Sal ’e Porcus saline pond in western Sardinia, Italy, as a candidate reference surface for cross-scale spectral comparison. Aim: The main aim of the study is to assess the level of knowledge and attitude of autopsy practice in Bayelsa State. Method: The study adopted a mixed method using both quantitative and qualitative methods, adopting both a descriptive survey design and thematic analysis. title: Automated Sailboat Navigation using Controllabilty-Aware Nonlinear Model Predicitive Control under Stochastic Winds
abstract: This paper presents a systematic approach to plan and execute a time-efficient sailboat trajectory under the challenging stochastic wind conditions for automated sailboat. Unlike deterministic scenarios, stochastic wind disturbances introduce challenges such as gust unpredictability, directional shifts, and fluctuating apparent wind speeds. These characteristics render traditional planning methods, such as Line-of-Sight (LoS) and waypoint approaches, to be ineffective and not applicable, as they often rely on static or deterministic environmental models. title: Six objects reported at 480 mph in a declassified military infrared video show brightness flicker at bird wingbeat rates
abstract: In September 2026 the U.S. Department of War released an infrared video recorded from a military aircraft over the Middle East, with a mission report describing six small spherical objects moving at an estimated 480 miles per hour. We measure the brightness of each object in every frame. All six brighten and dim steadily at 7.1-7.9 times per second, each at its own rate and out of step with the others. title: HGP:An on-device personalized agent memory via hybrid graph storage
abstract: LLM-based agents face challenges in personalized interactive tasks due to heterogeneous, multi-typed, and implicitly constrained long-term traces. Existing memory mechanisms struggle with accurate routing and retrieval, especially on-device where personalization is critical. Most methods use single-vector representations, blurring type distinctions and relational structure. We propose HGP, a hybrid graph memory framework. title: The CosmicWatch Desktop Muon Detector (v3X): Prototype Design and Adaptation for Spaceflight
abstract: The CosmicWatch Desktop Muon Detector (v3X) is a compact and low-cost scintillator-based instrument designed to detect ionizing radiation, including cosmic-ray muons. Built around a plastic scintillator, a silicon photomultiplier (SiPM), and a dual-core Raspberry Pi Pico microcontroller, the v3X achieves a 400 microsecond dead time per event, sustained event logging at 700 Hz, and two-detector coincidence triggering for more accurate counts. title: Estimation and inference in penalized function-on-function regression with dependent residual curves
abstract: Penalized function-on-function regression, as implemented in the R package refund, treats all grid values of all curves as independent. Residual curves are smooth, so values within a curve are dependent. We study what this does to point estimates and pointwise confidence intervals, in a simulation with Gaussian, count and binary responses and in a plasmode study built on nine real datasets. title: Split Skies: Operational Experiences Extending a Multi-Cloud Network Telescope into the Asia-Pacific
abstract: Comprehensive visibility into Internet Background Radiation (IBR) requires diverse measurement infrastructure. Recent work showed that cloud IBR depends on the provider making single-provider telescopes systematically biased. These studies relied entirely on Western providers and left the Asia-Pacific region as a blind spot. In this report we extend a multi-cloud network telescope onto Tencent Cloud inside mainland China. title: Precise Stellar Age Constraints and Habitable Zone Evolution in Exoplanet Systems
abstract: Abstract Accurate stellar ages are fundamental to interpreting the evolutionary histories of habitable zone (HZ) planets. Because stellar luminosity evolves over time, HZ boundaries migrate outward, meaning that present-day HZ planets may have experienced different irradiation environments earlier in their evolution. Accurate ages are therefore required to estimate HZ residence times and place planetary habitability in an evolutionary context. abstract: We introduce HyperBrowseComp, a multilingual and multimodal browsing benchmark comprising 423 manually authored and human-validated questions across 13 languages, written by native or highly proficient speakers. Questions are designed to be extremely challenging. Each question targets a concise, publicly verifiable answer whose discovery requires locating obscure evidence, following multi-step clue chains, or inspecting heterogeneous sources such as videos, scanned documents, images, or maps. title: Connectedness, Cognitive Load, and Human-AI Oversight in Cyber Operations
abstract: AI-assisted cyber situational awareness triggers machine-generated reasoning traces (step-by-step justifications for anomaly classifications) that a human operator is expected to review. Because cyber signals and their traces arrive faster than any operator can process, human review is the limiting constraint on oversight. The standard approach is to identify the riskiest cyber events for review using model-side signals such as confidence or uncertainty. title: AdHImEx: Adaptively High-Order Implicit-Explicit Transport for Large Time Steps
abstract: Adaptively Implicit-Explicit (AdImEx) time stepping provides stability for large time steps for mass-conservative transport, making it attractive for the numerical representation of advection in weather and climate prediction. Existing AdImEx transport schemes become first-order accurate in the large-time-step, implicit regime and may require multiple sparse matrix solutions per time step. This work introduces AdHImEx, a new AdImEx scheme that addresses both limitations simultaneously. abstract: Given a subvariety of the Grassmannian and a data point, we seek to find a point on the subvariety minimizing the Euclidean distance to the data point. title: Persistent Context Graphs for Efficient Memory Compaction in LLM Agents
abstract: As LLM capabilities advance, agents are tackling increasingly complex tasks over longer horizons. Their growing interaction histories make memory compaction essential for staying within context windows and reducing prefill cost. Existing methods summarize the history or compress its KV cache, often adding model computation to preserve information for future requests. title: AI-Generated Disinformation in the UK: Risk of Harm, Context, and Classification
abstract: More people across the UK are today exposed to more AI-generated and AI-altered disinformation and misinformation than ever before - exposing individuals and society to a growing range of harmful consequences and potential consequences. We analyse evidence from a dataset of 112 pieces of AI-generated or AI-altered disinformation or misinformation seen tens of millions of times across the UK between 1 January 2025 and 31 March 2026. title: The muon charge asymmetry and the directional distribution of thunderstorm events observed by the GRAPES-3 muon telescope
abstract: Abstract The intense electric fields inside thunderstorms can significantly modify the intensity of secondary cosmic ray muons at the ground level, producing measurable variations in their intensity (|ΔI μ | >0.3%). title: ULTRADISCOVERY: Abductive Exploration in an Interconnected, Epistemically Open Universe
abstract: Scientific discovery often begins when scattered clues call for a new way of describing the world. Such abductive exploration can require constructing the representation in which an explanation is stated, when the world is epistemically open, and composing evidence scattered across contexts, when it is structurally interconnected. title: Magnus: neutrino oscillation probabilities for any Hermitian Hamiltonian, any number of flavors, and any matter profile
abstract: Neutrino oscillation probabilities computed with the Magnus expansion, for an arbitrary number of flavors and any Hamiltonian, time-dependent or not. Every truncation of the series lives in the Lie algebra, so the evolution operator it exponentiates is unitary exactly rather than to the accuracy of the truncation.

abstract: A key challenge for disease ecology is predicting the size of epidemics. Most models forecast disease in a single population using long-term historical data from that population. However, long-term data is not always available and a possible alternative is to borrow data from multiple similar populations to forecast disease for a population of interest. abstract: The Horseshoe Canyon Formation in southern Alberta, Canada, preserves abundant plant fossils from the upper Campanian to upper Maastrichtian. abstract: The increasing demand for sustainable separation technologies has intensified interest in polymeric membranes due to their energy efficiency and versatility. However, many conventional membranes are fabricated from permanently crosslinked or non-degradable polymers, limiting their recyclability and contributing to environmental waste. abstract: ABSTRACT Irregular acquisition geometries in field seismic surveys lead to non‐uniform spatial sampling, which introduces spatial aliasing, reduces spectral utilization and degrades the accuracy of subsequent wavefield reconstruction and imaging. abstract: Abstract Climate change is reshaping drought patterns across Australia, increasing pressure on water-resource security and highlighting the need for more informed and adaptive river-basin management. abstract: Taking the debate over whether space exploration constitutes a necessity or a mere indulgence as its starting point, this essay adopts a philosophical and interdisciplinary perspective to re-examine the value of human space activities inspired by the Pale Blue Dot photograph. abstract: Abstract The United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 2 (SDG) underscores the need for eliminating hunger, improving nutrition, and promoting sustainable agriculture. abstract: ABSTRACT In the present work, we address some aspects related to the numerical solution of the Poisson equation within the framework of the Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics (SPH). abstract: Abstract Microplastics (MPs) have emerged as ubiquitous contaminants in the environment. abstract: Autonomous docking of miniature unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) requires compact, low-cost, and robust sensing for estimating angles within short ranges. abstract: : Satellite thermal infrared (TIR) data are essential for remote sensing of energy exchange processes at the Earth-atmosphere interface. Current satellite sensors are subject to a trade-off between spatial resolution and temporal coverage. Daily TIR observations from MODIS and VIIRS are limited to coarse spatial resolutions of ∼400–1000 m, whereas higher-resolution Landsat TIRS observations (∼100 m) provide infrequent temporal coverage (∼8 days). abstract: Leaf length and width are key dimensions of tree leaf size and can influence leaf boundary-layer development and leaf-environment heat exchange. abstract: Although inland wetlands are among the most important and impacted biodiversity hotspots worldwide, they remain poorly assessed. title: Spatiotemporal Dynamics of Olive Fruit Fly (Bactrocera oleae) Populations in a Mediterranean Olive‐Growing Landscape: An Eight‐Year Study From Samos Island, Greece
abstract: ABSTRACT Olive fruit fly ( Bactrocera oleae , Rossi) is one of the most significant pests in the Mediterranean olive groves, causing both quantitative and qualitative losses. Understanding its spatial and temporal dynamics is essential for effective and sustainable control of the pest. This study analyses an eight‐year dataset (2017–2024) of the olive fly populations on Samos Island, Greece, based on an extensive monitoring network of McPhail traps. abstract: The use of natural bioactive ingredients is a promising strategy to improve fish health and enhance disease resistance in sustainable aquaculture. The present study evaluated the effects of dietary supplementation with Hifas Aqua , a mushroom-derived product containing Pleurotus ostreatus , Lentinula edodes , and Herimax ® (fermented Hericium erinaceum mycelium), on the immune response and disease resistance in European seabass ( Dicentrarchus labrax ). title: Deciphering the anticorrosion performance of Arnica montana extract for mild steel in 1.5 M HCl using experimental and computational insights
abstract: The increasing demand for environmentally benign alternatives to conventional corrosion inhibitors has stimulated interest in plant-derived materials. This study explores Arnica montana extract (AME) as a sustainable corrosion inhibitor for mild steel (MS) exposed to 1.5 M HCl, employing an integrated experimental and computational strategy. The novelty of the work lies in coupling a renewable botanical inhibitor with advanced soft-computing and molecular simulation approaches to simultaneously optimise, predict, and explain corrosion inhibition behaviour. title: Protecting Ports using Range-Free Triangulated Sensor Networks: A Case Study
abstract: Range-free wireless sensor networks rely on sensors that detect only the bearing of an incoming signal, so that localizing a transmitter requires simultaneous detection by at least three sensors, a condition known as triangulated coverage. This paper extends a previously developed geospatial computational framework with a formal treatment of sensor activation and applies it to the protection of the port of Thessaloniki, Greece. title: Blue-Green-Grey Infrastructure for Urban Carbon Reduction and Heat Resilience: A Review of Mechanisms, Methods, and Assessment Challenges
abstract: Urban blue-green-grey infrastructure (BGGI) is increasingly discussed as a strategy for reducing carbon emissions and improving heat resilience, but evidence on its mechanisms and assessment methods remains fragmented. This review synthesizes BGGI studies retrieved from Web of Science and ScienceDirect, focusing on carbon reduction pathways, analytical approaches and unresolved assessment challenges. title: Iran’s nuclear retrenchment, 1977–1980: the unravelling of US-Iran nuclear cooperation
abstract: In August 1978, as protests swept Iran, a quieter crisis unfolded within Prime Minister Jamshid Amuzegar’s government. A high-level commission recommended suspending Iran’s nuclear programme, then among the most ambitious in the developing world. This article argues that Iran’s nuclear retrenchment began not with the 1979 revolution but months earlier, driven by fiscal crisis, the erosion of institutional autonomy at the Atomic Energy Organization of Iran, and the withdrawal of Western suppliers during the final years of the Pahlavi monarchy. title: Improved assessment of in-situ and recoverable resources in brine deposits of the Lithium Triangle: A geostatistical perspective
abstract: Continental brine deposits hosted in salar-type systems of the Central Andean Lithium Triangle (Argentina, Bolivia, and Chile) account for more than 60% of known global lithium resources, making the accurate spatial characterization of lithium concentration a matter of paramount importance for resource evaluation and investment decision-making. title: Innovative performance indicators for effective Quality, Safety, and Environment management in oil drilling operations
abstract: Abstract Effective management of Quality, Safety, and Environment (QSE) performance is critical in high-risk oil drilling operations. Despite extensive research on generic Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) frameworks, there remains limited guidance on context-specific, operationally validated methodologies that integrate leading and lagging indicators within unified QSE systems for drilling operations. title: Pluvial flood risk assessment and nature-based mitigation in urban environments: a pragmatic Curve Number and Initial Abstraction approach
abstract: Urban pluvial flooding represents a growing threat to contemporary cities, driven by the compounding effects of climate change, rapid urbanization, and inadequate stormwater infrastructure, prompting the study of nature-based solutions (NBS) as potential interventions for mitigating the detrimental effects of urban flooding. Two-dimensional (2D) hydrodynamic assessments of pluvial flood risk and NBS mitigation potential require a detailed description of the urban drainage system that is not always available. title: Quantifying the Net Environmental Benefits of Food-Grade Recycled PET in Cameroon: Application of the Circular Footprint Formula to Mid-Scale Mechanical Recycling
abstract: Mechanical recycling is often assumed, rather than demonstrated, to deliver a net environmental benefit relative to virgin plastic production, particularly in Sub-Saharan African contexts where primary process data are scarce. This study quantifies that benefit for food-grade recycled polyethylene terephthalate (rPET) produced at mid-scale in Cameroon, using the European Commission’s Circular Footprint Formula (CFF) applied to a gate-to-gate life cycle assessment (LCA; ISO 14040/14044) of the Opur and Supermont mineral-water bottle streams recycled at Ecogreen Sarl, Douala. title: Multi-frequency acoustic metasurface carpet cloak based on groove structural unit
abstract: This paper presents a multi-frequency acoustic metasurface carpet cloak (AMCC) composed of groove-structured units. These structural units function as multi-frequency metasurfaces and operate effectively at both the fundamental and harmonic frequencies. Numerical simulations demonstrate that the proposed AMCC can effectively cloak a triangular object, with a broad operational bandwidth ranging from 3110 to 3750 Hz near the fundamental frequency. abstract: Abstract To address the challenges of thermoset resin circularity, the solvolyzed products from biobased succinic acid/epoxidized linseed oil (ELO) cross-linked resin were valorized into new starting materials for the preparation of recycled cross-linked systems. First, the recycled product was characterized by using spectroscopy and chromatography techniques (FT-IR and LC-MS), providing insights into their molecular composition. title: Technoeconomic and Life Cycle Analyses of the Co-production of Olefins, Aromatics, and Alkanes Using Microwave-Assisted Conversion of Polypropylene Plastic Waste
abstract: Abstract There is a growing interest in utilizing plastic waste to produce olefins and aromatics, which serve as essential building blocks for polyolefin production. In this paper, a novel microwave-assisted catalytic process is developed for converting polypropylene plastic waste into propylene, with simultaneous co-production of ethylene, aromatics, and alkanes, thereby closing the material loop by returning end-of-life plastic waste back into the petrochemical value chain as a high-value chemical feedstock, a key principle of the circular economy. title: Fish locomotor dynamics quantified using multiple inertial measurement units
abstract: Abstract Animals exhibit a diversity of locomotor behaviours that vary with body shape, ontogeny, motivation and environment. Documenting these behaviours often relies on recording videos of animals in controlled conditions displaying stereotyped behaviours. By contrast, animal-borne motion sensing data loggers can document diverse behaviours of animals in their natural environment. title: Geotechnical parameters estimation using electrical resistivity tomography data: Case study of Jorf Lasfar, western Morocco

abstract: Abstract This study investigates the statistical correlation between ground movement rates in landslide areas, as derived by Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) results, with geological, geomorphological, environmental and geotechnical causal factors in southwestern Cyprus. The analysis examines ground velocities derived using Multi-Temporal Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (MT-InSAR) for both active and inactive landslides that are recorded in an existing inventory, using ascending and descending orbit datasets. title: Comparing Remotely Sensed and Weather Station Measured Rainfall Data for Flood Prediction in KwaZulu Natal, South Africa
abstract: ABSTRACT Extreme rainfall events frequently trigger flash floods, which cause widespread damage to ecosystems, infrastructure, and livelihoods. Accurate rainfall estimation is therefore essential for flood modeling and early warning systems. This study assessed the performance of the Tropical Rainfall Measuring Mission (TRMM) and the Global Precipitation Measurement Integrated Multi‐Satellite Retrievals for GPM (GPM‐IMERG) against weather station rainfall observations collected across KwaZulu‐Natal, South Africa, between 2000 and 2022. title: Liberation-controlled beneficiation of Moroccan andalusite ore through particle size optimization and integrated gravity–magnetic separation
abstract: The beneficiation efficiency of andalusite ores is strongly governed by particle size because of its effect on mineral liberation and separation selectivity. In this study, the effect of particle size on the upgrading performance of an andalusite ore from the Moroccan Sidi Bou-Othmane deposit was investigated using shaking table gravity concentration followed by dry high-intensity magnetic separation. title: Improving the Quality of Chest X-rays Through Adaptive Image Enhancement Filters (ACEF)
abstract: Respiratory diseases are difficult to identify due to picture distortion, hence chest X-rays are commonly used to diagnose lung ailments, particularly in low-light settings. Raw radiographs frequently exhibit issues such as insufficient contrast, picture distortion, and poor tissue border definition, all of which can have a negative impact on radiographic accuracy, especially in low light. This paper describes the Adaptive Chest Enhancement Filter (ACEF), a three-stage preprocessing filter that combines image decongestion, lung-specific contrast enhancement, and tissue boundary preservation. title: A review of research on programmable airburst less-lethal munitions
abstract: As the demand for less-lethal response operations and their application in complex scenarios increases, the limitations of conventional less-lethal munitions in terms of strike accuracy, effective coverage, safety and controllability have become increasingly apparent. Programmable airburst less-lethal munitions have garnered attention due to their ability to detonate in a preset airspace and provide a controllable dispersal footprint. abstract: OBJECTIVES To evaluate the physiological rationale, mechanism of action, and emerging clinical evidence supporting sonic debridement as an adjunctive approach for wound hygiene and maintenance debridement in chronic wound management. METHODS A structured review of wound healing principles, biofilm biology, and current debridement modalities was performed alongside analysis of clinical observations and case series data using a sonic debridement device. abstract: This study reconstructs the smelting conditions of ancient copper production in the eastern Srednogorie metallogenic zone (SE Bulgaria) based on the mineralogical and chemical composition of archaeological slags. Slag samples from three ore fields were investigated: Rosen (Propadnala Voda, Korucheshme and Rosen deposits, and Atiya metallurgical centre), Zidarovo (Krushevets archaeological site) and St. Ilia (Boyadzhik archaeological site). abstract: ABSTRACT Functional diversity links species traits to ecosystem functioning, yet its large-scale patterns and vulnerability to species loss remain poorly understood. title: A Spectral–Semantic integration framework for hydrothermal alteration characterization using Landsat-8 OLI and AlphaEarth Foundations in the Eastern Tien Shan, China
abstract: Remote sensing-based hydrothermal alteration mapping plays an important role in regional mineral prospectivity analysis but remains challenging in structurally complex regions because of spectral mixing, weak peripheral anomalies, and fragmented spatial distributions. This study proposes an integrated spectral–semantic framework that combines Landsat-8 OLI multispectral imagery with AlphaEarth Foundations (AEF) semantic embeddings for hydrothermal alteration characterization and prospectivity evaluation in the Tuwu copper belt, Eastern Tien Shan, China. title: Hybrid GA-DQN for opportunistic cluster head selection and routing in resource constraint Internet of Things networks
abstract: Abstract Energy efficiency and reliable data transmission are two important challenges in Internet of Things (IoT) networks because of the limited energy resources of sensor nodes and their dynamic nature. Accordingly, this research develops a Genetic Algorithm Deep Q-Network (GA-DQN) based hybrid framework for intelligent cluster head selection and adaptive IoT Network routing to counter these threats. abstract: Os Modelos Digitais de Altura (MDA) da vegetação são gerados pela subtração entre o Modelo Digital de Superfície (MDS) e o Modelo Digital de Terreno (MDT), que podem ser construídos pela interpolação das coordenadas tridimensionais obtidas por sistemas de perfilamento a laser (LiDAR). abstract: Methods capable of monitoring groundwater systems are essential to support decisions and resource management. In recent years, techniques based on the analysis of ambient seismic noise have consolidated passive seismic methods as valuable monitoring tools. abstract: ABSTRACT Accurate estimation of evapotranspiration (ET) is essential for sustainable water management, particularly in arid and semiarid regions. This study aimed to establish relationships between the normalised difference vegetation index (NDVI) derived from satellite imagery and stress‐adjusted crop coefficients ( K c_adj ) obtained using the METRIC (mapping ET at high resolution with internalised calibration) model and to develop efficient models for rapid ET estimation. abstract: Abstract This study investigates the suitability of sustainable, highly porous nanosponges, composed of TEMPO-oxidized cellulose nanofibers (TOCNF) and branched polyethylenimine (bPEI, cross-linker), as scaffolds for PEDOT:PSS poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene):polystyrenesulfonate dip coating to design piezoresistive pressure sensors. title: AirComm: Your Smartphone Can “Smell” Fine Particles via Light
abstract: Fine-grained air quality monitoring is critical for assessing personal exposure to air pollution in indoor micro-environments; however, dedicated air quality sensors are costly and offer limited spatial coverage. In this work, we present AirComm , a smartphone-based air quality sensing system that requires no additional hardware. title: Hydrochemical Analysis and Associated Health Risk Assessment of Groundwater Quality of Hisar District of Haryana, India
abstract: ABSTRACT Groundwater is a major drinking water resource supporting nearly half of the world's population but its quality is being compromised by various anthropogenic factors. This study provides an in‐depth analysis of groundwater quality in Hisar district, Haryana, India by integrating hydrogeochemical parameters and advanced analytical techniques. abstract: OBJECTIVE: This in vitro study evaluated the color accuracy and image sharpness of common macro and zoom lenses on a full-frame body and tested whether differences among macro-lens brands are clinically meaningful. title: A life cycle-based Green Manufacturing framework for environmental decision-making: an application to heavy-duty vehicle chassis frame rail manufacturing
abstract: Abstract Heavy-duty vehicles (HDV) are essential to global transportation and logistics systems, yet environmental assessments have predominantly focused on the use phase, leaving the environmental impacts of the manufacturing stage comparatively underexplored. This study evaluates the cradle-to-gate environmental performance of steel chassis frame rail manufacturing using a process-level Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) based on primary industrial data collected directly from the shop floor. abstract: Abstract. Evapotranspiration (ET) is the dominant hydrologic flux in wetlands, and partitioning into transpiration (T) and evaporation (E) is essential for understanding water and carbon dynamics, guiding sustainable water management practices, and predicting responses to climate change in these systems. However, the presence of moss layers in many wetlands challenges the assumptions of commonly used partitioning methods. title: Real-time heuristic evacuation pathfinding algorithm for flood avoidance
abstract: Floods rank among the world’s most devastating annual disasters in terms of casualties and economic losses, making evacuation route planning crucial for mitigating flood risks. This study proposes a Real-time Heuristic Flood Evacuation Path Planning Algorithm (RHEPFA) based on dynamic flood simulations using the ANUGA 2D model. abstract: ABSTRACT The circular transformation in the silk industry is crucial for enhancing resource efficiency and minimizing waste. Despite growing interest in circularity within the textile sector, the silk industry remains underexplored. title: Genetic Structure Along Temperature Gradient in a Recent Invader Cardamine hirsuta in Eastern Japan

title: Mechanisms of long-term degradation in plasticized PVDF pressure barriers under offshore service exposure
abstract: ABSTRACT Poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF) is commonly used as a pressure sheath material in offshore flexible pipelines; however, there is limited experimental data from long-term service exposure. In this study, three PVDF layers recovered from a flexible riser after ten years of offshore operation were examined to understand the degradation mechanisms that occurred under field conditions. title: A novel multi-application heat recovery system with adsorption cooling and seasonal energy storage for liquid cooling data centers
abstract: Liquid-cooling data centers are emerging as the infrastructure for high-performance computing. They generate substantial heat, which is very promising for energy recovery. However, the seasonal mismatch between continuous waste-heat generation and winter-concentrated heating demand remains insufficiently addressed. This study proposes a novel multi-application heat recovery system that integrates waste-heat-driven cooling, cross-seasonal thermal storage, and winter heat supply to enable year-round energy recovery. title: Local geographies of housing inequality: Neighbourhood trajectories of housing purchasing (un)affordability across neighbourhoods in England and Wales (2010-2023)
abstract: In recent decades, housing purchasing prices have outpaced incomes, increasing spatial inequalities and creating a growing challenge to homeownership. Despite housing markets being highly localised with most residential moves made at local scales, analyses of housing affordability have typically focused on national- and regional-level trends. We draw on a novel housing price dataset, to present the first neighbourhood-level analysis of housing (un)affordability trajectories across England and Wales (2010 to 2023). title: Bridging Albanian monitoring and Water Framework Directive oriented assessment: A surface water quality index
abstract: The implementation of the European Union Water Framework Directive (WFD) presents an important methodological challenge for countries whose established environmental monitoring systems are not yet fully harmonised with WFD compatible surface water body delineation and assessment structures.This situation is particularly relevant for EU candidate countries, where existing station-based monitoring programmes must increasingly support integrated river basin assessment and alignment with the environmental acquis.This study addresses this challenge by developing a composite surface water quality in

title: Conservation genetics of the spotted bat: Insights from ancient, historical, and modern samples
abstract: Spotted bats (Euderma maculatum) are cryptic (nocturnal, volant, and roost solitarily) and thus their biology remains largely undescribed. Only 35 specimens were known to science before the mid-1960s. Hence, they are ideal candidates for genetic studies to uncover population genetic diversity and structure, and thereby inform conservation. abstract: Accurate characterization of subsurface heterogeneity is essential for understanding groundwater flow and contaminant transport. However, the value of integrating multiple data and how it relates to heterogeneity requires further investigation. This study systematically evaluates individual and joint inversion of head, temperature and concentration data using mildly heterogeneous (MH) and highly heterogeneous (HH) synthetic fields. title: Resolving sub-daily variability in the GPP–SIF relationship and its implications for GPP estimation at a temperate savanna site
abstract: Savannas cover approximately 20% of the global land surface and contribute nearly 30% of terrestrial net primary production, making them an important component of the global carbon cycle. Solar-induced chlorophyll fluorescence (SIF), which is closely linked to photosynthetic activity, has shown considerable potential for estimating ecosystem gross primary productivity (GPP). However, temporal variability in the GPP–SIF relationship, particularly at sub-daily timescales, remains insufficiently understood, limiting the accurate estimation of high-frequency GPP dynamics. title: Assessing earthquake potential and fault activity from a newly estimated high-resolution geodetic velocity field in Hispaniola
abstract: Abstract The transpressive plate boundary between the Caribbean and North American plates in Hispaniola is a complex system of strike-slip faults, subduction zones, fold-and-thrust belts, and normal faulting. Tectonic deformation studies in this region have traditionally relied on sparse Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) networks. title: A self-adaptive fuzzy pitch control method for suppressing vibration of large-scale wind turbines under combined wind-seismic loading
abstract: Abstract For large-scale wind turbines subjected to sudden seismic excitation during operation, a self-adaptive fuzzy pitch (SFP) control method is proposed to mitigate the structural seismic response. The displacement and velocity of tower-top fore-aft (TTFA) are used as input variables for the fuzzy controller, and a self-adaptive proportional factor is established through an exponential function. title: Quantifying baseflow-driven non-point source nutrient losses using a novel self-adaptive algorithm in a rain-fed agricultural watershed of eastern China
abstract: Accurate estimation of baseflow non-point source (NPS) pollutant loads during non-pure baseflow recession periods—when discharge is influenced by precipitation or surface runoff—remains a major challenge for watershed NPS management. To address this issue, we developed a self-adaptive baseflow load estimation algorithm (SA-BLEA) for a rain-fed agricultural watershed in eastern China. title: Geochemical Profiling and Health Risk Assessment of Heavy Metals in Yemeni Bottled Water: A Multivariate Statistical Approach
abstract: Objectives The quality and safety of bottled drinking water are of growing concern in Yemen due to increasing dependence on groundwater resources and potential contamination by trace metals. This study presents an integrated secondary analysis of previously published inductively coupled plasma–mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) data to evaluate the concentrations of seven heavy metals (Hg, Cd, Cr, Ni, Al, Co, and Cu) in 27 bottled water brands marketed in Yemen, combining health risk assessment with multivariate statistical analysis. title: A Parallel One‐Field Fictitious‐Domain Finite Element Method for Large‐Scale Fluid–Structure Interaction
abstract: ABSTRACT We present a distributed‐memory finite‐element framework for large‐scale incompressible fluid–structure interaction (FSI) based on a monolithic one‐field fictitious‐domain formulation. The velocity and pressure are defined on a fixed Eulerian background mesh and discretized using Taylor–Hood finite elements with quadratic velocity and linear pressure approximation, while the immersed solid is represented by an updated Lagrangian mesh. title: Imagens Mentais na Terapia do Esquema: uma revisão de escopo
abstract: A Terapia do Esquema (TE) utiliza imagens mentais como um recurso central na mediação entre cognição e emoção, facilitando o acesso a memórias emocionais implícitas e a modificação de esquemas iniciais desadaptativos. O presente estudo teve como objetivo analisar a produção científica acerca do uso de técnicas de imagens mentais na TE, mapeando suas características metodológicas, efeitos terapêuticos e áreas cerebrais implicadas. title: COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS OF RADAR SYSTEMS IN REGIONAL AVIATION: A CASE STUDY OF DEBLIN AIRFIELD
abstract: This article presents the results of an experimental study on the registration performance of two radar-based systems - GCA-2000 and AVIA-W - using flight operations between the regional airfields of Deblin and Radom as a case study. GPS satellite navigation data were employed as a reference source to enable both quantitative and spatiotemporal comparisons of radar registration characteristics. title: Artifact-to-True Seepage Detection in RGB Images Using CLIP Representations
abstract: Red-Green-Blue (RGB) vision based supervised learning is demonstrated for the purpose of identifying subsurface groundwater seepage for low-cost and accurate inspection of dams and slope embankments using unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). Supervised learning is constrained by the scarcity of confirmed true seepage-positive images. Our study investigates artifact-to-true seepage detection at the earliest intervention point. title: Increasing exposure to potential flooding in high-mountain catchments
abstract: Abstract Exposure to flood hazards in high mountain catchments is expected to increase alongside natural hazards, driven by climate change, glacier retreat, and landscape evolution, yet temporally consistent, high-resolution exposure data remain scarce. Here we quantify changes in the exposure of buildings and people to flooding in Nepal and transboundary regions of India and China. Validation against a manually derived reference dataset revealed considerable differences in accuracy and completeness across five building footprint products. title: Integrated Assessment of Groundwater Quality and Suitability for Drinking and Irrigation in the Nineveh Plain, Iraq.
abstract: Groundwater is the principal source of domestic and agricultural water supply in the Nineveh Plain, northern Iraq, where population growth, agricultural expansion, climate variability, and declining surface-water availability have increased pressure on groundwater resources. A study of the groundwater hydrochemistry, irrigation suitability, trace metal occurrence, and microbiological quality was conducted in the Al-Qosh and Tel-Kif area of the Nineveh Plain during summer 2025. abstract: Reservoir water-quality management requires forecasts that remain dynamically plausible and scenario choices that balance water-quality objectives against the magnitude of requested trajectory change. Historical monitoring archives, however, rarely contain labelled control actions. title: Effects of pre-harvest salicylic acid and irrigation interval on rhizome yield and phytochemical accumulation in Curcuma aromatica Salisb.
abstract: Curcuma aromatica Salisb. is a medicinal plant valued for its rhizomes rich in essential oils and phenolic compounds. This study aimed to determine (i) an optimal concentration of salicylic acid (SA) to improve plant performance and secondary metabolite accumulation, and (ii) the effects of different pre-harvest irrigation intervals on plants pre-treated with the selected SA concentration. title: Reliability gated cross-modal attention with shear reparameterized directional reasoning for RGB-thermal salient object detection
abstract: Abstract RGB-Thermal (RGB-T) salient object detection localizes salient regions where appearance cues alone are insufficient, since thermal radiation stays informative under poor illumination. Two limitations persist. Cross-modal attention is applied at a strength fixed in advance, so a momentarily uninformative stream continues to contribute in full, and directional reasoning is confined to the two image axes, because diagonal coverage has required a dense affinity mask of quadratic cost. title: Agroecological zoning of mezcal and tequila agaves in Mexico through MaxEnt ecological niche modeling: Sustainability and climate resilience implications
abstract: Agave‑based distilled‑beverage production in Mexico, particularly mezcal and tequila, is facing intensifying sustainability challenges driven by climate change, monocropping expansion, and degradation of socio‑ecological systems. In this context, agroecological zoning represents a strategic tool for improving territorial planning and strengthening climate resilience. abstract: Abstract Water-soluble poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVOH) offers high tensile strength and an excellent oxygen barrier, but its dense hydrogen-bond network places its melting point close to its decomposition temperature, making it difficult to melt-process. title: Life-cycle incremental cost-benefit model for passive buildings and a case study in Zhejiang Province, China
abstract: Passive buildings (PBs) offer substantial advantages in reducing carbon emissions and improving energy efficiency, making their promotion a strategic priority for China’s carbon goals. However, high upfront costs, unclear long-term benefits, and long payback periods hinder adoption. This study develops a Life-Cycle Incremental Cost-Benefit Model (LCICBM) covering design, construction, and operation. The model quantifies and monetizes economic, environmental, and social benefits. title: A Multi‐Scale Collaborative Framework for Transforming Cultural Power in Traditional Villages Through Ecological Resilience: Evidence From Zhejiang Province, China
abstract: ABSTRACT Traditional villages are heritage settlements whose continuity depends on interactions among cultural practice, ecological condition and governance capacity. This study examined how cultural power and governance networks are associated with ecological resilience in nine traditional villages in Zhejiang Province, China. A mixed‐methods design combined remote‐sensing analysis, spatial overlay, social network modelling, cultural inventories, interviews and institutional document review. abstract: In humans, dietary intake is thought to be the main route of exposure to perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA). The gastrointestinal tract is the primary entry point for this highly persistent and bioaccumulative environmental pollutant; however, its fate and effects within the digestive system remain largely unknown. title: Extreme Rainfall Modeling Using the Generalized Extreme Value Distribution for r-Largest Order Statistics
abstract: Heavy rainfall is a major driver of floods, flash floods, and landslides, significantly impacting lives, property, and infrastructure. These risks are intensifying under climate change, which increases both the frequency and intensity of extreme rainfall events. This study analyzed the characteristics and assessed the risk of maximum daily cumulative rainfall in Thailand using the Generalized Extreme Value for the r-largest order statistics (GEVr) model. title: Diversity and disparity in mammalian fossil assemblages of the John Day Formation, Oregon, USA
abstract: Abstract The John Day Formation offers a remarkably complete terrestrial record of Eocene-, Oligocene-, and Miocene-aged mammalian faunas in central Oregon. Sites in the John Day Formation have yielded numerous mammalian species spanning across many taxonomic orders, offering a unique opportunity to closely examine changes in mammalian diversity and disparity across a geographically constrained region. title: Average Temperature Trends and Rainfall patterns within Jere Local Government Area of Kaduna State, Northwest-Nigeria: A Case from 1989 to 2018
abstract: The Average Temperature Trends and rainfall patterns within Jere local government area of Kaduna State, Nigeria have been studied from 1989 to 2018. title: Future Extreme Climatic Events May Reshape Butterfly Distributions Across Biomes in Italy
abstract: ABSTRACT Aim Extreme climatic events (ECEs) are increasingly recognized as major drivers of insect declines, yet remain rarely incorporated into biodiversity projections. Butterflies may be especially sensitive to prolonged ECEs because they are short‐lived ectotherms, while voltinism can influence their capacity to absorb climatic shocks. title: Detection of Personal Privacy Information in Social Data Taking Into Account Data Augmentation and Mask R‐ CNN
abstract: ABSTRACT Visual privacy‐sensitive objects in social images are often small, partially occluded, and unevenly represented in available training data, which limits the reliability of automatic privacy detection. This study develops a privacy‐sensitive object detection framework combining multi‐strategy image augmentation with SE‐Mask R‐CNN. abstract: La regeneración natural es fundamental en la dinámica de los ecosistemas forestales y su comprensión contribuye al diseño de prácticas de conservación, restauración y silvicultura. En 3 localidades del Parque Estatal Bosque Mesófilo del Nevado de Colima, México, se evaluaron la composición, diversidad y estructura de la regeneración natural de plantas leñosas con altura ≥ 10 cm y diámetro normal ≤ 2.5 cm, así como los factores ambientales que influyen en su distribución y abundancia. abstract: Abstract. This paper defines an Accumulated Risk Index (ARI) to quantify regional risk levels in a global perspective utilizing Emergency Events Database (EM-DAT) from 2013 to 2023. Building on the World Risk Index (WRI) released from World Risk Report 2023, the ARI focuses more on major events caused by multiple natural hazards within 5°×5° latitude-longitude grids, and calculates their accumulative effects during the period. abstract: Cellulose-based bioplastics have emerged as a promising alternative to conventional petroleum-derived plastics, offering a sustainable and eco-friendly solution to the growing environmental concerns associated with plastic waste. Derived from renewable resources such as wood, cotton, and agricultural residues, cellulose bioplastics exhibit biodegradability, biocompatibility, and low environmental impact. abstract: Introduction Highway lane-change maneuvers pose a safety challenge for SAE Level 3 autonomous driving because conventional threshold-based decisions and isolated surrogate safety measures may inadequately capture the coupling between longitudinal braking demand and evolving inter-vehicle gaps. This study develops an interpretable, risk-aware framework for continuous lane-change assessment during maneuver initiation and execution. abstract: Abstract Hydrology and water resources demand robust, scalable analyses of river‐basin dynamics to inform policy. Network science offers a compact language for such systems—capturing inequality, connectivity, accessibility, and redundancy. In this study, we model European rivers as dynamic, flow-weighted graphs across 30 basins during 1992–2024. abstract: Abstract Glacial lake outburst floods (GLOFs) pose a growing risk in high mountain regions as climate-driven glacier retreat accelerates lake expansion and new lake formation. In the Hindu Kush Himalaya, particularly in Afghanistan, triggering processes and GLOF propagation downstream are largely unstudied. title: Insights into life cycle assessment and rapid removal of malachite green by biochar derived from shrimp shell and sheep manure
abstract: Malachite green (MG) contamination of water resources poses significant ecological and human-health risks, while the environmental sustainability of its treatment strategies has rarely been evaluated. This study addresses this critical gap by integrating the synthesis of hybrid biochar from sheep manure and shrimp shells at a 2:1 ratio for MG removal with a comprehensive life cycle assessment (LCA). title: The Role of BAZNAS in Improving Access to Healthcare Services for Mustahik in Banten, Indonesia
abstract: Background: The National Board of Zakat is Indonesia's official body responsible for managing zakat. As such, it supports the efforts of the Indonesian government to improve access to healthcare for disadvantaged groups. Objective: Investigate how BAZNAS enhances healthcare access in Banten Province via zakat-based health programs. title: Economic Losses Associated With Tropical Cyclones in Mexico: A Two-stage Model
abstract: Tropical cyclones (TCs) are among the primary drivers of disaster declarations in Mexico, causing substantial economic losses. This study assesses reported TC-related economic losses in Mexican states from (Funk 1980 ) to 2023 and identifies the hazard and socioeconomic determinants of both the probability of loss occurrence and loss magnitude. abstract: The growing demand for environmentally responsible construction materials requires reliable tools to predict the compressive strength of concrete incorporating agricultural waste and natural fibers. This study investigates the prediction of compressive strength of sustainable concrete incorporating wheat straw ash (WSA) and coir fiber (CF) using explainable ensemble machine learning. abstract: An individual’s personality is made up of their thoughts, emotions, and behaviour patterns, which determine who they are. abstract: Real time observation of students' exercise load is very important for scientific sports teaching and injury prevention. abstract: Index images provide opportunities for monitoring phenotypic characteristics such as plant height and disease symptoms, as well as the detection of pest presence. abstract: Detection of defects such as porosities is important in additive manufacturing to ensure the desired material properties. Most additively manufactured components require finish machining to achieve the desired surface finish and geometric tolerances. This paper presents an unsupervised machine learning approach using an autoencoder to detect defects during the machining of additively manufactured components. abstract: This study investigates the influence of green space on environmental quality and its role in mitigating the Urban Heat Island (UHI) effect, with a specific focus on George Town, Penang. abstract: Transportation activities are among the most influential factors shaping economic growth and development. Since freight mobility and transport infrastructure play a strategic role in sustaining economic activity, understanding how different transport modes contribute to economic performance has become a critical research issue. abstract: Endotoxins, also known as lipopolysaccharides (LPSs), are structural components of the outer membrane of Gram-negative bacteria and some cyanobacteria. They are among the most potent pyrogens and remain a persistent challenge in environmental, occupational, and clinical settings. This review brings together current understanding of their structure, stability, and methods of detection, while also highlighting the main routes through which humans are exposed. abstract: ABSTRACT Fatigue testing of large wind turbine blades is a critical step in ensuring their operational reliability, however, repeatedly developing loading fixtures for different test phases (such as static and fatigue testing) often entails significant time and financial costs. title: Directional policy alignment in water resources carrying capacity for sustainable city futures in drylands
abstract: Sustainable city futures in drylands are increasingly constrained by hard water resource limits under climate change, city expansion, and low-carbon transition. Water resources carrying capacity (WRCC) is not only an indicator of water security, but also a diagnostic tool for identifying development boundaries, policy-deviation risks, and adaptive governance priorities. abstract: Adaptive reforestation under climate warming will increasingly involve northward or upslope movement of tree species and seed sources. However, in western Canadian boreal and sub-boreal forests, release from cold constraints may be offset by emerging drought limitations, where low evapotranspiration has historically supported tree growth despite modest precipitation. abstract: Se construyen mapas híbridos de índices de Aire y Salud (IAS) de partículas en suspensión menores a 2.5 micrómetros (PM2.5), de mediciones de la Red Estatal de Monitoreo Automática (REMA) y estimaciones basadas en datos satelitales del Servicio de Monitoreo Atmosférico de Copernicus (CAMS). abstract: A key challenge in inferring gene regulatory networks (GRNs) governing cellular processes such as differentiation and reprogramming from experimental data lies in the impossibility of directly measuring protein dynamics at the single-cell level, which prevents establishing causal relationships between regulator activity and target responses. title: Integrating temperature and CO2-concentration impact on crops into an input–output framework
abstract: Abstract Environmental Input–Output Analysis (IOA) incorporates feedbacks in coupled economic-environmental systems, driven by an exogenous demand and fixed input–output coefficients with a linearity assumption. For some environmental problems, or over longer time periods, the IO coefficients and exogenous drivers may change. title: An eco-friendly magnetic catalyst based on copper nanoparticles supported on lignin/iron oxide cores
abstract: Transforming renewable biomass into high-performance heterogeneous catalysts represents an attractive strategy for advancing sustainable chemical processes. This work reports a sustainable strategy for the development of highly efficient copper-based nanoparticles supported on lignosulfonate and magnetite or maghemite cores. Controlled thermal transformation of a copper-containing lignin matrix was shown to be a decisive factor in tailoring the textural properties and catalytic performance of the resulting materials. abstract: Abstract Carbamazepine (CBZ) is a persistent pharmaceutical contaminant that is poorly removed by conventional wastewater treatment processes. Although non-thermal plasma can promote efficient CBZ degradation, the elementary molecular mechanisms governing its initial oxidative transformation remain incompletely understood. abstract: This paper develops and validates a provincial Environmental Technology Transition (ETT) indicator for Vietnam and uses it to assess whether green finance is associated with cleaner technology upgrading, eco-innovation, and energy-efficiency improvement. Using a balanced panel of 63 Vietnamese provinces over 2014-2024 (693 observations), the study combines indicator construction, principal-component validation, Spatial Durbin modelling, and an IV-spatial estimator to examine both within-province and cross-province technology-transition dynamics. abstract: Dual‐network (DN) hydrogels possess tunable polymer network architectures, exceptional mechanical robustness, and superior water retention capability. They demonstrate substantial potential in structural optimization and performance stabilization, thus garnering widespread attention from both the academic and industrial sectors in the field of flexible devices such as supercapacitors, temperature sensors, and zinc‐air batteries. abstract: This paper addresses the regulation of theft as an illicit act in two major medieval Croatian legal monuments: the Vinodol Code (1288) and the Statute of Poljica. Rather than offering a systematic comparison of legal systems, the study concentrates on the legal nature, normative structure, and penal treatment of theft within these statutory frameworks, situating the offence in its broader social and institutional context. title: The effects of asynchronous interruption on arc motion characteristics of a triple‑break medium-voltage DC air circuit breaker
abstract: Abstract Multi‑break DC air circuit breakers are subject to asynchronous interruption due to dispersion of operating mechanisms, resulting in nonuniform transient voltage distribution among the breaks and thereby compromising interruption reliability. abstract: Industrial relocation offers a novel solution to help mitigate the “resource curse” by reducing dependence on natural resources and fostering diversified economic systems, thereby optimizing the industrial structure. This paper explores the mechanism and economic consequences of industrial relocation’s dependence on the host country’s resources, focusing on the National Industrial Relocation Demonstration Zones (NIRDZ). title: Assessing OpenStreetMap Road Currency with Sentinel-2 Time Series: Seven High-Growth Sites in Türkiye
abstract: OpenStreetMap (OSM) is the most widely used open road dataset, yet how late it records new roads is rarely measured. This study assesses the currency of the OSM major road network at seven high-growth sites in Türkiye by comparing monthly reconstructions of the map from its full edit history with Sentinel-2 summer composites of 2020, 2022, 2024 and 2025. abstract: The properties of mutualistic networks may vary depending on the habitat structure in which partners interact. abstract: Introduction Against the backdrop of increasingly frequent extreme heat events, mitigating land-surface heat exposure on urban streets is crucial for safeguarding public health. Existing studies have often overlooked the spatially differentiated effects of complex street environments on land-surface heat exposure and the associated cooling thresholds. abstract: Predicting turbulent flows is vital for advancing aerospace, energy, and environmental technologies, yet remains critically limited by the accuracy of turbulence models. While machine learning has led to the widespread development of data-driven turbulence models, existing approaches predominantly rely on monolithic dense networks that struggle to generalize across diverse flow regimes. abstract: Abstract The deuterium-to-hydrogen (D/H) ratio in solar system volatiles is commonly used to diagnose volatile formation conditions. This ratio may be altered by a range of processes under solar nebula conditions, however, including energetic processing of icy grains. abstract: This paper compares economic growth, carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions, and renewable energy use in the United States and China—the world's two largest economies and largest greenhouse gas emitters—over the period 1990 to 2024. Prepared as a capstone project for the final year of secondary school, the study draws on freely available data from the World Bank, Our World in Data, and the European Commission's EDGAR database. abstract: ABSTRACT Drylands cover nearly half of Earth's terrestrial surface and are expanding under climate change. Biogenic volatile organic compounds (VOCs) significantly influence atmospheric chemistry, yet microbial VOC emissions from dryland soils remain poorly understood. abstract: Biodiversity informatics has made occurrence records widely accessible, yet many databases remain optimized for human browsing rather than structured machine consumption by large language models (LLMs) and AI agents. This creates a bottleneck: analytical capacity is accelerating while biodiversity evidence remains fragmented, weakly documented, and difficult to cite reproducibly. abstract: Background: Paclitaxel (PTX) remains a cornerstone in breast cancer treatment, but its effectiveness is limited by both chemoresistance and significant side effects. abstract: In a mobile-sink wireless sensor network (WSN), the cluster-head (CH)-to-sink uplink periodically enters the distance-fourth-power multipath regime, where electing a CH far from the sink incurs a disproportionate energy penalty. abstract: Lack of transgenesis methods impedes functional studies in platyhelminths. abstract: Thin-ply unidirectional (UD) carbon-fibre reinforced polymer (CFRP) tapes enable improved mechanical performance in advanced aerospace structures but remain highly sensitive to manufacturing-induced defects. abstract: ABSTRACT Accurate monitoring of rainfall intensity is essential for forecasting and managing floods. The surveillance video-based rainfall measurement method has potential for high spatial and temporal resolution rainfall monitoring. abstract: Abstract. We present NeuPlume, a neural-physical probabilistic inversion framework that returns an ensemble of data-compatible plume fields rather than a single point estimate.
