title: Improved seasonal hydrological forecasting for Great Britain
abstract: Abstract. Great Britain’s variable maritime climate has until relatively recently limited the utility of seasonal hydrological forecasts. The latest generations of seasonal atmospheric forecasting systems have created new opportunities to improve flow forecasting across Great Britain, such as for the UK Hydrological Outlook. abstract: Cryptography is essential in many digital fields to provide information security and confidentiality. title: Differential responses of ecosystem services and their trade-offs to environmental gradients in mountainous areas
abstract: Mountain ecosystems are functionally diverse and have concentrated environmental gradients. Exploring the changing characteristics and trade-offs of ecosystem services (ESs) under different environmental gradients is beneficial to the conservation and sustainable use of mountain resources. This study evaluated the spatial-temporal changes of habitat quality (HQ), soil conservation (SC), water yield (WY), water purification (N output load) and net primary productivity (NPP) in the Qilian Mountains from 2000 to 2018, and analyzed their responses to environmental gradients. abstract: Plastics are widely used as food contact materials, which have the potential to release microplastics (MPs), nanoplastics (NPs), and plastic-associated organic and inorganic chemicals into foodstuffs, thereby posing a potential risk to human health. Furthermore, ingested micro- and nanoplastics (MNPs) can leach chemicals in the gastrointestinal tract, causing additional potential risks. title: ENHANCING SOIL PROPERTIES AND CAPSICUM (CAPSICUM ANNUUM VAR. GROSSUM L.) PRODUCTIVITY THROUGH THE APPLICATION OF RICE STRAW-DERIVED BIOCHAR
abstract: Capsicum, often known as sweet pepper (Capsicum annuum var. grossum L.), is becoming more and more popular in Bangladesh as a vegetable. However, a number of obstacles must be overcome for its production to occur, such as limited cation exchange capacity, poor soil fertility, fast mineralization of soil organic matter, and acidity of the soil. abstract: Hybrid design approaches are essential for developing porous lattice structures with integrated multifunctional performance. While previous studies have focused on hybridization among different topologies, combining distinct structure types-such as integrating the high mechanical strength of triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) sheet structures with the meta-structural characteristics of strut-based architectures-remains underexplored due to challenges in creating effective connections between these disparate forms. title: Multiscale feature fusion based CNN with feature ranking for satellite image classification
abstract: Satellite image classification plays an important role in various applications like monitoring, surveillance, land cover planning, etc. Deep learning models with many learnable parameters face overfitting as model depth increases and have struggled to extract both fine details and broader patterns simultaneously. To overcome the aforementioned issues, an efficient CNN model of <0.23 million parameters is proposed, utilising the extraction of multiscale features across different CNN branches. abstract: Abstract In response to the insufficient conformability, limited grasping stability, and low force threshold of existing magnetically driven grippers for highly curved and fragile workpieces, this study proposes a magnetically actuated adaptive gripper that integrates spring-based energy storage and magnetorheological particle blocking. The gripper consists of a spring energy-storage unit, a magnetic control module, and a strip-shaped flexible variable-stiffness body. abstract: This study presents a Direct Numerical Simulation (DNS) of a turbulent, globally rich, premixed NH 3 /H 2 /N 2 –air slot flame at 25 bar, representative of partially cracked ammonia combustion. abstract: Experiments using a dynamic 1–atm gas–mixing furnace simulated oxidation and reduction processes, as observed during volcanic degassing, by manipulating the oxygen (log f O 2 ) and sulfur fugacities (log f S 2 ). title: Numerical solution of the HJB equation using a hybrid Bernstein–fractional Chebyshev spectral collocation method
abstract: The Hamilton–Jacobi–Bellman (HJB) equation is fundamental in stochastic optimal control but is often difficult to solve accurately because of its nonlinear and multidimensional structure. This paper develops a hybrid tensor-product spectral collocation method based on shifted Bernstein polynomials in time and fractional-order Chebyshev polynomials in the state variables. title: Distribution of TENORM-contaminated soils in residential areas of Bangka Island, Indonesia
abstract: Radioactive contamination in residential areas of Bangka Island, Indonesia, a major tin- and rare earth-producing region, has rarely been studied, although material stored near mineral-processing workshops may pose a long-term health risk. We collected 46 soil samples around 9 mineral-processing workshops in the Selindung District, Pangkal Pinang City: residential soils from 20 locations at two depths (n = 40) and 6 workshop-related sediments. abstract: Abstract Effects of wind direction in realistic urban boundary layers remain difficult to characterize systematically because local flow patterns, and turbulent statistics within a realistic urban canopy may respond differently to changes in the approaching wind. To investigate these multi-scale directional impacts, we conducted high-resolution large-eddy simulations of the atmospheric boundary layer over the Zona Universitària Pedralbes district in Barcelona. abstract: Abstract Understanding how fire activity reorganizes across space is key to interpreting long-term interactions among climate variability, land-use change, and integrated fire management in Brazil. Yet this reorganization is difficult to read directly: annual maps of millions of burn scars saturate the national territory, and year-to-year spatial shifts are visually indistinguishable at that scale. abstract: Arthropod declines have been reported widely, and yet the spotlight has fallen on relatively large, colourful insects, rarely considering the abundant, small-sized, yet charismatic flying insects and ballooning spiders we class as neglected and undervalued 'Cinderella species'. This diverse set of arthropods contributes important ecosystem services, such as decomposition, pollination, pest regulation and nutrient cycling. abstract: Clean electricity production has become a major focus in recent years due to the rise in greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions annually. In this context, a site in Karachi, Pakistan, is considered for implementing a Renewable Energy System (RES) that integrates a photovoltaic (PV) system with hydrogen storage. abstract: The implementation of the Middle Route of the South-to-North Water Diversion Project (MRP) has effectively alleviated the severe water shortage in northern China; however, whether and how it produces synergistic effects on the ecological, economic, and social systems of the water-receiving areas remains a key issue requiring in-depth assessment. title: The role of nacelle drag in open fan design
abstract: Abstract This paper investigates the performance of an open fan operating in the high subsonic flight regime, with emphasis on the interaction between the blades and the nacelle and its impact on thrust, drag and overall efficiency. Strong spatial gradients in static pressure induced by the curved geometry of the nacelle can locally accelerate or diffuse the flow over rotor and stator blades. abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is primarily identified through behavioral and developmental assessment, which may require specialist expertise and considerable time. Electroencephalography (EEG) offers non-invasive neurophysiological information, but reliable ASD classification remains challenging because EEG signals are nonstationary and highly variable across individuals. abstract: This study examines the impacts of climate change on blue water flow (BWF), green water storage (GWS), and green water flow (GWF) components of water resources in the Tekeze Atbara watershed of the Nile basin. It employed five CMIP5 climate models under RCP4.5 and RCP8.5 scenarios along with a satisfactory SWAT model with acceptable predictive uncertainty. abstract: Abstract Amber is one of the most important national treasures in Lithuania, as well as in some other Baltic countries. In the recent era, some other materials that resemble amber have been introduced in the market, which are sometimes sold as real amber. abstract: Photodetectors (PDs), which are core components of modern optoelectronic systems, are widely used in medical diagnostics and biosensing. abstract: Abstract High-entropy materials have emerged as a versatile platform for electrocatalysis because their multicomponent nature enables broad tunability of electronic structure, adsorption energetics, lattice distortion, defect chemistry, and chemical functionality. abstract: Drought is intensifying under a warming climate, while the lag of vegetation response and the drought trigger thresholds for relative vegetation loss remain insufficiently quantified. abstract: This study addresses a critical need in regional development planning by combining aspatial biclustering with spatial autocorrelation analysis to examine European industrial competitiveness. Focusing on NUTS 2 regions, we move beyond broad categorizations by identifying data-driven “industrial leagues”—clusters of regions with similar strengths and weaknesses across 71 retained Industry 4.0 (I4.0)+ readiness indicators covering 320 regions. abstract: Abstract The rapid scaling of wellness tourism in China has produced striking spatial homogenisation, eroding the place-specific cultural texture that distinguishes one region from another. This study proposes a digital design framework that couples local knowledge graphs with parametric generation, and positions it as an addition to the evidence-based, simulation-supported and participatory traditions that already govern spatial design rather than as a replacement for them. abstract: Groundwater decline in irrigated semi-arid alluvial plains reflects interacting land-surface, climatic, pumping, and hydrogeological controls. abstract: Abstract As a key component of the climate system, terrestrial carbon dynamics are commonly simulated using Dynamic Global Vegetation Models (DGVMs), which provide essential information for estimating the global carbon budget. abstract: Water scarcity constrains agricultural production in semi-arid regions and particularly affects water-sensitive crops such as haricot bean ( Phaseolus vulgaris L.). Although supplemental irrigation is widely promoted in these environments, the partitioning of haricot bean water use into green (rainfall) and blue (irrigation) components has not been quantified for southern Ethiopia, and this partition determines how far the crop draws on contested dry-season water sources. abstract: Adjusting the installed wind–photovoltaic (PV) ratio can improve renewable integration without increasing total renewable capacity. abstract: Reducing CO 2 emissions from the cement industry is challenging because a large share of the emissions arises from core chemical processes, and the further handling of the CO 2 depends highly on regional CO 2 storage availability. title: GeoCaseRec: a knowledge graph semantics-driven framework for sustainable urban renewal recommendation
abstract: As urbanisation shifts from outward expansion to the regeneration of existing built environments, sustainable urban renewal increasingly depends on the effective reuse of historical cases. However, this remains constrained by fragmented multi-source geo-referenced data, semantic heterogeneity, and limited case evaluation. To address these challenges, this study proposes GeoCaseRec, a knowledge graph semantics-driven framework for urban renewal recommendation. title: A global base temperature dataset for residential building energy demand modelling
abstract: Abstract. Accurate building energy demand modeling is critical to decarbonizing regional energy systems. The cooling and heating degree-day models are widely used due to their simplicity and low data requirements; however, the lack of accurate base temperature data limits their performance. In particular, the scarcity of high temporal resolution building energy demand data constrains regional-scale base temperature estimation through conventional methods such as the energy signature method and the performance line method. title: Additive manufacturing of superelastic NiTi braided metamaterials: an innovative strategy for engineering minimally invasive vascular medical devices
abstract: Additive manufacturing of superelastic Nitinol (NiTi) braided metamaterials is demonstrated in this study, enabling the creation of a wide variety of concepts for personalized vascular medical devices. Engineering contributions include the algorithmic design of lattices and woven structures, which can be adjusted to anatomical surfaces and whose mechanical properties can be controlled by design, enabling functional gradients of stiffness and transitions between lattices and wovens, as well as the creation of fully-connected braided structures achieved in a single printing step. title: Staged digital transformation and firms’ total factor productivity: evidence from Chinese cultural firms
abstract: This study explores the effects of digital transformation (DT) on firms’ total factor productivity (TFP) across the digital technology application (DTA) stage and digital business model innovation (DBMI) stage. Using a sample of 245 Chinese listed cultural firms from 2011 to 2022, we examine how DT impacts TFP differently across these stages. The results show that DT significantly enhances firms’ TFP in both the DTA and DBMI stages. However, productivity gains materialize only after firms reach the transformation threshold in both stages. title: Detection of old-growth forests using airborne laser scanning and other auxiliary data combined with National Forest Inventory field plot data
abstract: Accurate detection and mapping of old-growth forests (OGFs) are essential for biodiversity conservation and forest management, yet remain challenging due to their structural complexity, rarity and varying definitions. In this study, we developed a framework for classifying OGFs in boreal forests by integrating airborne laser scanning (ALS) data, and multispectral Sentinel-2 imagery and aerial imagery with different modelling approaches. title: A dual-functional antiviral and anticancer peptide to target intricate host-pathogen interacting proteins of human papillomavirus associated with head and neck cancer
abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma is increasingly being reported worldwide, and a major contributing factor is the incidence of human papillomavirus infections. The viral infection activates proto-oncogenes and signalling mechanisms aiding in tumorigenesis. An efficient way to block the virus-induced carcinogenesis is to identify a common medicament that can effectively inhibit the viral and host proteins. abstract: Abstract Agricultural drought significantly threatens food security, livelihoods, and ecosystem stability, especially in regions prone to drought, such as the East Bale zone. This study investigates the spatial and temporal patterns of agricultural drought over 30 years (1993–2024) by combining meteorological station data with satellite‐derived vegetation and thermal indices. To assess meteorological drought, the standardized precipitation index (SPI) was calculated at 3‐, 6‐, and 12‐month intervals. title: Microenvironment Design and Regulation of M‐N‐C Catalysts for Oxygen Reduction Reactions: Mechanisms, Synergies, and Future Pathways
abstract: ABSTRACT Fuel cells represent the core components of next‐generation high‐efficiency electrochemical energy conversion technologies. The performance of the cathode oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) catalyst determines battery efficiency and lifespan. Thus, developing efficient, cost‐effective ORR single‐atom catalysts is essential for fuel cell commercialization. title: Indicators from fish habitat time series for climate change and environmental flows assessment
abstract: Mediterranean rivers are exposed to climate-driven hydrological change, yet environmental-flow assessment relies on static habitat metrics that poorly represent fish habitat variability over time. We developed a time-explicit framework that converts monthly weighted usable area (WUA) series into indicators of the magnitude, variability, duration, frequency and persistence of limiting physical habitat conditions. title: Spatiotemporal patterns and driving mechanisms of cultivated land multifunctionality evolution: evidence from county-level data in Sichuan Province, China
abstract: The pursuit of socioeconomic development, food security, and ecological sustainability has driven the multifunctional evolution of cultivated land. Under the constraint of limited cultivated land resources, achieving synergy among the economic, food security, and ecological functions of cultivated land has become a major challenge for agricultural modernization in Sichuan Province. This study evaluates the spatiotemporal evolution of cultivated land multifunctionality (CLM) and investigates the driving mechanisms underlying the CLM synergy level. title: Climate policy uncertainty and agricultural digital-intelligent transformation in China: evidence from provincial panel data
abstract: Introduction Climate policy uncertainty can affect long-term investment decisions in agriculture, yet its influence on agricultural digital-intelligent transformation remains insufficiently understood. This study examines how lagged climate policy uncertainty affects agricultural digital-intelligent transformation and whether rural finance and agricultural service policies can moderate this relationship. title: Urea-loaded nanoclay biopolymer composites integrated with beneficial microbes enhance nutrient uptake and mitigate greenhouse gas emissions
abstract: Low nitrogen use efficiency of prilled urea contributes to substantial economic loss and environmental pollution through leaching, denitrification, and ammonia volatilization. This study evaluated urea-loaded nanoclay biopolymer composites (NCBPCs), synthesized from clay-acrylic acid + aczrylamide-based polymer composite grafted with maize flour (NCBPC-M) and mango kernel flour (NCBPC-MK), integrated with phosphorus- and zinc-solubilizing bacteria ( Lactococcus lactis and Pseudomonas aeruginosa ), as a sustainable alternative nitrogen source in a maize–wheat cropping system. title: Cloud computing and global satellite products for potential groundwater recharge estimation: application to the Basin of Mexico
abstract: Groundwater recharge (GWr) estimation is fundamental for assessing aquifer storage changes, ensuring groundwater sustainability, and supporting effective water management. However, regional groundwater recharge assessment remains challenging because it requires integrating large geospatial datasets, computational resources, and hydrogeological information that are often unavailable in data-limited regions. title: Understanding urban energy policies as transition pathways toward sustainable and smart cities
abstract: The transition of urban energy systems toward sustainability and smartness depends on effective policy design. Despite significant scholarly attention, research remains fragmented across policy instruments, system components, and analytical perspectives. To address these limitations, this study presents an integrated framework that combines a PRISMA-guided systematic review, artificial intelligence-assisted topic modeling (BERTopic), and Multi-Level Perspective (MLP) transition theory. title: Molecular detection and characterization of flea-associated bacteria: genetic diversity and co-occurrence patterns involving Bartonella, Rickettsia, and Wolbachia in Ctenocephalides felis felis from an Atlantic Forest region of Brazil
abstract: Ctenocephalides felis felis is a widespread ectoparasite of dogs and cats and has been associated with transmission of several microorganisms of veterinary and public health relevance. This study investigated the molecular occurrence, genetic diversity, and co-occurrence patterns of Bartonella spp., Rickettsia spp., and Wolbachia spp. in fleas collected from dogs and cats in an Atlantic Forest area encompassing the Ilhéus and Itabuna microregions, Bahia State, northeastern Brazil. title: Maternal edible THC consumption alters offspring neurodevelopment and emotional behavior in rhesus macaques
abstract: BACKGROUND: Prenatal cannabis exposure is associated with adverse offspring outcomes including altered neurodevelopment. However, there is insufficient evidence to establish a direct association. We sought to determine the impact of chronic prenatal delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) exposure on offspring neurodevelopment and emotional behavior in a translational rhesus macaque model. METHODS: Animals were divided into two groups, control and THC-exposed, with both groups receiving a daily edible (placebo or THC) pre-conception, throughout pregnancy, and postnatally. title: DNA methylation maintenance at heterochromatin
abstract: DNA methylation at CpGs silences repetitive elements and transposable elements (TEs) within constitutive heterochromatin in the genome. Deregulation of DNA methylation at these sites and their subsequent derepression promotes genomic instability. Hypomethylation of constitutive heterochromatin is a molecular hallmark of aging and cancer, as well as the rare genetic disorder Immunodeficiency, Centromeric instability and Facial anomalies (ICF) syndrome. title: Robust and replicable effects of ageing on resting-state brain electrophysiology measured with MEG
abstract: Abstract Non-invasive recordings using brain electrophysiology provide credible insights into decline in neuronal functioning with age. New approaches are required to translate these results into compelling clinical metrics and meet the global challenge of preserving brain health in ageing. Changes in neuronal dynamics with ageing are observable in the power spectra of EEG and MEG recordings. Highly promising candidates for electrophysiological markers have been identified, but progress is hindered by substantial methodological variability across studies. title: Rapid planning of deposition strategies for wire arc additive manufacturing: from target-geometry design to dimensional-accuracy control
abstract: The accuracy and efficiency of wire arc additive manufacturing (WAAM) depend on the geometrically consistent translation of a target geometry into multi-layer multi-pass bead layouts and robot-executable toolpaths under prescribed process parameters. To bridge this design-to-deposition gap, this study introduces a target-geometry-driven framework that integrates four capabilities: weld bead geometry prediction, primitive-based deposition geometry modelling, layout parameter optimisation, and toolpath generation. title: Exchange and Exclusion in the Non-abelian Anyon Gas
abstract: Abstract We review and develop the many-body spectral theory of ideal anyons, i.e. identical quantum particles in the plane whose exchange rules are governed by unitary representations of the braid group on N strands. Allowing for arbitrary rank (dependent on N ) and non-abelian representations, and letting $$N \rightarrow \infty $$ N → ∞ , this defines the ideal non-abelian many-anyon gas. title: Wave-induced erosion and notch development at the Fimbul Ice Shelf front
abstract: Abstract. Ocean waves erode the waterline of Antarctic ice-shelf fronts and carve a thermo-erosional notch. The notch is hidden from satellites, yet it preconditions front collapse and footloose calving, so the link between notch growth and observable front retreat matters for how wave-exposed ice shelves lose mass. We study this link at the Fimbul Ice Shelf, East Antarctica, in January–February 2024. The widely used White et al. abstract: Winkelmann conjectures that every smooth flexible complex affine variety of dimension at least two is a Rosay--Rudin space. title: Projected Sensitivity to Atmospheric Neutrino Oscillations using a 1725 m$^{3}$ Liquid-Nitrogen Detector at CJPL
abstract: In atmospheric neutrino analyses, the usable zenith-angle range is generally restricted to upward-going events to suppress the cosmic-ray muon background. Motivated by the exceptionally low underground muon background at the China Jinping Underground Laboratory (CJPL), we investigate whether extending the zenith-angle acceptance can improve the sensitivity of atmospheric neutrino oscillation measurements. abstract: We establish global well-posedness of classical solutions to the two-dimensional primitive equations with fractional horizontal dissipation for arbitrarily large initial data in the full subcritical range $1<α\leq2$. Together with the known ill-posedness results for $0\leqα<1$, this establishes the sharp dissipation threshold for large-data global well-posedness in the corresponding solution framework. title: Fast and Stable Harmonic Approximation from Ill-distributed Data using Moving Least Squares
abstract: We consider harmonic approximation on the torus $\mathbb{T}^d$, the sphere $\mathcal{S}^d$, and the rotation group $\mathrm{SO}(3)$. While several global approaches are available for computing a harmonic expansion from scattered data, their stability and, especially, their runtime depend strongly on the geometry of the nodes, in particular on a sufficiently small fill distance. title: Measurement of the $^{39}$Ar specific activity in atmospheric argon with DArT at the Canfranc Underground Laboratory
abstract: We report the measurement of the $^{39}$Ar specific activity of atmospheric argon using DArT, a low-background single-phase liquid-argon detector read out by cryogenic silicon photomultipliers, at the Canfranc Underground Laboratory (LSC) in Spain. DArT was first filled with atmospheric argon and then with a sample of underground argon of known radioactivity from the DarkSide-50 experiment. title: Model-Order-Adaptive Channel Estimation for AFDM Systems with Fractional Delay and Doppler
abstract: Affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM) has emerged as a promising waveform for high-mobility communications owing to its ability to exploit multipath diversity. However, channel state information (CSI) acquisition remains challenging in channels with fractional delay and Doppler and an unknown number of propagation paths. In this paper, we investigate the channel estimation for AFDM systems. We first analyze the AFDM response in the presence of fractional-delay-induced frequency wrapping. abstract: We prove a weighted Wasserstein spectral gap for the three-dimensional primitive equations on $\mathscr E=\{u\in H^1\cap L^8: \partial_zu\in L^4\}$ under finite-rank additive Brownian forcing that is phase-complete finite Fourier and satisfies a quantitative quadratic saturation condition. title: MUNITE: Unified Multimodal Latent Inference for Any-to-Any Multimodal Generation
abstract: We introduce MUNITE, a latent-variable framework for flexible any-to-any multimodal generation that treats encoding and latent generation as the same inference problem under different amounts of observed evidence. Given any subset of modalities, MUNITE models the conditional distribution over the latent representation associated with the complete observation. abstract: We establish interior and global Hölder estimates for linearized Monge-Ampère equations in divergence form in all dimensions $n\geq 3$, when the Hessian determinant of the convex Monge-Ampère potential is bounded above and below by positive constants and the vector field on the right-hand side is bounded. title: Multi-scale spectral statistics of intermediate quantum chaos in ultracold erbium collisions
abstract: Characterizing intermediate quantum chaos in systems with mixed phase spaces requires probing spectral correlations across multiple scales. Here, we present a multi-scale statistical analysis of the resonance spectra of ultracold 166Er and 168Er atoms using higher-order spacing ratios, spacing increments, and the accumulated power spectral density of decimated level sequences. abstract: The LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) experiment has recently reported a nuclear-recoil candidate at $E_R\simeq248$ keV. title: The TIB Terminology Service and Its Terminology Collection for the Earth System Sciences
abstract: Advancing Earth System Sciences (ESS) depends on our ability to integrate highly diverse data from a range of disciplines, including geographical information sciences, palaeontology, marine science, biodiversity research, atmospheric sciences and biology. A major scientific obstacle to this integration is semantic heterogeneity: different disciplines use different methods and terms to describe data, resulting in fragmented vocabularies. title: Africa’s first permanent Ocean Observatory: powering science, defending nature, and shaping policy for ocean governance and the blue economy
abstract: Sustained, high-resolution ocean observation is essential for understanding how marine ecosystems respond to climate variability, human pressure, and conservation action. Yet long-term observing platforms remain scarce across the Global South, limiting the capacity to detect environmental change, evaluate management interventions, and support evidence-based ocean governance. To help address this gap, we established Africa’s first permanent, multi-ecosystem Ocean Observatory in Mozambique’s Bazaruto Archipelago, operated by the Bazaruto Center for Scientific Studies (BCSS) and Kisawa Sanctuary

title: Staphylococcus aureus in bovine mastitis in northwestern Iran: patterns of antimicrobial and multidrug resistance, biofilm formation, and virulence/resistance gene carriage
abstract: Abstract Staphylococcus aureus ( S. aureus ), a major cause of bovine mastitis, represents a significant challenge for the dairy industry due to its economic and zoonotic importance. This study aimed to investigate the distribution of major virulence-associated genes (lukE, seA, sei), the methicillin-resistance gene (mecA), antimicrobial susceptibility, and biofilm formation in S. aureus isolates obtained from cases of bovine clinical mastitis in dairy farms of East and West Azerbaijan provinces, Iran. title: Threshold Type Responses of Indo Pacific Coral Reefs to Local Human Induced Degradation
abstract: Coral reef ecosystems face cumulative pressures from ocean warming, ocean acidification and diverse coastal human disturbances. As ecologically critical habitats and socio economic resources for coastal human communities, reef systems require improved understanding of how local anthropogenic activities drive degradation trajectories. Existing monitoring datasets covering the Indo Pacific region provide large scale observational evidence to disentangle reef responses against human related stressors and distinguish threshold driven shifts from gradual dose response decline. abstract: Online enterprises can buy digital visibility before they have earned confidence in the transaction that follows. This study develops and tests a dual pathway model in which digital promotion shapes purchase intention through attitude, while perceived transaction security operates through trust and post-purchase satisfaction. The model also separates purchase intention from completed-shopping behaviour, allowing the analysis to identify where favourable evaluation fails to become action. title: The bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA) international database: an update and ongoing call for data
abstract: The Bioelectrical Impedance Analysis International Database (BIAID) is an initiative aimed at pooling, standardizing and harmonizing bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA) data across populations. This report provides a synthesis of the data currently available in the BIAID and an overview of the actions undertaken to date. The repository, which is based on raw bioelectrical values as minimal required data, has expanded over the past two years to include 321,680 individuals across the lifespan, encompassing both healthy and clinical populations and representing all WHO regions. abstract: La disponibilidad de datos abiertos demográficos en los portales autonómicos españoles presenta diferencias territoriales que dificultan identificar si los catálogos más amplios ofrecen también una mayor cobertura de esta categoría. title: Governing access: Freedom of information, knowledge politics, and the limits of transparency in public health research
abstract: Introduction Freedom of Information (FOI) laws are presented as mechanisms of transparency and democratic accountability, yet their operation as tools of public health research remains under-examined. title: From emergence to exposure: one health attribution of azole-resistant Aspergillus fumigatus in Southeast Asia
abstract: Southeast Asia is a hotspot for azole-resistant Aspergillus fumigatus yet remains underrepresented in global surveillance. Disciplinary approaches, including genomics, environmental sampling, and social science, have progressed but remain poorly integrated. We outline a One Health attribution framework linking selection pressures, environmental reservoirs, exposure pathways, and clinical resistance signals to prioritise surveillance, target interventions, and allocate resources where they will have greatest impact.

title: Ocean sunfish M. mola in the Mediterranean Sea: Shedding light on an enigmatic species through 14 Years of spatial and environmental assessment
abstract: The ocean sunfish M. mola is frequently sighted in marine waters worldwide, including the Mediterranean Sea, yet information on its distribution and ecology in this region remains limited. This study synthesizes current global knowledge on M. mola and investigates its spatial occurrence in the Mediterranean Sea using long-term visual observations from the Fixed Line Transect Mediterranean Monitoring Network, complemented by environmental DNA (eDNA) samples collected through the Life Conceptu Maris project. abstract: Keadilan sosial dalam pendidikan bahasa di Asia Tenggara menjadi isu kritis di tengah keberagaman etnis, bahasa, dan budaya kawasan. Penelitian ini mengkaji interseksi ras, etnisitas, gender, dan seksualitas dalam pendidikan bahasa di Asia Tenggara melalui tinjauan literatur sistematis. title: From Local Evidence to Regional Leadership: Post-Preeclampsia Care in Thailand
abstract: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, particularly preeclampsia, identify women at increased risk of persistent hypertension and later cardiovascular disease, yet postpartum services often remain organized around short-term obstetric recovery. Thailand is well positioned to address this discontinuity because prospective local studies have demonstrated elevated blood pressure, hypertension, and selected cardiovascular and renal risk markers at 6 weeks and 6-12 months after preeclampsia or gestational hypertension. title: Coastal residents’ support for marine spatial planning: The role of values, place attachment, and community impacts
abstract: Coastal environments worldwide are subject to rapid transformations, including to mitigate against climate change, biodiversity loss, and pollution. The potentially significant impacts of these transformations on coastal communities makes it imperative to understand their response to Marine Spatial Planning (MSP) decisions. title: Coastal Vegetation as Nature-Based Solutions: A Bibliometric and Proxy Matrix Review of Ecosystem Services and Coastal Protection
abstract: Climate change and coastal development are intensifying coastal hazards and increasing the need for evidence-based Nature-based Solutions (NbSs) in integrated coastal zone management. However, proxy-based evidence for evaluating the ecosystem services and coastal protection functions of coastal vegetation has not been systematically synthesized across these dimensions. title: Current gender equality status in EU blue economy – Gaps and recommendations for a more inclusive and fair sector
abstract: Gender equality and the empowerment of women are core priorities of the European Union. However, strategic sectors such as the blue economy remain comparatively underexplored in terms of structural and cultural barriers to female participation with both traditional and emerging industries being still male dominated. Against this backdrop, this paper presents the findings of a systematic review of publications from 2010 to 2024 addressing gender equality issues in the European Union blue economy. title: Modeling and Energy–Optimal Neuro–Fuzzy Control of Cylindrical Autonomous Underwater Vehicles
abstract: This paper presents a reduced–order mathematical model and an energy–optimal neuro–fuzzy control method for a cylindrical autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV). The standard six DOFs formulation is simplified to translational motions under the assumption that rotational motions are stabilized near a nominal operating point. title: A blueprint for Vibrio surveillance and risk reduction in Europe
abstract: Vibrio bacteria, long regarded as pathogens of tropical waters, are now emerging across numerous European coastlines as rising sea surface temperatures and extreme weather reshape microbial ecologies. Wound and foodborne infections caused by Vibrio vulnificus , Vibrio parahaemolyticus and other non-cholera species are increasing in frequency and latitude. title: Open-data remote sensing framework for peat hydrological unit condition scoring in South Sumatra Peatlands (2018-2024)
abstract: Tropical peatland degradation remains a critical environmental challenge in Southeast Asia, yet operational monitoring frameworks that align with governance boundaries remain limited. This study aimed to develop an open-data remote sensing framework for assessing peatland condition at the Peat Hydrological Unit (Kesatuan Hidrologis Gambut, KHG) scale in South Sumatra, Indonesia. title: Beyond Vulnerability: Women’s Water Stewardship and Adaptive Agency in Climate-Vulnerable Bangladesh

Using a Feminist Political Ecology (FPE) lens, this study explores women’s adaptive agency in daily water management practices at both household and community levels. The study was conducted in three climate-vulnerable regions of Bangladesh: Mongla (cyclone-prone coastal Bagerhat), Naogaon (drought-prone), and Cox’s Bazar (flash flood- and landslide-prone). The study employed a qualitative approach incorporating in-depth interviews with women

title: SOCIOECONOMIC IMPACTS AND STAKEHOLDER COMPLIANCE WITH THE SINGLE-USE PLASTICS BAN IN LAGOS STATE, NIGERIA
abstract: Single-use plastic has been reported to block urban drainage facilities in Lagos State, leading to a regulatory ban. This study evaluated policy awareness, compliance behaviour, economic impacts, and policy challenges across the state. All respondents in this study were selected through a multistage stratified sampling process across 20 local government areas, with a total sample size of 430. Chi-square (χ²) tests and multivariable binary logistic regression were used to analyse the data. Policy awareness reached 72.6%, with 52.4% of aware respondents reporting the ban. title: Educación, menstruación y tecnología: estrategias digitales para mejorar la gestión menstrual en el ámbito universitario
abstract: La salud menstrual como concepto ha entrado en la legislación laboral principalmente a través de la institución de la baja menstrual, pero esta, incluida en derecho español en 2023, no ampara a las estudiantes que por razón de su periodo tengan que ausentarse de actividades en la universidad. Es imprescindible el acercamiento a este fenómeno para establecer unas condiciones justas y decentes, que no penalicen a las estudiantes que sufren de dismenorrea. title: Revealing the unequal availability and socioeconomic factors of health facilities based on taxi trajectory data and geospatial analysis
abstract: As China’s economy grows, healthcare equity concerns intensify. Historically, healthcare resource allocation often mismatches cities’ economic status, and their spatial distribution remains uneven. This study examines healthcare disparities at a grid level using a two-step floating catchment area (2SFCA) that accounts for distance decay. It utilizes big data and API technology to develop a more accurate distance decay function based on travel data, obtaining results that reflect the healthcare fairness. journal: European journal of transport and infrastructure research

title: Why do people migrate irregularly? Evidence from a lab-in-the-field experiment in West Africa
abstract: Irregular migration to Europe by sea, though risky, remains one of the most popular migration options for many Sub-Saharan Africans. This study examines the drivers of irregular migration decisions using an incentivized lab-in-the-field experiment in rural Gambia, the African country with the highest per-capita rate of irregular migration to Europe. Potential migrants substantially overestimate the probability of dying en route , reporting an average belief of 51 percent compared with a best available estimate of about 20 percent. title: Aligning climate policy with energy justice through remedial stakeholder theory
abstract: We contribute to this special issue by exploring climate policy and energy justice through the lens of remedial stakeholder theory. While stakeholder theory traditionally focuses on present and forward-looking relationships, we argue that climate change and the energy transition provide a compelling case to examine the nexus of past, present, and future organisational action. title: Documentation of Ethnic Meat Products as Cultural Heritage in Borno State, Nigeria
abstract: This study aimed to identify and document the ethnic meat products of Borno State, Nigeria, addressing a critical gap in the documentation of Nigeria's intangible culinary heritage. A cross-sectional survey was conducted across eight major ethnic communities (Babur, Chibok, Guduf, Kanakuru, Kanuri, Marghi, Shuwa-Arab, and Terawa) using 24 focus group discussions (FGDs) with elderly participants aged 50 years and above, with data transcribed and triangulated for reliability. title: The Lunar Water Rush: Space Resource Rights, Safety Zones, and India's Regulatory Concern
abstract: The Moon is becoming a realistic site for scientific missions, permanent research facilities, and commercial activity. One resource has become especially important: water ice near the lunar south pole. Lunar water is extremely valuable for future commercial space operations. Yet international space law does not clearly answer who may extract it, own it after extraction, exclude others from a working area, or resolve conflicts between competing missions. title: Ground-motion dataset for shallow earthquakes in Colombia
abstract: Abstract. The tectonics of Colombia is characterised by the interaction of multiple oceanic plates subducting beneath the continent, generating active transpressional deformation and a wide range of subduction-related and crustal earthquakes. We present a flatfile containing ground-motion intensity measurements from 694 shallow earthquakes. The dataset includes 8,086 three-component acceleration records that were uniformly processed. title: Bebas-Aktif and Pragmatic Assertiveness: Continuity and Change in Indonesia’s Foreign Policy under Prabowo Subianto
abstract: This article examines whether Indonesian foreign policy under President Prabowo Subianto (October 2024–August 2026) represents a doctrinal departure from bebas-aktif or a programmatic reconfiguration of strategic autonomy. It develops the Doctrinal Continuity–Instrumental Reconfiguration (DCIR) model, integrating foreign-policy-change theory, role theory, leader-centered Foreign Policy Analysis, and hedging. title: Optimization of Wind Power Generation in Ambon City Using the Queen Honey Bee Migration (QHBM) Method
abstract: The increasing demand for sustainable electricity generation highlights the importance of efficient wind power optimization, particularly in island regions with variable wind resources such as Ambon City, Indonesia. This study proposes an intelligent optimization framework based on the Queen Honey Bee Migration (QHBM) algorithm to improve wind power generation performance. A simulation model of a grid-connected wind energy conversion system was developed, integrating aerodynamic turbine modeling, generator dynamics, and power conversion stages. title: Economic Valuation of Informal PET Bottle Recovery Using Market Price and Avoided Cost Approaches: Evidence from a Local Circular Economy in Southern Philippines
abstract: This study performed a Waste Economic Valuation (WEV) of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) bottle recovery within the informal recycling system of Linamon, Lanao del Norte, Philippines. The study used a qualitative approach with embedded quantitative analysis, integrating WEV estimates with Key Informant Interview (KII) data from 15 respondents, including 10 informal PET collectors, 3 junkshop operators, and 2 Municipal Environment and Natural Resources Office (MENRO) personnel. title: Ethical Dilemmas of Green Leadership in Corporate Social Responsibility: Implications for Community Welfare in the Cirata Geulis Program
abstract: This study examines how green leaders navigate ethical dilemmas during the implementation of Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) programs in vulnerable communities and how these decisions influence community welfare. Challenging the prevailing assumption within Green Transformational Leadership (GTL) scholarship of a linear alignment between ecological and social objectives, the study explores right-versus-right moral tensions in community-based CSR practices. title: Multi-Generation YOLO Comparison for Indonesian Banknote Detection Under Challenging Conditions
abstract: This study presents a comparative analysis of multiple YOLO model generations, namely YOLOv5, YOLOv8, YOLOv11, and YOLO26, for Indonesian banknote detection under real-world conditions. The evaluation focuses on challenging scenarios, including brightness variation, background clutter, and occlusion. A dataset of 1,400 images is used for training, while 200 real-world images are manually annotated and utilized for evaluation. title: Legal Strategies for Biodiversity Conservation in Southern Nigeria: Lessons from International Laws
abstract: Southern Nigeria is currently facing a profound environmental crisis characterized by rapidly rising sea levels, recurrent and intensified flooding, and widespread ecological degradation. These developments pose a growing threat to human settlements, critical infrastructure, and fragile ecosystems. Alarmingly, government projections suggest that over 30 Nigerian states could soon be impacted by severe flood events, amplifying the urgency for a robust and integrated legal response. title: KNOWLEDGE AND FLOOD RISK PERCEPTION AMONG HOUSEHOLDS IN FLOOD-PRONE RURAL AND URBAN COMMUNITIES IN KADUNA STATE, NIGERIA
abstract: Disasters have devastating effects on communities, especially where knowledge and perception are limited, vulnerability is high, and capacity is low. Nigeria has suffered from recurrent flood disasters, with Kaduna State among the affected regions. Household heads are important elements in flood disaster management, and their knowledge and risk perception are crucial. This study assessed household knowledge and flood risk perception among households in flood-prone rural and urban communities in Kaduna State. title: Nutrición Infantil como experiencia formativa: cambios reportados en estudiantes de Educación Infantil y transferencia de aprendizajes al entorno familiar
abstract: The present study analyzes the changes reported by students enrolled in the Bachelor’s Degree in Early Childhood Education after completing the Child Nutrition course unit, with emphasis on self-assessment of nutritional knowledge, personal eating practices, and the transfer of learning to the family environment. A descriptive, cross-sectional study with a quantitative approach was conducted. The participants were 61 students who completed a 23-item self-report instrument at the end of the semester. title: Benefit Compensation and Allowance Procedure Adjustment Strategy to Strengthen the Performance of PT Samudera Crew's Human Resources at Jakarta
abstract: Background: The global maritime industry operates in a highly demanding environment characterized by severe labor shortages and intense competition for skilled personnel. Optimal operational performance depends heavily on both technical proficiency and fair compensation. PT XYZ Samudera Crewing faces a critical need to adjust its current reward system because these structures directly influence crew motivation and retention. title: International Law and Sustainable Development: Emerging Trends and Future Research Directions
abstract: Sustainable development has evolved from a largely aspirational policy concept into a principle with increasing normative weight across multiple branches of international law, including international environmental law, human rights law, trade law, and the law of the sea. This paper examines the legal status and evolving content of sustainable development in international law, tracing its doctrinal development from the 1987 Brundtland Report and the 1992 Rio Declaration through its treatment in international jurisprudence, most notably the International Court of Justice's Gabčíkovo-Nagymaros Pr

title: Nocturnal arthropod occurrences across Natura 2000 protected areas of Madeira Island (Portugal)
abstract: Artificial light at night (ALAN) is increasingly recognised as an important anthropogenic pressure affecting nocturnal biodiversity, particularly in oceanic islands with high endemism levels. Arthropods, especially moths (Lepidoptera), are key components of nocturnal ecosystems, yet their distribution and abundance patterns in Madeira Island remain insufficiently documented and their responses to ALAN are poorly understood. title: Prospects and constraints of cultural tourism development in Bangladesh: An empirical insight towards its sustainability
abstract: Bangladesh is home to a wide range of both tangible and intangible cultural heritage. The country has three tangible UNESCO World Heritage Sites and five elements inscribed on UNESCO’s Intangible Cultural Heritage list. It hosts over 50 indigenous ethnic groups and 1,500 documented tourist attractions. Despite its diverse features, cultural tourism, however, remains underdeveloped in the country. This study investigates the potential, challenges, and pathways toward sustainable cultural tourism development in Bangladesh. title: Overtourism governance and resident wellbeing. A social exchange framework for understanding community support under visitor management measures
abstract: Overtourism has moved destination scholarship from the description of visitor pressure to the design of measures that contain it. Caps, timed entry, tourist taxes, short-term rental controls, cruise berth limits and dispersal schemes are now common, yet the field still explains community reactions with a model built for a different question. Social exchange theory has long framed resident support as a judgement about the benefits and costs of tourism itself. title: The Temporal and Spatial Patterns of Cholera Outbreaks in the Rohingya Refugee Camps, Cox’s Bazar, Bangladesh
abstract: Cholera remains a major public health threat in humanitarian settings such as the Rohingya refugee camps of Cox's Bazar, Bangladesh, which are characterised by congestion, inadequate water and sanitation, and overstretched health services.This study analysed the temporal and spatial patterns of cholera in the camps to identify seasonal variation and distribution across camps and to inform control.We used secondary data from the World Health Organization's Early Warning, Alert and Response System (EWARS), sentinel surveillance, and laboratory surveillance to construct annual weekly trend lines

title: Risk perception, institutional trust and misinformation as correlates of public avoidance behaviour in South Korea following the Fukushima treated-water discharge: implications for radiological protection communication
abstract: Public avoidance behaviour following radiological events can persist even when authoritative assessments judge the associated exposure to be negligible, posing a persistent challenge for radiological protection communication. Taking Japan's discharge of Advanced Liquid Processing System (ALPS)-treated water from the Fukushima Daiichi site into the Pacific Ocean as a case, this study asks why comparable levels of perceived risk translate into avoidance behaviour for some individuals but not others. abstract: BackgroundEuthanasia remains a highly debated issue in end-of-life care because it raises ethical concerns surrounding patient autonomy, relief of suffering, professional responsibilities, and the sanctity of life. Nurses and midwives frequently face these ethical challenges in caring for patients with advanced illness, yet evidence on their perspectives within sub-Saharan African cancer care settings remains limited.AimThis study explored nurses' and midwives' ethical perspectives and perceived implications regarding the potential legalisation of euthanasia in advanced cancer care in Ghana.Re

title: Redesigning Iran’s water-energy-food nexus: A path to sustainability and shared value creation
abstract: The Water-Energy-Food (WEF) nexus is a critical framework to address interconnected resource management challenges in Iran, particularly amid increasing environmental constraints and socio-economic pressures. This study applies the System Redesign toward Creating Shared Value (SYRCS) methodology to redesign the WEF nexus, emphasizing stakeholder engagement, sustainability, and systemic reforms. title: Human-Hippopotamus conflicts and socio-ecological tensions in the Ruzizi plain: a one health and political ecology perspective
abstract: Introduction Human-wildlife conflicts have intensified in the Kamanyola and Katogota areas of South Kivu, Democratic Republic of Congo, leading to human fatalities, injuries, crop losses and retaliatory killings of hippopotamuses. These conflicts illustrate the need for integrated conservation approaches that account for biodiversity protection, livelihood security and ecosystem health. abstract: Abstract As visitors increasingly rely on AI-enabled apps and recommender systems, AI is becoming an important mediator of tourism choice. Tourism decision-making is cognitively demanding, and visitors rarely evaluate all available destinations, attractions, travel periods, and services equally. Consistent with bounded rationality, they simplify complex choice environments through limited information, heuristics, and platform-mediated evaluation. title: Assessing awareness and attitudes among Middle Eastern and North African populations regarding antimicrobial drug resistance: a regional cross-sectional study
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is an escalating global health crisis, yet patterns of public understanding and antibiotic consumption in the Middle East and North Africa remain under-researched. This study aimed to evaluate the current landscape of AMR awareness, knowledge gaps, and self-medication practices among the general populations of seven Middle Eastern and North African nations. A large-scale, multicenter, cross-sectional study was conducted involving participants from Egypt, Palestine, Algeria, Sudan, Syria, Libya, and Jordan. title: E. coli and total coliform presence in private drinking water wells on Maryland farms: Determination of the impact of well properties, geographic, and precipitation factors
abstract: Over 43 million individuals in the United States use private wells for drinking water, but these wells are not regulated by the Safe Drinking Water Act. Unmaintained private wells on farms could become contaminated from pathogens from various potential sources including on-farm animal waste. Microbial contaminants in private wells could increase infectious disease risks among well users, therefore it is important to conduct well water testing and keep a well maintained system. title: Making living infrastructure legible: Patricia Johanson’s legacy for water-centered nature-based solutions
abstract: Nature-based solutions (NBS) are increasingly advanced as responses to climate change, urban flooding, water pollution, biodiversity loss, and declining ecosystem resilience. Yet their evaluation often gives less attention to the cultural, educational, and experiential conditions through which ecological functions become publicly understood and maintained. title: How to address challenges in the life cycle assessment of innovative cropping systems: Insights from a comparative study of a pesticide-free and a conventional system
abstract: CONTEXT Understanding environmental impacts of innovative cropping systems is integral to their development process. The most common method used for this purpose is life cycle assessment (LCA). However, several methodological challenges complicate the reliable application of LCA to such systems. OBJECTIVE This study critically reflects on six methodological challenges in the LCA of innovative cropping systems. title: Right on time: evaluating accuracy and timing of burn-severity assessments to support post-fire management
abstract: Abstract Effective post-fire management – including flood mitigation, revegetation, and salvage logging – depends on timely and reliable burn-severity assessments that characterize impacts to vegetation and soils. These assessments are typically derived from satellite-based change detection but can be delayed or degraded by aerosols (i.e., dust or smoke), clouds, and snow. title: Large language models show distinct multidimensional performance profiles and variable reproducibility in consensus‐based bone stress injury
abstract: Purpose: This study evaluated five publicly available large language model-based systems using a multidimensional, expert-based assessment of consensus-based clinical questions on bone stress injuries. Methods: Ten standardised questions derived from a 2025 international Delphi consensus on bone stress injuries were submitted to ChatGPT-5, Perplexity AI, Claude 4, Google Gemini 2.5 and Microsoft Copilot. title: Accelerated weathering of limestone for CO 2 capture and storage: a critical review of unbuffered, buffered, and modified pathways
abstract: Accelerated weathering of limestone (AWL) converts CO2 into dissolved bicarbonate by reacting calcium carbonate and water, an alternative to geological storage. This review examines AWL as a branching family spanning the unbuffered concept, buffered AWL (BAWL), and modified routes (potable-water, construction-grade waste limestone, promoter-assisted, utilization-based, ship-based, and electrochemical AWL), grouped into six classes covering reactor configuration, feedstock, dissolution promotion, effluent conditioning, downstream utilization, and electrochemically driven alkalinity generation.

title: Experimental data integration with fuzzy multi-criteria decision-making framework for matrix material selection of 2XXX series aluminium alloys
abstract: Matrix material selection for engineering purposes presents difficulties because specific requirements in economic, physical, mechanical, and thermal terms are not always compatible in the face of uncertainty in decision-making. While prior studies have employed Multi-Criteria Decision-Making (MCDM) models for material selection, most studies are concerned with reinforcement selection, achieving composite optimization, or knowing the rank of a certain material. title: Eleven tenets for the integrated, evolving and sustainable management of European Research Infrastructure Consortia
abstract: Research Infrastructures are increasingly central to scientific discovery, innovation and evidence-informed policy, but their management requires the integration of many dimensions that are often treated separately. This paper proposes an eleven-tenet framework for the integrated, evolving and sustainable management of European Research Infrastructure Consortia, extending existing tenet-based approaches by adding the explicit dimension of enabling scientific excellence. title: Novel Occurrence of Breeding Second-Year Gyrfalcons Suggests Elevated Mortality in Alaska
abstract: La presencia de individuos sub-adultos en una población reproductora de rapaces por lo demás estable suele considerarse un posible indicador de cambios en la demografía poblacional o de declive de la población. Como parte de un proyecto de monitoreo e investigación en curso en el oeste de Alaska, realizamos censos aéreos de rapaces que nidifican en paredes rocosas entre 2005–2025 en 550–850 sitios por año, e instalamos cámaras activadas por movimiento en 92 territorios ocupados por Falco rusticolus entre 2014 y 2025. title: Melting frontier: Great power competition in the Arctic from polar periphery to geopolitical epicenter
abstract: For most of the post-Cold War era, the Arctic was governed as an exception to great-power politics: a “zone of peace” in which scientific cooperation, not strategic rivalry, set the tone. That exception is closing. As Arctic Amplification strips away the ice that once made the region marginal, it is exposing a geography rich in shipping lanes, hydrocarbons, and critical minerals, and drawing the United States, Russia, and China into overlapping contests for military advantage, economic access, and legal control. abstract: The role of Cabinet in the implementation of fisheries legislation and the promulgation of regulations relating to fishery-related offences remains under-studied. This is a global phenomenon and entails instances where the relevant Minister promulgates regulations for the outlawing of fishery-related activities that are not sanctioned by law. title: Ecopreneurship and Sustainable Business Practices: Exploration through Literature of the Northeast
abstract: Introduction: This paper explores the intersection of ecopreneurship and sustainable business practices through the lens of Northeast Indian literature. Northeast Indian literature skillfully intertwines themes of ecopreneurship and sustainable business practices, showcasing the area's vibrant cultural heritage and profound relationship with nature. Writers from this region frequently illustrate how traditional ways of life harmonize with ecological conservation, highlighting the significance of indigenous knowledge in fostering sustainable development. abstract: Sustainable local economic development at the village level requires a balance between community welfare, environmental protection, and effective local governance. In Madura, the utilization of natural resources remains insufficiently aligned with environmental carrying capacity, creating challenges for achieving sustainable village development and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). title: Ecological status of sathurukondan mangrove wetland, Batticaloa, Sri Lanka: composition, diversity and vegetation pattern
abstract: Sathurukondan wetland in the Batticaloa District contains valuable mangrove resources, yet baseline ecological information remains rather scarce. This study assessed mangrove vegetation from May to October 2023, focusing on species distribution, abundance, and diversity. A total of 59 line transects and 99 quadrats were established to compile a species checklist and evaluate community structure using diversity indices such as the Shannon–Wiener index, Pielou’s evenness, and Margalef richness. abstract: Baleen whale strandings are rare in the southern Gulf of Mexico and can provide valuable molecular information where species are infrequently documented. We analyzed tissue from a highly decomposed whale stranded on the central coast of Veracruz, Mexico, by amplifying and bidirectionally sequencing the mitochondrial DNA control region. abstract: This study examines how communities in Atlantic Canada recognize, value, and integrate local knowledge into climate change adaptation, focusing on the enabling and constraining roles of funding, governance, and institutional structures. Guided by the Socio-Ecological Systems (SES) framework, the research forms part of a larger transdisciplinary project on collaborative governance in financing climate adaptation and mitigation. title: Contingency planning for incursions of alien taxa at priority sites: a practical decision support tool
abstract: Abstract The need for effective management of biological invasions is compounded by the escalating costs of inaction. Proactive measures are widely considered the most cost-effective approach to management. However, when regional or national preventative actions are not implemented or fail to stop new incursions, site-specific contingency plans can provide a crucial next line of defence for priority sites. title: The limits of Antarctic conservation governance
abstract: Abstract The Antarctic region exerts a profound influence on the Earth system, making its conservation fundamental to sustaining planetary health and human wellbeing. The Antarctic Treaty System (ATS) holds near-exclusive authority for environmental protection across the region, yet questions remain regarding its capacity to address a growing range of conservation threats. title: How does climate risk affect fisheries? New evidence from the operating cash flows of Chinese listed firms
abstract: Listed fisheries companies depend heavily on natural conditions, leaving their operations particularly exposed to climate change. Using Chinese listed fisheries companies as the research sample, this study examines the effect of regional climate risk on operating cash flow and investigates potential mitigating mechanisms. title: Investigating perspectives and emotions on climate change among children and adolescents in San Cristóbal, Galápagos
abstract: An estimated one billion children live at extremely high risk of adverse effects from climate change. Even when children are not exposed to direct physical impacts, the existential threat of climate change can have a psychological impact by creating a stressor that exacerbates underlying mental health disorders or contributes to the development of new disorders. abstract: During the three decades following the publication of the first comprehensive monograph on the European mudminnow ( Umbra krameri Walbaum, 1792), knowledge of the species’ biology, distribution, genetics, ecology, and conservation has expanded substantially. abstract: Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) enables continuous monitoring of dynamic strain along tens of kilometres of optical fibre, generating massive datasets whose interpretation and automated analysis remain challenging. DAS data can be understood as a time-distance image array. abstract: La informalidad laboral en México representa un obstáculo estructural para el ejercicio pleno del derecho a la seguridad social y para la sostenibilidad del sistema de protección social. abstract: Geoscience in Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC) operates amid persistent variability that challenges the continuity, credibil-ity, and public value of scientific work. This paper analyzes the resilience of the geoscience enterprise in the region—how science is designed, conducted, synthesized, and shared to serve public mandates—under shifting political, institutional, economic, environ-mental, and social conditions. abstract: Today European ports have moved beyond their traditional role as logistical gateways to become strategic infrastructure for energy, supply-chain resilience and urban development. In this context, port competitiveness can no longer be understood only in terms of logistical performance but must be assessed within a governance model capable of integrating environmental sustainability and territorial resilience. abstract: ABSTRACT Magnesium–aluminum‐layered double hydroxides (MgAl‐LDHs) are used in flame retardants, remediation, and catalysis. Sustainability comparisons of industrial routes are insufficient. This study couples techno‐economic analysis with life cycle assessment (LCA) to evaluate two routes (hydrothermal synthesis and modification) at 1000 t/a using industrial data. abstract: ABSTRACT Sorption‐based atmospheric water harvesting (SAWH) offers a promising route for decentralized freshwater production, but practical water output is often limited by slow sorption kinetics in salt‐loaded hydrogel sorbents. Here, a biomimetic multi‐layer heterogeneous hygroscopic (MHH) membrane is developed to decouple vapor capture from bulk liquid storage. title: Multi-year temporal and seasonal abundance patterns of common bottlenose dolphins near Sarasota, Florida
abstract: Long-term demographic monitoring is critical for understanding population stability and responses to environmental disturbance. Bottlenose dolphins ( Tursiops truncatus ) inhabiting Sarasota Bay, Florida, have been studied by the Sarasota Dolphin Research Program since 1970. While most dolphins in the resident community are individually identifiable via photographic-identification (photo-ID), direct census datasets are largely unavailable elsewhere. abstract: Abstract The Songliao River Basin, a critical hub for China's food security and renewable energy development, is increasingly vulnerable to extreme temperatures, yet raw Earth System Models (ESMs) exhibit substantial uncertainties in projecting future regional climate extremes. title: The neglected role of knowledge organization in disaster risk management: A scoping review
abstract: Knowledge plays an important role in Disaster Risk Management (DRM). However, although processes of organization, representation, classification, retrieval, and sharing are widely mobilized in this field, their relationship with Knowledge Organization (KO) remains insufficiently explicit and is frequently addressed from the perspectives of Knowledge Management (KM), Information Management (IM), and technological solutions. abstract: For decades, plant biology has relied on a narrow set of classical model organisms—such as Arabidopsis thaliana, Oryza sativa, and Zea mays —to uncover core physiological, developmental, and molecular pathways. These systems enabled foundational discoveries, yet their glycophytic, annual, and domesticated life histories limit their relevance for studying many adaptive traits found across global plant diversity. abstract: Abstract Urban flooding severely disrupts emergency services. Equitable mitigation requires identifying if socially vulnerable neighborhoods face disproportionate travel delays. abstract: This paper presents a communication-constrained coordinated path planning method for heterogeneous unmanned surface vehicle (USV)-unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) systems operating in maritime environments. abstract: Tourism is a pivotal driver of economic growth, cultural preservation, and social cohesion. However, in Nigeria, and particularly in Rivers State, the tourism sector remains largely underutilized despite the state's vast natural resources, vibrant cultural heritage, and strategic location in the Niger Delta region. abstract: Indonesia, as a megabiodiverse country, faces serious challenges from the degradation of protected forests caused by land conversion into illegal agricultural areas. abstract: Abstract Host-associated microbiomes are shaped by environmental heterogeneity across spatial gradients. abstract: Ports are increasingly central to decarbonisation, energy-system integration, and resilience, yet less is known about how port governance shapes experimentation and whether learning becomes embedded in organisational practice. Living Labs (LLs)—organised forms of multi-actor experimentation in real-life settings—offer a promising approach, but are often treated as governance-neutral. abstract: Sacred forests have a long history of protection and many of them are old-growth forests with centuries old trees important for conservation. abstract: Big History characterizes cosmic evolution as a sequence of thresholds where ordered systems—from stars to civilizations—harvest energy to maintain rising complexity. The system employs an innovative TiO 2 -based photo-electrocatalytic (PEC) filter that combines the photocatalytic properties of TiO 2 with the biocidal effect of UV radiation to remove nitrogen compounds from rearing water. title: From Reactive Remediation to Predictive Prevention: A Systems Synthesis of Global Soil Salinization and Sodicity
abstract: Soil salinization and sodicity are accelerating worldwide, reducing crop productivity across more than 160 million hectares of farmland and causing production losses approaching USD 27 billion annually. Despite decades of research documenting these impacts, the extent of salt-affected soils continues to expand. Salt-affected soil degradation emerges from feedbacks among physical, biological, and socioeconomic processes that operate across scales and resist intervention when addressed in isolation. title: Common Nitrification Inhibitors Exhibit Distinct Mechanisms on the Ammonia-Oxidizing Archaeon Nitrososphaera viennensis
abstract: Abstract Microbial ammonia oxidation, the first and rate-limiting step of nitrification, plays a central role in soil nitrogen cycling. It is most relevant in agricultural soils as nitrifiers compete with crops for ammonia-based fertilizers. Therefore, synthetic nitrification inhibitors are widely used alongside fertilizers to reduce the activities of dominant drivers of this process, i.e., ammonia-oxidizing archaea (AOA) and bacteria (AOB). title: DEVELOPMENT AND EVALUATION OF EFFERVESCENT GRANULES ENRICHED WITH DEFATTED WATERMELON SEED FLOUR
abstract: Watermelon seeds are nutrient-dense, phytochemical-rich by-products often discarded by the food industry. The present study aimed to develop effervescent granules from defatted watermelon seed flour and to evaluate their physicochemical characteristics. Watermelon seeds were processed and defatted using n-hexane solvent extraction. Ten distinct formulations (WSFG01–WSFG10) were prepared by wet granulation using precise stoichiometric ratios of citric acid, tartaric acid, and sodium bicarbonate. title: Analysis of urban heat islands in the study of urban environmental problems based on remote sensing
abstract: As global urbanization accelerates cities increasingly face ecological challenges, most notably the Urban Heat Island (UHI) effect. This study investigates the formation and spatial distribution of UHI’s in the cities of Mingachevir, Shirvan and Yevlakh, located in the central region of the Republic of Azerbaijan. Utilizing ArcGIS, the analysis processed Landsat 8 OLI/TIRS satellite imagery from August 2023. title: Data-driven accessibility to critical facilities using connected vehicle data: implications for future mobility and urban systems
abstract: Accurate measurement of accessibility to critical facilities is essential for equitable and efficient transportation and land-use planning, particularly in data-driven mobility systems. This study develops a novel hybrid framework to estimate travel time–based accessibility to schools and libraries using high-resolution connected vehicle (CV) data supplemented with Google Distance Matrix API to ensure complete spatial coverage. title: From Narrative to Algorithm: A Risk Mechanism Theory Index for Urban Infrastructure Investment in Sub-Saharan Africa
abstract: Rapidly expanding metropolitan areas across Sub-Saharan Africa face systemic risk from hazard-induced disruptions, exacerbated by infrastructure deficits and socioeconomic vulnerabilities. Traditional risk assessment frameworks frequently fail decision-makers by offering static, qualitative narratives that cannot prioritize capital allocation or track resilience over dynamic budget cycles. title: Tree Canopy Configurations and PET-Based Outdoor Thermal Comfort in Two Urban Parks of Tehran: An ENVI-met Scenario Study
abstract: Urban trees modify pedestrian thermal exposure through shading, evapotranspiration, radiation exchange, and interactions with surrounding surfaces. This study evaluates four combined surface-canopy configurations in representative 100 m x 100 m computational domains associated with Mellat Park and Saei Park, Tehran, using ENVI-met 5.5 and Physiological Equivalent Temperature (PET). title: Religion, Slavery and African Diaspora: A Historical Analysis
abstract: This study examines the interplay between African traditional religion, Islam, and Christianity in shaping slavery and the African diaspora, highlighting a shift from humane master-slave relationships to dehumanization during medieval Christian Europe, culminating in the transAtlantic slave trade. Through historical texts, it observes that slavery predates Christianity and Islam, with universal prevalence and local variations before its abolition. title: Beyond production: understanding aquaculture narratives, public engagement, and visibility on TikTok and Instagram
abstract: Public acceptance and societal trust are increasingly recognized as critical challenges for sustainable aquaculture development. While previous research has examined consumer perceptions and social acceptance, limited attention has been given to how aquaculture narratives are constructed, circulated, and gain visibility within contemporary digital media environments. This study examines how thematic patterns, sentiment, audience engagement, and narrative construction shape aquaculture communication on TikTok and Instagram. title: Sustainability agreements in port terminals and competition policy: A European opening?
abstract: This paper analyses the European Commission’s first informal opinion on a sustainability agreement between competing port terminal operators, representing a landmark case aimed at reconciling decarbonisation objectives with European competition law. Our study focuses on a specific project involving APM Terminals and its competitors in jointly purchasing and standardising electrical container handling equipment. title: Africa in the New Asian Century: A Comparative Study of India-China Foreign Policy
abstract: Africa has acquired strategic, economic, and diplomatic importance for emerging powers such as India and China in the 21st century. This article presents a comparative study of the African policies of India and China, analyzing the historical, political, economic, security, and social perspectives of both countries. India’s relations with Africa have been based on historical solidarity, anti-colonial movements, South-South cooperation, and the important role of the Indian diaspora.
