Developing a sustainable development strategy to improve the adaptation of the Nexus of food, energy, and water in the Sahara of Morocco
abstract: In the southern Moroccan regions, the interdependencies between water, energy, and food resources remain critical amid ongoing climate challenges and post-pandemic recovery. Despite increasing recognition of Nexus-based approaches, policy integration remains fragmented, limiting effective resource management. This study analyses the Food-Energy-Water Nexus under extreme environmental and socioeconomic conditions to identify sustainable strategies for rural resilience. abstract: Introduction Accurate mapping of grassland vegetation and bare land is important for grassland degradation assessment and ecological management. This study investigated the effectiveness of integrating visible and multispectral imagery with staged feature selection for fine-scale grassland land-cover classification. Methods Four representative grassland land-cover classes, including Caragana microphylla, Artemisia scoparia, Agropyron cristatum, and bare land, were selected as classification categories. title: Evaporative Loss of Volatile Elements during Impact-Induced Melting: Evidence from the Sudbury Impact Structure
abstract: Abstract Large impact events generate extensive volumes of high-temperature silicate melt and are widely recognized as fundamental processes in the evolution of terrestrial planets. However, the extent to which impact-induced melting and volatilization can modify volatile element inventories remains poorly constrained. The Sudbury Impact Structure, Canada, preserves one of the largest and best-exposed differentiated impact melt sheets on Earth and provides an exceptional natural laboratory for investigating volatile element behaviour in impact-generated melts. abstract: Abstract This article investigates the world of the late Seleucid Empire on the eve of Roman control of the Eastern Mediterranean. It introduces additional actors in first-century Syria and uses the local archaeology of Syria and the Levantine coast, and the spread of Eastern Sigillata A wares in particular, to interrogate rising consumption and disposable wealth in the region. abstract: Migration is an intrinsic and historically significant aspect of human civilization, mirroring natural phenomena such as the movement of birds, the dispersal of seeds, and the flow of rivers across borders. While migration has long been a driving force behind cultural and economic development, it has become a contentious issue in the contemporary global landscape. Many nations perceive immigration as a threat to national identity, economic stability, and resource distribution. title: Documenting toilet graffiti as vernacular data: methodological and ethical considerations from a Finnish case
abstract: Purpose This study examines how toilet graffiti can be documented and organised as a researchable form of vernacular material for qualitative research. Rather than analysing the content of graffiti, the study focuses on the methodological and ethical conditions under which ephemeral and anonymous expressions found in public toilets can be rendered researchable. abstract: Abstract. Bedload transport dynamics during rapid increases of stage remain poorly constrained, particularly in ephemeral streams where such conditions are common. We combined two cutting-edge monitoring techniques – smartrocks and seismic measurements – to investigate bedload transport patterns during rapid increase of stage in two ephemeral channels with different morphologies. title: Digital Colonialism and the Reproduction of Hegemony in Africa: A Postcolonial Approach
abstract: This article presents a critical analysis of contemporary manifestations of digital colonialism in Africa, focusing on how global technology powers reproduce traditional patterns of domination through modern digital infrastructures and platforms. Drawing on a postcolonial analytical framework, the authors examine how data extraction, technological dependency, and regulatory asymmetries reinforce new forms of digital hegemony across the continent. title: A generalized lineage nomenclature for viral genomic epidemiology
abstract: Pathogen genomics has become increasingly integrated into outbreak response, with recent virus epidemics better characterized by large numbers of viral genetic sequences. Effective international communication of viral diversity requires a scalable, adaptable nomenclature, and existing systems may not accommodate rapid sequence generation. The Pango lineage nomenclature system was designed to address these problems and has been applied to SARS-CoV-2 since early 2020. abstract: La Antártica se ha consolidado como un espacio de relevancia estratégica creciente por la convergencia entre gobernanza internacional, presencia estatal, producción científica y cambio climático, factores que incrementan la incertidumbre y elevan el costo del error en la decisión pública. title: Rarefaction is better than robust Aitchison PCA and other compositional data analysis methods at controlling for uneven sequencing effort
abstract: Amplicon sequencing typically results in a wide distribution in the number of sequences obtained from each sample. How best to account for this variation has been a persistent problem in the microbial ecology literature. Historically, rarefaction has been used in ecology and this practice was adopted by microbial ecologists. However, rarefaction has been strongly criticized, leading to the development of compositional data analysis and normalization methods. title: Innovation for Climate Change Adaptation: A Meta‐Analysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Evidence on climate adaptation innovations remains fragmented, limiting evidence‐informed policy. This meta‐analysis of 418 studies (2010–2023), stratified by outcome and design with publication‐bias adjustment, synthesizes effectiveness, equity, and scalability. Hybrid approaches showed a 39% advantage over single‐domain innovations ( g = 1.24), although bias correction reduced this by 18%. Outcomes varied across domains. title: Integrating Socioscientific Issues into Cypriot Science Education: Preparing Students for a VUCA World
abstract: In a world of rapid technological advancements and global challenges, education must equip students with the skills to navigate complexity, uncertainty, and ethical dilemmas. This paper explores integrating socioscientific issues (SSIs) into the Cypriot primary science curriculum to foster critical thinking, ethical reasoning, and interdisciplinary learning. The paper analyses the curriculum’s theoretical foundations, goals, and con- tent and identifies existing strengths and areas to enhance, preparing students to en- gage with real-world scientific and societal challenges. title: Contract enforcement and foreign direct investment in Nigeria: A critical review of legal predictability and investor confidence
abstract: This paper critically examines the relationship between contract enforcement and foreign direct investment (FDI) in Nigeria, highlighting the legal, institutional, and economic factors that shape investor behaviour. Employing a structured review methodology, the study synthesises evidence from peer-reviewed literature, policy analyses, and legal scholarship to identify trends, challenges, and gaps in Nigeria’s commercial legal environment. title: Sharing the benefits and costs of conservation: public preferences for transboundary lynx policy
abstract: Transnational conservation is becoming ever-more important, yet reaching consensus on international conservation agreements remains challenging when decision-makers prioritise national benefits. Whether such approaches align with public preferences, however, remains unclear. We conduct a Discrete Choice Experiment to understand preferences for Iberian lynx conservation in Spain and Portugal, with a focus on the distribution of costs and benefits across countries. title: How the historical structure of local gazetteers conditioned modern science: Machinery in China, 1840–1949
abstract: Abstract This study asks why certain Western materials and practices came to be understood as modern science in China. By examining a corpus of Chinese local gazetteers ( difangzhi 地方志) representing roughly 52% of all collated titles within this genre, it argues that the gazetteer actively mediated an emerging technological reality between 1840 and 1949, thereby shaping a Chinese scientific modernity through material, geospatial and epistemic paths. title: Just transition: measuring efficacy and adaptation in Africa in the context of the Euro-African partnership for a sustainable energy transition
abstract: La transition des énergies fossiles vers les énergies durables et soutenables est devenue le but ultime de la communauté internationale afin de lutter contre les effets nocifs du réchauffement climatique. title: Divergent narratives: community perceptions of illegal bushmeat hunting dynamics in the Serengeti-Mara ecosystem
abstract: Conservation outreach programs (COPs) aim to reduce illegal bushmeat hunting by providing communities with tangible benefits and fostering positive attitudes toward wildlife, but their influence is difficult to separate from law enforcement and wider social change. We compared how COPs beneficiary and non-beneficiary communities perceived and explained illegal bushmeat hunting dynamics in the Serengeti-Mara ecosystem across 2018-2024. abstract: Background. Complementary feeding practices and timing are thought to significantly influence early life immune development, with the early introduction of allergenic foods being especially important for prevention of food allergy. We hypothesized that allergen-containing foods such as peanut, tree nuts and sesame may indirectly influence the immune system via their effects on gut microbiota composition and metabolism. Methods. abstract: Raw hyperspectral imaging (HSI) data require multiple processing steps before physically meaningful reflectance products can be derived. Quality issues at the radiance level – e.g., detector artifacts, low-signal regions, or excessive noise – can propagate through the processing chain and compromise subsequent analyses. HSI workflows typically focus on calibration and correction but often lack standardized integrity checks prior to atmospheric compensation. title: Network diagnosis and governance-coupled optimization in seaport–dry port multimodal transport corridors under the Maritime Silk Road
abstract: Research into seaport–dry port corridors has tended to focus on the design of the physical network on the one hand and the coordination of governance on the other. It is hard to maintain this separation in well-established Maritime Silk Road corridors. A corridor might have routes, inland nodes and digital platforms, and still not function smoothly at the rail/dry-port interface. This article therefore tackles corridor optimization as a problem of diagnosis and governance. title: Prediction of Potentially Suitable Areas of Hazelnut (Corylus avellana L.) in Romania Based on Bioclimatic Variables
abstract: The hazelnut (Corylus avellana L.) is widespread throughout Europe, except in the northeastern parts. Due to its exceptional nutritional profile and associated health benefits, it’s recognised as a premier nut crop, ranking fifth among nut crops, based on total harvested area. The objectives of this study were: to identify the bioclimatic variables that influence the distribution of hazelnut in Europe, to predict its current and future habitat suitability in Romania and to evaluate the range dynamics. abstract: This article theorizes a singular form of temporal and historical immanence—or poetic historicity—manifest in the Church of St. Dimitrios Loumbardiaris, designed by Dimitris Pikionis (1887–1968) as part of the landscape setting of the Acropolis and Philopappou Hill in Athens (1951–1957). title: Collateralization of the Body in the Central Sahara: On Forms and Effects
abstract: ABSTRACT This article tracks a transporter along the route linking Tripoli to the Saharan town of Ghadames in post‐2011 Libya, asking what secures an obligation when the institutions that normally underwrite it (offices, courts, recognized names) have receded. I distinguish the debt, the sum owed, from the security pledged to answer for it: what may be taken if the owing fails. abstract: This study appraised the governance structure in Nigeria petroleum industry, and as contained in the recent enacted PIA 2021 which is now the principal legal instrument as far as Nigeria’s petroleum industry is concerned. The challenges faced by regulators of the petroleum industry, being integral part of the system, are highlighted. It is observed that in seeking to proffer solution to tackle the problems facing Nigeria’s ailing petroleum industry the Norwegian model was resorted to. title: A major monastic centre? Rethinking Lismore’s place in the ecclesiastical landscapes of early medieval Britain
abstract: Until recent decades, the monastery of Lios Mòr (Lismore) in Argyll, Scotland, established by Saint Mo Luóc in the sixth century, was attested only via historical references and local traditions. Community-led investigations have now revealed an early medieval cemetery, sophisticated craftworking of international importance and early structures around the island’s parish church. title: Social context information and acoustic convergence in elephant vocal choruses
abstract: Abstract Elephants use low-frequency rumbles to communicate among individuals. Rumbles occur in several patterns: as discrete, non-overlapping calls, in antiphonal sequences where individuals alternate vocalizations, and in choruses where multiple individuals produce overlapping calls. Despite the wide availability of bioacoustics tools, most studies focus on non-overlapping signals rather than on choruses. abstract: Effective image analysis relies on robust feature extraction, a capability well-suited for Swin Transformer. title: Reservoir-computing-based chaos synchronization and its application to medical image encryption
abstract: Abstract Chaos synchronization provides a physically interpretable route for generating common dynamical states at spatially separated terminals, but most existing schemes require an accurate model and explicitly injected actuation. This paper develops a data-driven synchronization framework based on reservoir computing (RC) that learns nonlinear state couplings directly from observed trajectories. title: Sustainability and Willingness to Pay: A Review of Approaches in Urban Mobility and Climate Change Resilience
abstract: Willingness to pay (WTP) is widely used to inform sustainability-related policy and investment decisions, yet its application remains fragmented across research domains. In urban mobility, WTP is typically employed to value service quality improvements, technological adoption, and efficiency gains, while climate change resilience research primarily frames WTP around risk reduction, loss avoidance, and adaptation measures. title: Spatial prioritization of habitats and conceptual framework for impact assessment and mitigation planning for protected wetlands
abstract: Reconciling development and biodiversity conservation remains a critical challenge in contemporary conservation planning. Our study is based on a case study for the assessment of the Harike wetland, a Ramsar site and a Protected Area, a human-made reservoir, for understanding the impacts of proposed desilting operations and mitigation planning. A multi-taxa biodiversity assessment was undertaken to generate baseline ecological information for spatial prioritization, mitigation, and monitoring. title: A phosphoproteome atlas of human cell lines reveals the landscape of kinase activity
abstract: Protein phosphorylation orchestrates cellular signaling and controls most biological processes, with its dysregulation driving diseases, notably cancer. Comprehensive, high-throughput phosphoproteomics remains limited by detection sensitivity, data completeness and computational bottlenecks, especially in low-input settings. Here we present a comprehensive empirical human phosphoproteome resource, regrouping over 200,000 class I phosphosites across 33 diverse human cell lines. title: Spatiotemporal modelling of post-COVID recreation reveals persistent and emerging pressures on freshwater ecosystems
abstract: Restrictions during the COVID-19 pandemic pushed large numbers of recreationists towards freshwater ecosystems, but whether this shift was temporary or lasting has remained unclear. Using 129045 freshwater-related Wikiloc records (2016–2024), we modelled how recreation changed in time and space along the entire river network of the Catalan River Basin District (NE Spain), separating the pandemic effect from the platform's own growth. title: The evolution of Pakistan and China’s engagement with Afghanistan since 9/1
abstract: This study examines how Pakistan’s and China’s interests toward Afghanistan have evolved since 9/11 in pursuit of their security and political and economic objectives. Existing scholarship tends to treat Pakistan–Afghanistan and China–Afghanistan relations separately and rarely trace continuity and change across the whole post-9/11 period. abstract: Apple ripeness detection in complex orchard scenarios is plagued by fruit occlusion, overlapping, intense illumination interference, and subtle maturity feature differences among similar fruits. Conventional lightweight detection models also suffer from low accuracy and severe feature loss in field environments. title: Biodiversity conservation and its associations with economic performance, inequality, and peace
abstract: Abstract Biodiversity conservation is increasingly recognized as a product of coupled social–ecological systems shaped not only by ecological processes, but also by economic capacity, social inequality, and geopolitical stability. Here, we examined whether national conservation performance is systematically associated with economic prosperity, income inequality, peace, and the importance of natural resources in the national economy across 142 countries. abstract: To unify the decoupled dimensions of scientific rigor and contextual narrative in virtual heritage display, this paper uses the VR project developed for Jingdezhen’s bid for World Cultural Heritage as a case study, and establishes a workflow for the virtual recreation of urban heritage that includes data collection and processing, spatial script, virtual reconstruction, and asset production. title: Curating the Polycrisis: Affective Assemblages, the Interactive Synopticon, and Trans-Corporeal Narratives in the Anthropocene
abstract: Humanity currently navigates an era defined by the Anthropocene and the “polycrisis”—a complex, destabilizing web of interconnected ecological, social, and political emergencies. Concurrently, our primary mode of processing, debating, and governing these existential threats is mediated through the algorithmic infrastructure of digital platforms. title: Household and community drivers of Aedes aegypti infestation in tropical cities: Guiding community-led interventions
abstract: Disadvantaged communities characterised by poor sanitation conditions, overcrowding, and limited vector control are highly susceptible to Aedes aegypti proliferation and arboviral disease transmission. Effective mosquito vector control requires a detailed understanding of Ae. aegypti oviposition preferences and spatial distribution within such urban environments. title: Infrastructure and Inclusiveness in Election Administration: Insights from India’s General Elections
abstract: The Lok Sabha (Lower House of Parliament) elections of India, represent the world’s largest democratic exercise, requiring an extraordinary scale of logistics, manpower and infrastructural readiness. This paper analyses the operational magnitude of Lok Sabha elections by assessing candidates, electors, polling stations, mobility assets, observers, surveillance teams, home-voting facilities, etc. The findings suggest that India's electoral process is characterised by a strong emphasis on inclusiveness and involves substantial human and material resources and elector-friendly polling stations. abstract: Abstract Wastewater management (WWM) is vital for protecting human health and the environment, yet conventional centralized systems are resource-intensive and unsuited to growing urban pressure. Small and medium WWMs offer a potentially more sustainable alternative, but the lack of standardized life cycle assessment (LCA) approaches limits robust comparison and informed decision-making. abstract: The relationship between human beings and nature has been interpreted in various ways throughout history, and the meanings attributed to the natural environment have evolved in response to social, cultural, and economic transformations. title: BIOSECURITY IN THE INDO-PACIFIC: BIOLOGICAL RISKS, REGIONAL COOPERATION, AND STRATEGIC COMPETITION
abstract: The Indo-Pacific is a major centre of global population, trade, and strategic competition, but it also faces growing biological risks from disease outbreaks, animal diseases, laboratory accidents, and the deliberate misuse of biological agents. This study examines how biological risks interact with regional cooperation and strategic competition in the Indo-Pacific. It addresses the problem of uneven regional cooperation, particularly in sensitive areas such as laboratory oversight, information sharing, and biosecurity governance. abstract: Tahyna virus (TAHV) is a neglected mosquito-borne Orthobunyavirus pathogenic to humans. In Italy, TAHV was first recorded in Friuli Venezia-Giulia and then repeatedly in Emilia Romagna Region (Northern Italy). This study was set up to verify the presence of TAHV in Central Italy and to identify its potential vectors. abstract: Introduction: Klebsiella pneumoniae carbapenemase (KPC)-producing carbapenem-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa is a global health burden due to its multidrug resistance. However, the resistance characteristics, molecular epidemiology, and dissemination mechanisms of bla KPC-2 -producing carbapenem-resistant P. aeruginosa in China remain limited. title: Nepalese Calamity of 2026: Manmade or Climate Driven
abstract: The flash floods of August 26, 2026, along the Nepal-Tibet border are one of the most devastating Himalayan disasters since the 2015 earthquake. Some believe that the event was driven by anthropogenic activities. Others attribute it to climate change. To have greater clarity of the primary cause and to draw lessons for the future, this paper examines the catalysts behind the disaster. Although the primary geological event may have been rooted in climate change, the catastrophic scale of downstream destruction seems to have been greatly amplified by manmade vulnerabilities. abstract: Surface water governance depends not only on monitoring capacity but also on whether residents can access relevant information, navigate institutional responsibilities, and recognize opportunities to participate. This study examined these dimensions in Jalisco, Mexico, through a statewide, face-to-face household survey assessing exposure to and perceptions of surface water quality communication, information-seeking practices, awareness of inquiry and feedback mechanisms, and interest in public hearings and participatory monitoring, including perceived motivations and barriers. title: Access and Benefit Sharing in India: Reconciling Biodiversity Conservation, Sustainable Development and Community Rights
abstract: International environmental law has historically centered on the control and ownership of natural and biogenetic resources. Numerous environmental conventions have addressed this question, prioritizing benefit-sharing mechanisms. Among these, Access and Benefit-Sharing (ABS) emerged as a key solution, aiming to balance the interests of developed and developing nations while conserving biodiversity. title: Nature and interbeing: an ecocritical-postcolonial reading of Thich Nhat Hanh's poetry
abstract: Purpose The purpose of this research article is to explore nature and interbeing in the poetic works of Thich Nhat Hanh within the context of ecocritical-postcolonial theories. Design/methodology/approach This research article is designed to discuss two key dimensions: nature as a witness to war and colonization, and interbeing as ecology's resistance to colonial violence. title: Motif Migration and Visual Sovereignty: Chinese Export Porcelain and Early Modern Global Exchange
abstract: ABSTRACT This article examines Chinese export porcelain as a site of transcultural image production and proposes motif migration as an empirically grounded framework within global art history. Focusing on the Maritime Silk Road from the seventeenth to the nineteenth century, the study moves away from diffusionist and hybridity‐based explanations that frame decorative imagery as either copied or stylistically merged. title: Ancient Indian Knowledge Traditions and Modern Scientific Thought: A Critical Review of Hindu Philosophical and Scientific Texts
abstract: Ancient Indian philosophical literature, including the Vedas, Upanishads, Bhagavad Gita, Mahabharata, Ramayana, and classical scientific treatises such as the Vaisheshika Sutra, Sushruta Samhita, Charaka Samhita, and Aryabhatiya, contains numerous discussions concerning cosmology, mathematics, medicine, astronomy, causality, and the nature of matter. title: Genomic tracking of Campylobacter jejuni along poultry and pig value chains in Northeast India: Implications for food safety
abstract: Campylobacter jejuni is the predominant causative agent of human campylobacteriosis. A total of 864 samples (poultry cloacal swabs, chicken intestine, chicken meat, pig rectal swab, pig intestine, pork) were screened for the presence of C. jejuni using standard methods. abstract: Abstract Indirect competition is a fundamental mechanism shaping the structure of biological systems, from food webs to antimicrobial resistance (AMR) networks. Translating directed interaction data into a quantitative measure of competition remains a modelling challenge. This paper develops a spectral framework that maps directed bipartite networks into symmetric, positive semidefinite (PSD) competition matrices via the shared-target principle (C=AA⊤). title: Remote estimation of plastic distribution in California agriculture using Sentinel-2 imagery: a case study
abstract: Global application of agricultural plastic mulch is increasing. While these films offer benefits for crop production, they also are a large source of plastic waste and pollution in both terrestrial and aquatic systems. The current scale of global mulch application and its deleterious impacts are unclear. Current estimates of agricultural plastic use remain limited by field-specific growing patterns and data limitations. title: Dual‐Timescale–Based Cache and Bandwidth Control Scheme in Integrated Satellite‐Terrestrial Networks
abstract: ABSTRACT Recently, the integrated satellite‐terrestrial network (ISTN) system offers a promising solution for extending wireless communication services to remote and underserved areas. To effectively provide a variety of services, it is essential to cache the corresponding services on satellites while dynamically allocating the satellite bandwidth. However, challenges arise due to dynamic ISTN service requests that vary over time and space, as well as limited cache and bandwidth resource capacities on satellites. title: An interaction perspective on situation awareness in human-AI teaming: A scoping review
abstract: Situation awareness (SA) is crucial for effective teaming and is becoming increasingly relevant in human-AI teaming as AI systems take on more active roles. AI systems rely on designed interactions to communicate information and coordinate with humans, which may influence how human teammates perceive, interpret, and anticipate task situations. title: Sustainable Risk Management of the Porang Supply Chain as an Agro-Industrial Commodity in Madiun Regency
abstract: Porang is a key agro-industrial commodity in Madiun Regency, Indonesia. Its supply chain currently faces numerous challenges, particularly in terms of risk management and sustainability issues. Various risks continue to affect the stability and performance of supply chains, posing a threat to their long-term viability. Additionally, stakeholder involvement remains fragmented, with limited collaboration across supply chain networks in the industry. This study aimed to identify and analyze supply chain risks and develop relevant risk mitigation strategies from the perspective of sustainability.

title: Joint routing and clustered medium access control scheduling for energy-aware internet of things data dissemination
abstract: Efficient data dissemination in large-scale internet of things (IoT) networks remain challenging due to energy constraints, congestion, and delay under dynamic network traffic. This paper introduces a joint routing and medium access control (MAC)-layer scheduling framework (JRSM), incorporating priority-aware clustering to enhance energy efficiency and reduce latency in the IoT data acquisition layer. abstract: Background: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a leading cause of preventable vision loss, yet retinal screening remains suboptimal in low-resource settings. This study assessed DR-related knowledge, risk perception, screening practices, and barriers among adults with diabetes attending selected healthcare facilities across multiple Syrian regions. abstract: BusyBox is widely reused in Linux-based Internet-of-Things (IoT) firmware, but stripped symbols, heterogeneous instruction sets, uncertain component versions, and selective patch backports make N-day vulnerability localization difficult. We propose EvoPatch-IoT, an evolution-aware retrieval framework whose novelty lies not in another standalone encoder, but in coupling target-local geometric localization, architecture-normalized anonymous multi-view evidence, and a version-causal historical prototype memory for reference-guided retrieval. abstract: Documentation related to software system development may become outdated with respect to the actual implementation, making it more difficult to understand and maintain business processes. In this study, a JavaScript framework was developed based on a transactional model used as the source for generating structured HTML documentation. abstract: Amid rising global demand for sustainable energy, agricultural and forestry residues (AFRs) emerge as a key yet underutilized resource in energy transition. Mechanisms of how optimizing multipath AFR utilization advances sustainability contributions in varied socioeconomic contexts remain underexplored. title: Prioritizing climate-resilient housing recovery in conflict-affected Yemen: a district-level MCDA and uncertainty framework
abstract: Abstract Yemen’s housing recovery requires choices among districts where flood exposure, conflict, displacement and humanitarian need overlap. This study develops a district-level multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA) framework to identify districts that remain high priorities for early climate-resilient housing recovery under alternative assumptions. abstract: Objective This study investigates the spatiotemporal variation of iodine concentrations in drinking water and soil across Gansu Province, aiming to generate observational evidence for adjusting iodine deficiency disorder (IDD) prevention strategies, given inherent methodological limitations of historical unpaired cross-sectional surveys. title: Joint species distribution modelling for restoration of American chestnut ( Castanea dentata ) in the United States under current and future climate conditions
abstract: Abstract American chestnut ( Castanea dentata ) was once a dominant tree species spanning the eastern temperate forests of the United States until the introduction of chestnut blight in the early twentieth century resulted in its functional extinction. Recent advances in the development of blight‐resistant American chestnut could support widespread restoration, but optimal locations for restoration plantings remain uncertain. title: The prince and the scientists
abstract: Scientific institutions pose a peculiar leadership challenge: their ultimate purpose, scientific discovery, cannot be commanded or predicted. I argue that scientific leadership is less about exercising authority than about cultivating the trust, diversity, interactions and intellectual freedom from which scientific excellence can emerge.

title: Reframing antimicrobial resistance as a land-system challenge through environmental pathways and climate interactions
abstract: Abstract Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a planetary health challenge, yet land-system change remains overlooked. This review examines how agriculture, urbanisation, waste management, deforestation, aquaculture and climate-driven transitions shape resistance through altered input intensity, habitat reorganisation and enhanced connectivity. abstract: Photoaging is a major contributor to premature skin aging and results from the cumulative effects of ultraviolet (UV) radiation on cutaneous structures. title: A Human Rights Analysis of the Legal Framework Governing Communication Surveillance and the Right to Privacy in Tanzania
abstract: The increasing adoption of digital communication technologies has enhanced States' ability to monitor communications for national security, crime prevention, and law enforcement. While such surveillance may serve legitimate public interests, it poses significant privacy risks if surveillance powers are broadly defined or poorly regulated. This article critically analyses Tanzania's legal framework for communication surveillance, evaluating whether it adequately protects the right to privacy. abstract: The availability of communication signals for dense wireless local area networks (WLANs) is being increasingly hindered by spectrum contention, interference, and traffic dynamics. Institutional capacity, technological capability, and regime characteristics help account for this variation, but they do not fully explain why similar interventions generated different trajectories as implementation unfolded. title: Spatiotemporal patterns of antimicrobial resistance in shared human-animal waterpoints in the Maasai Mara Ecosystem, Kenya
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) presents an existential One Health threat. The spread of AMR in arid and semi-arid landscapes is modulated by ecological interactions and exacerbated by endemicity of livestock diseases and poor sanitation in shared human-animal systems leading to misuse of antibiotics. This study characterized the prevalence, resistance patterns, and spatiotemporal variations of AMR in surface water sources in the Maasai Mara Ecosystem (MME), a rapidly changing water-stressed socio-ecological landscape. title: Distinct prosocial behaviors associated with persistent symptom trajectories in psychiatric disorders
abstract: Prosocial behavior, the tendency to act for others' benefit, is essential for mental health. Although social contexts strongly shape prosocial behavior in healthy individuals, its relevance across psychiatric disorders remains unclear. We examined whether context-dependent prosocial behaviors were associated with baseline psychiatric symptoms and longitudinal symptom trajectories. abstract: The North American bumble bee Bombus affinis (B. affinis) is an important wild pollinator that has experienced severe population declines since the late 20th century. While the volume of literary evidence regarding radiation safety continues to expand, study focuses and methodological approaches remains diverse. abstract: Abstract The nut of the Baru tree ( Dipteryx alata Vogel), native to Brazil’s Cerrado, has gained attention for its strong nutritional profile and growing market potential. At the same time, the Cerrado faces increasing deforestation driven by agricultural expansion. In this context, Baru is considered a promising sustainable land-use option within forest-based bioeconomy strategies. This article studies the use of digitization undertaken from afar to preserve heritage that is under fire. Based on the example of the old city of Aleppo, it explores the possibility of imagining a decolonized digital archive for preserving Aleppine built heritage, and of the broader Global South. title: Engineered Artificial Minerals (EnAM) Approach for Chromium Recovery and Stabilization in Steelmaking Slag
abstract: Steelmaking slag represents one of the largest industrial by-products, with estimated annual generation exceeding 500 million tons worldwide. These slag materials contain valuable alloying elements such as chromium, nickel, and vanadium that remain in the slag. Chromium, in particular, has a dual role: it is essential for corrosion resistance of steels but creates environmental and resource recovery challenges when transferred into the slag. title: Assessment of Impact of Cement Industry on Surface and Ground Water Quality
abstract: This study aims to assess the impact of the cement industry on surface and groundwater quality. The research focuses on a specific cement plant location Athwajan Srinagar J&K and evaluates the physico-chemical parameters of water samples collected from various points around the plant. Parameters such as pH, temperature, turbidity, dissolved oxygen, total dissolved solids, hardness, calcium, alkalinity, sulphate, nitrate, fluoride, chloride, and iron are analyzed to determine the extent of pollution. abstract: Abstract. abstract: Designing bioinspired functionally graded metamaterials with tailored energy absorption ( EA ) and energy dissipation ( ED ) capacities through spatially regulating structural topology and local relative density distribution without increasing the overall material volume, remains a significant challenge. abstract: Abstract Distributed Earth Observation (EO) workflows require cluster configurations that balance competing objectives (execution time, computational cost, energy consumption, and resource-use efficiency), yet practitioners typically provision resources using fixed heuristics that ignore most of these dimensions. This paper presents an outcome-as-a-service framework for Dask-based EO processing that jointly optimises all four objectives. abstract: Abstract Two actinobacterial strains, DSM 43699 T and JZT32 T , isolated from water and soil samples collected in Germany and Tunisia, respectively, were investigated using comprehensive polyphasic taxonomic studies. title: The model alga Chlamydomonas reinhardtii forms mutualistic interactions with Verticillium fungi
abstract: Abstract Algal–fungal interactions are widespread in natural environments and contribute to key ecological processes such as primary production, nutrient cycling, and soil formation. Yet, molecular mechanisms underlying these associations remain poorly understood due to the complexity of natural systems and the lack of experimentally tractable models. title: Dynamic Perspective of the Evolution of the Environmental Kuznets Curve in Ecuador and Mexico
abstract: The Environmental Kuznets Curve (EKC) posits that environmental degradation increases during the early stages of economic development and decreases once a certain income level is reached. Ecuador and Mexico illustrate contrasting patterns within this framework: the former relies heavily on natural resources, while the latter has a more diversified economy, albeit with persistent environmental challenges. title: A new delta-headed branchiosaurid temnospondyl from the early Permian Meisenheim Formation of Germany
abstract: Two temnospondyl specimens from the Ruthweiler deposit (M8) in the early Permian Meisenheim Formation of the Saar-Nahe Basin are identified as pertaining to a new branchiosaurid taxon, Schoenfelderpeton brevifrons . They are distinct from all other temnospondyls in the region by the delta-shaped skull, small orbits, and short frontals. The maxilla fails to contact the cheek and has tiny, pin-shaped teeth, a feature that persists in the mature specimen. title: Fine Brown Carbon Aerosol Emitted by Wood Pyrolysis - New Harmful Tracers and Cytotoxicity in Human Lung Cells
abstract: Abstract Biomass burning (BB) is a major global source of light-absorbing organic aerosols, the so-called atmospheric brown carbon (BrC), which negatively affects human health. However, the interplay between the molecular composition and toxicity of BB emissions remains ambiguous. In this study, cytotoxicity analyses and molecular-level characterization of fine BrC generated by wood pyrolysis at 350 °C, representative of smoldering combustion during vegetation fires, were performed. abstract: BACKGROUND: Planetary health is an increasingly important transdisciplinary approach in nursing because it links human health and equity to the integrity of Earth's natural systems. title: Censorship or Accident? Distinguishing Natural and Intentional Geometric Errors on Cold War City Plans Published in the Eastern Bloc
abstract: During the Cold War, maps published in Eastern Bloc countries were subject to strict censorship. From the 1960s, Warsaw Pact states were required to geometrically distort maps intended for public use, although methods varied by country. Some inaccuracies, however, may have resulted from technological limitations or restricted access to reliable source materials. abstract: Biodiversity credits (BCs) are one innovative financing scheme that the Global Biodiversity Framework proposes to mobilise private capital and narrow the biodiversity financing gap. abstract: Abstract: Multidrug-resistant enterococci, particularly vancomycin-resistant enterococci (VRE), represent an important clinical challenge because of their antimicrobial resistance, intestinal persistence, and potential for transmission and infection. abstract: Abstract Bird-window collisions are a major threat to wild birds. Collision monitoring programs that train volunteers to collect standardized data on bird-window collisions are an important tool for advancing the understanding of collisions, evaluating mitigation effectiveness, and promoting bird-safe actions and policies. abstract: Introduction: This paper explores the sustainable lifestyle practices of tribal communities in Andhra Pradesh, focusing on their deep-rooted connection with nature. The history of human evolution is a story of adaptation, survival and transformation, and while some early groups chose permanent settlements, tribes continued a mobile existence deeply connected to the natural world. title: Highly pathogenic avian influenza as a systemic risk - implications for control and preparedness
abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) has evolved from episodic outbreaks into a globally entrenched, multi-host panzootic, with recurrent spillover into mammals. The expanding host range and increasing wildlife–livestock interfaces challenge traditional control strategies, increase opportunities for viral adaptation, and thereby elevate zoonotic risk. We therefore propose that HPAI should be reframed as a long-term systemic risk requiring resilience-based governance, and strengthened One Health control and preparedness.

abstract: Abstract Localizing the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) is critical for achieving global sustainability, yet translating international commitments into actionable local policies remains challenging, not least because interdependent goals require coherent implementation. This article examines how external pressure, local capacity, and local demand condition coherent SDG localization at the level of discourse, norms, and institutions. abstract: The increasing proliferation of the Internet of Things (IoT), wireless sensor networks (WSN), wearable electronics, and smart sensing platforms have intensified the demand for sustainable and maintenance-free power sources. abstract: This study presents a comprehensive national-scale assessment of biomethane potential from organic waste streams in Qatar, evaluating its impact on two strategic climate mitigation pathways: (1) sustainable energy in water supply and agriculture, and (2) potential natural-gas substitution in Qatar’s gas-to-liquids (GTL) industry. abstract: Abstract Ice crystal microphysical properties govern cirrus cloud radiative effects, yet their representation in climate models remains inadequate due to insufficient understanding of how thermodynamic histories control crystal morphology. abstract: This article mobilises generation as a lens for theorising and examining the contingent and permuting character of settler colonial formations, with a specific focus on Gaza. Generation, we argue, calls attention to settler colonial rule as situated and embodied, and temporalities of survival and resistance as layered and heterogenous. abstract: ABSTRACT This paper presents a sliding variable‐based optimal control (SVBOC) framework for canonical nonlinear systems with unknown control direction. abstract: This research was conducted in response to the increasingly urgent need for digital transformation in port services in Eastern Indonesia to improve efficiency, transparency, and service quality amid the development of information technology. abstract: Introduction The World Health Organization (WHO) Pandemic Agreement, adopted in May 2025, represents a major step toward strengthening global pandemic governance after COVID-19. abstract: ABSTRACT This teaching case study is designed for students in introductory managerial accounting classes and integrates the fictional events of the movie Jaws with real‐world financial data from Martha's Vineyard Island and the fishing industry. The case study reinforces key concepts of cost–volume–profit analysis, special‐order decisions, and managerial decision‐making in conditions of uncertainty. abstract: Background Feedlot nutrition is formulated to maximize growth rate and feed efficiency for high-quality meat production; however, high-grain diets can disrupt rumen function and cause digestive disorders, the inclusion of non-nutritive feed additives helps counter these effects, thereby enhancing growth performance and overall feed efficiency. abstract: How do the legacies of colonisation, cultures of exploitation and marginalisation undermine the needs of historically marginalised populations across geographies? abstract: This study presents the design, fabrication, and preliminary experimental evaluation of a locally manufactured vest-type Personal Flotation Device (PFD) for adults weighing 75–80 kg under controlled calm-water conditions. abstract: This article analyses the implementation of innovation policies in Alicante (Spain) between 1982 and 2024, exploring public-private collaboration in the Digital District of the Valencian Community (DDCV) and its predecessors: the Innovation Triangle and Ciudad de la Luz. Drawing on qualitative methods and primary business sources, it reconstructs the historical trajectory of these initiatives and assesses the impact of political cycles on their continuity. abstract: Uintatheres, mammals belonging to the extinct order Dinocerata, are among the most recognizable of all Paleogene (~66-23 Ma) organisms. Unmistakable for their bizarre skulls with multiple pairs of horns and saber-like upper canines, uintatheres have captivated paleontologists since the late nineteenth century. abstract: Introduction: 2025 is likely to be a critical year for environmentally friendly products as environmental issues keep attracting worldwide interest. Customers are more dedicated than ever to lower their carbon footprints, which forces companies to create new ideas and use sustainable methods. Driven by technology advancements, shifting customer preferences, and regulatory systems meant to lower carbon emissions and waste, the environmentally friendly product industry is predicted to see explosive expansion by 2025. abstract: The introduction of metaverse technology is transforming the way tourists feel, judge, and experience destinations before they visit them. abstract: Urban Woody Vegetation Cover (UWVC) near schools shapes the thermal and psychological conditions of students' daily environments, yet canopy cover surrounding schools remains poorly documented. abstract: Abstract Urban resilience is a critical challenge amidst escalating risks of climate change, rapid urbanization, and systemic disruption, particularly in the Global South. This research seeks to fill a gap in the literature that often overlooks the institutional and relational mechanisms that generate adaptive capacity. title: Catchment hydrologic function is widely time-variant
abstract: Abstract Catchment hydrologic function describes how meteorological conditions are transformed into streamflow. Whether this transformation is stable or varies from event to event, and what controls that variability, remains unknown at the global scale, limiting confidence in flood-risk and water-security assessments. Here, we analyze about 1.7 million runoff-producing events across 4838 catchments on six continents. abstract: Cotton cultivation is an important source of livelihood for farmers in Western Odisha; however, cotton farmers in Kalahandi and Balangir districts face several socio- economic and marketing constraints that influence their choice of marketing strategies. This study examines the socio-economic factors affecting cotton farmers’ marketing decisions, compares marketing practices across the two districts, and identifies major challenges affecting market efficiency and price realisation. abstract: The ODD (Overview, Design Concepts, Details) protocol began in 2006 as a standard for describing agent-based ecological models and is now widely used in many disciplines. abstract: Objective: This study aimed to identify and explain the individual, family, and social factors contributing to psychological empowerment among women in Hungary. abstract: Accurate Land Use/Land Cover (LULC) classification is important for efficient natural resource management and for understanding how weather conditions modify the environment. title: Ecological responses of soil bacteria to rapid and slow temperature fluctuations
abstract: Fluctuating temperatures profoundly affect microorganisms' coexistence, biogeographic distributions and responses to future climate change. abstract: Abstract Intellectual property (IP) is frequently approached through its codified forms and formal institutions, with less attention to the deeper social foundations from which protection of intangible creations arose. This study considers an earlier layer of such protection, termed primal IP rights, formed among communities that safeguarded creative works through custom, oral tradition, and social regard before the advent of codified law. abstract: Abstract Microbial decomposition of complex soil organic matter (OM) is often regulated by labile organic carbon inputs, a phenomenon known as priming, which plays a critical role in belowground biogeochemical cycling. abstract: ABSTRACT This paper advances Systems Modeling for Just and Sustainable Futures (SMJSF) as a conceptual framework for ethical and epistemic socio‐ecological modeling in field‐based science education. abstract: Agritourism is increasingly positioned as a practical route to encourage more responsible environmental behaviour by bringing tourists into direct contact with farms, local landscapes, and everyday sustainability practices. abstract: Centella asiatica (L.) abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to judge how well an advertisement matches a query, but the fairness of these judgments has received limited attention. title: Understanding the Hierarchical Structure and Functional Landscape of the Model Context Protocol Ecosystem
abstract: AI agents increasingly rely on tools exposed through the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to complete user tasks. Hundreds of thousands of MCP servers are listed across marketplaces, yet they are organized only by coarse, marketplace-specific server categories. This makes it difficult for agents and users to identify tools for a given operation, find functional alternatives, and assess how those alternatives differ. title: Incremental Open-Ended Deep Research with Structured Harness
abstract: Existing Open-Ended Deep Research (OEDR) systems primarily generate reports from scratch, making them inefficient for scenarios where research reports need to be continuously maintained as new information emerges. We introduce \textbf{Incremental Open-Ended Deep Research (Incremental-OEDR)}, a research setting that treats a report as an evolving research state and incrementally updates it by preserving valid knowledge, revising outdated or incomplete content, and incorporating newly available information. abstract: Quantum annealers can sample degenerate optima unevenly, so the composition of finite-read output matters when multiple solutions are sought. title: Distributed Model-Free Turbine Repositioning for Wake Overlap Minimization in Floating Offshore Wind Farms
abstract: This paper presents a model-free method for turbine repositioning control in floating offshore wind farms. The method uses a distributed online optimization framework to mitigate the wake effect. Conventional approaches rely on centralized, model-based control architectures, which suffer from poor practical feasibility. To overcome this limitation and address nonconvexity and inaccessible gradient information, we incorporate physics-informed knowledge of wake dynamics into the control system design. title: Looking at radiative corrections to the $Σ^\pm\toΛe^\pm \barν$ semileptonic decay-rate ratio
abstract: We investigate the impact of radiative corrections on the ratio of the semileptonic decay rates $Σ^\pm\toΛe^\pm \barν$. Phenomenological analyses point to sizable radiative effects on the experimentally measured ratio. From a theoretical perspective, this observable is particularly appealing because several hadronic and electroweak contributions partially cancel in the ratio, providing a cleaner probe of electromagnetic effects. title: Debug2Fix: Can Interactive Debugging Help Coding Agents Fix More Bugs?
abstract: While significant progress has been made in automating various aspects of software development through coding agents, there is still significant room for improvement in their bug fixing capabilities. Debugging and investigation of runtime behavior remains largely a manual, developer-driven process. Popular coding agents typically rely on either static analysis of the code or iterative test-fix cycles, which is akin to trial and error debugging. title: Beyond the Transcriptome: Chromatin-Informed Prediction of Cell-State-Dependent Perturbation Responses
abstract: Predicting transcriptional responses to genetic perturbations is central to understanding gene function. Existing predictors primarily rely on transcriptomic measurements, although chromatin accessibility provides complementary information about the cellular context in which perturbations act. Using this information requires linking chromatin context to specific perturbations and accounting for baseline differences between independently sampled control and perturbed populations. title: TEIDAN: A Multilingual Multiparty Dialogue Corpus
abstract: Multi-party interaction is a central setting for human communication and a necessary target for human-agent interaction systems that must participate in group conversation. Yet available corpora often focus on meetings, task-oriented interaction, text-based interaction, or acted scenarios, and fewer resources support cross-linguistic comparison of spontaneous face-to-face triadic discussion. This paper presents TEIDAN, a multilingual multimodal corpus that currently consists of Japanese and English three-party conversations. title: A Gate-Based Quantum Computing Framework for Codon Optimization
abstract: Codon optimization is a challenging combinatorial optimization problem with important applications in synthetic biology, protein expression, and biotechnology. While quantum annealing has previously been explored for this problem, the application of gate-based quantum algorithms remains largely unexplored. In this work, we present a gate-based quantum computing framework for codon optimization by formulating the optimization objective as an Ising Hamiltonian and expressing it in terms of Pauli operators suitable for gate-based quantum processors. abstract: We present a theory of fluid flow in long axisymmetric channels induced by salt concentration and pressure drops between their ends. The consideration is restricted to electrostatic diffuse layers that are thin compared to the local radius, but remains valid even when the concentration drop is quite large. title: Hybrid Unmanned Underwater Vehicles: A Review of Architectures, Enabling Technologies, and Engineering Trade-Offs
abstract: Hybrid underwater robotic vehicles integrate features typically found in separate classes of vehicles: autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs), remotely operated vehicles (ROVs), amphibious robots, and cross-medium robotic vehicles. We review this field from a system-level perspective and identify four types of hybridization: (i) control-mode hybridization (hybrid AUV/ROV, autonomous and remotely operated vehicle (ARV/HROV)), (ii) amphibious mobility (water–land), (iii) cross-medium mobility (water–air), and (iv) propulsion-mode hybridization. title: A safety-consistent hybrid global–local path planning framework for AUVs in bathymetry-constrained 3D marine environments
abstract: Autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) operating in marine environments must navigate rugged bathymetry, ocean-current disturbances, sudden obstacles, and limited perception. These conditions require long-range route guidance and short-range reactive avoidance, but inconsistencies can arise when planning stages use different clearance definitions, final supervision modifies local commands, or abrupt switching produces directional discontinuities. title: Optimisation-based motion control for AUVs under non-linear wave-current disturbances
abstract: With the increasing exploitation of marine resources, autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) are being applied more extensively in a variety of tasks, such as maritime search, rescue, and marine archaeology. The attitude stability of AUVs can be significantly disturbed by highly non-linear waves and currents near the sea surface, yet the influence of wave non-linearity on AUV motion and the associated control strategies remains insufficiently studied. title: Modular dual-critic reinforcement learning control for AUV path tracking and collision avoidance
abstract: Autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) operating in complex and uncertain ocean environments require reliable path-tracking and obstacle-avoidance capabilities to maintain safety in the presence of currents and obstacles. Traditional end-to-end deep reinforcement learning (DRL) methods often struggle with coupled navigation objectives, which can lead to oscillatory control and unreliable trajectory recovery. title: Method for generating program control signals for the positioning of a vessel supporting auv operations
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of ensuring stable hydroacoustic communication between an autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV) and support vessel or unmanned surface vessel (USV) supporting its operation during the AUV’s underwater missions in open sea conditions using an ultra-short baseline hydroacoustic communication and navigation system. title: Adaptive curriculum learning-based path planning and data collection for autonomous underwater vehicles under extreme sea conditions
abstract: Path planning and data collection for Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs) under extreme sea conditions face severe environmental disturbances and high task complexity, leading to low training efficiency and divergence in traditional reinforcement learning. To address the limitations of existing fixed curriculum learning (CL) methods—namely manual stage presetting, tedious hyperparameter tuning, and restricted generalization—this paper proposes an adaptive CL framework tailored for partial differential equation (PDE)-coupled ocean environments. title: Launch and recovery systems for autonomous underwater vehicles on unmanned boats
abstract: The article examines the design and operating principle Launch and Recovery Systems (LARS) for autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) based on unmanned boats (UBs) of various purposes. Some of the patented technical solutions of the IPMT FEB RAS in this field are described. The results of experimental studies of the operational characteristics of the LARS for a small-sized AUV based on the UB are presented.

title: Effect of wave-induced motion on the energy harvesting performance of a floating solar-powered AUV
abstract: This paper proposes a novel concept of a solar-powered autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV) featuring a foldable solar wing panel. The design enables energy harvesting during surface floating operations. We investigate the time-varying energy harvesting characteristics due to the combined effects of wave-induced motion and submergence depth. title: Customized Design of Power Electronics for Deep-Sea Energy and Industrial Applications: Environmental Adaptation, Technical Bottlenecks, and Development Pathways
abstract: This narrative review examines the design of power electronics for deep-sea energy and industrial systems, where converter performance is constrained by electrical demands and prolonged exposure to pressure, seawater, temperature cycling, and limited maintenance access. Targeted, non-systematic literature searches covering studies available through September 2026 were used to connect offshore renewable generation and hydrogen production, sub-sea distribution and motor drives, and autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV) power and charging. title: Low-cost single-beam SONAR localization in AUVs: Systematic experiments with acoustic and optical perception
abstract: This work presents a low-cost acoustic sensing framework for underwater localization and perception using single-beam sonars (SBS) and a forward-looking sonar (FLS). A Kalman filter (KF) based sensor fusion approach is developed to integrate SBS measurements with inertial sensing, incorporating pre-filtering and confidence-based gating to mitigate acoustic outliers and reflective disturbances. title: Quantifying Deep Ocean Methane Along the Central Chilean Margin
abstract: Abstract Cold seeps are dynamic seafloor environments that provide conduits for methane (CH 4 ) to be transferred from marine sediments to the global ocean and, in shallow settings, the atmosphere. These seeps are ubiquitous along continental margins yet their spatial extent and impact on the marine carbon cycle are poorly constrained. During a research expedition to the underexplored Chilean Margin, we utilized an ROV‐mounted in situ CH 4 sensor and multibeam sonar to map seep fields. title: Optimized underwater tracking method pipeline based on stereo images
abstract: The problem of automatic tracking of an underwater pipeline (UP) from stereo images using an autonomous uninhabited underwater vehicle (AUV) is considered. It is noted that traditional methods of boundary recognition on vectorized images are often ineffective in an underwater environment due to poor image quality, partial immersion of the pipeline in the ground, and high computational complexity. title: Paleochannels Facilitate Large‐Scale Submarine Groundwater Discharge on the Southwestern East China Sea Shelf
abstract: Abstract In addition to surface runoff, coastal seas receive water and nutrients via subsurface pathways, including submarine groundwater discharge (SGD) at the meter‐to‐kilometer scale and porewater exchange (PEX) at the centimeter scale. Partitioning SGD and PEX fluxes is important for understanding their biogeochemical impacts, particularly on continental margins. abstract: Computer vision in underwater environments faces significant challenges due to severe visual degradation caused by light absorption and scattering. These optical phenomena hinder semantic segmentation and depth estimation, which are critical for Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs) to perceive their surroundings, identify obstacles such as reefs, and execute safe motion planning. title: Drag-reduction mechanisms in autonomous underwater vehicle formations: Physical analysis and physics-guided surrogate optimization
abstract: The hydrodynamic interaction between closely spaced autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) in formation produces strongly nonlinear drag responses. In the present configuration space, two dominant pressure-related mechanisms are identified: stern pressure recovery at the leader and bow low-pressure immersion at the follower. abstract: Subsea pipeline monitoring must deliver urgent alarms quickly while moving much larger inspection records over constrained underwater links. This creates a deployment choice: send all data through a prioritized acoustic network, or collect routine records with an autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV) undertaking a finite collection mission. title: SA-SRDC-Loc: Single-AUV-assisted three-dimensional underwater localization via selective residual distance learning and depth-constrained robust optimization
abstract: Accurate three-dimensional localization in underwater acoustic sensor networks remains challenging because irregular acoustic propagation and multi-hop connectivity weaken the relationship between network topology and physical distance. This paper proposes SA-SRDC-Loc, a single-AUV-assisted localization framework that treats successive AUV reports as temporally ordered observations of one continuously moving platform rather than as independent anchors. title: Nonlinear hydrodynamic coupling effects of free-surface and bottom boundaries on an AUV
abstract: Autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) frequently operate in shallow waters, where they are simultaneously subjected to the coupling effects of free-surface wave-making and bottom boundary restrictions. Existing studies have primarily focused on single-boundary conditions, leaving the complex, non-linear coupled hydrodynamics in dual-boundary shallow water environments insufficiently understood. abstract: Abstract Surface riblets have emerged as a highly efficient passive drag-reduction strategy for enhancing the endurance of autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs). Nevertheless, current research less frequently deploys riblets in the complex aft-body region of underwater vehicles. To address this gap, we propose a drag-reduction scheme utilizing streamwise rectangular riblets distributed along the tail contraction section of the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency submarine (DARPA SUBOFF) bare-hull model. abstract: The paper proposes a cost-effective solution for simultaneously determining the coordinates for a group of inexpensive autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs). The presented method for providing navigation support for a group of AUVs is based on the use of a short-baseline acoustic navigation system (SB ANS). title: Measurement-Interval Dynamically Iterated Kalman Filtering for Tightly Coupled INS/USBL Navigation of AUVs Under Large Initial Errors
abstract: Reliable navigation is fundamental to the operation of autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) in exploration, environmental monitoring, and so on. Tightly coupled inertial navigation system/ultra-short baseline (INS/USBL) integration provides continuous and drift-constrained navigation for AUVs. abstract: This paper addresses the station-keeping control problem of remotely operated vehicles (ROVs) under near-surface head-sea conditions, where narrow-band wave disturbances induce significant periodic motion. Instead of treating wave effects as unstructured lumped disturbances, a frequency-adaptive disturbance rejection framework is proposed by combining EKF-based frequency estimation, harmonic extended state observation, and prescribed-performance fast super-twisting sliding mode control. abstract: To fulfill the requirements for rapid development of high-performance AUV motion control systems, a three-dimensional (3D) path- following control system is designed and implemented based on the MOOS-IvP/ArduSub architecture. Using Lyapunov stability theory, an adaptive line-of-sight (ALOS) guidance law with variable look-ahead distances (VΔ-ALOS) is designed. title: Underwater Platform for Long-Term Observation Using a Cable-Restricted Underwater Vehicle and Its Design Concept for Trajectory Planning
abstract: Long-term and repeated observation of shallow seafloor environments is required to evaluate temporal changes in seagrass meadows and other coastal ecosystems. In this study, we propose a cable-restricted observation system consisting of an underwater vehicle, a tether cable, and a seafloor station equipped with a reel. abstract: Reliable short-horizon trajectory prediction for autonomous underwater vehicles is difficult during Doppler velocity log (DVL) outages because the latest valid navigation state becomes stale relative to the current vehicle state. This paper presents a lag-compensated kinematic integration network (LC-KIN) that treats this staleness as a prediction-boundary displacement. title: Design and Open-Water Validation of an Autonomous Underwater Robot for Physical Diver Safety Assistance
abstract: Diving accidents remain frequently fatal, and most stem from preventable human factors: panic, failed buoyancy control, and disorientation. Underwater human–robot interaction research has focused on observing the diver and offers little help when a diver must be pulled to safety. This paper presents the design and sea validation of NADIA, an autonomous underwater robot that combines diver guidance and following with diver-commanded physical assistance. title: Adaptive reference management and model predictive control for near-surface depth–heading control of autonomous underwater vehicles
abstract: Near-surface operations conducted by underwater vehicles (UVs) feature strong nonlinear disturbances and speed-dependent control effectiveness, which make depth and heading regulation challenging under strict state and actuator limits. abstract: How oceanic architecture defines its scope in relation to waterfront regeneration, marine habitation and climate adaptation is the central question of this interview. title: A review of the development, research progress and key challenges in underwater bionic soft robotics
abstract: Conventional rigid underwater robots possess high structural stiffness and exhibit a single mode of locomotion, showing poor adaptability in complex flow fields, narrow spaces and eco-friendly underwater operations. abstract: Reptadeonella Busk, 1884, is one of the most common bryozoan genera reported from warm waters across all oceans and is currently represented by 29 species. title: Maternal Intertextuality, Diasporic Identity, and Narrative Hybridity in Amit Chaudhuri’s Odysseus Abroad
abstract: Amit Chaudhuri’s Odysseus Abroad is a subtle expedition of identity, belonging, and meaning in the globalised era. The novel’s explorative narrative structure interweaves genres, blending themes of diasporic experience, cultural hybridity, and existential introspection. Through its non-linear narrative, stream-of-consciousness narration, and intertextuality with Homer’s Odyssey, Chaudhuri both reinstates essentialist notions of identity and celebrates its temporal, conditional nature. title: Exploring Spitsbergen’s Potential for Sustainable Development and Geopark Creation
abstract: There is growing evidence of environmental degradation in the Arctic, reflected in rising temperatures, ice melt, and more frequent extreme weather events. In this context, tourism development in Spitsbergen must be balanced with nature conservation. This study aims to examine experiences of tourism and opinions on sustainable activities, as well as to explore the potential for establishing a geopark on Svalbard. title: Global length–weight relationships of deep‐pelagic fishes: Coverage, biases and variability
abstract: Length-weight relationships (LWRs) are morphometric tools that allow body mass to be estimated from fish length, providing input for fisheries, ecological and biodiversity studies. For deep-pelagic fishes, however, LWR data remain fragmented and unavailable for most species. Here, we present a global synthesis of LWRs for deep-pelagic fishes, consolidating available data into a single harmonised dataset and mapping taxonomic and geographic gaps. abstract: The installation and recovery process of Christmas tree is complex and technically difficult, and it bears high internal and external loads during production and has extremely high requirements for operation reliability. This study compares Euripides’ Iphigenia at Aulis and Idegu's The Legendary Inikpi to examine how sacrificial womanhood is constructed and used to sustain social order within two distinct cultural logics. abstract: Background: The global and Indonesian maritime sector requires accounting systems capable of addressing distinctive transaction characteristics, operational risks, and sustainability demands. Maritime accounting refers to accounting practices adapted to shipping, port, marine, and fisheries industries. However, its conceptual boundaries and scope remain insufficiently defined in the literature. title: PRESERVING REGIONAL HISTORY THROUGH CULTURAL TOURISM: A CASE STUDY OF THE SAVITSKY MUSEUM AND ITS GLOBAL AUDIENCE
abstract: This paper examines the pivotal role of cultural tourism in safeguarding regional history and ethnic identity, focusing on the I.V. Savitsky State Museum of Arts in Nukus, Uzbekistan. Known globally as the "Louvre of the Desert," the museum holds a unique dual repository consisting of the world's second-largest collection of Soviet avant-garde art and an extensive archive of traditional Karakalpak applied arts alongside ancient Khorezm archaeological antiquities. abstract: We report 100 individuals of the Longfin Batfish, Platax teira (Forsskål, 1775), from the Mexican Pacific. abstract: This practice-based paper examines how embodied, queer and neurodivergent modes of perception shape the interpretation of photographic archives. Focusing on Latent: A Hidden History, a project developed through the South East Archive of Seaside Photography (SEAS), it explores how mid-twentieth-century seaside photographs, produced under the social and legal constraints of male homosexuality, can be reengaged through sustained acts of photographic looking. title: Conservation Messages as Catalysts of Post-Visit Action: Insights from Zoo and Aquarium Visitors
abstract: Zoos and aquariums face an urgent challenge to convey conservation messages that motivate visitors to change their environmental behavior. This study explores the reflections of 768 visitors to one of twelve zoos and aquariums in Australia, USA, and Canada regarding the features of conservation messaging that prompted their post-visit involvement in specific environmental behaviors. Thematic analysis uncovered eight features of conservation messaging that visitors felt prompted them to adopt new behaviors or increase their engagement in existing environmental actions. title: Upper Palaeolithic mariners? Evaluating experimental evidence for intentional early seafaring
abstract: Brought to popular consciousness by Thor Heyerdahl in the 1940s, the role of seafaring in human migration has been intensely debated. Aiming to stimulate discussion around the ways in which experimental archaeology is used to support such grand narratives, the authors of this debate critically assess a recent claim for Upper Palaeolithic seafaring in the Japanese archipelago. Here, they argue that creating a boat for which there is no archaeological evidence with generic tools that were not widely available in the region risks a confounding circularity of logic.

Hyperbaric medicine in Latin America did not emerge from a single institution or a single pioneering individual. title: Acoustic emission monitoring of infrastructure using distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) techniques - possibilities, limitations, and optimization
abstract: Acoustic emission (AE) testing is an established method for structural health monitoring and damage detection in engineering structures. Conventional AE systems are based on piezoelectric sensors that are applied at discrete locations, requiring extensive cabling and offering limited spatial coverage. Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) provides an alternative approach as a fiber-optic measurement technique, in which a single optical fiber cable serves as a continuous, spatially distributed sensor. title: Impacts of the 2026 US-Iran War on Environmental Security in the Middle East
abstract: Modern warfare does not merely inflict human casualties; it also degrades the environmental systems vital for daily life. The 2026 US-Iran conflict poses a severe threat to regional ecosystems, as belligerents deliberately target critical infrastructure and weaponize natural resources to secure military advantages or compel concessions. title: A New Record of Dirivultus spinigulatus (Copepoda: Dirivultidae) from Japan Associated with a Siboglinid Tubeworm
abstract: The siphonostomatoid copepod Dirivultus spinigulatus Humes, 1999 (Dirivultidae) was originally described as an associate of the siboglinid tubeworm Paraescarpia echinospica Southward, Schulze, and Tunnicliffe, 2002 from the Edison Seamount hydrothermal vent in Papua New Guinea. abstract: Recently the phylogeny of the order Neogastropoda based on exon-capture [Fedosov et al., 2026], has confirmed the monophyly of the group and achieved high resolution for many deep nodes. Thorough examination of the sequenced species frequently revealed novel and distinctive morphological characters, and in several cases highlighted unresolved taxonomic issues. title: On the edge: habitat patchiness and island isolation fracture the distribution of the endemic Kimberley rock-rat
abstract: We integrate demography, morphology and genetics to assess the biology and population structure of the endemic Kimberley rock-rat (Zyzomys woodwardi), a habitat specialist of the monsoonal tropics. The species is confined to the extreme north-west of the continent and 16 adjacent islands that were part of the mainland during the last Pleistocene glaciation. abstract: This study aims to analyze the determinants of ship safety in Indonesia by integrating three key constructs: crew competence, port digitalization, and ship technology innovation. abstract: Abstract The nature of mantle sections exhumed at magma‐poor rifted margins remains poorly constrained, largely because direct sampling of mantle in modern passive margins is exceptionally rare. abstract: Abstract Closed‐circuit rebreather (CCR) and helium‐based breathing mixtures are widely used in technical diving. This study compared the effects of Heliox and Trimix on pulmonary function and decompression stress during CCR dives.
