abstract: Abstract Design optimization of floating wind turbine (FWT) substructures remains computationally demanding due to the extensive time-domain simulations required to explore high-dimensional design spaces. This study builds upon the previously developed Pywind-based integrated design optimization (IDO) framework, extending it by comparing two sampling strategies: Latin Hypercube Sampling (LHS) and Maximin LHS. abstract: This paper investigates the role of science-tourism practices in shaping tourists’ perceptions and ethical positioning within Antarctic deep-field tourism. Drawing on ethnographic fieldwork in East Antarctica and semi-structured interviews, the study examines how operators’ support for science influences tourists’ pre-trip decision-making, perceptions of legitimacy, and environmental responsibility. abstract: The taxonomy of heteropolar, tapering, and unbranched heterocytous cyanobacteria has undergone significant changes over time. abstract: This study focuses on developing a stabilization system suitable for the actual operating conditions of a water hyacinth shredding machine on inland rivers and canals, with the aim of maintaining roll stability throughout operation. abstract: Food safety remains an absolute cornerstone of global public health and socioeconomic stability. abstract: Multiagent settings are naturally characterized by coevolutionary dynamics, where agents must adapt and learn in the context of their teammates. A key challenge in such domains is determining how to credit an agent for its individual contribution to team performance. Fitness shaping approaches partially address this by identifying and isolating an agent's direct contribution to team success. abstract: Born in Halifax, UK, in 1839, and shipwrecked on Madagascar as a youth, Alfred Crossley had returned to the island by 1869 and in the ensuing eight years made hugely important collections of mammals, birds, butterflies, and other natural history specimens. Many of these are now in major museums in the UK and Europe (including numerous holotypes), but unknown quantities went to private collectors and are now lost. title: Spatial variation in aquatic arthropod biodiversity in floating photovoltaic host waterbodies
abstract: Abstract Floating photovoltaic (FPV) solar energy is a rapidly expanding renewable energy technology in which photovoltaic panels are deployed on floating structures atop waterbodies. While FPVs may alleviate pressure on terrestrial biodiversity, relatively little is known about aquatic biodiversity within FPV host waterbodies. title: A Love Made of Stones: Contemporary Anishinaabe Lyric and Asiniig Sovereignty
abstract: This article delves into the literary motif of the stone (asiniig) in contemporary Anishinaabe poetry as an ontological assertion of Indigenous sovereignty. title: Regulatory Intermediation and Energy Transition Readiness at the Port of Keelung, Taiwan
abstract: International maritime environmental regulation is changing port sustainability from a predominantly local environmental-management task into a cross-organisational challenge involving vessels, energy systems, terminal operations, logistics customers, public authorities, and port-city communities. This article examines how the International Maritime Organization’s greenhouse-gas framework and the European Union’s FuelEU Maritime regime transmit strategic pressure to the non-EU Port of Keelung in Taiwan. abstract: A tengeralattjárók fejlődése a haditechnika egyik legizgalmasabb és legdinamikusabb területe, amely a kezdeti, egyszerű víz alatti járművektől a modern, nukleáris meghajtású, nagy hatótávolságú tengeralattjárókig terjed. This review explores Rift Valley fever virus (RVFV), Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus (CCHFV), and hantaviruses (HTVs) within the framework of One Health, emphasizing the ecological and epidemiological factors that govern their emergence and transmission. title: Archipelagic memories at Lau King Howe Hospital Memorial Museum
abstract: Colonial pasts, geopolitical differences, and plural social constructions of Malaya/post-independence Malaysia contributed to and were reflected in hospital design. Sarawak in East Malaysia, on Borneo Island, saw developments that paralleled those in Singapore and Kuala Lumpur. title: Analysing user-generated overtourism posts on social media: a content analysis
abstract: Overtourism is an increasing concern for destinations seeking to accommodate visitor growth while protecting residents’ quality of life and long-term sustainability. Yet, how overtourism is represented through user-generated social media content remains underexplored. Drawing on destination image theory, this study analyses 600 Instagram posts tagged #overtourism to examine the visual themes, attraction types, sentiment, and thematic framing associated with overtourism. abstract: This article examines how China expands security influence in the Persian Gulf without alliances, bases, or direct intervention. It introduces indirect military engagement to explain influence through technology diffusion, defence-industrial cooperation, intermediary partnerships, and partner adaptation. abstract: Swedish botanist Kåre Bremer (b.1948) reshaped modern botany across three interconnected domains: the systematics of Compositae, the theory and practice of cladistics, and the phylogenetic classification of flowering plants. abstract: The Rime of the Ancient Mariner by Samuel Taylor Coleridge explores themes of sin, guilt, retribution, and salvation. According to the research, the Mariner’s killing of the Albatross violates the sacred bond among humans, nature, and the divine and is a moral transgression. The study examines how Coleridge portrays punishment as a psychological and spiritual process rather than a consequence, drawing on the poem’s symbolism, supernatural imagery, and religious themes. title: Etymologies of Australian reptiles
abstract: Australia, covering almost 7.7 million km2 (3 million mi2), is a mega-biodiverse region with 19 recognised families, 164 genera, six subgenera, 1152 species, and 60 subspecies of reptiles. This study resolves the etymologies of their scientific names (nomina). Most generic and subgeneric names (69%) are derived from Greek, while half (50%) of species and subspecies originate from Latin. Greek-derived names are more often composites than Latin-derived ones. abstract: Libya, one of the largest countries in North Africa, is characterized by a Mediterranean climate along its northern coast and an extensive hot desert climate across much of its territory. abstract: Travel serves as a doorway to other worlds and a tool for self-discovery, allowing travellers to transcend preconceptions and gain a more profound comprehension of individuals and locations. This paper explores how firsthand interactions with foreign cultures, environments, and social realities alter perception. title: Further revisions to the catalogue of skeletal material from megatooth sharks, with a response to Sternes et al. (2024)
abstract: One specimen of Otodus auriculatus and three specimens of O. megalodon are added to the catalogue of skeletal material from megatooth sharks. Criticisms of the Lamnoidea hypothesis and reconstruction of Cretalamna sp. by Sternes et al. (2024) are responded to. abstract: Abstract This article examines the global networks underpinning colonial forestry in the Dutch East Indies in the interwar period. In the aftermath of the First World War, a renewed surge towards the internationalisation of the forest sciences served to open up imperial knowledge systems to a wider pool of outside expertise. abstract: Battery thermal management systems (BTMS) on electric vehicles are crucial for efficiently managing battery temperature. The development of BTMS has been a crucial part of the commercialization of electric vehicles. The efficiency of the BTMS has become a bottleneck to increasing the battery's charging and discharging rates. title: When heritage becomes a burden: an evidence-based reference class of tourism stress in historic cities
abstract: Overtourism and carrying-capacity models have traditionally explained heritage-city stress through visitor volume and density. However, these approaches provide limited explanation of why comparable tourism pressures produce different forms and levels of stress across historic cities. This study addresses this gap by examining heritage stress as a perception-driven, context-dependent process shaped by interactions among spatial, social, infrastructural, cultural, and governance conditions. abstract: Fungal diversity is an important component in maintaining ecosystem balance, especially in campus environments that have a variety of habitats such as soil, litter, and vegetation. abstract: This study aims to analyze less familiar Orthodox sites in Blagoevgrad District of Southwestern Bulgaria, defined here as “sacred places in a shadow” as a factor for religious tourism development, specifically through community-led charitable activities for their renovation. Observations and visual data serve as the starting point of the analysis. abstract: Wheat (Triticum spp.) is a staple food for approximately 35% of the world’s population and is cultivated in 102 countries, covering 32% of global arable land. Disease agents are among the factors that decrease wheat yield and quality. Embryo and root infections caused especially by soil-borne pathogens reduce yield by negatively affecting plant growth and tillering. Pythium species are polyphagous pathogens that cause root rot and damping-off diseases on various plants. abstract: Climate change is not a distant risk but an everyday lived experience. This article examines climate change in Catalonia, Spain by focusing on daily routines, relationships, and emotions. In doing so, it moves beyond predominantly abstract, technical, and quantitative approaches to the climate crisis by foregrounding everyday experiences through three mutually constitutive dimensions: embodiment, intersectionality, and situatedness. abstract: Agricultural lands in East Kazakhstan region cover a significant area, with large portions of pasture and cropland situated in close proximity to operating industrial facilities. abstract: Para comprender las capacidades fluctuantes de la imagen en movimiento, quienes trabajan e investigan en animación deben ser conscientes de las consecuencias que conlleva el continuo histórico desde la animación predigital hasta la animación digital actual. abstract: La personalización del aprendizaje mediante tecnologías digitales ha demostrado ser una estrategia efectiva para mejorar la enseñanza de la historia, específicamente en el estudio de Cristóbal Colón. Este artículo analiza cómo las herramientas digitales personalizadas impactan en la comprensión histórica, la motivación estudiantil y los desafíos de implementación. title: From Difficult Heritage to Difficult Temporality: The Political Life of History in Cities With Scarce Heritage
abstract: This article examines the challenges in self-narration faced by cities with short, sparse, and monotonous histories. Moving beyond the concept of “difficult heritage,” which focuses on problematic historical content (e.g., legacies of forced labor), the authors introduce “difficult temporality” to describe a structural scarcity of historical events. abstract: Despite advances in resident–tourism discourse and overtourism research, it remains unclear how place-based emotions and perceptions of injustice become collectively articulated and connected to resistance. Drawing on emotional geography and the right to the city, this study challenges the assumption that resistance is a direct response to tourism pressures. abstract: The article considers the application of the concept of linguistic worldview in translation education at the university level from the perspectives of both the teacher and the students. Special attention is paid to those dimensions of translation that linguistic worldview can help elucidate, and thus help to formulate a strategic approach that balances creativity with awareness of the cultural specificity of the source material. abstract: Is limited or battlefield nuclear employment re-emerging as a usable instrument of statecraft? This article takes the four-day India–Pakistan confrontation of May 2025 as its empirical anchor for that question. The study is a theory-guided interpretive single-case analysis that draws on official statements and briefings issued by both governments, post-crisis reconstructions by research institutions, and contemporaneous reporting, read against the established scholarly literature on deterrence thresholds. title: Guadua londonoae (Poaceae, Bambusoideae), a new bamboo species from the Amazon Basin with remarkably large foliage leaf auricles
abstract: Summary A new species of Guadua (Poaceae, Bambusoideae) from the Amazon Basin is described and illustrated. Guadua londonoae is easily distinguished from other species in the genus by a unique combination of primarily vegetative morphological characters. The most prominent diagnostic feature is the size of the auricles on the foliage leaves, which are on average four times longer than the maximum length previously recorded for any Guadua species. abstract: This research article presents a comparative analysis of economic development efforts in four West Michigan communities: Grand Haven, Holland, Hudsonville, and Zeeland. These cities have developed economic development plans specifically targeting the revitalization of their downtowns and commercial districts. This paper discusses the history of each community, assesses their current economic development efforts, and frames them within a greater discussion of scholarship on economic development strategies in small and rural U.S. communities. abstract: The study explores the impact of technology on the preservation and promotion of cultural heritage in Southwest Nigeria. This study used a mixed-methods approach, incorporating qualitative and quantitative methods to gather comprehensive data. abstract: Dystopian fiction usually warns us about the future, but its most critical force often lies in what it erases from the past. Patricia McManus identifies a “hollow space” in dystopian narrative where history is suppressed, yet critical scholarship frequently treats this absence as a mere structural device. abstract: Introduction This article examines relations between the Ulus of Jochi and the Grand Duchy of Lithuania in 1380–1395 in their military-political, diplomatic, and legal-fiscal dimensions. abstract: Redefining Liminality in the Reading of Icelandic Sagas. This article introduces a revised and expanded definition of the concept of liminality, with the purpose of utilising it as a methodological tool in the study of the corpus of medieval Icelandic sagas. The paper proposes an alternative interpretation of liminality, distinct from that established in foundational works such as those of Arnold van Gennep and Victor Turner. abstract: The purpose of this study is to analyze how the Cyprus issue was addressed in the European Commission’s Regular Reports on Turkey published between 1998 and 2025, the thematic shifts it underwent, and its impact on Turkey-EU relations. title: The Pillars of Faith: A Guide to the 28 Fundamental Seventh-day Adventist Beliefs
abstract: The Seventh-day Adventist Church, a Christian denomination with a global presence, articulates its theology through a formal statement of 28 Fundamental Beliefs. This article, titled "The Pillars of Faith: A Look at the 28 Fundamental Beliefs of Adventists," seeks to demystify these doctrines by presenting them not as a rigid checklist, but as a cohesive and interconnected story. abstract: Charles Hose (1863–1929) is widely recognised for his contributions to ethnography, natural history and colonial administration in Sarawak during the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries. title: The scientific consensus on the beauty of snowflakes: A case study for the aesthetics of science
abstract: Philosophers of science interested in aesthetics have tended to privilege the epistemic and cognitive dimensions of science. Historians of science interested in aesthetics have largely focused on the aesthetics of scientific images and artefacts. Productive exchanges between these traditions of scholarship have been few and far between. abstract: Abstract Settlement, the transition of a swimming planktonic larva to a benthic juvenile, is a key process during the development of many marine invertebrates. title: The timescale of forming Earth’s earliest water ocean in the Hadean Eon

Using a heat-budget model for the early atmosphere-ocean system, this study quantifies the transition from the final solidification of the magma ocean to the establishment of a stable hydrosphere. The results demonstrate that once the mantle transitioned to solid-state convection, a thick primordial steam atmosphere can radiatively cool and condense into a global water ocean within 10,000 years. abstract: Shallow nearshore habitats can serve as nursery areas for coastal elasmobranchs but are increasingly exposed to coastal development. title: Going against the grain: return mobilities and rural transformation in coastal Bangladesh
abstract: Return mobilities are often conceptualised as an economic necessity or a failed migration outcome. However, in climate-vulnerable regions such as coastal Bangladesh, return mobilities emerge as an active process of adaptation shaped by intersecting socio-economic, political and environmental dynamics. This study explores return mobilities in two coastal villages in Bangladesh, examining how water politics, translocal ties and livelihood opportunities shape reintegration. abstract: ABSTRACT Hydroclimate in Portugal is influenced by the North Atlantic subtropical high‐pressure system (the Azores High) and by internal climate modes, most prominently the North Atlantic Oscillation, which may shift in position and/or intensity due to anthropogenic climate change. abstract: Abstract Dam regulation of tropical monsoonal rivers enhances seasonal contrasts in the tidal river zone (TRZ) hydrology, altering the delivery of dissolved silicon (DSi) to the coastal ocean. title: Assessment of Beach Plastic Waste Pollution Using the Clean Coast Index: Evidence from Thanh Hoa Province, Viet Nam
abstract: Marine plastic pollution is an increasingly important environmental and socio-economic challenge for coastal provinces of Viet Nam, where tourism, fisheries, river discharge and coastal urbanization interact to shape the accumulation of beach litter. This study assesses the status, composition and seasonal variation of beach plastic waste in Thanh Hoa Province using a field-survey approach adapted from UNEP and NOAA guidance and the Clean Coast Index (CCI). abstract: Abstract Body size is a integrative trait that has declined across ecological assemblages in the last decades. The Concept of the Maritime, or How to Decolonize the Uncolonizable with Hegel and Coleridge
abstract: This essay interrogates the maritime as a concept and principle of colonization in Hegel’s philosophy of history and seeks to interrupt this imperializing logic with an alternative conception of the maritime from Coleridge’s The Rime of the Ancient Mariner . Examining the sea as history in Hegel and as archive in Coleridge, I argue that, for the latter, the maritime is no mere object of conquest, but throws the human back upon herself and discloses an unexplored psychic landscape. abstract: Latvian urban space has been formed over many centuries due to human activity. title: Setting the course for American manatee conservation in Brazil: Quantifying and mapping vulnerability to anthropogenic threats
abstract: Manatees are charismatic, wide-ranging megaherbivores increasingly threatened with extinction across much of their distribution. Although many studies have documented threats to manatee populations, no standardized framework has been applied to quantify their vulnerability, leaving available knowledge scattered and lacking a comprehensive assessment of impact magnitude and spatial scale. Here we aimed to quantify and map vulnerability of the American manatee to anthropogenic threats in Brazil. title: A long-term trend toward wetter conditions during MIS 2 inferred from modern-monitoring-based stalagmite multi-proxy records from Remi Cave, Central China
abstract: The ongoing debate regarding the spatial pattern of precipitation and effective moisture changes in monsoonal eastern China during the Marine Isotope Stage 2 (MIS 2) centers on the hydroclimatic evolution of the middle and lower Yangtze River Valley. Here, we present an approximately four-year (December 2020 to December 2024) systematic modern monitoring program and multi-proxy records (δ 18 O, δ 13 C, Mg/Ca, Sr/Ca, Ba/Ca) from stalagmite RM4 in Remi cave, Hunan Province, Central China, spanning ∼25.7‒14.5 kyr BP. title: Preventing Invasive Non‐Native Species: A Horizon Scanning for the Canary Islands
abstract: ABSTRACT Aim Oceanic islands host exceptional biodiversity and endemism but are highly vulnerable to biological invasions. We aimed to identify non‐native species with high potential to invade the Canary Islands within the next decade and to prioritise them based on their environmental and socioeconomic risks. Location The Canary Islands, Macaronesia, northeastern Atlantic Ocean. Methods We applied a structured horizon scanning protocol with a global scope. title: Invested objects: found childhood, materiality and the migrant child in Valería Luiselli’s Lost Children Archive (2019) and Ali Smith’s Spring (2019)
abstract: In a laboratory in San Marcos, Texas, is a box containing a small stuffed lion and a luchadore’s mask. The laboratory is associated with Operation Identification, an initiative working to identify the remains of migrants found on the Texas-Mexico border. Many of the bodies are those of children. It is not only corporeal remains which are recovered. The soft toy and child’s mask are among a range of personal effects collected at sites along the border. title: Revisión Semisistemática del VaR (Valor en riesgo) en la Cadena de Suministro
abstract: Risk management is key for companies, and the combination of finance and logistics is essential to support risk-related decisions made by supply chain managers. One financial tool that can be used for this purpose is Value at Risk (VaR). Therefore, the objective is to conduct a semi-systematic literature review with a qualitative approach to VaR in supply chain risk management, using Rayyan software and two databases: the UNAM Repositories and Redalyc. title: Provenance of the Middle‐Upper Triassic Songpan‐Ganzi Flysch of Western China Revealed by Anisotropy of Magnetic Susceptibility Measurements: Implications for the Tectonic‐Paleogeographic Evolution of the Paleo‐Tethys Ocean
abstract: Abstract The Triassic Songpan‐Ganzi turbidite complex (SGC) on the eastern Tibetan plateau is one of the largest flysch turbiditic complexes on Earth. However, the provenance of its extremely thick turbidites is hotly debated. We conducted the measurement of anisotropy of magnetic susceptibility (AMS) of Triassic turbidites from nine profiles in Ruo'ergai, Aba, Ganzi, Seda, and Xiaojin counties in the Songpan‐Ganzi Basin. title: PERANCANGAN SISTEM PEMBANGKIT TENAGA LISTRIK HYBRID PLTS DAN PLTB UNTUK VILLA DAN PETERNAKAN DI PESISIR PANTAI PARANGTRITIS BERBASIS HOMER ENERGY
abstract: The coastal area of Parangtritis Beach, Bantul Regency, Special Region of Yogyakarta, is experiencing growth in tourism facilities and livestock farming that demands a reliable electricity supply, while the reliability of the distribution network in coastal areas remains limited. This study aims to design a hybrid PV–wind power generation system to serve the combined load of a villa and a horse farm through simulation and optimisation using HOMER Energy software. title: From Waste to Health: A Qualitative Case Study of the Punggawa Nusantara Social Innovation Program for Community-Based Tuberculosis Control in Jakarta’s Urban Coastal Settlements
abstract: Tuberculosis (TB) remains one of the major public health challenges in Indonesia, particularly in densely populated urban coastal settlements where environmental degradation, poor sanitation, and socioeconomic vulnerability intersect. This study examines Punggawa Nusantara, a social innovation program implemented by PT PLN Nusantara Power Generation Unit (UP) Muara Karang in Pluit Subdistrict, Penjaringan District, North Jakarta, which positions TB control as a cross-sectoral issue connecting health, the environment, and the local economy. title: Source-to-sink controls on the environmental fate of short-chain chlorinated paraffins: a review
abstract: Short-chain chlorinated paraffins (SCCPs) are persistent, bioaccumulative industrial chemicals whose environmental fate remains poorly constrained. This review synthesizes published occurrence data and process-level understanding across air, water, soil, and sediment matrices to construct a hierarchical source-to-sink framework that links congener-specific partitioning properties to observed mobility, retention, and transformation patterns. title: Palestine in Foreign Travelogues: A Spatial and Social Reading from Sacred Geography to Everyday Life (1839–1864)
abstract: Seven foreign travel accounts published between 1839 and 1864 are examined comparatively to reveal how Ottoman Palestine was represented through sacred geography, mobility, and everyday life. While Jerusalem remains the principal focus, the study also considers Jaffa, Ramle, Bethlehem, Hebron, the Jordan River, the Dead Sea, Nablus, and Mount Gerizim within the same spatial framework. title: Anatomy of foredunes progradation: successive phases of erosion and recovery related to storm scarping and post-event reconstruction (Normandy, France)
abstract: This study provides a detailed stratigraphic characterization of the successive stages within the erosion–accretion cycle of a beach–foredune system. We combine high-resolution ground-penetrating radar (GPR) data with targeted trenching across multiple field sites on the western coast of Cotentin (Normandy, France) to reconstruct the internal architecture and depositional history of foredunes in relation to known storm-induced erosion and recovery events. title: Patterns of Indian Migration and Early Settlement in Kakamega Municipality, Kenya, 1901-1920
abstract: While existing scholarship extensively documents the dominance of Indian migrants in coastal and urban hubs of Kenya, the localised rural role of the diaspora in Western Kenya remains critically underexplored. Consequently, this study addresses the unresolved historical paradox in Kakamega. The study traces the history of migration and early settlement of Indians in Kakamega Municipality, Kenya, between 1901 and 1920. title: Research on Embedded Hypervisor Technology Selection: Requirements Analysis and Capability Comparison for Extreme Environment Application Scenarios
abstract: As embedded devices grow more complex, running multiple operating systems on a single device—and deploying virtualization beyond data centers into embedded systems—has become standard. This paper focuses on the hypervisor Virtual Machine Monitor and examines its selection challenges in extreme environments: disaster rescue, space exploration, deep-sea and polar operations, and security confrontations. title: Diatom–lipid–copepod nexus under threat by global change
abstract: The central role of lipids in the ecology of high-latitude and temperate seas is under threat by global change. This hinges on the tight ecological links between diatoms and copepods of the genus Calanus and similar (e.g. Neocalanus, Calanoides) that produce and accumulate energy-rich lipids. Strongly coupled through seasonal water-column stability, nutrient supply, spring-bloom succession, and overwintering life strategies, this nexus is foundational to the highly productive food webs of these regions. title: Geochemistry and detrital zircon geochronology of the Bagong Formation clastic rocks in the Queerchaka area, central part of the Qiangtang Basin: evidence for the Late Triassic chemical weathering and tectonic evolution
abstract: Late Triassic was not only a key episode for the evolution of the Qiangtang Basin but also a critical interval marking the final closure of the Paleo-Tethys Ocean on the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau. However, the nature of the Late Triassic Qiangtang Basin and its response to the evolution of the Paleo-Tethys Ocean remain unclear. Here, elemental geochemistry and detrital zircon U–Pb dating data of clastic rocks from the Upper Triassic Bagong Formation in the Queerchaka area (central part of the Qiangtang Basin) were integrated to infer the chemical weathering history, provenance, and tectonic evolut

title: Community Structure of Chitons (Polyplacophora) in Open and Sheltered Intertidal Habitats on The Boulder Beach of Magarizaki, Tomioka Peninsula, Amakusa, Japan
abstract: The intertidal zone of the boulder Magarizaki beach in Amakusa, Japan, is a dynamic coastal ecosystem that serves as a critical habitat for chitons (Polyplacophora) as grazers and ecological indicators. This study aims to identify chiton species and determine their community structure in exposed and sheltered intertidal habitats. The study was conducted in August–September 2025 using quadrat sampling and purposive sampling techniques at two locations. title: Underthrusting linked to closure of the Rocas Verdes Basin: insights from Turonian/Coniacian satellite plutons, Isla Capitán Aracena, southern Patagonia, Chile
abstract: The Petite and Mercurio satellite plutons of the Patagonian Batholith intrude folded marine sedimentary successions and ophiolitic sequences within the Magallanes fold-and-thrust belt on Isla Capitán Aracena (~54° S), south of the Cenozoic transcurrent Magallanes-Fagnano Fault System. Their petrogenesis and tectonic significance were investigated through an integrated approach combining field observations, U-Pb zircon geochronology, whole-rock geochemistry, mineral chemistry and thermobarometry. title: Cosmogenic 10 Be as a Tracer for Recent Heliospheric Encounters With Interstellar Cold Clouds and Nearby Supernovae
abstract: Abstract Recent works suggest there are periods when the Sun encountered massive interstellar cold clouds which compressed the heliosphere to within Earth's orbit, exposing Earth to interstellar galactic cosmic rays and energetic particles of heliospheric origin. We model 10 Be production in Earth's atmosphere during possible interstellar cloud encounters and supernovae. We find that, if the heliosphere is compressed to 0.2 AU ( AU), the 10 Be production rate is elevated above the background. title: Benthic foraminiferal turnover and the paleoenvironmental evolution of the Maikop Basin: From agglutinated to calcareous dominance (Kerch Peninsula, late Oligocene–Middle Miocene)
abstract: Based on the revision of archival data by M.F. Kozyreva (1947–1949) and their modern reinterpretation, the paleoecological evolution of the Maikop Basin on the Kerch Peninsula sector during the Late Kerleutian–Tarkhanian (late Oligocene–Middle Miocene) was reconstructed using benthic foraminifera. title: BaSIC: A Bayesian Inversion Model for Basalt Source Investigation and Characterization
abstract: Abstract We present BaSIC: Basalt Source Investigation and Characterization, an open‐source Python based Bayesian inversion method to constrain the source mineralogy of basalts. Using bulk rock geochemistry, the model takes the averages and standard deviations of six elemental ratios (Mn/Fe, Zn/Fe, Mn/Zn, Sc/Zn, Co/Fe, and Ga/Sc) for a given basalt suite and inverts for the most likely source mineral assemblage and melt fraction. title: Against the View From Nowhere: Situated Drawing as an Ethics of Attention on the North Coast of Northern Ireland
abstract: This article explores situated drawing as a method of attending to place, memory, and embodied knowledge through an artist-researcher practice developed along the north coast of Northern Ireland. Working through walking, observational drawing, annotation, photography and animation, it treats drawing not as a secondary record of place but as a way of thinking with it, asking what becomes visible when drawing is understood as a cartography of practice: not a neutral map viewed from above, but a relational tracing produced through movement, pause, encounter, affect and the layered social historie

title: Life Cycle Assessment of Reinforced Concrete Structures using Pozzolanic Materials
abstract: Abstract Sustainability goals and stricter environmental protection requirements now guide a wide range of experts, from material scientists to architects, to find practical ways to incorporate byproducts and waste materials into concrete construction. The urgent focus on climate change has led researchers to investigate materials, such as polymers and pozzolans, as additives, offering ecological solutions to reduce heavy cement use and lower carbon emissions from concrete structures. title: Comparison of Bacterial and Potentially Pathogenic Bacterial Communities in Ballast Water from Different Source Waters
abstract: Ballast water can transport microorganisms, including potentially pathogenic bacteria (PPB), between aquatic environments. This study examined bacterial communities and PPB assemblages in 11 ballast water samples using 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing. Samples were classified into six groups based on the country of uptake and water type. Total bacterial community composition differed significantly among groups (PERMANOVA, p = 0.037), whereas no significant differences were detected in PPB community composition (p = 0.138). abstract: The purpose of this paper is to present the results of a theoretical study about the approach to environmental education for indigenous communities in Latin America; it forms part of a master’s thesis entitled: “Intercultural Dialogue Between the U’wa Indigenous Knowledge System and Environmental Education with in-service Indigenous Educators.” The methodology employed consisted of a literature review of scientific databases and repositories, which enabled a general mapping of the documents and an analysis of the frequency of academic output on the topic. title: Evolving motivations for participation in community-based conservation: A relational perspective
abstract: Successful outcomes of community-based conservation, both ecological and social, rely on local actors being motivated to engage at the outset of the programme and to sustain their motivation over time. Using semi-structured interviews, we explore the motivations of 22 community Conservation Officers who have participated in marine turtle conservation in Tanzania for more than two decades. We focus on factors that motivated initial participation, as well as those that contributed to sustaining their participation over the past 20 years. title: Mixotrophy as an alternative strategy under iron-limited upwelling conditions
abstract: Abstract Mixotrophs, phytoplankton capable of both phototrophy and heterotrophy, serve crucial yet complex roles in ocean food webs and carbon cycling. As climate change is expected to reduce iron bioavailability within upwelling zones, mixotrophs may have an advantage due to an array of possible iron acquisition strategies. We paired physiological measurements with metatranscriptomics to investigate the molecular mechanisms of mixotrophs within an upwelling zone as a function of iron status. title: Concordance between phylogenomics and growth in describing cryptic speciation of little tunny (Euthynnus alletteratus, Scombridae)
abstract: Abstract The little tunny ( Euthynnus alletteratus, Scombridae) have great economic importance with a large volume of catches. Recently, both the south-eastern and northern stocks were found to be at high and moderate risk of overfishing, respectively. Here we investigated the stock structure of E. alletteratus and the phylogenetic relationships through a combination of genetic, genomic and growth analysis. title: Genetic analysis of bone morphometry and ivory vertebrae in threespine stickleback
abstract: Previous genetic studies of skeletal variation in threespine stickleback fish (Gasterosteus aculeatus) have focused primarily on striking morphological differences. Here, we examine the largely unexplored genetic architecture of internal bone microstructural variation between marine and freshwater stickleback. Micro-computed tomography X-ray analysis revealed differences in the porosity, bone thickness, and bone volume fraction within armor plates and vertebrae from a marine and freshwater stickleback. title: Review of reintroduction as a conservation tool for Pacific salmon in western North America
abstract: Abstract Objective Reintroduction of Pacific salmon Oncorhynchus spp. into historically occupied habitat is a widely used management strategy in western North America. Since the last major review, new information on donor populations, fish passage, dam removal, ecological interactions, monitoring, and cultural and societal considerations has emerged. We conducted a comprehensive review to synthesize these advances and inform best practices. title: The role of host resource dynamics in shaping life-history evolution of pine processionary moths
abstract: Synchronization between larval development and peak resource quality drives life-history evolution in forest defoliators from cold-temperate regions but is less considered in other ecosystems, such as those in the Mediterranean region. Studies on Thaumetopoea pityocampa , the main Mediterranean pine defoliator, which typically develops during winter (winter population [WP]), have mostly focused on climate. title: Potential of cloud and aerosol retrievals using highly accurate hyperspectral satellite imagery
abstract: Abstract Reducing uncertainty in anthropogenic climate forcing requires improved observational constraints on aerosol and cloud properties. This study demonstrates how hyperspectral observations with exceptionally low radiometric uncertainty, exemplified by the proposed Traceable Radiometry Underpinning Terrestrial and Helio Studies (TRUTHS)-like configuration, can strengthen these constraints relative to PACE Ocean Color Instrument (OCI)-like configuration. title: Macrofungi Diversity in a Community Forest, Tha Mai District, Chanthaburi Province, Thailand
abstract: This study aimed to survey macrofungi diversity in a community forest in Tha Mai District, Chanthaburi Province, Thailand, and to evaluate their trophic mode and edibility; the knowledge gained from this study will help to establish a macrofungi database as part of a biodiversity learning center for the community. Macrofungi sampling was performed in the area, with identification being done by morphological analysis and internal transcribed spacer (ITS) sequencing. title: Estado del arte del material manipulativo para transformaciones geométricas en estudiantes con discapacidad visual.
abstract: This article aims to analyze the state of the art on teaching geometric transformations in inclusive education contexts, with special attention to studies that address visual impairment and the use of hands-on materials. To do this, a documentary review of scientific articles, theses, and institutional documents located in academic databases and open-access repositories was con-ducted, which allowed for systematizing the existing work and outlining the main theoretical and teaching approaches present in the literature. title: Identifikasi Rumput Laut yang di Budidaya di Perairan Sulamu, Kabupaten Kupang, Nusa Tenggara Timur
abstract: The coastal waters of Sulamu, Kupang Regency, East Nusa Tenggara, hold significant potential for seaweed aquaculture, yet taxonomic certainty and morphological characterization remain essential to explore. This study aims to identify cultivated seaweed species, describe their morphological traits, and evaluate the physical-chemical parameters at the cultivation sites. Sampling was conducted using a purposive sampling method across active farming locations in Sulamu waters. abstract: # Individual identification of brown bears using pose-aware metric learning Multi-year re-identification for brown bears collected at McNeil River (2017–2022) Identifying individuals within a species is a cornerstone of ecological and biological research, holding the key to understanding behavior, population dynamics, and conservation needs. title: Natural compounds in products of plant and animal origin
abstract: Natural compounds of animal and plant origin play a key role in maintaining human health and preventing diseases. Camel milk and sea buckthorn Hippophae rhamnoides are traditional food products and medicinal remedies with a unique composition and therapeutic properties. The aim of this work was a comprehensive study of the natural compounds in camel milk from Bactrian and Dromedary camels in the village of Nura (Ili District), as well as a comparative analysis of the biochemical composition of large-fruited and dessert varieties of sea buckthorn from the highland region of the village of Naryn

title: Aterian Lithic Technology and Functional Studies in North Africa: A Review of Current Evidence and Perspectives
abstract: Abstract In North Africa, the Middle Stone Age (MSA) has been associated with the emergence and evolution of Homo sapiens and is considered a pivotal period in the development of behavioral complexity. Recent archaeological discoveries have yielded a range of technological innovations, which are likely connected with ecological adaptations as well as new social and symbolic practices. title: Resilience assessment of pile-supported wharves under the effects of sequential earthquake and soil liquefaction incorporating vine copula captured dependence
abstract: Pile-supported wharves (PSWs) constructed in seismically active coastal environments are susceptible to earthquake-induced liquefaction and the cumulative effects of sequential seismic events. This study develops a probabilistic framework to assess the seismic resilience of conventional and seismically isolated PSWs subjected to mainshock-aftershock (MS-AS) sequences while accounting for liquefaction-induced soil degradation. title: Presence and characterization of microplastics in pet blood (dogs and cats): Evidence of environmental contamination
abstract: Increasing evidence identifies microplastics (MPs) as ubiquitous environmental contaminants, across marine, terrestrial, and atmospheric ecosystems. Their size and physicochemical properties facilitate widespread distribution and bioavailability, raising increasing concerns regarding their potential impact on animal and human health. Their presence in aquatic organisms (e.g., fish, mussels), marine mammals, and birds is demonstrated but evidence related to dogs and cats are relatively few. title: Widespread hybridization in sympatric populations of allis shad Alosa alosa (L.1758) and twaite shad Alosa fallax (Lacépède 1803): A transnational perspective for conservation and management
abstract: The dynamics of hybridization between co-occurring species in environments that have been modified by anthropogenic activities are important for generating new understandings of how species respond to disturbance and to support conservation management. Accordingly, the patterns of hybridization between anadromous allis shad Alosa alosa (L.1758) and twaite shad Alosa fallax (Lacépède 1803) were investigated, where these species historically co-occurred across rivers in Europe. title: Gendered landscapes of loss: climate change, disaster, and women's resilience in rural India
abstract: This article examines the gendered dimensions of climate-induced disasters in rural India through a systematic archival analysis of five community testimonies published by the People's Archive of Rural India (PARI). Drawing on stories from Odisha, Maharashtra, Assam, and Kerala, the study analyses how climate change manifesting as erratic monsoons, intensifying floods, accelerating riverbank erosion, and catastrophic landslides disproportionately impacts women in agrarian and indigenous communities. title: Landed estates and cottage provision in rural England: The Manvers Estate, Nottinghamshire in the 19 th and early 20 th century
abstract: Abstract This paper investigates changing housing provision in rural Nottinghamshire during the 19 th and early 20th centuries using archival material and historical census data. The Manvers estate archives contain valuable information to reconstruct the role of landed estates, land agents and tenant farmers in shaping housing provision and conditions. The role of structural circumstances, such as the agricultural crisis, the poor law regime and the open-closed settlement model, discourses around cottage sanitary conditions and the development of governmental regulations are considered. title: Sand flies of Maranhão State, Brazil: checklist, distribution updates, and reported Leishmania associations
abstract: Phlebotomine sand flies are the vectors of Leishmania parasites, comprising an important component of disease ecology. In the Brazilian state of Maranhão (MA), environmental heterogeneity associated with the transition between Amazonian, Cerrado, and coastal biomes favors high species diversity, yet available information remains fragmented. This study provides an updated checklist of sand fly species recorded in MA, synthesizing published records, refining geographic distributions at the municipal level, and compiling reported Leishmania associations. title: Popski’s Private Myth: Vladimir Peniakoff, the Libyan Arab Force and the Problem of Memoir Evidence
abstract: Abstract Vladimir Peniakoff’s Popski’s Private Army remains one of the most influential published accounts of the Libyan Arab Force (LAF) during the Second World War. This archive-led article reassesses Vladimir Peniakoff as a problematic source for the LAF, showing how his memoir preserved valuable traces of LAF activity while distorting chronology, agency, reputational memory and attribution. This has contributed to the marginalisation of Libyan, and specifically Senussi, wartime agency. title: Effects of Krill-Based Product Supplementation on the Growth Performance and Immunity of Pacific White Shrimp (Litopenaeus vannamei): A Literature Review
abstract: The increasing scarcity and price volatility of fish meal (FM), largely driven by overexploitation of marine fisheries, have intensified the search for sustainable and functional alternatives in shrimp aquaculture. This review synthesizes current evidence published between 2016 and 2026 to evaluate the nutritional and immunological effects of Antarctic krill (Euphausia superba)-based products on the growth performance and health of Pacific white shrimp (Litopenaeus vannamei). title: Residential proximity to oil and gas development and socioeconomic conditions: A comparative analysis of 33 countries
abstract: Abstract Fossil fuels continue to dominate the global energy supply. As emerging technologies drive up global energy consumption (e.g., cryptocurrency mining, data centers), identifying which populations are exposed to oil and gas extraction will become increasingly important. Yet, no prior study has done so internationally. We combine the Oil and Gas Infrastructure Mapping database with the Global Human Settlement Layer to estimate population exposure to oil and gas wells through residential proximity across 33 countries in 2024. title: Gastropod Diversity at Azheekkal, Kollam, Kerala, India: A Historical Baseline from August–November 2017
abstract: Motivation: Historical biodiversity records provide useful reference points for coastal biodiversity monitoring, particularly in areas subject to continuing human use. Azheekkal, Kollam, Kerala, supports a diverse molluscan fauna, but historical records of its gastropod assemblage remain limited. Objectives: This study documents the gastropod assemblage recorded at Azheekkal during August–November 2017 and provides a historical reference dataset for future biodiversity assessments. title: ASTAXANTHIN AS A NEUROPROTECTIVE AGENT AGAINST ACUTE STRESS-INDUCED COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT
abstract: The sympathetic-adrenomedullary system and the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis are both activated by acute stress. Although adaptive initially, excessive acute stress causes glucocorticoid overload, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and neuroinflammation. These changes particularly affect the hippocampus and prefrontal cortex, impairing synaptic plasticity, neurogenesis, and cognition, including working memory, spatial learning, attention, and executive function. title: CLIMATE-RELATED DISASTERS AND PROVINCIAL CONTINGENCY BUDGET ADAPTATION IN INDONESIA
abstract: This study examines whether Indonesian regional contingency budgets adapt to realised climate-related disaster experience, treating budget responsiveness as one dimension of fiscal resilience. A balanced province-year panel covering 32 provinces is estimated using fixed effects with standard errors clustered by province. The dependent variable is the budgeted share of contingency expenditure (Belanja Tidak Terduga/BTT) in total regional expenditure. This study revisits three human burials previously analyzed for funerary practices, paleopathology, and lifestyle. abstract: Ichthyoelephas humeralis (bocachico) is a native fish species of high ecological and socioeconomic importance in Ecuador. This study integrates a systematic review and a spatial analysis to synthesize its distribution, biology, ecological requirements, economic importance, threats, and conservation strategies. abstract: This article examines how documentary cinema establishes relationships between art and memory in three documentaries: Lemebel, Cicatrices en la tierra, and Este arte que abraza. abstract: Center-pivot irrigated cropland (CPIC) is a large-scale, intensive agricultural irrigation practice with high water-use efficiency. This characteristic enables CPIC to increase crop yields and promote agricultural development, while simultaneously causing groundwater overexploitation and subsequent environmental issues. abstract: Functional profiling of meta-omics is essential for understanding microbial communities, yet support for custom genome-resolved reference databases is limited. We introduce Leviathan for integrated taxonomic and functional profiling at both genome and pangenome resolution. Leviathan combines Sylph for ultrafast alignment-free taxonomic profiling with Salmon for pseudo-alignment-based read quantification in DNA space against (pan)genome-resolved gene catalogs, producing dual metrics per (pan)genome: pathway abundance and graph-based pathway coverage. title: A new Caribbean species of the giant isopod genus Bathynomus (Crustacea, Isopoda, Cirolanidae) with notes on its evolutionary history
abstract: Abstract The new species Bathynomus tuebingoborikensis sp. nov., discovered in an historic museum collection, is described. We provide preliminary phylogenetic analyses of the genus, including extant and fossil species, using morphological characters. We reconstruct the evolutionary origin of the genus in the Caribbean, and suggest ten different migration waves all over the world oceans, including multiple recolonizations of the Americas. abstract: This review of salmonid alphavirus provides a collection of the most recent knowledge on the factors relevant for the transmission and control of the virus including updates on SAV survival, viral shedding, detection, and effects of vaccination as reported in peer-reviewed literature, presentations, theses, and annual reports. SAV can survive in all water types, being the longest in colder marine waters without organic loading. The biophysical properties of SAV indicate a moderate to high robustness. abstract: Environmental degradation requires broader forms of social accountability that extend beyond formal regulations. Although social media has become an influential platform for environmental campaigns, limited studies have examined its role in fostering environmental awareness from the perspective of Social and Environmental Accounting (SEA). This study aims to explore how the social media content of @PandawaraGroup contributes to the formation of environmental awareness and expands the concept of social accountability in the digital sphere. title: Indian MAHASAGAR and the Evolution of India's Maritime Diplomacy
abstract: India's maritime diplomacy has undergone a decisive transformation over the past decade, evolving from a continental-focused posture toward a proactive, maritime-centric vision for the Indo-Pacific. This article examines that evolution and assesses the operational relevance of minilateral architectures in advancing India's strategic objectives. abstract: This article describes how, in the wider context of the Cold War, Indonesian-Soviet diplomatic relations developed from the Bandung Conference of 1955 through to the commencement of the L. Brezhnev era and the early 1970s. This research employs comparative historiographical methodology with Critical Discourse Analysis (CDA) to account for Soviet political and media discourse framing Indonesia as a postcolonial model of independence and a vanguard leader of the Non-Aligned Movement. abstract: Abstract This paper examines Fahmīdah Riyāẓ’s collection of Urdu poems titled Tum Kabīr as a (meta-)archive that maps the affective, semiotic, and mnemonic landscapes of her dialogic poetic imagination. Through a sustained exploration of the implications of dialogism, it analyzes the interplay among different voices, texts, languages, and competing parts of the self that animate Riyāẓ’s poetic practice, using subjectivity and linguistic innovation as analytical lenses. abstract: This study develops the Sargassum-Based Concrete Integrated Carbon Evaluation Framework (SBC-ICEF) to assess the environmental implications of incorporating processed Sargassum particles into concrete for potential non-load-bearing wall applications in coastal China. Laboratory measurements are linked to production-stage carbon inventories and supplementary carbon-retention scenarios, with potential operational-energy effects discussed qualitatively, using 1 m 3 of concrete and a reference building as complementary functional units. title: Macroevolutionary insights into the range limits of species and lineages
abstract: Understanding the intrinsic and extrinsic factors that determine the range limits of species is an important goal in biology. Much work has focused on understanding the range limits of populations and individual species, whereas the factors that determine the distributions of evolutionary lineages have received less attention in the range limits literature. abstract: Historiography of Japonisme in Latin America has logically prioritized the study of prominent figures such as José Juan Tablada, leaving the role of cultural mediators whose influence proved decisive yet to be examined. Among them, Pedro Carrere stands out; however, his diplomatic career and collecting activities have lacked a systematic reconstruction until now. abstract: Objectives: The present study aimed to assess the neuroprotective properties and memory enhancement of the ethanolic extract of Sargassum tenerrimum (ST) with regard to the scopolamine-induced amnesia model in Wistar rats and explore the underlying mechanism involved in cholinergic neurotransmission. abstract: In the mid-1980s, scientific studies first highlighted the role of anthropogenic methane in global warming and emissions from cows as an important source. Using scientific studies, archival documents, media interviews, and various government reports, we analyzed how the National Cattlemen’s Association (NCA), a trade association for the U.S beef industry, reacted to news about its products’ impacts on global warming between 1986 and 1996. abstract: Yellow-legged gulls (Larus michahellis), which exhibit opportunistic feeding behavior, face a high global risk of interacting with anthropogenic waste originating from urban and fishing activities. abstract: Acanthus ilicifoliusbelongs to the family Acanthaceaeis a medicinal plant widely distributed in the coastal areas of tropical and subtropical regions. It has been traditionally used in various systems of folk medicine for managing conditions such as wounds, fever, inflammation, and respiratory problems. title: Toponymy and Shifted Identity: A Study of the Language Change in Rejang-Language Village Names
abstract: This study examines the changes in village names from the Rejang language to Indonesian in Kepahiang Regency, Bengkulu, focusing on referential meanings, community perceptions, and the impact on local cultural identity. Using referential meaning analysis and thematic analysis based on interviews with both older and younger generations, the findings show that the language shift alters not only linguistic forms but also the cultural, historical, and spiritual values embedded in the original toponyms. abstract: Nuclear melt glass provides a valuable archive of information about the nature of the nuclear detonation. Study of melt glasses provides information on the device materials and performance, the emplacement conditions, the venting conditions (if any), and future environmental and human health impacts. abstract: Abstract Sustainable Development Goal 12.2 aims to achieve the sustainable management and efficient use of natural resources by 2030. abstract: Abstract. The Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) is a key component of the Earth’s climate system, and is theorized to have multiple stable states. Critical slowing down (CSD) can detect stability changes in Earth system components, and has been found in sea-surface temperature (SST) based fingerprints of the AMOC. title: Institutional Development and Political Activities of the Permanent Ottoman Embassy in Madrid (1857–1922)
abstract: Although the Ottoman Empire experienced a chronological delay in transitioning to permanent diplomacy, it established an embassy in Madrid, as it did in various other European cities, to improve its relations with European states and to closely monitor continental politics. abstract: This paper interrogates how Eurocentrism structures what counts as violence and, by extension, what counts as peace. abstract: Abstract Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a progressive ocular complication of diabetes and is commonly graded into five severity levels, ranging from no DR to proliferative DR. Automated severity grading is challenging because the classes are imbalanced and misclassification between severity levels may have different implications depending on the distance between the true and predicted grades. abstract: Abstract In this assessment, we reviewed existing literature to assess the ecological risks, benefits, and uncertainties associated with reintroducing Chinook salmon ( Oncorhynchus tshawytcha ) into the McCloud River, a tributary of the Sacramento River, California. abstract: Within the first few years of life, children go from nonverbal infants to fluent users of hundreds of words. This feat unfolds as children are immersed in a sea of words in conversations, stories, and other language contexts. title: Prevalence and multimorbidity patterns of thyroid dysfunction in Chinese adults
abstract: The risk of thyroid dysfunction (TD) persists in the Chinese population. However, large-scale epidemiological studies investigating TD prevalence and its geographic disparities are limited. Previous studies have mostly focused on associations between TD and individual organ systems or single medical conditions. This nationwide, large-scale study utilized data from the Meinian Health Check-up database across all 31 provinces of the Chinese mainland. abstract: 1. The fundamental unit of spatial ecology is a species range: the geographic area that it occupies. Species ranges are delineated by range edges (also known as boundaries or limits). Why range edges occur where they do and not elsewhere, and what makes them move, has been an active area of research since the 19th century. abstract: Bottom sediments of Arctic lakes are widely used as archives of environmental change and indicators of trace element accumulation. title: Regional sonic cosmopolitanism: Palestinian musicians and Arab urban music in the Galilee region, 1948–1980
abstract: This article examines how Palestinian wedding musicians in the Galilee region sustained engagement with regional Arab urban music traditions during the decades following the 1948 Nakba. While the events of 1948 shattered the musical infrastructure that had connected Palestinian cities including Haifa to the broader Arab world, cosmopolitan Arab art music continues until today to form part of the everyday sonic lives of Palestinian communities in northern Israel. abstract: The purpose of this study is to determine the relative importance of energy saving measures (ESMs) and alternative biofuels for the improvement of ship efficiency and for compliance with new regulations imposed on the maritime transport sector. In light of the fact that ESMs have proven that they are capable of providing a significant fuel saving potential by enhancing the hull condition, propulsion, and internal combustion efficiency as well as through operational optimization, the aim of this study is to investigate the advantages and disadvantages of ESMs compared to biofuels. title: Overturning urban visuality: knockoff aesthetics and the unruly kings of Hong Kong
abstract: This article examines the aesthetic and political significance of the street writings of Hong Kong’s King of Kowloon (Tsang Tsou-choi) and Plumber King (Yim Chiu-tong) beyond celebratory framings of collective memory. Drawing on archival research and extensive fieldwork-based visual analysis, it develops knockoff aesthetics as a framework for understanding how political force can emerge from urban inscriptions widely received as improper and visually unappealing. title: Petrophysical Dataset of Representative Volcanic Rocks from Dokdo, South Korea
abstract: Dokdo, a volcanic island in the East Sea, comprises alkaline volcanic and pyroclastic rocks formed during multiple stages of Cenozoic volcanism. This study presents a petrophysical dataset for 61 rock specimens collected from Dongdo and Seodo, Dokdo, to support the interpretation of geological and geophysical data. The specimens comprise trachyte, trachyandesite I, II, and III, lapilli tuff, and ash tuff. abstract: Abstract Using archival and unofficial sources, this article examines how political calculations, economic considerations, local consumption patterns and international dynamics shaped the colonial administration’s water governance strategies in Hong Kong. It focuses on how the 1967 water emergency prompted the colonial government to recalibrate its approach, from a policy of manageable dependency to one of risk aversion. title: GOVERNING INFORMALITY : Eviction, Recognition, and Legal Ambiguity in Kampung Akuarium, Jakarta
abstract: Abstract Informal settlements in Jakarta have long been governed through cycles of tolerance, eviction, and selective recognition. Rather than resulting from the absence of planning, informality is often produced through spatial regulations, legal ambiguity, and political intervention. This article examines Kampung Akuarium, a settlement in North Jakarta, to explore how informality is governed through planning instruments and political change. abstract: In September 1947, a train traveling under the auspices of the Red Cross departed Romania carrying over 420 Jewish children, via Prague, to the Netherlands. The children, among them Holocaust survivors from Transnistria, had been gathered from different parts of Romania, including orphanages, and were taken to the “Ilaniah” children’s village, located on the grounds of a former Jewish psychiatric hospital in Apeldoorn. abstract: This article reassesses the transimperial flight of enslaved Afro-Curaçaoans from the Dutch island of Curaçao to the Spanish mainland of Tierra Firme, particularly Coro, during the eighteenth century. abstract: The crucian carp ( Carassius carassius ) has declined markedly in recent decades due to the ongoing invasion of its congeneric species complex, the gibel carp ( Carassius gibelio ) and widespread habitat degradation. abstract: Abstract Rural e-commerce in China’s central and western regions is often framed as a scalable pathway to rural revitalization. abstract: Dried fish processing businesses support coastal economies by generating employment and increasing the value-added of fisheries products. Sustainability remains challenged by limited financial management capabilities, restricted access to formal financial services, and inadequate utilization of financial technology. abstract: This article uncovers an overlooked archive of religious poetry embedded in five Kyiv-Mohylian poetics manuals from 1685 to 1736, demonstrating how these poems served as a crucial mechanism by which Orthodox Kyiv participated in the learned culture of early modern Europe. title: Dissecting the urban anatomy: modernist layers, institutional landmarks, and the Heritage-City Synergy in Cartagena
abstract: Cartagena, Spain, is a unique Mediterranean coastal city defined by its transition from a rigid 18th-entury military stronghold to a dynamic modern center. While its ancient ruins are well-documented, the city’s later layers – specifically its modernist architecture and institutional landmarks – are often overlooked in urban discourse. This neglect creates a gap between heritage preservation and the living city, risking a “museumification” that disconnects historical sites from contemporary social life. abstract: This article examines a major controversy that occurred in Manchester during the Crimean War between John Bright (1811–1889), one of the city’s MPs, and his constituent and friend Absalom Watkin (1787–1861). title: Boron isotope fractionation in siliceous hot spring sinters: Geochemical implications for biosignatures
abstract: Siliceous hot spring sinters preserve coupled mineralogical, geochemical, and isotopic signatures generated during microbial silicification and therefore represent valuable archives of biosignature formation. However, the mechanistic criteria for distinguishing biologically influenced silicification from abiotic silica precipitation remain poorly constrained. title: Isolation and phenotypic characterization of bacteriophages targeting multidrug-resistant biofilm-forming uropathogenic Escherichia coli from hospital sewage
abstract: Abstract Uropathogenic Escherichia coli (UPEC) is a major cause of urinary tract infections (UTIs), with multidrug resistance (MDR) and biofilm formation complicating treatment. This study isolated and phenotypically characterized bacteriophages targeting MDR and biofilm-forming UPEC from hospital sewage in Ethiopia. abstract: BACKGROUND: Malaria rapid diagnosis tests (mRDTs) detecting Plasmodium falciparum histidine-rich protein 2 (Pfhrp2) are the most widely adopted diagnostic tool in malaria-endemic areas. However, extensive polymorphisms in Pfhrp2 could modify Pfhrp2 epitopes, rendering it undetectable by Pfhrp2-based mRDTs. title: CORAL: Cross-modal Vector Retrieval via Incremental Graph Construction at Scale
abstract: Cross-modal vector retrieval is widely used in multimodal systems, such as search engines and vector databases. It typically operates in out-of-distribution (OOD) settings, where query vectors follow a distribution that differs from that of the vectors stored in the database. In such cases, conventional indexes suffer significant performance degradation, and even methods specially designed for OOD remain limited by inefficient use of query modal characteristics, restricted GPU parallelism, and inadequate support for dynamic updates. title: Irradiated Atmospheres VII. Effect of Mixing Energy Flux on Atmosphere-Interior Coupling
abstract: Highly irradiated, underdense rocky planets such as puffy Venuses may host strong coupling between their atmospheres and magma-ocean interiors. Previous studies have mainly treated this coupling through radiative transfer and chemical equilibrium, leaving the role of vertical mixing unclear. Here we quantify how energy transport associated with vertical mixing modifies the thermal structure, volatile chemistry, and emission spectra of puffy Venuses. title: Building Macroeconomically Relevant Climate Indices via the Assemblage VAR
abstract: What should a macroeconomically relevant climate index contain? The composition is inherently ambiguous, and aggregation choices affect structural inference. We introduce the Assemblage VAR, which jointly estimates nonnegative aggregation weights and VAR parameters by maximizing the system likelihood-gain criterion, effectively outsourcing aggregation to observed macroeconomic dynamics. title: Effects of Periodic Migration on Selection in Subdivided Populations
abstract: Migration and selection jointly shape evolutionary outcomes in spatially structured populations. Migration can vary over time as ecological shifts, such as changes in sea level, alter habitat connectivity. Here, we study the impact of periodic migration on selection within a geographically subdivided population. Using a two-deme Moran model with spatially heterogeneous selection, we analyze a scenario in which a mutant genotype is advantageous in one habitat and disadvantageous in the other. title: Labour reallocation and production-network recomposition in the green transition
abstract: A growing number of countries are adopting policies to reduce greenhouse-gas emissions, a process expected to reshape production systems and labour markets by altering relative prices and changing production and demand patterns across sectors. We develop an agent-based monetary input--output network model to analyse the medium-term effects of climate policies on production networks and sectoral labour allocation. title: Consensus for Compressed Static Functions
abstract: The Consensus technique marked a breakthrough in the construction of minimal perfect hash functions (MPHFs), reaching a linear tradeoff between construction time and space overhead relative to the optimum. Consensus provides a clever scheme to search for and encode seeds of tasks in random data structures. We apply Consensus to the related field of compressed static functions (CSFs). abstract: Small, trade-dependent economies often exhibit limited maritime connectivity, yet empirical evidence on the structural configuration of their container systems remains limited. This study analyzes route concentration and node distributions in Mauritania’s maritime container system during 2019–2022 using shipment-level data measured in forty-foot equivalent units (FFE). abstract: At $\sim$3.9~Ga (stellar age $\sim$0.6~Gyr), the young Sun was far more magnetically active than today. It launched $\sim$$10^2$ large, fast coronal mass ejections (CMEs) per year into a denser, more magnetized wind. We follow these eruptions to Earth's atmosphere with a semi-analytic model chain. title: Energy dissipation and free boundary stability of the Stefan problem
abstract: In this paper we prove the stability and the continuity of the free boundaries of two-phase and one-phase weak solutions to the Stefan problem in any dimension. Our proof has two main ingredients. The first one is an energy conservation principle for weak solutions that we derive for general domains in both the one-phase and the two-phase settings; this energy conservation principle provides the modulus of continuity for the displacement of the free boundary and is a flexible tool for analyzing long-time behavior of solutions. abstract: Smart ports increasingly depend on IoT-enabled digitalization to turn heterogeneous operational processes into measurable, optimizable workflows. Accordingly, this paper first provides a concise review of IoT-enabler technologies for port digital transformation, emphasizing how sensing, connectivity, and data integration capabilities support real-time decision-making in port environments. title: CreativeFlow: A One-to-Many Analogical Relation Transfer Method for 3D Asset Generation
abstract: Inspired by cognitive science, we present CREATIVEFLOW, an analogical generation framework that explicitly models analogical divergent thinking to mitigate creative homogenization in text-to-3D pipelines. Our method derives a series of meaningful yet relationally similar source-target asset pairs, each featuring distinct geometric configurations. Expert evaluations demonstrate that our framework substantially enhances creative novelty and visual fascination. This workflow and its resulting assets establish a foundational dataset and benchmark for future relation-aware 3D model training.

abstract: Abstract Interest in the topic of geodetic co-location in space and space ties has recently intensified within the geodetic community, particularly following the approval of the European Space Agency’s Genesis mission. From the perspective of very long baseline interferometry (VLBI), observations of Earth-orbiting satellites are not standard practice yet. title: Personality Without Persons? A Psychometric Critique of Big Five Testing in Large Language Models
abstract: Human personality inventories are increasingly used to characterize large language models (LLMs), compare systems, and inform downstream governance claims. Yet, these inventories were developed and validated for humans, and it remains unclear whether they are valid for non-human systems. title: JWST MIRI Reveals a Potential Atmosphere on the Ultrahot Rocky Planet TOI-431b
abstract: Abstract An open question in exoplanet science is whether rocky exoplanets extremely close in to their host stars, “lava worlds,” can retain significant atmospheres. Thermal emission observations via secondary eclipse can be used to determine whether a rocky exoplanet possesses an atmosphere. abstract: We investigate the weakly nonlinear evolution of phototaxis-induced bioconvection in an absorbing and isotropically scattering algal suspension subjected to oblique and normal collimated irradiation. abstract: Topological polaritons provide a route to engineer optical Chern bands, but realizing large gaps or efficient electrical tunability remains challenging because time-reversal-symmetry breaking in semiconductor polariton systems is typically limited by weak Zeeman splittings. abstract: Abstract Graphs and hypergraphs are commonly distinguished by the order of the relations they represent, with graphs encoding pairwise relations and hypergraphs encoding interactions among arbitrary groups. We show that, for node-update dynamics, a more natural viewpoint is to regard a graph as a collection of focal neighbourhoods, each centered on a vertex and consisting of the vertex and its neighbours. abstract: Sample-based quantum diagonalization can reduce the classical cost of many-body calculations by restricting diagonalization to configurations identified through quantum sampling, but its efficiency depends on how compactly the target state is represented in the sampled basis. title: High-resolution Antarctic sea surface temperatures from Landsat enabled by cloud-native processing and novel seal-tag validation
abstract: Ocean heat transport drives approximately half of Antarctic ice mass loss, yet in situ ocean observations near glacier ice fronts remain exceedingly scarce given the challenges of data collection in this remote environment. abstract: Abstract Acoustic backscatter from gas bubbles is key to detecting and quantifying marine seeps and related processes, yet practical tools for target strength (TS) prediction remain limited. abstract: At present, there is no single open-source electronic hardware platform that natively integrates 24 V industrial RS485 sensors with marine robotic and hydroponic actuation. abstract: Worldwide reef ecosystem degradation is inspiring efforts to enhance in-situ coral larvae settlement onto degraded or artificial reefs. title: Ecosystem accounting to support coastal restoration decision-making
abstract: Ecosystem accounting is a structured approach to compiling environmental and economic information, but accounts are most often used to report past trends and current ecosystem states rather than to evaluate future management options. abstract: Deep bow immersion (bow–diving) during operation in severe cross seas (\phi \neq 180^\circ ) poses significant survivability risks to surface vessels due to asymmetric waterplane variations that generate hazardous transverse hydrodynamic forces and heeling moments. abstract: Since the dawn of cartography, mapmakers have experienced the need to give myths and legends a real space by locating them within maps. The Great Ocean, which comprised the known world until the end of the Middle Ages, and the remote lands at the edge of the world, were the best places to locate imaginary places. abstract: The Landsat archive and the Harmonized Landsat and Sentinel-2 (HLS) 2.0 virtual constellations enable monitoring of long-term and rapid environmental change with optical imagery, but differences in sensor design and atmospheric correction algorithms require cross-sensor normalization to ensure consistent observations. This study evaluates methods for such normalization using two global datasets: Landsat ETM+/OLI and HLS 2.0. title: Personalized drug discovery from rare diseases to cancer
abstract: Precision medicine selects individual treatments from a small toolbox of therapies already available. Personalized drug discovery (PDD) brings this concept one step ahead, developing drugs for individual patient's diseases. Currently, PDD is being developed for rare disorders, where conventional drug discovery paradigms are non-applicable due to small patient sizes, but also for cancer. As a new frontier in precision medicine, PDD should be upscaled in rare and non-rare diseases.

abstract: This article examines the opportunities and limitations of the Joint Expeditionary Force (JEF) as a regional defense cooperation framework and assesses prospects for partnership with Ukraine. abstract: ABSTRACT This article examines drug cartels as creative, innovation‐driven organizations rather than solely violent criminal enterprises. abstract: ABSTRACT Drone photogrammetry provides a minimally invasive morphometric tool to assess growth and energy reserve in marine mammals. abstract: Abstract As important policy and diplomatic progress is reached around climate-related loss and damage, attention has shifted to existing gaps regarding science-based methods and frameworks to inform effective action. abstract: In the twenty-first century, international politics unfolds within a battlespace where narratives, imagery, and algorithmic influence operate alongside conventional instruments of power. abstract: Background: The growth of digital technologies has expanded opportunities for online freelance work among youth.
