abstract: Background: Employee retention is increasingly challenging as Generation Z enters the corporate workforce with distinct expectations regarding career growth, compensation, supervisory support, organizational culture, and work–life balance. abstract: The civil infrastructure is becoming more and more prone to earthquake and flood hazards whereas climate change is adding another level of uncertainty for infrastructure designs, structural performance, and sustainability. abstract: Abstract Introduction Arctic Grayling Thymallus arcticus were extirpated from Michigan in 1936. abstract: Timely and accurate projections of when global warming will exceed the Paris Agreement’s 1.5 °C threshold are essential for effective climate policy. abstract: Pandemics are disasters whose causes and consequences are both rooted in the environment, yet emergency management and environmental management are usually reviewed apart. abstract: Background The emergence of cephalosporin-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae strains, encoding altered Penicillin-Binding Protein 2 (PBP2), has become a major global public health concern. abstract: Earth’s continental crust is its most chemically evolved and diverse reservoir. abstract: The El Gigante Metamorphic Complex, in the homonymous range (Sierras Pampeanas, Argentina), consists of three lithostratigraphic units that, from bottom to top, are: Quebrada Grande (Mesoproterozoic protoliths), Loma Cortada (Ediacaran-early Cambrian sedimentary protoliths), and Los Morteritos (middle to late Cambrian protoliths), all reworked by the Famatinian orogeny. title: Assessment of multiple ecosystem services and interrelation-ships in Forest-rich regions: a case study of Guilin, China
abstract: Ecosystem services (ES) are fundamental to achieving human well-being. To systematically evaluate ES and their interrelationships in forest-enriched regions, this study takes Guilin, a representative forest-rich area in China, as the study area and develops an integrated coupling model for the comprehensive measurement and interaction analysis of provisioning, regulating, and cultural ES. abstract: Purpose This study aims to assess flood-prone areas in Auckland, New Zealand, using stream order analysis as a geospatial tool to delineate flood risk zones. The research addresses the growing need for efficient flood risk mapping in urban settings by providing a simplified, yet effective, method for identifying high-risk zones. abstract: Abstract The extracellular polymeric substance (EPS) matrix serves as a structural scaffold for biofilm organization, contributing to structural integrity and antimicrobial tolerance by modulating the penetration and distribution of antimicrobial agents. However, whether this EPS matrix can also potentiate antimicrobial localization and activity remains poorly understood. abstract: Understanding phage K. pneumoniae –host interactions is essential for elucidating phage infection mechanisms and developing phage-derived antibacterial strategies. title: PackMonitor: Towards Zero Package Hallucinations via Decoding-Time Monitoring
abstract: As Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly integrated into software development workflows, their trustworthiness has become a critical concern. However, in dependency recommendation scenarios, the reliability of LLMs is undermined by widespread package hallucinations, where models often recommend hallucinated packages. title: Simulated visual attention modelling in digital tourism interfaces: an integrative approach to destination communication
abstract: This paper introduces a simulation-based methodological and conceptual study addressing a critical gap in tourism research: the fragmented treatment of spatial, sequential and temporal dimensions of visual attention. It proposes the Simulated Visual Attention Integrative (SVAI) Model, combining predicted saliency heatmaps, simulated scan paths and saccadic timing within a unified analytical framework. abstract: Biopharmaceutical (therapeutic) proteins are biologically-derived drugs used to treat a variety of diseases. Producing these proteins naturally from mammalian cells presents significant challenges. As a result, non-native hosts, including plants, algae, yeast, and bacteria, have been employed to produce these proteins; however, the complex genetic reconstruction process, high cultivation costs, contamination risks, and regulatory hurdles have hampered commercial success. abstract: Background Patient education is a core component of cardiac rehabilitation (CR), yet it is frequently delivered as a standardized transfer of information rather than as a structured intervention aimed at promoting behavioral change and long-term self-management. This limitation may be particularly relevant in culturally, geographically, linguistically, and socioeconomically diverse populations, such as Mexico. abstract: Firefighters at a wildland-oilfield interface (WOI) encounter complex smoke particle mixtures from biomass and hydrocarbons. These particulates settle onto Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) surfaces, remaining long after fire suppression activities. abstract: Logic-Based Therapy (LBT) is a method of philosophical counseling and psychotherapy based on Rational-Emotive Behavior Therapy (REBT) that uses logic, philosophy, and a network of “guiding virtues” to treat behavioral and emotional dysfunctions. abstract: ABSTRACT Hospitals generate wastewater enriched with human-derived microbes, making them strong sites for focused, near-source surveillance of pathogens. abstract: Abstract Despite the widespread use of zebrafish as a biological model, comprehensive baseline elemental data across its developmental stages remain limited. In this work, ion beam analytical techniques were employed to establish the elemental composition of zebrafish larvae and adults under controlled vivarium conditions. abstract: Abstract Cryptococcus neoformans and Cryptococcus gattii are environmental fungi that cause cryptococcosis, a severe, life-threatening infection, particularly in immunocompromised individuals. Current treatments are limited by toxicity, restricted availability, and the emergence of resistance, highlighting the need for novel antifungal agents. title: Automated fledgling call detection links adult songbird abundance to reproductive success in restored habitat
abstract: Many wildlife monitoring programs assume that adult abundance reflects habitat quality and, by extension, reproductive success, despite the possibility of these parameters decoupling. Abundance may be more likely to decouple with reproduction in human-modified landscapes such as those created through habitat restoration. However, the extent to which this occurs remains unclear due to extensive manual effort required for monitoring reproduction, especially at scale. Passive-acoustic monitoring (PAM) has recently shown promise for detecting fledgling begging calls to infer reproductive success.

abstract: The genus Baccharis exhibits high taxonomic diversity and marked morphological plasticity, which complicates the species-level delimitation of closely related taxa. abstract: Rotors operating in confined flows, or blockage, are commonly encountered in wind and water tunnels, as well as in shallow or dense deployments of hydrokinetic turbines. abstract: Microalgae represent a promising biological platform for CO2 sequestration and the sustainable production of high-value metabolites, particularly carotenoids such as lutein and astaxanthin. However, industrial performance remains constrained by low carbon conversion efficiency, reduced photosynthetic performance, and competing metabolic fluxes that limit product yield. abstract: Fragmentation of urban habitats necessitates governance that spatially aligns ecological requirements with legal structures. abstract: The aim of this study was to investigate the development and physico-mechanical evaluation of an epoxy matrix biocomposite reinforced with multi-short Cynara Scolymus fibers of lengths 0.5, 1.0 and 1.5 cm, in a bid to bridge the gap in studies conducted in the millimeter scale and to statistically validate the results obtained. abstract: Marburg virus (MARV), a highly virulent filovirus of the Filoviridae family, causes severe hemorrhagic fever associated with high case-fatality rates, while effective therapeutic options remain limited. abstract: Himalayan soils are highly susceptible to the impacts of climate change and land-use shifts. Soil organic carbon (SOC) and the carbon management index (CMI) are key measures of soil health in response to land use changes. abstract: Parasites are an important component of freshwater ecosystems due to the ways they regulate energy flow and shape community structure. abstract: Biodiversity is undergoing an unprecedented global decline, and genetic diversity plays a fundamental role in ensuring species persistence. Miconia ulei, an endemic species from the eastern Atlantic Forest in Santa Catarina, southern Brazil, is rare and has few known populations. abstract: Cool façades — building walls with high solar reflectance and high thermal emittance — are promoted as a passive urban cooling strategy. abstract: Functional diversity plays an important role for ecosystem services of managed grasslands such as their gross primary productivity (GPP) and soil organic carbon (SOC) stocks. title: Readers of the Living: Interpretive Mastery and Natural Thinking in Plutarch, Celsus, Origen, and Porphyry
abstract: Abstract This article examines the intersection between imperial writings on animals and post-Hellenistic debates about exegesis. It is the first study to argue that interpreters drawing on Aristotelian theories of voice and Hellenistic ideas of natural sympathy treated the meaningful but non-verbal animal as a test case of nature’s availability to reading, and as an opportunity to reflect on how exegetes transfer their skills between literature and the natural world. title: Development of a browser–based computational tool for preliminary estimation of vertical-axis wind turbine power output
abstract: Rapid estimation of vertical-axis wind turbine (VAWT) power output is essential for preliminary assessment. However, existing approaches using spreadsheets, software, or simulations are resource-intensive and require a tedious process. This study presents a lightweight browser-based computational framework developed using JavaScript for rapid preliminary estimation of VAWT power output. The framework provides an interactive web interface that automatically estimates swept area, available wind power, mechanical power, and electrical power from user-defined parameters. title: Granivorous forest mice select herb seeds on the basis of native origin, not seed size or microenvironment
abstract: Abstract Dietary choice of seed-consuming rodents potentially determines the survival and dispersal success of shade-tolerant forest herbs – a group at risk in post-agricultural landscapes of eastern North America. Optimal foraging theory predicts that large, energy-rich seeds will be most attractive and seed consumption will be greater in structurally complex habitats, which provide protection from predators. title: Political Advantage, Political Risk: The Nascent Stage of Statoil’s International Expansion, 1978–1999
abstract: This article analyses how the dynamics between the Norwegian national oil company Statoil and its government owner gradually changed during the 1980s and 1990s, as Statoil invested in politically risky business environments outside its domicile. Yet, despite this seemingly profit-maximizing behaviour, the NOC was closely intertwined with its government owner and this owner’s pursuit of a value-based foreign policy with emphasis on support for poverty reduction, democracy, human rights and peace building. title: Adsorption–crosslinking immobilization of SHSL on NKA macroporous resin: Operational stability and molecular dynamics at the enzyme–resin interface
abstract: Lipase immobilization can improve operational stability, while enzyme–support interactions may alter conformational behavior near the catalytic region. How local support association relates to catalytic-region dynamics remains unclear. Here, SHSL was immobilized on NKA macroporous resin by hydrophobic adsorption followed by glutaraldehyde post-treatment. The optimized preparation showed 91.44 ± 2.39 U/g activity, 65.47% immobilization yield, and 26.2% activity recovery, retaining 53.7% activity after 10 reuse cycles and 61.0% after 35 days of storage versus 11.7% for free SHSL. title: Disturbance‐Associated Plant Communities in Africa's Largest Alpine Ecosystem: Evidence for Long‐Term Anthropogenic Influence
abstract: ABSTRACT Questions Africa's largest alpine ecosystem is perceived as relatively pristine; nonetheless, it contains numerous pastoral settlements and some of the world's oldest evidence of human presence in an alpine ecosystem. This study aims to address (i) demarcation of settlement vegetation and boundary delineation, (ii) investigation of settlement indicator plants, (iii) species composition of settlement vegetation, and (iv) since when the time of human footprint amplified by pastoralism. title: Shadow Pricing Ecosystem Services in Boreal Forests
abstract: Abstract Boreal forests jointly produce marketed goods and non-market ecosystem services, generating unavoidable trade-offs. We estimate shadow prices with the directional distance function (R. G. Chambers et al. 1996), endogenizing the directional vector and correcting for sampling variation via bootstrap methods. Using a county-by-year panel of Swedish forests, we find that shadow prices vary spatially and temporally yet remain generally low, implying modest opportunity costs for improving biodiversity and carbon sequestration relative to timber. title: Alkaline salt impairs germination recovery more severely than neutral salt in the euhalophyte Suaeda salsa
abstract: Introduction Soil salinization and alkalization increasingly threaten global ecosystem stability, necessitating a clearer understanding of how dominant halophytes respond to complex salt stresses. Methods This study examined the differential effects of neutral and alkaline salt stresses on seed germination and early seedling growth of Suaeda salsa , a dominant halophyte in the Yellow River Delta. abstract: In the arid regions of Kazakhstan, agricultural crops are grown on low-productivity saline-alkali soils with varying properties across different horizons. Soil tillage is performed using non-plow implements that generate high traction resistance and turn over large clods of soil with a low degree of fragmentation. The aim of this study is to provide technical support for primary tillage to maximize soil moisture accumulation and humus conservation. title: Detection of degradation products of Chemical Warfare Agents in Halabja Soil: In Vitro Genotoxicity and Effects in Exposed Humans
abstract: ABSTRACT The town of Halabja in Iraqi Kurdistan remains a symbol of the devastating impact of chemical weapons. More than three decades after the attack, inhabitants continue to suffer from increased cancer rates and severe respiratory, neurological, and psychiatric disorders. While the acute effects of chemical warfare agents have been widely studied, their long-term environmental persistence and associated health impacts remain poorly understood. title: The Effect of i-PUBERS Implementation on Subsidized Fertilizer Distribution Effectiveness
abstract: The implementation of digital systems in public administration has become increasingly important in improving the effectiveness, transparency, and accountability of public service delivery. In the agricultural sector, digitalization is expected to support more accurate and efficient distribution of subsidized fertilizers to eligible farmers. This study aims to analyze the effect of i-PUBERS implementation on the effectiveness of subsidized fertilizer distribution at the Agricultural Office of Cirebon Regency, with a focus on the Agricultural Extension Center in Sedong District. title: Hatching failure and embryo mortality in endangered populations of Eurasian Curlew ( Numenius arquata )
abstract: Hatching failure represents a significant and growing barrier to reproductive success in threatened birds and yet is often poorly understood. Populations of the Eurasian Curlew Numenius arquata in the United Kingdom and Republic of Ireland have experienced significant declines over recent decades, and low breeding productivity is a major barrier to conservation efforts. However, data on hatching failure, infertility and embryo mortality rates are currently lacking. abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Floral scent is crucial for mediating plant-pollinator interactions, a primary driver of angiosperm diversity. The dynamic nature of olfactory cues means they can be fine-tuned to suit pollinator activity, making them an effective method of adaptation to local pollinator niches. Asarum sect. Heterotropa is one of the most species-rich lineages in Japan with remarkable variation in floral scents. title: FuChi is a cell cycle biosensor for tracking cell cycle dynamics during avian development
abstract: The ability to monitor the proliferative status of live cells both in vitro and in vivo over time has revolutionised our understanding of development, growth and disease. This was first made possible by fluorescent ubiquitination-based cell cycle indicator (Fucci) technology, which distinguishes specific cell cycle phases through the reciprocal degradation of fluorescently tagged, truncated forms of human CDT1 and GMNN proteins. title: Repurposed lives: shipping containers as contested sites of urban citizenship in Accra
abstract: This study investigates how shipping containers are repurposed as architecture in Accra, Ghana. The study reveals the spatial factors shaping the emergence of these adaptive structures. Rather than being randomly situated, containers cluster in strategic locations enabling access to livelihoods while also avoiding eviction threats. Their positioning highlights contradictions between top-down urban planning favouring elite interests and the needs of marginalised residents. title: Magmatic U-Pb zircon ages west of the Domeyko Fault System, Collahuasi District (Chile): implications for its potential westward continuity
abstract: This study presents new high-precision U-Pb zircon age data to document previously unrecognized igneous bodies in a poorly explored sector in the western part of the Collahuasi District, northern Chile. By integrating these new geochronological constraints with detailed geological mapping, petrography, and mineralogical observations, the temporal and spatial patterns of magmatism west of the Domeyko Fault System, the most relevant tectonic structure in the zone, are refined. title: Differentiated mosquito adaptive strategies underlie regional dominance of three ECSA sub-lineages in chikungunya virus
abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) has emerged as a rapidly expanding global health threat and has been reported in 119 countries and territories, with recent outbreaks across Asia, Europe, and the Americas. The East/Central/South African (ECSA) genotype has increasingly predominated in multiple regions, yet the molecular basis of its competitive advantage remains unresolved. abstract: The growing burden of infectious and chronic diseases associated with bacterial infections and oxidative stress highlights the need for novel antibacterial and antioxidant agents. Fungal endophytes are promising sources of bioactive metabolites with pharmaceutical potential. This study focused on the isolation, characterization, and biological evaluation of endophytic fungus extract obtained from the leaves of Centella asiatica (L.) Urban. abstract: Purpose This study investigates the spatiotemporal and seasonal variations of land surface temperature (LST), surface urban heat island (SUHI) intensity, and the urban thermal field variance index (UTFVI) in Khartoum State, Sudan. The study aims to characterise seasonal thermal patterns and identify areas experiencing greater thermal stress to support climate-responsive urban planning and heat mitigation. abstract: Here we report exploratory pollen (and spores) and starch analyses of soils/sediments from the Cloudman site, encompassing the Early Late‐Woodland ( ad 500/600−1000) to modern times. Pollen results reflect the regional Late Holocene vegetation dominated by the Pinaceae, with angiosperm forest trees less represented. Consistently moderate amounts of grass (Poaceae) pollen in many samples reflect the local alvar vegetation, and charcoal particles, Taraxacum ‐type pollen, and bracken ( Pteridium aquilinum ) spores also in many samples suggest vegetation fires set by people. abstract: Abstract Polysaccharide-based materials, particularly dextran (Dex) derivatives, have emerged as versatile platforms for biomedical and materials science applications primarily due to their tunable chemical functionality and intrinsic biocompatibility. abstract: One of the most studied biomaterials for biomedical applications is hydroxyapatite (HAp), a bioactive ceramic (Ca-P) with structural and compositional similarity to the mineral phase of human bones and teeth. HAp is investigated for various applications, such as bone regeneration, dental implants, tissue engineering, implant coatings, and controlled drug delivery systems, due to its excellent biocompatibility, osteoconductivity, and ability to accommodate ionic substitutions. abstract: A one-pot, three-component reaction of aromatic aldehyde, malononitrile, dimedone or ethyl acetoacetate was developed in which the reaction medium and promoter was 1,1,1,3,3,3-hexafluoro-2-propanol (HFIP). title: Integrating Bioacoustics and Community Science for Advancing Bat Research: Insights From Urban–Rural Landscapes Across Regions in Peru
abstract: ABSTRACT In the tropics, rapid urbanization, scarce research, and limited resources for studying bats constrain conservation efforts, positioning community science as a practical approach to address these challenges. This study presents the first integration of community science and passive acoustic monitoring for bat research in the Neotropics, implemented across urban and rural landscapes of the Peruvian Coast, Andes, and Amazon to investigate bat community structure and environmental responses. abstract: Gas sensor science is currently an experimental field and relies only to a small extent on theoretical calculations. However, novel recent advances in theoretical gas sensor models can predict the exact doping ratio for maximum sensitivity and lowest response time. In this work, WO3 doped with Co3O4 is used to monitor colorless, toxic H2S gas. abstract: This study presents a bio-inspired open knee joint for biofidelic robots with an anatomically correct range of motion. Bio-inspired joints contribute to robot performance and understanding living organisms by providing dynamic motion data as the real-world physical twin. The proposed joint structure features the integration of the open joint and ligamentous constraint. abstract: Study purpose. This study aimed to analyze 2D kinematic characteristics (joint angles and posture displacement) and evaluate the effects of the maneuver side (port and starboard) and movement phase transitions (before, during, and after) during hiking maneuvers in elite Optimist class sailing. abstract: The search for novel organic compounds as PSII inhibitors and copper (Cu2+) ligands addresses key agricultural challenges. title: Multiple stressor effects of hypoxia and metals on ventilation, activity, bioaccumulation, and loss of equilibrium in fathead minnows
abstract: Hypoxia is an increasing concern in freshwater ecosystems, driven by warming, stratification, and nutrient enrichment. Fish cope with hypoxia through behavioural and ventilatory adjustments, yet growing evidence suggests that certain metals can impair these critical compensatory mechanisms. It is currently unknown whether lead (Pb) and nickel (Ni), released in part through expanding mining operations, may alter these critical survival responses. abstract: Introduction In India, Argemone mexicana is known for its pharmaceutical value. The plant hosts many endophytes. Plant-associated microbes also help plants with development and protection. Material and methods A metagenomic study of rhizospheric soil, roots, and shoots was conducted to investigate variation in the organization and diversity of fungal communities from two different locations (Amlighat and Dergaon, Assam, India) for the first time. title: Impact of Armed Banditry on Agricultural Productivity Among Rural Farm Households in North Central Nigeria: A Propensity Score Matching Approach
abstract: Armed banditry has emerged as a major threat to rural livelihoods and agricultural production in Nigeria, particularly in North Central Nigeria, a major food-producing region. Despite growing evidence linking insecurity to agricultural decline, empirical evidence on the causal effects of banditry on household’s farm productivity remains limited. This study examines the impact of banditry on agricultural productivity among rural farm households in Niger and Plateau States Nigeria. abstract: The discovery of the Huanglongling-Tashidaban giant lithium ore-field represents a major breakthrough within the Altyn Tagh metallogenic belt. abstract: The tawny-bellied cotton rat, Sigmodon fulviventer dalquesti, is a Texas endemic subspecies reported only from a collection that occurred in 1991 near the town of Fort Davis in the TransPecos region. abstract: Long-term amplitude and phase variations in pulsating stars produce side peaks or multiplets in the Fourier spectrum of the light curves around the pulsation frequency and its harmonics. Such structures are often attributed to modulation, although linear beating and the non-linear coupling of close oscillations can also produce similar patterns. abstract: Background: Employee performance is critical to service organizations, where employee attitudes and organizational support can directly shape service delivery. Internal marketing practices such as empowerment, rewards, supportive supervisor relationships, and career opportunities can strengthen organizational commitment and enhance employee performance. Here, the chemical degradation of GO-AgNPs was investigated by sodium hypochlorite (bleach water) linked to its antimicrobial and ecotoxicological effects. abstract: Abstract Seismic safety assessment of nuclear power plant (NPP) sites depends critically on the simultaneous characterisation of ground motion intensity and the capacity of the local soil to amplify that motion. While global probabilistic seismic hazard models and global shear-wave velocity (Vs30) compilations are now available, no prior study has combined these two open global datasets into a single, reproducible screening metric spanning the multi-country reactor-unit inventory. title: Unveiling the gut microbiome-immune-brain axis in schizophrenia
abstract: Schizophrenia (SCZ) is frequently associated with gastrointestinal disturbances, suggesting that gut microbiota alterations may contribute to disease pathophysiology through the gut-immune-brain axis. However, the mechanisms linking gut dysbiosis to neural dysfunction remain poorly defined. Here we show that gut microbiota from SCZ patients is associated with systemic immune dysregulation and altered brain-immune homeostasis in recipient mice. abstract: Context Rainfed woody crops in the Mediterranean are deeply embedded in and well-adapted to local socio-ecological conditions. These agroecosystems have the potential to provide a range of ecosystem services (ES), including flood and erosion control, drought mitigation, biodiversity enhancement, and preservation of cultural identity. abstract: Canada’s potential to generate more renewable energy than it needs has led to visions of it becoming a leader in low-carbon hydrogen. In the Atlantic provinces, this has involved proposals aimed at producing ‘green’ hydrogen and its derivatives, predominantly for export to Europe. Despite trade being a contributor to carbon emissions, green hydrogen offers an alternative vision where trade is used to spur a clean energy transition and decarbonize hard-to-abate industries, driving growth, jobs and investment. abstract: The practical adoption of orbital angular momentum (OAM) in technologies ranging from high-capacity communications to quantum information science has been severely hindered by the lack of integrated devices capable of dynamic OAM manipulation across broad bandwidths. title: Integrating cortical microtubules into plant gravity signaling: dynamics, tubulin phosphorylation, and growth regulation
abstract: Plant gravity responses depend on coordinated signaling and growth-control mechanisms that convert directional and mechanical stimuli into differential cell expansion. Cortical microtubules are central to the conversion: they pattern cellulose synthase trajectories, set cell-wall anisotropy, and are remodeled in altered-gravity and tubulin-mutant systems. abstract: A moment magnitude (Mw) 7.7 earthquake, as reported by the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS), struck central Myanmar on 28 March 2025. Its epicenter was situated near the Sagaing Fault, a major right-lateral strike-slip fault system that accommodates the relative motion between the Indian and Sunda plates. abstract: In recent years, climate change has significantly increased the severity and frequency of wildfires across Europe, with the 2025 season marking an unprecedented peak of one million hectares burned. Rapid and cost-effective mapping of these damaged areas is crucial for environmental recovery, making satellite remote sensing an indispensable tool. abstract: Abstract Background and Aims Actinorhizal root nodule symbioses are formed between a diverse group of mostly woody dicotyledonous plants and nitrogen-fixing soil Actinomycetota of the genus Frankia . abstract: Reproductive performance in strawberry is influenced by pollen fertility and stigma receptivity, which may vary among cultivars. The present palynological study was conducted to evaluate key reproductive traits in six strawberry (Fragaria × ananassa Duch.) cultivars, viz., Chandler, Kimberly, Larson, Sweet Charlie, Winterdawn and Selva, during the 2024–25 and 2025–26 growing seasons at SKUAST-Kashmir, Shalimar, India. abstract: ABSTRACT Dung beetles are a vital component of ecosystems, providing essential ecosystem services. However, the factors that regulate the functional response of dung beetles and dung removal across altitudinal gradients have been scantily explored. Along an altitudinal gradient in rainforests of the Talamanca Cordillera of Costa Rica, we assessed the structure, composition, functional diversity, and dung removal rates of the dung beetle assemblage. title: Bridging the cultural divide to improve drinking water security, sustainability and resilience in first nations communities: A case study from Australia
abstract: First Nations communities (Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples) in remote Australia experience disproportionate risks to drinking water security, compounded by climate change. Community drinking water systems are operated predominantly by government service providers to meet regulatory requirements, yet many systems fail to meet quality standards. title: Retrieval-to-abstraction LLM-assisted literature synthesis: Case demonstrations in digital health technology-enabled randomized controlled trial outcome reporting
abstract: Systematic reviews of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) support evidence-based clinical advancement. Clinical trial reporting guidelines, including CONSORT, establish common data elements that support systematic synthesis of published trial outcomes. However, the rapid rise of digital health technologies presents new challenges for reporting guidelines, and substantial real-world reporting heterogeneity has been observed. abstract: ABSTRACT Graphical abstract showing the assessment of EcoSan sustainability in Kabale District, Uganda, using a multi-criteria analysis approach based on health, technical, environmental, socio-cultural, economic and financial, and legal and institutional criteria. This study evaluated the sustainability of ecological sanitation (EcoSan) systems in Kabale Municipality, Uganda, using a multi-criteria analysis framework based on the analytical hierarchy process (AHP). abstract: ABSTRACT The anti‐inflammatory activity of Cotula cinerea essential oil (EO) was evaluated using integrated chemical, in vivo, histological, and computational approaches. Gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (GC–MS) identified trans‐thujone (51.86%), santolina triene (10.60%), and sabinene (6.17%) as the most abundant constituents. abstract: The Pomacea canaliculata is a globally invasive freshwater pest that poses significant threats to both agriculture and aquatic ecosystems; however, conventional molluscicides, such as niclosamide, exhibit high toxicity toward non-target organisms, leading to substantial ecological risks. To develop highly potent and environmentally benign molluscicides, we designed and synthesized a series of 15 novel compounds, among which D-1 emerged as the most promising candidate. title: Real-time process analysis and optimization of nitroguanidine synthesis in microflow using inline Raman spectroscopy
abstract: Non-contact inline Raman spectroscopy is used as a fast, flexible, and safe method for monitoring and optimizing continuous-flow processes involving highly hazardous and corrosive materials. The synthesis of nitroguanidine (NQ), an energetic material, was characterized and optimized as a model for hazardous reactions. abstract: This study analyses the free vibration and thermal buckling of size-dependent, axially functionally graded Euler–Bernoulli nanobeams using a nonlocal thermo-elastic Fredholm integral model based on Eringen’s nonlocal elasticity. abstract: Abstract Persistence of SARS-CoV-2 has been proposed as a biological driver of Long COVID, a disabling chronic illness with no proven treatments. We conducted an exploratory, placebo-controlled, double-blind, 2:1 randomized mechanistic trial (NCT05877508) of the SARS-CoV-2-specific monoclonal antibody AER002 in 36 participants who met the World Health Organization case definition of Long COVID. title: Aridity-driven shifts in plant–microbial diversity relationships across the arid and semi-arid grasslands of northern China
abstract: Abstract Climate change-driven aridification threatens above- and belowground biodiversity, yet how the relationships between plant diversity and soil microbial diversity change along aridity gradients remains unclear. Here, we conducted a 4,000-km field survey across arid and semi-arid grasslands in northern China. title: Weak and inconsistent associations between birch-feeding insects and pollution levels around two industrial towns during substantial emission decline (1988–2025)
abstract: Industrial emissions have historically altered terrestrial ecosystems, but their long-term effects on insect herbivores remain insufficiently understood, particularly during ecosystem recovery following emission decline. We analysed a dataset on the densities of 24 Recognisable Taxonomic Units (RTUs) of birch-feeding insects collected from 1988 to 2025 around two industrial towns in northwestern Russia previously identified as pollution hotspots. title: Environmental Factors' Effect on Alpha and Beta Diversity of Butterflies in North‐East Algerian Forests
abstract: ABSTRACT The specific factors determining butterfly alpha and beta diversity in Algerian forests remain insufficiently understood; not a single study has yet addressed this issue. Most previous studies in the region have exclusively focused on richness and abundance without evaluating how environmental variables shape community diversity. To address this knowledge gap, we conducted a field survey from May 2019 to March 2021 across three forest massifs in North‐east Algeria. title: Structural and Evolutionary Analysis of Non-specific Lipid Transfer Proteins (nsLTPs) in Cereus (Cactaceae)
abstract: The genus Cereus (Cactaceae), widely distributed across arid and semi-arid environments of South America, exhibits adaptive capacity that is partly associated with proteins involved in lipid metabolism and stress responses, such as non-specific lipid transfer proteins (nsLTPs). Although well-characterized in model plants, the structural diversity and functional roles of these proteins in cacti remain largely unexplored. In this study, we characterized the nsLTP repertoire of Cereus by integrating transcriptomic data, phylogenetic analyses, structural modeling, and ligand-binding site mapping.

abstract: Purpose: This study examines the relationships between professionalism, mindfulness, and job satisfaction among airline pilots and explores the mediating role of mindfulness in the relationship between professionalism and job satisfaction. Design/methodology/approach: The study employs a quantitative survey design. The sample consists of 171 airline pilots. abstract: Despite advancements in the field, generation of community science data exceeds its application. To better understand what shapes data use at a system level, we examine perceptions of data quality and trust in data usage from the perspectives of volunteers and professionals by leveraging a community wildlife monitoring program. We surveyed 486 volunteers on their perceptions of the data before and after participation. abstract: Abstract Liquid-phase separation underpins numerous sectors of modern chemical industry, yet achieving high selectivity for separation of mixtures of organic compounds remains a persistent challenge. Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), showing exceptional tunability in composition, topology and pore environment, hold unique promise to address this challenge. title: Thermostability and pH Differentiation in Geobacillus Hydrolases: A Comparative Perspective
abstract: Thermostable enzymes are central to high-temperature industrial processes because they combine catalytic efficiency with structural resilience under demanding conditions. Among thermophilic bacteria, Geobacillus has emerged as a prominent source of industrially relevant enzymes, particularly hydrolases such as proteases, lipases, and carbohydrate-active enzymes. title: Soil-plant-animal properties and microbial reassembly distinguish cattle oral disease prevalence across converted Amazon pasture systems
abstract: Forest-to-pasture conversion can alter soil properties, forage composition, and microbial communities, but whether these changes are associated with bovine periodontitis remains unclear. We compared eight pasture systems in the Western Brazilian Amazon classified by high or low herd-level prevalence of periodontal lesions. title: Infant-caregiver vocal contingency changes across varying interpersonal space
abstract: Vocal contingency between caregivers and infants is a fundamental building block for socio-communicative development. This paper investigates vocal contingency in home settings and how it varies as a function of the physical distance between infants and their caregivers. We recorded 61 mother-infant dyads when infants were 5-14 months old during long-form home recording sessions (M = 7.2 h; SD = 2.3; Range = 1-13), using wearable audio and proximity sensors. title: Genetic diversity in soybean [ Glycine max ( L .) Merr.] genotypes based on agro‐morphological traits using univariate and multivariate statistical techniques
abstract: Abstract Soybean [ Glycine max (L.) Merr.] is a versatile leguminous crop that plays a vital role in biodiesel production, livestock feed, and enhancing global food security. Soybean production and productivity in Ethiopia are low compared to the national potential, mainly due to the lack of high‐yielding genotypes. Substantial genetic variability is essential for developing high‐yielding, climate‐resilient soybean varieties. abstract: Biobased fertilizers could be sustainable alternatives to mineral inputs and restore soil functionality, but their effect in calcareous soils with limited phosphorus (P) phytoavailability remains unclear. abstract: Remote areas remain among the least-monitored environments worldwide because conventional field-based monitoring programs are constrained by logistical challenges, limited accessibility, and high operational costs. These limitations create persistent spatial data gaps that hinder ecosystem assessment and evidence-based management. abstract: Understanding how topography and forest structure drive the transformation of incoming solar energy into local microclimatic conditions is essential for predicting forest resilience under climate change. Quantifying the importance of such attributes on the stratification of microclimates requires the integration of heterogeneous ecological data streams. abstract: ABSTRACT Visible/near‐infrared (Vis/NIR) spectroscopy offers a promising non‐destructive technique for assessing round eggplant ( Solanum melongena var. esculentum ) quality. For the purple‐black round eggplant samples examined here, however, dark pericarp coloration and multi‐layered tissue structure limit light penetration and accurate internal evaluation. abstract: The Scincella silvicola complex is a ground skink endemic to Mexico and comprises S. s. silvicola, S. s. caudaequinae, and S. gemmingeri forbesorum, distributed along the Atlantic slopes from Nuevo León to northern Oaxaca. title: Occupational branches of Japan’s ruling party: building linkages while hedging clientelist exposure
abstract: Abstract Reassessing the underappreciated grassroots of Japan’s Liberal Democratic Party (LDP), I argue that the party’s localized institutions not only mobilize votes but also mitigate the risks of clientelism. Informed by field research and relying on documentary evidence, descriptive statistics, and financial records, I identify mechanisms that link the party to citizens, even in the periphery. title: Wind energy in european balancing markets: policy challenges, market design, and a multi-criteria feasibility index
abstract: The transformation of the European electricity market under the Clean Energy Package (CEP) has positioned wind power as a cornerstone of the EU’s renewable energy transition. Balancing markets have consequently become strategically important, requiring wind power to assume a more active and technically capable role. Despite ongoing reforms, technical, regulatory, and economic barriers still affect its effective participation. title: Brechas de interoperabilidad y adopción de salud digital en los establecimientos sanitarios del Perú
abstract: The digital transformation of the Peruvian healthcare system faces challenges relating to interoperability, infrastructure, connectivity and training, which limit the secure and timely exchange of clinical information. The coexistence of incompatible platforms between the Ministry of Health (MINSA), EsSalud, the Armed Forces, the National Police and the private sector fragments care, hinders longitudinal patient follow-up and contributes to the duplication of tests, diagnostic delays, clinical errors and administrative overload. title: Development and validation of a simple impulse-based method for inductor design in electromagnetically driven tools for high-speed material processing
abstract: Electromagnetically driven tools offer a promising way to accelerate conventional tools to high speeds in order to take advantage of the beneficial effects of high strain rates in material processing. title: Overwintering Strategies Drive Climate Change Impacts on Body Mass in Northern Mammals
abstract: Climate change drives variable shifts in mammalian body sizes, yet the mechanisms underlying this variation remain unclear. Two explanations prevail: (1) higher temperatures reduce thermal constraints, favouring smaller bodies; or (2) warming enhances primary productivity, supporting larger bodies. We propose that species' overwintering strategies, which mitigate exposure to winter temperatures, determine which mechanism predominates. abstract: Decellularized extracellular matrix (dECM)-based hydrogels in previous research demonstrated as promising biomimetic scaffolds. However, conventional decellularization protocols are commonly based on harsh detergents that disrupt ECM integrity. While milder detergents such as sodium lauryl ether sulfate (SLES) and physical methods like ultrasonication have been proposed to reduce these negative effects, their combined application and the influence of ultrasonication parameters remain insufficiently explored. title: Enhancing Environmental Predictability and its Effects on Rhesus macaque (Macaca mulatta) Behaviour
abstract: Animals in captive conditions are often exposed to variation in environmental predictability, in part because management practices share similar incidental cues that prevent animals from anticipating what is about to occur. This unpredictability can have negative welfare implications. title: Spatial and Temporal Scale Sensitivity in NDVI-Based Greenness Exposure Assessment for Alzheimer’s Disease Incidence: A Miami-Dade County Medicare Cohort Study
abstract: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a leading cause of dementia, and neighborhood greenness may represent a protective environmental exposure. However, greenness-health associations may depend on how vegetation exposure is defined across spatial and temporal scales. We examined the influence of the modifiable areal unit problem (MAUP) and modifiable temporal unit problem (MTUP) on associations between Landsat-derived Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) and incident AD among Medicare beneficiaries in Miami-Dade County, Florida. title: Comparing wolf feeding ecology between historical ranges and recently colonized human-dominated lowlands
abstract: The recent spread of wolves into highly human-modified landscapes in Europe is an important example of large carnivore recovery and illustrates their ability to live in environments very different from those usually considered suitable for the species. This study aimed to evaluate how wolf feeding habits vary over time and across space by comparing diet composition, trophic niche breadth, and key prey consumption between the historical Apennine range and the recently colonized Po Plain in north-western Italy, based on scat samples collected between 2021 and 2025. title: Contextual Microplastic Impacts on Croplands From Field Trials and Global Synthesis
abstract: Microplastic accumulation is an increasingly widespread anthropogenic disturbance in agricultural soils, yet ecological risk assessments remain dominated by simplified laboratory assays that may not capture context-dependent responses under field conditions. Here, we combined a five-year experiment across four semi-arid cropland sites with a global synthesis restricted exclusively to outdoor field observations to quantify microplastic effects on crop yield, soil quality, and ecosystem multifunctionality. abstract: The rapid adaptation of future specialists to extreme conditions of professional activity highlights the relevance of introducing interactive simulations for realistic modeling of scenario-oriented didactic situations. The study assesses the pedagogical effectiveness of interactive simulation training in developing decision-making, situational awareness, and team interaction skills among cadets. title: Travel time budgets and the potential to replace travel by car in urban regions: A case study from Finland
abstract: A shift towards sustainable modes of transport (walking, cycling, and public transport) is urgently needed to reduce the negative externalities of private car use. Whereas active travel is a feasible alternative for relatively short distances, public transport can substitute for a larger share of car use. City regions are often seen as the main targets for this mode shift given the availability of public transport options and the proximity of services. abstract: We present SW1D, a Python version of a legacy code for the forward computation of Rayleigh and Love wave dispersion curves as well as synthetic seismograms, in elastic, isotropic, laterally homogeneous media. title: Phoenix: A Modular and Versatile Framework for C/C++ Pointer Analysis
abstract: We present Phoenix, a modular pointer analysis framework for C/C++ that unifies multiple alias analysis algorithms behind a single, stable interface. Phoenix addresses the fragmentation of today’s C/C++ pointer analysis ecosystem by cleanly separating IR construction, constraint generation, solver backends, and client-facing queries—making analyses easy to compare, swap, and compose while exposing explicit precision–performance trade-offs. title: Estimating High-Energy Neutrino Effective Areas from Muon Propagation
abstract: Neutrino telescopes observe neutrinos through the muons produced by charged-current interactions. Most of those muons are born kilometers outside the detector, and how much energy they lose on the way is stochastic. We show that we can compute analytically the distance a muon travels before it falls below the detection threshold, while describing the statistical properties of its losses. abstract: Heterogeneous high--performance computing architectures expose numerical algorithms to perturbations arising from the non--associativity of floating--point arithmetic. abstract: Stagnation in the summation of floating-point numbers occurs when the running sum, or the accumulator, does not change its value despite addends being greater than zero. title: Safe Hypergraph Contraction via Capacity-Aware Repair Certificates
abstract: Multilevel partitioners shrink circuit hypergraphs through vertex contractions, yet a contraction that satisfies block capacity can still eliminate every optimal balanced bipartition.
